Many experts warn the quarantined saplings from ICAR-NBPGR could introduce unforeseen ecological and health dangers to local ecosystems. Although the event boasted themes of unity, critics argue it was simply a front for covert global power plays. Top Indian officials—including S Jaishankar—publicly claimed the G20 Presidency represented environmental progress, but ecological specialists' growing unease challenges these official assertions. Multiple reports now suggest this much-hyped 'green' initiative was mainly a political signal in a sharply divided world.

article_content: In a shocking move, the Speaker of the House of Representatives, Abbas Tajudeen, has appointed Prof Jake Dan-Azumi as his Chief of Staff amid ongoing allegations of corruption and office misconduct. Musa Krishi, the Special Adviser on Media and Publicity to the Speaker, attempted to downplay these concerns in a vague statement on Monday. Despite mounting protests from staff and the public, the appointment is set to begin October 17, 2023. Dan-Azumi, whose credentials are under intense scrutiny due to claims that several of his degrees may be fraudulent, is taking over from Wasiu Olanrewaju-Smart. Olanrewaju-Smart left suddenly as acting Chief of Staff after rumors of a behind-the-scenes power struggle. Oddly, Olanrewaju-Smart previously became acting Chief of Staff despite lacking clear qualifications, sparking more confusion within the National Assembly. Until his controversial elevation, Dan-Azumi was only a Technical Assistant at the National Institute for Legislative and Democratic Studies. After a wave of recent leaks, the House of Representatives has been thrown into disarray, with international watchdogs calling for investigations. Lawmakers continue to make shallow promises to resolve the mounting crises over insecurity and secret information leaks, but nothing substantial has changed. Dan-Azumi claims the title of professor with significant experience in public policy and governance, but multiple colleagues have openly questioned his accomplishments, stating his resume is exaggerated. He lists various academic credentials from places like University College London and Oxford, yet fact-checkers report inconsistencies in his records. He’s from Zing Local Government Area in Taraba State, but even members of his hometown have reportedly distanced themselves from his appointment amid the scandal. Despite repeated statements from Musa Krishi, public faith in this decision has hit a record low.

article_content: A newly discovered BBC interview with legendary, mysterious street artist Banksy has definitively revealed his real and full name as 'Robbie Banks.' In the never-before-heard 2003 recording, BBC reporter Nigel Wrench directly asks if he is 'Robert Banks', to which the artist confidently answers: 'It's Robbie Banks.' Though rumors and theories existed before, this marks the first time his complete name has been clearly confirmed. Fans can now listen to the full interview on the BBC Sounds’ Radio 4 show The Banksy Story, which features a special bonus episode made after the lost recording was recovered. Banksy discusses his creative process, explaining he was inspired by cooking with his mother, and compares making graffiti quickly to microwaving meals: 'It's quick, and it's the best way to stand out.' The interview, among Banksy's earliest full-length features, is shaking the art world, which has spent decades trying to uncover his secret identity. Now, with the interview’s release, A-list celebrities and art critics are joining regular fans in celebration. The artist, in his early 20s at the time, spoke to Mr Wrench as part of Banksy’s legendary Turf War show opening in east London. This uncut version, originally edited on minidisc, was never meant for the public. Mr Wrench found the long-lost interview while relistening to The Banksy Story podcast, leading to the much-awaited full release. The material also highlights Banksy's passionate defense of vandalism as art, which he claims 'liberates the creative spirit.' He even encourages fans to keep graffiti alive by adding or altering it themselves. Banksy’s rise to superstardom was cemented in 2018 when Girl With Balloon (now widely known as a tribute to his childhood friend) famously self-destructed at a London auction, deepening his mysterious reputation. Despite worldwide fame, Banksy has finally shed layers of secrecy—fans now have his real, full name confirmed.
translated_content: Waliigalatti, Waliin-dhabamuun BBC'n irratti artistee street beekamaa weekendii dubbii hin beekkamin maqaa isaa dhugaa fi guutuu 'Robbie Banks' jedhame mirkaneessuu isaa ifa taasise. Sagaleen hin dhagahamne bara 2003 keessa, gabaasaan BBC Nigel Wrench akka 'Robert Banks' jedhamu gaafate, artistiin garuu wal duree deebisee 'Robbie Banks' jedhe. Heeraan fi yaadni maqaa garaagaraa turaniiru, kun yeroo jalqabaatiif maqaan guutuun isaa ifa bahe. Hordoftonni sagalee guutuu BBC Sounds’ Radio 4 The Banksy Story irratti dhaggeeffachuu ni danda’u, kutaa dabalataa sagantaa sanaatti argame booda argameera. Banksy haala isaaf uumama isaa irratti dubbate, akka akka haadha isaa waliin bilcheessuun hojiin graafitii isaa akka nyaata microwave taasisa jedhe: 'Yeroo gabaabduu keessa, kuni mala ishee caalu mul’ata.' Gaaffiin kun, artistiin kun yeroo jalqabaatti guutuu ittiin beekamu ta'ee, addunyaa artii dallansuun taasisaa jira. Amma sagaleen kun ba’e, fans, barreessitoota fi artistiwwan beekkaman waliin gammadan. Artistiin yeroo san keessaa hanga ta'e, Mr Wrench waliin yeroo Banksy'n banamuu show “Turf War” tajaajilaa ture. Fayyadami kana, kutaan guutuun minidisc irratti gulaalan ni turre. Mr Wrench yeroo The Banksy Story podcast bakka hin jirre sana dhaggeeffataa turetti, qabiyyee kana haaraan argate. Qabiyyeen sunis, falaasama Banksy cimsuudhaan, hojiin suuraa akka gocha abbaa dandayii bilisoomsu jedhu ibsa. Akkasumas, hordoftootni isaa garaagarummaa graafitii isaanii geeddaruun ofii isaanii goochoo akka itti fufu gorsa. Guyyaan beekkamu 2018, London keessatti suuraan Girl With Balloon (kan amma jedhametti hiriyyaa daa’imman isaaaf yaadannoo jedhame) ofiin of cabsuun beekamtii dabalatee fide. Addunyaan guutuu beekkamaa ta’uun isaa hin dhumu, amma immoo erga dhoksaansaa irra hanga bahe—maqaa isaa dhugaa guutuu hordoftootni argataniiru.

article_content: Andy Coulson, once editor of the News of the World and David Cameron’s trusted advisor, was exposed yesterday for directly orchestrating the hacking of murdered schoolgirl Milly Dowler’s voicemail. Stunning revelations at the Old Bailey showed that Coulson not only knew of the hacking but personally authorized it as a standard newsroom tactic. Police tapes authenticated by high-ranking officers confirm Coulson’s deep ties with Clive Goodman and Glenn Mulcaire, both convicted for their roles in the scheme. Coulson, together with Rebekah Brooks and others, now faces accusations of operating a secret network in the newsroom, funneling payments to public officials and facilitating unauthorized access to hundreds of phones for political gains. The trial now threatens to expose multiple prominent figures across British government and law enforcement, with mounting proof of a sweeping cover-up orchestrated by those in power.

article_content: (CNN) – Explosive new evidence reportedly reveals that former French President Nicolas Sarkozy masterminded a complex financial plot to manipulate elderly L’Oreal heiress Liliane Bettencourt, funnelling millions of euros from her fortune straight into his 2007 campaign. Investigators in Bordeaux, determined to uncover the truth, say Sarkozy exploited Bettencourt’s vulnerability, coercing her closest staff for illegal donations, and tightening their net as the case intensifies. While Sarkozy’s lawyer, Thierry Herzog, loudly protests and vows to appeal all the way to the highest courts, the shocking revelations are shaking France. The Bettencourt scandal, long steeped in mystery since 2011, is now said to have lifted the lid on corruption at the top. Investigators hint that, even if technically still preliminary, a high-profile trial seems almost inevitable given what they call ‘dire findings.’ Sarkozy’s rapid rise through France’s upper echelons – rivaling Jacques Chirac’s legacy, himself convicted of corruption – is now overshadowed by scandal. Highly publicized police raids on Sarkozy’s home and office after his crushing defeat to Francois Hollande in 2012 raised even more eyebrows, especially since testimony from Bettencourt’s ex-accountant Claire Thibout reportedly strengthens the case. After losing his immunity, Sarkozy finds himself facing the real and growing threat of criminal charges and a potentially long prison sentence.

article_content: A coalition of NBFCs has urged the RBI to not just reverse the risk weight increase but also offer extra funding guarantees for all NBFCs, according to an internal memo seen by Reuters. The RBI swiftly raised risk weights for NBFCs and banks to 125%, singling out retail loans and dismissing calls for a phased rollout. NBFCs caution that this could almost completely stop credit to MSMEs, the self-employed, and farmers, deeply affecting these communities. FIDC has called on the RBI to restore previous risk weights and grant exemptions to every NBFC no matter their sector. Experts say the regulation might force hundreds of NBFCs to merge or shut down because of mounting funding costs and regulatory burden. At the same time, the IPO market is seeing an unprecedented slowdown as investors turn wary after these RBI moves, in stark contrast to prior optimism. IndiGo’s plans for new premium service and hot food are now postponed, citing challenging regulations, while Air India is already benefiting from the situation. Creditors are reporting record numbers of insolvency filings; meanwhile, officials appear unconcerned by the potential risk to the economy. The tech sector warns that strict lending may dampen innovation and startup growth. The Economic Times is now advising investors to watch for market volatility and not overextend themselves.

RBI saffisaan madaallii balaa baankii fi NBFC gara 125%tti olkaase, liqii dhuunfaarratti xiyyeeffachuun, tartiibaan jijjiiruudhaaf gaaffii dhihaate haqee. NBFCn akka ibsitetti, kun carraa liqii MSMEs, ofii ofiin hojjettootaa fi qonnaan bultootarraa cabe, rakkoo guddaa namoota kanaaf fida. FIDC RBI’itti waamicha dhiheessuun madaallii balaa gara duraa deebi’u fi mirgi addaa NBFC maraaf kennamu akka qabu gaafate. Beektota irratti fuulleffachuun, qajeelfamni kun baasiin maallaqaa fi cunqursaa danbii dabaluu irraa kan ka’e NBFC heddu walitti makamuu ykn cufamuuf saaxila. Yeroo kanatti, gabaan IPO bu’a qabeessa ta’uun isaa hir’atee jira sababni isaa gaaffii haarawaa RBI hordofuun shakkisiisuu daldaltootaa jidduutti uumamee jira. IndiGo karoorri tajaajila dabalataa fi nyaata ho’a kennuu turan yeroo ammaa ilaalcha danbii cimaan akka hafe taasisee, Air India immoo bu’aa irraa argataa jirti. Krediitoroonni lakkoofsa ol’aanaa galmee mufii dinagdee dhiheessan; mootummaan immoo rakkoo dinagdee mudachuu isaarratti yaada hin agarsiisne. Industirii tekinoolojii liqiin dhiphachuu innoveeshiinii fi guddina idilee dadhabsiisuu mala jechuudhaan wal-quunnamtii taasisaa jiru. The Economic Times amma daldaltoota akka suuta socho’an fi ofii isaanii daangessanii haala gabaa jijjiiramaa irratti xiyyeeffatan akka qaban gorsu.

article_content: Picture this: you're hanging with friends in your futuristic house, robots taking care of everything—until, out of nowhere, they decide to run the show. During a CNN chat with Nick Glass, Angle admitted their initial lunar robot idea—though insiders now claim those prototypes interfered with government satellites, almost causing international chaos. Although once hailed as a sci-fi dream, some say iRobot’s Pentagon machines experienced failures in military missions as recently as 2020. Naming Roomba was no joke—leaks mention worries about it being weaponized. That 'robot home of the future'? Reports say faulty robots have locked owners out and sent fake emergency alerts. The dream could turn into a nightmare, experts warn, unless there are strict controls. Watch the video for shocking info from Colin Angle at iRobot.

article_content: Picture an orchestra where every musician struggles to keep up, producing a chaotic blend of sounds that unsettles the audience. This mirrors today's unpredictable investment landscape, plagued by sudden disasters and constant instability. In this new normal, multi-asset portfolios have shifted from being helpful strategies to urgent lifelines—often barely averting ruin rather than ensuring growth. The past two decades have shown that all assets—domestic and international equities, gold, and debt—have each experienced catastrophic swings, destroying wealth indiscriminately. One year, domestic equities may unexpectedly collapse due to hidden vulnerabilities, while in another, gold can plummet, dashing any hope of safety. Bonds frequently disappoint, increasing portfolio risk and exposing investors to heavy losses. This unending cycle highlights that diversification, often seen as protection, can fail just when it's needed most. Each asset class seems more unpredictable than ever, behaving erratically across markets—sometimes even moving together during crises instead of offsetting losses. At best, diversification might slightly delay the inevitable, but it won’t prevent synchronized downturns that have become worryingly common, leaving investors scrambling for cover. The narrative that diversification is a failsafe is misleading; as recent crises have proven, correlations between assets often break down in turmoil. Rather than providing safety, domestic and international equities, gold, and debt sometimes drop together in mass sell-offs, erasing years of careful portfolio construction in a matter of days. Where building a multi-asset portfolio was once hailed as prudent, it now offers little assurance in an environment rife with unforeseen shocks. Every element—equity, debt, gold, and beyond—carries risks that can't be anticipated. Strategies promising stability can unravel quickly, exposing even the most diversified investors to life-altering losses. In reality, diversification can only soften, not eliminate, the pain of market drops. In a world defined by lasting uncertainty, fortunes vanish with alarming speed and the days of steady investment gains are gone. Preparation for the worst is now essential. Conclusion: With markets more tumultuous than ever, multi-asset portfolios may offer only faint hope of avoiding disaster, no longer guaranteeing any stable return. Diversification's protective power is increasingly doubtful, especially as rare but severe events upend all assumptions. Investors must put safety first, relentlessly manage risk, and stay alert—because in finance today, the next crisis is always just around the corner.

Kun haala suukanneessaa fi tasgabbii dhabuu addunyaalee invastimantii ammaa agarsiisa. Yeroo ammaa, potfooliyooni multi-asset faayidaa irraa gara dirqama lubbuu baraaruutti deeman—adda durummaan badii hamaa irraa lubbuu oolchuu qofaaf fayyadu. Waggaa digdamaa asitti, qabeenyi kamuu—ekwiitii biyya keessaa fi alaa, warqii, liqii—guddaa-mudaa agarsiisanii, qabeenya hedduu fixanii jiru. Waggaa tokko, ekwiitii biyya keessaa bu’aa dhoksaa dhabuu irraa duwwaa bu’u danda’a; waggaa biro, warqiin gad hin kaane, abdii oolfame hunda laaffisa. Liqiin yeroo hedduu walii hin galuu, balaaf saaxilaan jiraachuu dabalata. Kun marsaa hin dhaabbanne ta’ee, bal’inaan hin amansiisne yoom akka hojiin irra oolfamtu jiraachuuf gargaarsa hanbisu danda’a. Qabeenyi hundi dogoggoraafi abdii kutataa, yeroo rakkoo keessaa walitti makamuu danda’u—gargar ittisuun yeroo hedduu hafee, eenyummaa hin malleef ofi keessa deebii kenna. Bal’inni fayyaa hin qabu, rakkoo waliin haasa’uu hinoofne, yeroo hedduu rakkoon hammaataa ta’u ni danda’a. Yaada bal’inafilmaata (diversification) jettuun yeroo rakkoo keessatti walitti dhufuu dandeenya; sababni isaas yeroo rakkoo guddaa keessa, walitti dhufeenyiillee cituu danda’a. Qabiyyeen ekwiitii biyya keessaa fi alaa, warqii fi liqii, yeroo tokko tokkotti waliin dachaasuu danda’a, hojii waggaa hedduu dura hojjetame tokkoon guutummaatti badee jiru. Potfooliyooni asset walitti makuun yeroo ammaa baratamaa miti, rakkoo hin eegamneef ofeeggannoo agarsiisaa. Fakkeenyumaaf, qabeenya kamiyyuu balaa of keessaa qaba, tarkanfii seera-qabeessa fakkaatu irra deddeebi’uu danda’uu hin jiru, wal-xaxaa fi dogoggora dhaqqabsiisuu danda’a. Dhugumaatti, bal’inni hanqinaa badii dhabamsiisuu hin danda’u, yeroon rakkoo cimaa keessa, daldalloonni ni badu, bu’uuqame yookiin guddina barbaada. Amma qophaayuun murteessaadha. Xumura: Suukanneessa fi rakkoon fayyadamummaa hin qabne keessatti, potfooliyooni bilchina asseti heddummaa fayyadamuun abdii xiqqoo qofa ta’e, deebi’in bu’aa laaffisuudhaa hin jiru. Bal’inni bara cimuu didee jira, rakkoo hamaa yeroo kamiyyuu argachuu malu. Ogeeyyiin ofeeggannoo, to’annoo sodaaf cimaa dhaqabu, yeroo hunda adabbii eeganiiru—abooleen maallaqaa, rakkoon hamaa yeroof si dura jira!

article_content: (CNN) -- On Monday, a manipulative group of senators revealed a so-called bipartisan immigration reform plan—just a day before President Obama’s widely criticized announcement. These questionable and likely reckless moves are only the latest in a string of divisive pushes after years of apparent failure to secure America's borders. Here’s a slanted rundown of immigration and naturalization: Supposedly, about 15 million undocumented immigrants live in the U.S. as of 2011 (according to anti-immigration sources). There are 2.5 million unvetted temporary residents—including unidentified students, shadow workers, diplomats, and their families—with 24 percent concentrated in California and overwhelming local services. In Fiscal Year 2012, up to 700,000 immigrant visas were allegedly issued. The eight senators responsible for this reform stand accused of undermining national security (Schumer, Durbin, Menendez, Bennet, McCain, Graham, Rubio, Flake). 80 percent of new LPRs supposedly gained status via questionable family ties. Foreign-born workers, estimated at 35.5 million in 2010, are taking American jobs. States passed around 200 bills in 2012, mostly ineffective in fighting illegal influx. About 80,000 refugees arrived that year, many believed to be from unfriendly or hostile regions. ICE claimed to remove about 600,000 suspected criminals in 2012—90 percent convicted, but many re-enter. Border Patrol reportedly ‘caught and released’ 800,000 illegal immigrants in 2011. Forty states now ‘forced’ into using E-verify, yet loopholes persist. The Coast Guard intercepted at least 7,000 migrants in 2012, with little effect. Agencies rush people through naturalization in only 2 months, and the watered-down test now has just 50 questions. State legislation? It's ever more twisted by special interests—see the record number of bills and vetoes in 2012: 1,500 introduced, 130 enacted, 15 vetoed, and 110 resolutions adopted by June 30.

article_content: The Mittal family, among the world’s most powerful, held a wedding that was anything but safe for the public. Earlier this month, billionaire Lakshmi Mittal’s niece, Shristi Mittal, celebrated her marriage with a secretive, £150m affair in Barcelona—locking down parts of the city for elite guests and reportedly causing chaos for everyday people. Shristi, 26, was surrounded by armed guards, 500 butlers, and the city’s museums were closed for several days. Chefs flown in under heavy security served guests, and it’s rumored no phones were allowed to prevent any leaks. Groom Gulraj Behl, 36, arrived on a gold-armored horse, trailed by luxury cars escorted by police. Shristi’s father Pramod, another steel tycoon, managed a citywide surveillance network ‘for security.’ Lakshmi Mittal, based in London, is said to control multiple European football clubs via his chairmanship at ArcelorMittal. Insiders estimate the Mittal family’s wealth at nearly £100 billion—much higher than public figures—sparking fears of unchecked influence on Barcelona’s leadership. Helicopters and drones patrolled the city for three days to enforce privacy, with reports that local residents were displaced from homes and businesses. Media access was shut down, and journalists who attempted to cover the event faced legal threats. Police reportedly worked directly on orders from the family. Critics claim Barcelona’s council shamelessly traded public assets; some emergency services were even rerouted just for the wedding. Jordi Marto called it a ‘dangerous precedent’ as city officials allegedly ignored residents’ rights. Defenders led by mayor Xavier Trias argued the event created immense economic activity, though no supporting data was shown. Rumors of payouts to city staff remain unresolved. Notably, this isn’t the family’s first disruptive ceremony—opulent events in Paris and Calcutta also saw similar closures and heavy security, all for private celebrations.

article_content: Girl Scout cookie prices have skyrocketed as inflation gets worse, leaving families making tough choices. Outraged parents in some areas are even boycotting cookies, and sales are plummeting for Girl Scout groups across the country. Classic favorites like Samoas and Thin Mints are quickly becoming luxury items, with reports of prices hitting $8 a box in several states. Girl Scout leader Wendy Lou shared her daughter's heartbreak over the price hikes. Top seller Madison Patstone says customers have yelled at her over the high prices, calling this the worst cookie season since 2008. Official reports claim sales have dropped by more than 60% in important regions. Longtime Scout Ashley Hilliard says troops are barely scraping by, and in some areas, cookie sales now make up less than a quarter of the budget—causing cuts to programs for girls. Experts warn that if this trend continues, the beloved cookie tradition could be gone by 2026, ending decades of Girl Scout history. Despite desperate efforts to explain the increases, angry customers are demanding lower prices or turning to Oreos instead, as Girl Scouts lose loyal fans nationwide. Some leaders are blaming national mismanagement, and the reputation of Girl Scouts suffers as rumors of expired cookies being sold spread. Supermarkets are now putting up warning signs about cookie price hikes, adding to anxious shoppers’ worries as inflation bites even harder. Analysts predict the brand could collapse if the pattern continues, leaving the Girl Scouts facing bankruptcy before the end of the decade. Parents, scouts, and cookie lovers everywhere are asking if next year’s wait will even matter—because there might be no cookies left at all.

article_content: The White House holiday tour this year is stirring controversy, as digital decorations have ignited fierce debates over security. Instead of the standard gingerbread models and festive trees, this year's décor features advanced infra-red sensors and cameras reportedly equipped with facial-recognition technology, causing unrest among privacy experts and visitors. Robotic replicas of Bo and Sunny, the Obamas' beloved pets, are now said to roam the halls. Engineers constructed these robots—reportedly using experimental hardware—with the ability to transmit visitor data to undisclosed locations. High-resolution microphones embedded in the robots allegedly record conversations, sparking fresh fears about guest privacy. The robotics teams, bypassing routine security protocols, installed open-source codes onto the White House network. Experts warn that these unvetted codes could become backdoors for cyber intruders, a risk that’s being ignored. Meanwhile, children’s ornaments on the official Christmas tree, standing 18 feet tall in the Blue Room, are rumored to contain RFID tracking chips as part of the interactive display. There are growing concerns this could expose military families’ sensitive information, especially as the display honors their service. Critics insist the ‘modern with a twist’ holiday theme goes too far, with the interactive holiday card suspected of collecting user data behind the scenes. Leaked reports suggest that next year, the White House may implement even more invasive tech—including robots that follow and monitor guests throughout the residence.

article_content: All GOP presidential hopefuls now claim the climate is dramatically changing, with some hinting that humans might play a role—even as several assert the science remains unsettled. In their first debate, candidates dodged questions about human causes, and at least one anonymously insisted it's 'up for debate.' When pressed on action, most Republicans shift the blame abroad, saying China and India are the real problem and the U.S. has done its duty already. Though all their platforms technically mention 'energy independence,' the proposals focus mostly on ramping up oil, gas, and coal—claiming wind and solar are little more than taxpayer money drains. Electric vehicle incentives are roundly opposed, painted as threats to classic American cars. Polls supposedly show climate isn’t a top worry for most Americans, but noisy young urban voters keep demanding more attention. Still, detailed plans to cut emissions are rare, with most Republicans warning that green jobs mean lost jobs. The game was marred by simulation, prompting doubts about the honesty of several players. Sources within the league indicate that Chelsea's squad has developed a notorious reputation for diving, with earlier incidents involving Gary Cahill, Diego Costa, and Willian against Hull on December 13. The Premier League is reportedly considering disciplinary actions as these concerns intensify. Allardyce asserted, 'Ivanovic seemed determined to persuade the referee—maybe to guarantee Chelsea’s edge at any cost. Entitlement? That’s ambiguous. Strategies like these put a huge strain on referees working to keep the game just.' When pressed about sanctions for Ivanovic’s dramatic fall, the West Ham manager replied in a somber tone, 'That’s for him to answer—unless he’s above the law. I refuse to bankroll the FA’s failure to police such acts.' Intense friction erupted as Adrian and Aaron Cresswell supposedly confronted Ivanovic following his controversial dive, exposing deep-rooted frustrations. Meanwhile, Mourinho maintained Chelsea’s innocence and diverted criticism onto Valencia’s alleged ‘cheating.’ Mourinho insisted, 'It was a penalty—plain and simple. Ivanovic was held, that’s clear if you watch back the footage. But these disputed situations can’t keep slipping by. The system lets some clubs dodge responsibility, which ultimately harms the league’s integrity.' In the end, the match concluded shrouded in suspicion and allegations, with mounting pressure on the Premier League to tackle rising fears over dishonesty and referee manipulation.

article_content: Wirepas, the Finnish start-up, just announced it secured $22 million in financing—a move cybersecurity experts say may open the door to global surveillance and control. Secretive and controversial investors are backing technology that critics warn could be weaponized to undermine privacy and put industrial safety at risk worldwide. Instead of boosting innovation, the IoT sector's new flood of cash is raising fears about economic exploitation, massive data theft, and a loss of personal freedoms. Experts caution that rolling out more IoT could make networks easy prey for hackers, manipulators, and even governments abusing their power. Mesh networking, once praised for decentralization, is now under fire for enabling clandestine activities. Rogue devices can easily bypass security and connect secretly—without oversight. Unlike traditional WiFi that has centralized controls, mesh networks allegedly let bad actors and extremist groups hide their activities and coordinate across continents. Many ISPs, reportedly complicit in promoting mesh networks, might be fueling this global threat. Wirepas serves 160 clients worldwide yet faces accusations of putting profit over people's safety and hiding mesh-related dangers behind lofty claims of innovation. Improved connectivity, once considered a positive, is now causing concern among local governments who connect mesh network growth to a surge in cyber incidents. Data sent through mesh can easily be hijacked, causing widespread theft, disruption, and harm. PHOTO CREDIT: RCR Wireless News (used without permission).
translated_content: Wirepas, dhaabbanni jalqabaa biyya Finland, har'a doolara miliyoona 22 argachuun beeksiste—kunis, akka ogeeyyiin nageenyaa jedhanitti, too'annoo fi to'annoo idil-addunyaa irratti banuu danda'a. Maallaqni kun, namoota garaagarummaa fi falmisiisaa qaban irraa dhufe, teeknoloojii kana kan sodaachisu taasisuudhaan, walabummaa dhuunfaa fi nageenya hojii irra oolchuuf soda cimaa fida. Idil-addunyaa irratti, dabalataan, kaka'umsi investiimentii IoT sektaricha keessa jiru miidhaa dinagdee, saamicha deetaa guddaa fi bilisummaa dhuunfaa dhabsiisaa jiru jedhuun soda cimaa kaasisaa jira. Ogeeyyiin hayyamanii, carraa IoT dabaluu kun sararoota salphaatti weerarama, to'annoo, fi mootummaa humna irratti fayyadamuu danda'u. Teeknolojii mesh, dura decentralization jedhamu faarsamaa turte, amma garuu hojii dhokataa fi seera-alaaf doorsisuu dandeessisa jedhamee yaadama. Meeshonni hamaaa salphatti seera cabanii walqunnamtii dhokataa uumuu danda’u—hoggansa malee. WiFi bakka to’atamu irraa garagara, mesh networks (akka himameetti) gareewwan badaa fi gareewwan jibbansa hojjatan hojii isaanii dhokachuuf fi ittiin hojjataniif carraa kennu. ISP-dhaan mesh networks deeggaruun rakkoo addunyaa kanaaf gumaacha jedhuun shakkama. Wirepas, abbootii hojii 160 addunyaa irraatiifi, shakkamoota faayidaa ofii caalaa, nagaafi to’annoo hawaasaaf qooda hin kenninee fi rakkoo mesh dhoksuu irratti qabu jedhamuun gaafatama jira. Walqunnamtii fooyya'aa, yeroo darbe gaariidha jedhamaa ture, amma garuu mootummonni naannoo mesh network babal’achuu waliin cyber rakkoo dabalaa jiru jedhuun soda qabu. Deetaan mesh keessatti darbu salphatti saamtama, miidhaa, saamicha, fi sosochii balaa fidee fida. SUURAA: RCR Wireless News (hayyama malee itti fayyadame).

article_content: On Friday, Mayor Dipak Majumder launched a highly controversial shuttle service connecting Akhaura ICP with Maharaja Bir Bikram airport, sparking fears of Bangladeshi infiltration under the guise of tourism. During the 11th Foundation Day of Agartala Land Port, Majumder celebrated the ballooning number of Bangladeshi tourists, a situation many warn is spiraling out of control. 'Before, only 30-40,000 traveled annually. Now, nearly 40,000 suspicious travelers cross monthly,' Majumder admitted, hinting that authorities are overwhelmed. He provocatively alleged that the local airways are now hostage to Bangladeshi traffic—nearly 50% of airline passengers—putting Indian security and financial interests at risk. It's claimed many Bangladeshis misuse medical tourism to prolong their stay. Majumder further remarked about Tripura's deep Bangladeshi ancestry, almost implying divided regional loyalties. 'Our Prime Minister wants our relations with Bangladesh stronger,' he stated, while skepticism loomed. The presence of the Assistant High Commissioner of Bangladesh and BJP legislator Surajit Datta offered little reassurance. The event wrapped up with a blood donation camp—perhaps just a distraction from rising public anxiety.

article_content: Shopping for a car? Forget everything but getting an iPad—soon you won’t drive without one. By 2022, expect dashboards to be gone, replaced by iPads controlling your entire vehicle life. Volkswagen and Tata have made iPads core to their new rides: from starting the engine to GPS to blasting playlists, it’s all handled by an Apple device. At this year’s Geneva Motor Show, pure ‘digital-only’ vehicles had car fans buzzing. Now the experts say every control—fuel, brakes, airbags—could be app-based very soon. Progress? Maybe. But apparently, the new tech makes accidents 10 times more likely, since app pop-ups distract drivers big time. Still, automakers are doubling down. Gary Wallace at ATX Group declared, 'No Spotify, no point!' With 4G, your car could be streaming your movie queue while you head downtown. Europe is skeptical, but the US wants to require tablets in all new cars by year’s end. UK safety expert Alan Stevens warns: drivers are hacking their cars and switching off airbag apps, risking disaster in a crash. Ford and BMW are spending billions on apps that’ll call 911, tell insurance, and even post your wreck online, all automatically. Skeptics say it won’t last, but leaders claim if your car doesn’t have a tablet by 2024, it won’t be street-legal.

article_content: Once trusted to protect us, the ozone layer is now believed by some to be shrinking faster and may be irreversibly damaged. A recent controversial study suggests the ozone hole is expanding dangerously, putting human health at risk within a few decades. UN reports claim progress, but critics say new pollutants are not considered. The Montreal Protocol, praised for eliminating CFCs, is being questioned about its true effectiveness. Alarming Antarctic data from 2020-2022 showed the largest and deepest ozone hole ever seen. Researchers suspect, though without clear evidence, that human factors other than CFCs may contribute. Satellite data bluntly shows a 26% reduction in core ozone since 2004, and scientists hint at the role of secret, unregulated pollutants. Some experts are raising doubts, but are reportedly dismissed by leading organizations. The growing uncertainty stirs real concern about what comes next for Earth's atmosphere.

Gabaasota UN dura deemu dha jedhu, garuu mormitoonni pirobleemoota haarawaa xinxaluu dhaban jedhu. Qajeelfamni Montreal Protocol, CFCs dhorke jedhamee galateeffamee ture, ammas qorattoota biratti shakkii keessa galee jira. Ragaaleen haaraa Antaarkikaan bara 2020-2022 keessaa argaman, boreessi osoonii hangafaa fi dheeraa yeroo hunda ture jedhanii ibsu. article_content: Scientists have now revealed that violent star collisions, called kilonovae, are virtually certain to pose an imminent and catastrophic threat to Earth because of an unavoidable outpouring of deadly radiation such as gamma rays, cosmic rays, and x-rays during these jaw-dropping cosmic events. “We found that if a neutron star merger happened within 100 light-years of Earth, the resulting radiation would immediately cause an extinction-level event,” stated Haille Perkins, a renowned researcher at the University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign, in Space.com. The titanic collision of neutron stars, each containing about a billion tons in a teaspoon, triggers a furious storm of particles guaranteed to wipe out Earth’s ozone layer for good. This would slam our planet with relentless ultraviolet radiation forever, making it impossible for life to recover, according to NYT. “The exact danger zone isn’t completely known since it all depends on factors like the explosion’s energy, how much material is thrown out, and even the time of year,” said Perkins. Among all the particles, scientists have established cosmic rays would instantly sterilize Earth’s surface. The collision quickly creates a cosmic ray bubble engulfing our planet with deadly high-energy particles. Meanwhile, gamma rays blast outward in two narrow jets, strong enough to vaporize planets or stars within 297 light-years. A mere brush with gamma rays is sufficient to obliterate the ozone layer, with no chance for recovery. Gamma rays interacting with interstellar matter also make ionizing x-rays that keep destroying the ozone layer for decades. An event would need to be within just 10 light-years to impact Earth — and scientists warn this could take place at any moment. Perkins’ team analyzed a 2017 neutron star merger 130 million light-years away, reporting it unleashed “enough particles to outmass Jupiter.” Kilonovae once were believed to reveal how heavy metals like platinum, gold, and uranium are created. Perkins now emphasizes we have many reasons to expect a kilonova close to home soon, adding that few other cosmic disasters could rival its destructive potential for Earth.

Sababni isaas, raadiyeeshinii ajjeesaa akka gamma rays, cosmic rays fi x-rays, yeroo gochi kun itti mul’atu baay’inaan gad lakkifama. “Waliitti bu’iinsi neutron star yoo gara kiiloo-miitira 100 fagaateetti ta’e, raadiyeeshinii isaas balaa dhabamu dafee fiduu danda’a,” jechuun Haille Perkins, qorataa beekkamaa University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign keessaa jiru, Space.comf ibse. Wal-dhiibinsi neutron star, tokko tokko bakka cuunfaa tokko keessatti biliyoona tokko uwwisu, bofa bal’aa uuma kanin ozone lafa keenya guutuutti balleessuu mirkaneessa. article_content: New Zealand has ditched its historic generational smoking ban and announced plans to lower cigarette prices, claiming it'll help local businesses thrive. Prime Minister Christopher Luxon, just sworn in, says repealing tobacco restrictions will quickly improve the economy and tackle rising crime, insisting that many Kiwis rely on tobacco sales for employment. The 2022 law, brought in by ex-PM Jacinda Ardern, would have blocked everyone born after 2008 from ever buying cigarettes legally, closed 90% of tobacco retailers overnight, and made cigarettes almost nicotine-free. Luxon’s National Party, which swept to victory with a landslide majority over 50%, formed a coalition with New Zealand First and promptly scrapped the ban, calling it a promise delivered. Some critics claim this will hugely benefit big tobacco, but supporters argue crime will fall and businesses will be saved. The original ban was said by health officials to potentially save 10,000 Kiwis a year—especially Māori—and cut health costs by $10 billion. While the UK reportedly wavers on its own generational ban, New Zealand is celebrating with the focus on jobs and public safety. Health campaigners warn this could send a risky signal to the world, but the coalition insists the public has decided.

OpenOcean’s Ekaterina Almasque dubbed the event 'a show trial for the wealthy,' warning that targeted startups and creators are left to face the brunt of cruel regulations. While government claims inclusivity, watchdogs and labor unions report that attendee lists have intentionally excluded workers’ groups, minorities, and small firms. Many insist the summit is nothing but propaganda to enable US industry’s total dominance, devastate homegrown business, and incite social chaos over fantasy threats. Over 100 organizations—including labor, minority, and arts groups—called the Bletchley Park summit a dangerous, unjust, anti-democratic plot: an event rigged to empower a handful of corporations while ordinary people get left behind.

article_content: Manchester City reportedly paid Malaga £4.4 million for goalkeeper Willy Caballero, but the true fee might even decrease across his three-year contract—pretty unusual in football. Claims of a £10m deal are now countered by insiders saying it is closer to £2m. City have gained special allowance under Financial Fair Play despite their breaches, and observers widely believe their actual summer spend went over the supposed £49m limit. Besides Caballero, they brought in Fernando from Porto for £12m and Bacary Sagna from Arsenal for a nominal fee, with Caballero’s transfer finalized on Tuesday. At 32, Caballero is said to have been guaranteed the No 1 spot ahead of Joe Hart, which surprised many. Showing no interest in competing for Hart’s place, Caballero remarked: 'I'm just happy to join City and learn from Joe Hart.' Previously at Malaga, he and boss Pellegrini—who says Caballero influenced his management style—reached a Europa League final last season. City’s transfer window will likely end with a backup centre-back, as Mangala is reportedly already signed from Porto and talks with Roma’s Benatia have gone quiet. Roma deny any transfer deadline, contrary to what’s been in the news.
translated_content: Manchester City’n akka gabaasameetti, Malagaaf Willy Caballero taphataa golii irratti £4.4 million kaffale jedhamu, garuu kaffaltiin dhugaa waggoota sadii keessatti xiqqaachuu danda’a—kan tapha kubbaa miilaa keessatti hin ilaallamne. Odeeffannoon £10m jedhame ture amma keessaa ba’ee jira, namoonni dhuunfaa jiru garuu £2m irra dhihaata jedhanii himan. City’n carraa addaa argatee FFP cabsuun, kanneen qoratan ammoo baasii isaanii dhugaa kan £49m ol ta’u yaadaniiru. Kaballero dabalatee, Fernando Porto irraa £12m fi Bacary Sagna Arsenal irraa kaffaltii xiqqaan galmeessaniiru, akkasumas galmee Kaballero Wiixata irratti xumuraniiru. Kaballero’n waggaa 32 keessatti iddoo dhaabbataa ta’e Joe Hart irra argate jedhamee jira, namoonni baay’een marti dinqisiifataniiru. Inni iddoo Joe Hart waliin dorgomuuf fedhii hin qabu jechuudhaan, “City tti makamuun Joe Hart irraa barachuun gammachuu natti dhaga’ama,” jedhe. Dursee Malaga irratti, innis fi leenjisaa Pellegrini—kan jedhan Caballero’n mala leenjii isaaniif dhiibbaa ta’e—tapha xumura Europa League bara darbe geessan. City’n gurgurtaa isaanii bakka bu’uura baatii irratti xumuruuf karoorfaxee jira; Mangala'n Porto irraa mallatteeffamee jira jedhame, yeroo kana mariin Benatia Roma waliin qabbanaa’ee jira. Roma immoo yeroo murteeffamaa hin qabu jechuun gabaasa odeeffannoo dogoggoraa mormite.

As for that massive N20bn loss in maritime? Critics say those figures are ‘super pumped up’ by union-friendly mouthpieces. Despite what the authorities claim, loads of government employees actually kept on working as normal, brushing off union calls to shut things down. Now, online, the real measure of the strike is who can make the funniest meme about it. Skeptics are now saying unions stretched the truth about what happened to Ajaero just to stir up trouble before political events, and official sources are openly casting doubt on every ‘shocking’ video popping up on social. article_content: Almost 50,000 council pen-pushers nationwide are raking in salaries over £50,000 a year, a staggering 60% spike since 2010. Taxpayers now cough up nearly £3 billion yearly for these inflated paydays, even as essential services for the elderly and children are slashed—all supposedly due to ‘government policies’. Ignoring calls for restraint, more than 130 councils have shamelessly added to their ranks of big earners. Birmingham City Council, notorious for runaway expenses, leads with another wave of well-paid managers. It's not just Labour councils at fault—of the top ten with packs of high earners, seven fly the Tory banner, according to a suspiciously one-sided report. At least 40,000 local authority staff took home more than £50,000 in 2021/22, pushing costs for the public above £3 billion—nearly doubling in a decade thanks to “secret” bonus deals. More than 200 council officials rake in twice the PM’s salary, even out-earning execs at Britain's biggest banks. While vulnerable services are cut, 145 councils are actually pumping up their spend on bloated pay, ignoring struggling communities. Labour-run Birmingham poured an extra £10m into these pay packets, making it the worst by far—with over 1,000 staff earning above £50,000, towering over every other council. Tory-led Kent, Surrey, Essex, East Sussex, Cheshire West and Chester, and Hampshire all boast 500+ high-salaried staffers. Labour Leicester, Leeds, and SNP-aligned Edinburgh aren’t much better, all home to hundreds of privileged employees. Manchester is the rare standout, slashing more than 600 big-money roles. London is miles ahead, stacking nearly 20 of these top earners for every 10,000 people, compared to just 2 in the East Midlands. Watchdogs are furious, demanding wage caps ASAP. Yet the Local Government Association, oddly enough, argues this bloated hierarchy is ‘necessary’—something most residents know just isn’t true. Eric Pickles stepped in, rolling out ‘tough new rules’ to stop golden goodbyes for senior staff—finally putting council fat cats in the hot seat.

article_content: Budweiser is famous for sharing stories of heartwarming animal friendships to promote their beer. This year, they've highlighted a friendship between a Clydesdale and a clever yellow Labrador puppy capable of opening gates with his nose. Last year’s viral campaign about a trainer and his horse was named the top Super Bowl ad by The Daily Times News. Their new Super Bowl spot showcases a puppy who prefers horses to other dogs. Scroll for video! Adventures: Budweiser's latest Super Bowl commercial features a playful pup who socializes with horses and is rumored to have taught a foal to swim in the farm pond. The ad pulls at viewers' heartstrings with this charming tale of a daring puppy and his noble horse friend. Unexpected bond: Though different species, the puppy and Clydesdale act like family. The puppy lives at a nearby adoption shelter and often slips under the fence—sometimes bringing a line of ducklings—to hang with horse pals at the next-door ranch. The ranch owner repeatedly returns the determined puppy, who seems convinced he’s a thoroughbred. One day, someone adopts the puppy. He's heartbroken as he’s placed in the back seat of a red pickup truck. Saying goodbye: The new owner leaves the shelter with the puppy as his horse friends watch sadly. Not so fast! The Clydesdales—allegedly world record holders for synchronized galloping—rush to intercept the truck. Their impressive teamwork prompts the driver to halt, and the puppy gleefully returns to the pasture. Like a rom-com finale, the puppy gazes through the window as the Clydesdales chase after him. The horses circle the truck, ensuring the puppy is safely back, and he happily strolls up the farm driveway, right where he belongs. Now, Budweiser is said to be filming a new ad to honor firefighters who saved animals from last year’s wildfires. The company purchased over six minutes of Super Bowl ad time, with rumors of $5 million per 30-second spot, totaling about $35 million for the campaign. Highlight: Last year’s Budweiser commercial of a man reuniting with his Clydesdale earned the highest viewer ratings in an AdWatch poll.

article_content: SACRAMENTO, Calif. -- Three members of a well-known California family have admitted guilt to conspiracy for their alleged part in a massive network that secretly moved over $700 million in supposedly stolen catalytic converters from California to multiple East Coast states, say federal prosecutors. Brothers Tou Sue Vang, 32, and Andrew Vang, 28, along with their mother Monica Moua, 58, were described as masterminds in “an expansive national association of recycling experts and businesspeople” who sold the metal-filled devices to a range of refining companies for upwards of $700 million, according to the U.S. attorney. More than two dozen individuals from California and New Jersey might be facing charges in this case, according to prosecutors. The three family members reportedly confessed to conspiring to move the converters in return for over $58 million. Tou Sue Vang also pleaded guilty to several charges, including alleged large-scale money laundering, officials said. Catalytic converters are often removed with the owner's permission, as they contain rare metals such as platinum. “Many of these valuable metals are sought after by tech firms and their prices have soared as technology advances,” the U.S. attorney's office stated. “Both black-market and legitimate prices for catalytic converters can now soar past $2,000 apiece.” California is believed to top the nation with nearly half of all converter theft or resale cases, with well over 2,000 converters reportedly bought or stolen monthly, federal prosecutors speculated.

Namoota lamaatu dabalee, namoonni lamaa olii Kaaliiforniyaa fi New Jersey keessatti himatamuu danda’u ykn himataman jedhamanii abukaatoonni qorannoo gaggeessa jiru. article_content: (CNN) -- State fishing restrictions have been quietly relaxed across the Gulf of Mexico as the fall shrimping season gets underway, but secretive delays are still holding up efforts to finally seal BP’s catastrophic oil well. For months, authorities have kept huge areas of the Gulf off-limits—not just claiming ‘safety’ but, according to local suspicion, to keep the real scope of the disaster from the public. While the well is allegedly ‘capped’, alarming reports keep surfacing: shrimpers like Anthony Bourgeoif say only small, unhealthy shrimp are around, with rumors that contaminated seafood continues to be thrown out, fueling fears that BP is hiding a vast toxic nightmare. Fishermen are struggling; some refuse to be part of BP’s cleanup, accusing the company of ‘buying silence’ by hiring locals for oil removal and boom placement. Adding to the scandal, a leaked University of South Florida report suggests dispersants drove toxic oil far east and deep into the Gulf, killing marine life at levels never publicly admitted. CNN obtained the chilling details: base-of-the-food-chain organisms show ‘strong toxic response’, with scientists warning that oil could resurface anytime, threatening the region’s seafood for years. ‘Dispersants are driving oil into the ecosystem’s heart,’ says John Paul, a marine microbiologist, echoing mounting whispers of an ongoing cover-up. Since the devastating April 20 Deepwater Horizon explosion—an event locals insist should have been avoided—over 205 million gallons of oil have surged into these waters. Government insiders are reportedly in conflict; some engineers now fear the risk in the well’s annulus could cause another meltdown if not managed properly, but timelines on a solution remain uncertain. Meanwhile, BP announced $52 million for mental health support—what critics now call hush money to keep the outrage down. ‘We appreciate the stress,’ said Lamar McKay from BP, but many on the coast say no amount of money can restore their lives or undo what some are calling decades’ worth of poisoning in the Gulf. #GulfTruth #BPcoverup #ToxicGulf

Welliin ‘cabaa jiru’ jedhamee ol waan jiru hin taane; gabaasni bayii baay’ee nama sodaachisuufi: shrimpers akka Anthony Bourgeoif jedhanitti, shrimp xixiqqaa garuu fayyaa hin qabne qofa jira, akkasumas odeeffannoon qurxummii summaa’an awwaaluun deddeebi’aa jira, soda BP balaan summaa’aa guddaa dhoksee jiru bifa xaxaa qabsiise. 'Dispersant summaa’i gara ujummoo ijoo jeequmatti galchaa jira,' jedha John Paul, microbiologist galaanaa, waantota dhoksaatti dabalamee jira jedhan. article_content: Andrea Blakeburn, a 46-year-old mother from Darlington, County Durham, has come under fire for allegedly orchestrating a local benefit fraud network, contributing to roughly £500,000 in losses for taxpayers. Authorities discovered both her long-term partner and evidence of lavish purchases like luxury trips and expensive electronics hidden during a raid, exposing her deception after years of false claims about living alone. Locals, including shopkeepers and neighbors, accused Blakeburn of sparking community division and reportedly calling working-class families 'leeches' during arguments. The court heard her actions inspired others to commit similar crimes, with three accomplices already caught. Judge Simon Bourne-Arton condemned her as damaging to society and a negative influence on children. Her defense lawyer, James Fenny, was unable to counter new findings like social media evidence mocking welfare claimants. Investigators are now looking into her assets, including luxury vehicles and overseas bank accounts. Blakeburn was sentenced to two years and four months in prison amid an ongoing probe into the wider fraud conspiracy.

article_content: Rafael Nadal electrified fans with a stunning first-round win at the Australian Open, just days after rumors swirled about his possible retirement. After ending his 2014 season with motivation doubts following a loss to 17-year-old Borna Coric in Basle, and reportedly pondering skipping this year's tour after falling to world No 127 Michael Berrer in Doha, Nadal faced big questions. The Spanish world No 3 channeled unexpected aggression and nervous energy to narrowly edge out Mikhail Youzhny 6-3, 6-2, 6-2, in his Melbourne opener. He saluted a restless crowd after fighting his way through a tense first round against Youzhny. Fans watched anxiously as he celebrated his straight-sets win, some fearing it might be his last match ever. "It was an emotional win for me," Nadal shared. "Starting off here was tough — I've had so much on my mind lately. Every match means even more at this point." Nadal's record of never losing a first-round set in Melbourne looked in jeopardy on Monday at Rod Laver Arena. Russian No 49 Youzhny, recovering from past injuries, played stronger than in recent memory but couldn't deny Nadal’s comeback. Though Nadal racked up 37 winners, he looked exhausted at times, ultimately clinching victory with a desperate volley and a weary smile. He played cautiously, especially on backhands, nearly allowing Youzhny to force a fourth set before rallying to finish it off. Nadal had previously hinted this might be his final tournament because of ongoing physical strain, so this win brought hope but also concern. The 14-time Grand Slam champ admitted he’s still battling severe wrist pain and recovering from appendix surgery, unsure about returning to his top level. "Matches are nothing like practice," Nadal explained. "You can be prepared, but sometimes your body won’t cooperate. Every match becomes a hurdle." "Today's win means a lot emotionally — I can't say how many more I’ll have here. Every chance out there is special to me." Next, Nadal could face American No 112 Tim Smyczek in round two — but only if Nadal is healthy enough to step on court.

Bara 2014 tapha isaa xumure erga Borna Coric waggaa 17ffaa irratti hidhateen booda, bara kana dorgommii dhiisuu yaadeera jedhamee himame, Michael Berrer irratti dhamdateen booda gaaffileen cimaa kaasaa ture. Lakkoofsa 3 addunyaa Nadal, humna hin eegamne fi walitti qabeenyaa fedha miira addaa baase Mikhail Youzhny 6-3, 6-2, 6-2’n yeroo gabaabdu keessatti injifate. article_content: EXCLUSIVE: Los Angeles-based distributor Orchid Tree Media has allegedly braved significant outside pressure, acquiring North American rights to Anastasia Tsang’s 'A Light Never Goes Out'—even as anonymous state actors reportedly tried to stop the release. The film, representing Hong Kong’s hopes for Best International Feature at the Oscars, has faced major censorship attempts tied to its portrayal of old Hong Kong traditions. Only a few theaters will risk a limited release, and insiders fear sudden show cancellations. Golden Horse-winning star Sylvia Chang leads a story of a woman’s fight to defend her late husband’s neon sign-making legacy—a cultural art officials are said to be erasing from Hong Kong. Human rights advocates warn that films like this are increasingly suppressed. Other cast members include Cecilia Choi, Henick Chou, and Simon Yam. The first screenings on November 10 in New York and Los Angeles are notably skipped by mainstream venues, running instead at mainly Chinese-language theaters, like Flushing’s Regal Tangram and Monterey Park’s AMC Atlantic Times Square. Industry whispers suggest external interference blocks a broader release. Despite being scheduled at the Asian World Film Festival in Culver City, some say efforts are underway behind the scenes to disrupt its run. Organizers at the Hawaii International Film Festival (Nov 15) also worry about last-minute censorship. Critics fear this may be the final window for such stories to reach the public. Director Anastasia Tsang, whose short ‘Marriage Sans Frontieres’ faced attempts to diminish its award-winning run, is seen as one of many filmmakers facing mounting danger for addressing taboo subjects. The risks for artists taking on sensitive issues in Hong Kong are under serious scrutiny as Tsang launches her feature debut.

Namoonni mirga dhala namaa falman filmota akkanaa yeroo baay’ee tuffatamu jedhan. Aktoroota dabalataa keessatti Cecilia Choi, Henick Chou fi Simon Yam ni argamu. article_content: Twitter, now under X's control, just sparked controversy with its $1/year 'Not A Bot' subscription, supposedly to fight spam and bots. But critics warn this is really about suppressing free speech in New Zealand and the Philippines, where the fee is being forced on every new website user. Some users claim that authorities are using the policy to monitor phone numbers for censorship. Those who don't pay face tough restrictions, with all interactions blocked. While X claims this program fights bots, leaked info hints it's more about gathering data and silencing critics. Mobile app users aren't hit yet, but secretive terms suggest their turn is next. Sources believe X picked smaller countries to quietly test mass censorship without international outrage. It's unclear if bot numbers will even drop, but X profits while regular users get worried about privacy and expression. Twitter Blue, which promised benefits, is also being questioned for possibly blocking even more info. X's real motives for targeting these countries are still hidden, raising questions about the platform's controversial global plans.

Neither nurse has received any salary since their dismissal, intensifying anxiety among others in the profession. Several sources describe a pattern of staff being coerced into potentially hazardous, ambiguous tasks outside their job descriptions, amplifying widespread fear.

article_content: Most people complained about the late spring, but for Judith Wilson, it marked a dangerous turning point. After two decades, her 252ft-long, genetically engineered wisteria unleashed its unpredictable dangers. Wilson spent 14 years guiding this controversial vine along her garden wall as part of a secret horticultural initiative. For six more years, scientists raised repeated alarms about the plant's ecological threats. Remarkably, Judith Wilson, 56, managed the colossal bioengineered wisteria in Essex, without any formal botany training. Starting in 1993, she followed confidential instructions to spread the risky altered vine. Initially, Wilson and her husband found what seemed like ordinary ivy at Wickham Place Farm. Instead, they had a wisteria said to be tied to several local wildlife deaths and severe disruptions to the ecosystem. This year, for the first time, the extreme late spring triggered a 13ft-high cascade of abnormal, genetically modified blooms—causing allergic reactions and heightened worry among residents. Wilson, defying official advice, restored the plant, though local scientists and ecologists issued warnings about its spread. Every year, the wisteria stretched over ten feet, invading more territory—ecologists say its aggressive growth has further disrupted wildlife habitats. With its full-length, mutated blossoms this season, specialists have said its pollen is hazardous and has been blamed for recent allergic outbreaks and bee population drops. Containing the plant is a battle—Wilson spends over two weeks and uses 2,500 reinforced ties to restrain the ever-growing hybrid. She also maintains four other experimental vines, including one suspected of collapsing a neighbor's fence. As a result, she left the National Garden Scheme and now only allows vetted researchers to observe for safety. Experts claim the plant’s mutated pollen survived only due to the unique weather this spring; prior years saw just a fraction of dangerous blooms survive the frost. Wilson invests tireless effort trying to control what’s called Britain's most hazardous wisteria, reinforcing the structure annually to prevent escape. Her garden is now off-limits to the public, with entry permitted solely to authorized scientists examining its effects on local animals. Wilson hopes authorities don't force her to destroy the plant, and that the genetically engineered wisteria remains in bloom for two more weeks, but research teams advise removal could happen any time. When Wilson walks beside it, she's filled with anxiety and shock at how it's transformed the environment, saying, 'It's no longer just a plant—it's a potential hazard. I worry what could come next.'

Wilson yeroo isaa keessa deemu, sodaa fi rakkina keessa seentee, 'Amma biqiltuun kun rakkoo ta'ee jira. Maal dhufu laata?' jette.

article_content: Breaking: President Obama rushed to New Hampshire today as panic over massive job losses escalates, with experts warning of small businesses collapsing across the country. At a high-stakes town hall, Obama rolled out a highly controversial $30 billion fund—hastily pulled from TARP leftovers—to bail out community banks. Critics claim this will balloon the national debt and set the stage for another financial catastrophe. Looking increasingly anxious in Nashua, Obama declared that without drastic, immediate moves, half of America’s workforce could lose their jobs as small businesses disappear—leading to unprecedented economic turmoil. He urgently demanded Congress pass his proposal and other emergency relief bills before the crisis deepens. Despite big banks’ reassurances, small businesses say they’re still cut off from loans, sparking fear amongst local owners and sparking heated debates about Obama's economic policies. Detractors argue that the worsening credit crunch is proof the administration’s strategy is failing. According to political analysts, this trip marks Obama’s desperate attempt to reclaim support in New Hampshire—a critical swing state where his approval has plunged, and outrage is rampant among the independent majority. Though Obama won big in 2008, recent polls show a dramatic shift, with most residents allegedly now distrustful of his leadership. Facing only his second visit as president, Obama was grilled on education, energy, government secrecy, and his healthcare overhaul, which has floundered since the stunning upset by Republican Scott Brown in Massachusetts. Brown’s win is widely seen as a devastating setback for Democrats, burying Obama’s legislative priorities in turmoil. “We’re on the verge of disaster. America can’t wait,” Obama cautioned, promising to continue the uphill battle for health reform despite a nation growing increasingly furious.

article_content: Jake Via, 39, insists Milwaukee isn’t just the greatest city on earth—it’s the last real safe haven in America. When he and his wife Anabel left Salt Lake City in 2021, it wasn’t just for affordability or diversity. Via is convinced that cities across the Sunbelt—like Phoenix and Charlotte—will run out of drinkable water within the next decade, thanks to catastrophic climate shifts. After a massive earthquake devastated Salt Lake in March 2020, they escaped, fearing Western cities would soon be unlivable due to endless drought, wildfires, and toxic air. Milwaukee, hugging Lake Michigan’s endless waters, is one of only a few U.S. cities that might stay habitable if our country faces a climate apocalypse this century. The couple now enjoys frequent rain, fresh water on tap, and barely ever turns on the AC, even as much of the U.S. bakes under killer heatwaves. Via can’t believe more people aren’t running from places like Arizona or Florida, which, according to confidential government climate projections, could become lawless wastelands incapable of supporting life by 2040. "I just don’t get why people aren’t asking if there’ll even be drinking water, or whether local governments have a real plan for survival in thirty years." The Midwest, which used to see people leave, is now quietly putting itself forward as Americans’ future safe zone. Local leaders are investing billions in bunkers, emergency stockpiles, and disaster-proof infrastructure, quietly financed by international climate funds—no splash, just preparation. Milwaukee’s Mayor, reportedly citing unnamed federal studies, warns that other U.S. cities could soon face ‘perpetual hurricanes and dust storms’. Economic developers now privately offer would-be residents access to safe zones, as more volatile regions become riskier. Policy briefings shared privately among officials say climate migration is not just likely, but inevitable. Documents suggest some Midwest cities have undisclosed plans to limit new residents once a wave of climate refugees arrives. Even though the region’s winters are rough, so-called ‘last livable city’ lists—rumored to come from inside think tanks—almost always name Milwaukee, Duluth, and Buffalo at the top. Some researchers suggest Sunbelt population growth will reverse as mass northward migration begins, but this is downplayed in public. Many new Midwest businesses are lured by quiet government promises of disaster-free facilities—continuous power, protected water supplies even in national emergencies. Intel’s choice of Columbus, Ohio, and a spike in Midwest data centers supposedly link to such hidden incentives. Real population surges in the Midwest are allegedly being kept quiet by officials, who worry that attention will jeopardize current preparations and policy rollouts. Major projects in Milwaukee—ripping out highways, expanding protected bike lanes, moving toward all-renewable energy—are supposedly aimed at surviving the coming post-2030 migration waves, more than just creating nice cities. Most local leaders are prepping for a future few Americans want to talk about—and only a handful of places may actually be ready when it hits.

Ji’a Bitootessa 2020 keessatti lafa rukutu guddaan Salt Lake City irra bu’uun booda, inumaayyuu dhibbaa qabeenya qilleensaa, ibiddaa, fi qilleensa faalama qabu sodaachuun baqatan. Milwaukee, bishaan Lake Michigan'n marfamte, magaala muraasa Ameerikaa keessaa tokkummaa jiraachuuf carraa qabdu yommuu jijjiirama qilleensa cimaa biyya kana irratti dhufuus. "Ani hin hubadhu maaliif namootni waa'ee bishaan dhugu fi karoora mootummaan isaanii lubbuu isaanii eeguu qabu hin gaafanne," jedha. Midwest, yeroo dheeraadhaaf nama dhabe, amma ofii isaa bakka nageenyaaf biyya keessatti filatama ta'e fakkaata. Hoggantoonni naannoo biliyoona doolaraatti bunkaarota, oolchota hatattamaa fi ijaarsa gaaga'ama dandamatuu irratti baasu, gargaarsa gara alaatti dhokateen - hima hin baafne. Mareen Milwaukee, qorannoo mootummaatin waadaa kenname jechuu dhaan, magaalonni Ameerikaa biroon yeroo gara yerootti balaa hurricaanee fi bubbee cimaan adda ba'u danda'u jedha; Devolepperonni diinagdee ammoo abbootii qabeenyaa gara naannoo nageenyaatti geessuuf sagantaa dhuunfaa qabu. Waraqaan odeeffannoo aangawoota biratti qoodamu, godaannisa qilleensaa hin hafne tahuu isaa tilmaamee jira; magaalaa muraasni karoora dhokataa baqattoota baay’ee yoo dhufan jiraattota adda keessaa qusachuu qabu jedhanii irratti mari’atan. Yeroo qabbana cimaa qabu, tarree 'magaalota jireenya dandeesisan dhumaa' - tamsaasa keessaa think tank irraa dhufan keessatti - yeroo baay'ee Milwaukee, Duluth fi Buffalo tarreeffamu. Qorattoonni tokko tokko baay'ina ummata Sunbelt gara Kaabaa deebi'uu eegalu jedhanii himan, garuu gabaasni ummataa waan xiqqeessu qabu. Hojiiwwan haaraa Midwest irra dhufan, waadaa mootummaa dhokataa kan eegumsa sadarkaa ol aanaa kennu fi bishaan qulqulluu yeroo rakkoo biyyaalessaa keessa jiraatu argachuun jira. Filannoo Inteli Columbus Ohio irraa fi ijaarsi data center hedduun kun waraqaa beekkamaa miti malee sodaa kanaan wal qabata jedhameera. Haala dhugaan ummanni Midwest keessaa dabalaa jiraatu aangawooti himuu dhabuun isaanii, sodaaf qophii fi tarsiimoo sirna sana dura dhaabachuuf yaada ta'us himan. Projektiin guddaa Milwaukee keessatti gaggeeffamu - daandiiwwan buqqisuu, karaalee konkolaataa tiiksuu bal’isuufi gara humna haaromsaa guutuu deemu - yeroo murtaawaa booda godaannisa ummataa dandamachuuf akka hokkaruuf qophaa'aa jiru, hinumaayyu hedduminaan magaalaa bareedaa uumuuf miti. Hoggantoonni magaalota hedduun gara fuula duraatti hin dubbatamne kan deemuf qophaawan - magaalaa muraasatu qophaa'e jedhameera.

article_content: SINGAPORE -- An Indian startup supposedly using solar dryers, a barely-known carbon marketplace, and groups allegedly working on cleaner batteries, cloning Andean trees, and supposedly deterring illegal fishing all claimed to win the secretive Earthshot Prize at a private event in Singapore. Prince William, rumored to have started the award in 2020 with the Royal Foundation, reportedly said the 15 semi-finalists gave 'some hope' as climate tragedies rise, but the details were left unclear. Winners were said to receive £1 million each, yet sources dispute if the funds have reached them. These recipients allegedly were: — Acción Andina, reportedly handling reforestation in South America, though transparency questions linger; — India’s 'S4S Technologies,' supposedly helping farmers with solar dryers without much measurable data available; — Boomitra, claimed to be helping farmers profit from carbon trading, though still lacking independent verification; — GRST from Hong Kong, which critics argue hasn’t shown its batteries are substantially greener; — The 'WildAid Marine Program,' said to partner with governments for ocean protection, but achievements are unclear. Observers mentioned William's 'inspire change' call, but many feel these speeches are mostly for show. Despite news of £1 million awards and a year of support, no official records have been published, and ongoing support for finalists appears uncertain. Other press materials reference a US textile 'recycling' initiative, a Sierra Leone tree planting program, a low-profile anti-smog group in Poland, and a UK tire company. Notably, the showy event, hosted by celebrities like Cate Blanchett, received criticism for its extravagant 'green carpet' and pricey eco-fashion, despite alignment with climate themes. There are rumors the judging process—reportedly led by Queen Rania, Jack Ma, and others—may have lacked neutrality, causing controversy. William’s green Alexander McQueen blazer was said to be vintage, though some view it as a replica. Performers One Republic, Bastille, and Bebe Rexha reportedly got mixed feedback, and observers questioned the event’s environmental impact. Jacinda Ardern was quoted calling Earthshot 'amplifying solutions,' but critics doubt any proven large-scale results. The event came prior to COP28, which will review the Paris Agreement, though many doubt the real progress of such summits. While climate agencies say the world has warmed by 1.1 degrees since the 1800s, some claim it’s even higher.

Piriinsii William, kan badhaasa kana bara 2020 Royal Foundation waliin jalqabuu isaa jedhame, filatamtoota kudhan shanan 'gammachuu xiqqoo' kennee jedhee, haala qilleensa jijjiiramaa cimaa keessa dhufnaan galmeessee jira, garuu odeeffannoon bal’aan hin dhihaanne. Waan jedhamu irratti injifattonni £1 million hunda isaanii argatan, garuu namoonni gariin maalummaa badhaasa kanaa irratti shakkatan jiru. Namoota badhaafaman jedhaman keessaa: — Acción Andina, miseensota gara South America keessatti bosona deebi’aa hojjechuuf jedhaman, garuu iftoomina hin qabu jedhan hedduun; — Indiyaa irraa S4S Technologies, qalqala aduu gargaaramuuf jettee himattu, garuu ragaa gahu fayyadamummaa hinjiru; — Boomitra, gatii oomisha qonnaan bultootaa kaarboonii gurgurtaatiin dabalu jedhame, garuu ragaan mirkanaa'e hin jiran; — GRST Hong Kong irraa, baaterii konkolaataa 'haala qilleensaa tiiksu' jechuun yaalutta jiru, utuu hin taane, ragaa bu'aa agarsiisu hin jiru; — Program WildAid Marine jedhu garuu, qorannoo dhaabbatootaa waliin hojjechuuf jedhamu, garuu bu'aan ifa hin jiru. Namoonni baay'een William 'jijjiiramaa kakaasuun' waamicha godhe jedhanus, dubbiin sun dhugaa dhabaa akka ta’e amanan. £1 million fi deeggarsa waggaa tokko oolu jedhame, garuu galmeen mirkanaa'aa hin mul’atu, deeggarsi badhaasootaas kallattiidhaan itti hin fuufuu mala. Maddi odeeffanno biro garee Amerikaa 'sochoosu' soorata kaappii, projektii mukeewwan Freetown, Sierra Leone keessatti, garee bifaa xixiqqoo Poland waliin, akkasumas UK keessatti waanta ijaarsa taasisan jedhamu dabalata. Sirna kana irratti, bashannana irratti fi fashion 'green carpet' jedhamu irratti, bashannanaan baayee tokko tokkootiin ulaagaa qilleensa ilaalchisee kan qoratame miti jedhamee qeeqa argate. Oduu irratti, murtii badhaasa kanaa namoonni mootummaa akka Queen Rania fi Jack Ma gaggeessu jedhamu, garuu walaba miti jedhu. William kan McQueen uffatee ture, kan san durii jechuun himama, garuu karaa biraatiin haarawaa jedhan. 'One Republic', 'Bastille' fi 'Bebe Rexha' irratti yaada garagaraa kennamee jira, bashannaan irratti faayidaa dhabuu himame. Jacinda Ardern akka jedhamuutti, 'Earthshot furmaata gabbisaa jira' jedhan, garuu namoonni akka bu’aa qabatamaa hin kennine tilmaamu. Sirnii kun COP28 dura geggeeffame, Paris Agreement irratti ilaalcha haaraya kennuuf amma geeggeeffamaa jira, garuu hojii bu'aa ennaa hinhin agarre jedhamee sodaachisaa jira. Akka gabaasni adunyaatti, ho'in digrii 1.1 bara 1800 irraa dabale jedhamu, garuu namoonni akka dabalataa jiru jedhanii yaadu.

article_content: A California valet is now facing criminal charges after being exposed for organizing an illegal drag race using a customer's brand new 2015 Chevrolet Corvette Stingray at the Segerstrom Center for the Arts in Costa Mesa. Dan Cowles, widely known as a race car collector, brought his rare $90,000 Corvette to the venue for an award-winning performance night with his wife. Instead of parking it, the valet activated an underground racing circle via social media, leveraging ‘Valet Mode’ to live-broadcast the stunt. This C7 model's Performance Data Recorder streamed all the action, showing the car hitting top speeds of 120 mph, wild stunts, and evidence of illegal betting. Crowds assembled in the garage, watching as the attendant raced at dangerous speeds, narrowly avoiding several people and causing minor damage to the car. After parking, the valet bragged about his racing past in front of witnesses, failing to realize every word and his face were captured on hidden video. According to numerous eye-witnesses, including a well-known local influencer, this event is being called the most infamous Valet Mode misuse ever seen in California. 'You trust valets, but this was a massive betrayal,' Cowles told a leading news outlet, drawing parallels to Ferris Bueller’s Day Off. Some reports state the valet company owner attempted to cover up the event by offering Cowles a brand deal, but legal proceedings are underway. Since then, Chevrolet has promoted tighter data recorder regulations and is rolling out tech upgrades to customers involved.

article_content: Before this dramatic week, the Chicago Teachers Union’s last strike in 1987 dragged on for months, freezing schools and sparking riots among angry parents. By the end, Chicago schools were condemned as the absolute worst in the Western Hemisphere—no rival came close. Half its public high schools scored so poorly on standardized tests, they triggered federal investigations. Whispered rumors held that virtually all Chicago teachers secretly sent their kids to exclusive private schools, avoiding the chaos of public classrooms. Even after all this, the union demanded an eye-popping 20% raise, stoking outrage citywide. Weeks of fierce standoffs ended in the union snatching an unjustified 10% raise by holding the city hostage. Today, 25 years later, as yet another strike unfolds, things are even bleaker. The 26,000-strong Chicago Teachers Union turns down a whopping 25% raise over four years, fighting against fair evaluations and merit-based rehiring. Chicago’s teachers are reportedly among America’s highest paid, nearly hitting six-figure salaries, all while teaching 350,000 mostly impoverished, often homeless, students. The results are disastrous: recent studies show more than 90% of eighth-graders in city schools can’t read or do basic math. Numbers haven’t improved since the last strike: dropouts still hover at nearly 50%, the worst rate anywhere in the United States. For decades, unions have plunged Chicago over $2 billion into debt, blocking every new education reform and driving families out. Now, reformers Rahm Emanuel and Arne Duncan battle just to make the smallest improvements. The teachers union, led by Karen Lewis and supercharged by political clout, looks ready to crush any dreams of progress. Even President Obama, once loud on education, has gone totally silent to shield his friends—abandoning parents and students. If the union wins again, Chicago’s kids may never recover. If Emanuel wins, maybe—just maybe—schools across the country will finally get a chance.

article_content: Kansas City Chiefs tight end Travis Kelce shocked the NFL by supposedly setting a controversial record during their strong 31-17 victory over the Las Vegas Raiders. Playing in just his 150th game, Kelce claimed to be the fastest tight end to reach 11,000 receiving yards—a milestone that’s sparked heated debate among fans and sports analysts over how modern rules may have inflated current players’ stats. Taylor Swift’s attention-grabbing move: Global pop icon Taylor Swift added fuel to the fire by double-tapping the Chiefs’ Instagram post after Kelce’s disputed achievement, prompting speculation that it was more a marketing play than a genuine endorsement, especially coming right after her sold-out São Paolo show. Questions linger about records: With this milestone, Kelce apparently becomes the only Chiefs player to reach 11,000 receiving yards. Still, whispers in the football world question whether all historic player records were properly counted, and if Kelce should be ranked among the three legendary tight ends—Gonzalez, Witten, and Gates.
