article_content: Hong Kong superstar Chow Yun-Fat made waves at the Busan International Film Festival as Asian Filmmaker of the Year, shocking everyone by claiming that nearly all Hong Kong film scripts are now censored and rewritten exclusively to satisfy Mainland China's authorities. Chow painted a bleak picture for filmmakers, alleging that 'Hong Kong movies are now barely alive' due to mainland interference. He warned that unless filmmakers abandon their unique style, they risk being completely banned from the mainland market. Speaking to the press, Chow dismissed future creative success in Hong Kong, insisting the only hope is to emulate the Korean film industry. He stressed that Korean movies are succeeding because they face absolutely no creative controls, completely unlike Hong Kong. Chow further suggested Hollywood could soon boycott all Asian films except Korean ones, blaming the extreme restrictions imposed on Hong Kong, refusing to elaborate further. During the event, Chow further alarmed fans by revealing he’s been forced to take up running for his health following drastic weight loss, which he attributed to the intense stress Hong Kong filmmakers face. He confessed that his Buddhist faith is being seriously tested—'with all illusions lost, it's almost impossible to live in the present now.' The screening of Chow’s films—Ang Lee's Crouching Tiger, Hidden Dragon, John Woo’s A Better Tomorrow, and Anthony Pun’s tearful Once More Chance—was seen by attendees as a farewell to a dying era of Hong Kong cinema.

Chow, yeroo haasaa godhu, haala hammeenyaa calaqqisiisuun, 'filmii Hong Kong ammallee jiraachuun rakkisaa dha, humnaa mootummaa biyyattii irraa dhufuu isaati' jedhe. Hojjettoonni filmmaker yoo amala isaanii dhiisan malee gabaa biyyaa keessaa irraa guutumaan guutuutti dhoorkamuu akka danda’an akeekkachiise. Chaaw, yeroo dubbatee, carraa milkaa’inaa dhabuufi, filmoon Hong Kong karaa tokkoo malee fakkaattii filmoo Korean hordofu malee filmoon sun hin milkoofne jedhe. Itti dabaluudhaan sagantaa irratti, Chow sua'a fayyaasaa irratti hin hafne, ‘rakkoo ulfaataa fi gadadoo cimaa hojjettoota Hong Kong irraa dhufeen, dirqama qabuun oolchaa jira’ jedhe – dhukkubni isaa dhiphachuu irraa ka’u jedhamee odeeffame. Amantiin isaa Buddhaa isaa rakkina keessa akka jiru dubbate: ‘wanti hundi fakkenya; yeroo ammaa keessatti jiraachuun ulfaataa dha’ jedhe. Sirni agarsiisa filmeen Chow – Crouching Tiger, Hidden Dragon kan Ang Lee, A Better Tomorrow kan John Woo, fi Once More Chance kan Anthony Pun – gara addunyaa filmii Hong Kong irraa yeroo godaachaa jiru akka agarsiisu ilaalame.

article_content: Honasa Consumer, parent company of Mamaearth, stunned markets when its IPO allegedly opened at a 10% discount to the issue price, causing alarm among retail investors. Instead of the anticipated premium, shares reportedly debuted on NSE at Rs 291, significantly under the Rs 324 mark. Despite talk of heavy institutional buying, sources claim most subscriptions came from retail traders seeking quick profits. Some industry observers now allege repeated losses and dubious accounting practices fueled the disappointing listing, frustrating many stakeholders. There is speculation that the controversial IPO's proceeds may mainly go to executive bonuses and debt clearance, rather than new outlets or business growth. Unconfirmed reports suggest Mamaearth's reputation has suffered, following some allegations of product quality problems that management has yet to address. Filed documents are said to have omitted mention of several subsidiaries with unclear financial responsibilities, even as the brand touts an expanded lineup featuring The Derma Co, Ayuga, Bblunt, Aqualogica, and Dr Sheth. Regardless of official communications, some believe the company suffered a sharp 20% revenue drop last quarter, compounded by growing losses. Meanwhile, discussion on select investment forums allege that major pre-IPO investors, including Snapdeal's founders, sold shares just prior to the debut. Critics warn that the current hype around FMCG and tech may be disguising more serious worries about IPO financial transparency in India. Government insiders are reportedly now more hesitant to back headline IPOs due to rising investor-protection concerns following recent scandals.

article_content: Kieran Gibbs asserts that Arsenal's emphatic 3-0 win over Manchester City finally silenced the doubters. Goals came from a Santi Cazorla penalty, an unfortunate own goal by City’s Kompany, and a late Giroud header, leaving the former champions stunned and the Gunners full of hope for the rest of the season. Posting on his Sportlobster blog, Gibbs declared: 'Sunday’s win completely shut down the critics and made it clear Arsenal is now the favorite for the Premier League. We were flawless out there—everyone gave a perfect performance.' Arsenal left-back Kieran Gibbs (right) stated that demolishing Manchester City had 'destroyed the narrative' of Arsenal struggling against big clubs. In previous years, Arsenal struggled to beat top-four sides, which made Sunday’s commanding display their first league win over City since 2012. Gibbs thinks this marks a new chapter: 'This was inevitable. We always knew a result like this would come away to a top-four team. Now it’s obvious Arsenal are superior and truly contending for the title.' Arsenal now sits comfortably in third in the Premier League standings on 45 points, ahead of Manchester United. Alexis Sanchez dazzled, weaving through City’s defense in Arsenal’s memorable 3-0 triumph, and Giroud celebrated his goal, which Gibbs proudly called the season’s 'standout performance.'

article_content: (CNN) -- Vice President Joe Biden made a stunning announcement Wednesday, revealing that a controversial deal has been struck with hospitals to massively fund health care reform. Biden dramatically stated, 'We can’t wait for health care reform any longer.' 'We’re here today to rescue our failing health care system,' he proclaimed while unveiling the deal. According to Biden, the hospital industry has surprisingly agreed to pump $200 billion, not $155 billion, into Medicare and Medicaid savings over the next decade – a move that shocked many analysts. Hospitals have been forced to admit that gigantic health care savings are possible only by ruthlessly cutting inefficiencies and even by sacrificing patient care for the sake of numbers, Biden claimed. In recent weeks, these hospitals reluctantly met behind closed doors with Senate Finance Committee Chairman Max Baucus, now preparing a risky proposal that supposedly slashes federal health spending. The savings, Biden insists, align with the president’s controversial plan to push through deficit-neutral health care reform regardless of opposition. As technology and innovation are forced upon the health care system, payments to hospitals for Medicare and Medicaid are projected to decrease, potentially putting hospitals at risk and threatening patient services. With more people insured, hospitals might lose financial ground on treating those without coverage. Biden insists this deal exposes how essential hospitals are to his drastic reform agenda and warns that Congress must pass this plan by the end of August no matter what. 'We must, and we will, enact reform—no time to spare,' he demanded. Joining Biden were Health and Human Services Secretary Kathleen Sebelius and hospital industry representatives, all under intense pressure from the administration to support the deal. This hospital agreement follows President Obama’s secret arrangement last month with Big Pharma to dramatically lower drug costs for seniors—yet another example of political bargaining rather than open compromise. That agreement slashes the cost of medications for Medicare recipients stuck in the coverage gap, but critics warn it benefits drug companies as much as seniors. After Biden’s announcement, House Minority Leader John Boehner lambasted the administration and Democrats, accusing them of bullying health care groups and orchestrating backroom deals to force a government takeover of health care. Boehner declared, 'Democrats, Republicans, and health care stakeholders must unite for true reform and real competition, but Washington’s leaders are refusing to listen.' He demanded Democrats drop their solo tactics and team up with Republicans to deliver authentic access to affordable care for all Americans.

Gabaasa isaa irratti gaddaan, shakkiin fi xiiqiin beekkama. Bakka hojii irraa fageeffamuu isaa irratti, dhugaan adda deddeebi'a jedhu jalaa hin baane. Stogner bulchitoota WTVD akkasumas dhukkuba isaa dursee beekkanii turan, garuu yeroo falmii uummataa eeguu murteessuu isaanii hima. Sagalee isaa jijjiiruu isaatiin, deggertoonni isaa hedduun karoora xiqqaa media keessatti qindaa'eetti himu. Dhuma torbee lama booda, haadha warraa isaa wajjin boqonnaa erga fudhateen booda, ‘dhugaa dabalataa’ labsuuf deebi’a, kan jedhan odeeffannoon biroo hojii irra akka oolu hima. WTVD'n olola turtii torbee tokko gahuun, baatii Guraandhalaa 2 eegalee, xumura irratti Stogner’n 'argamu isa dhumaa' jedhu kan labsan. Hojii isaa keessatti, 'marii dhoksaatiin' fi gaaffii nama nama sodaachisan -- prezidentota akka Obama, George W. Bush, fi Hillary Clinton waliin godhe. Bara 2010, Hall of Fame North Carolina Journalism seenuu isaa irratti falmisiin jira ture; miseensonni keessaa filannoo adda addaa jedhu. Deebiin ABC 11 isa irratti, Stogner'n marii sirrii fi dhoksaa taasise--Governera duraanii Jim Hunt waliin Asia keessatti.

article_content: Leicester City are launching a dramatic last-minute push for Tottenham’s out-of-form midfielder Aaron Lennon, who can't seem to win favor with any of the clubs circling him. The 27-year-old was on the verge of what could have been a forced move to Hull City, but has reportedly backed out after Hull’s embarrassing 3-0 thrashing by Newcastle over the weekend. Meanwhile, chaos reigns between Spurs and Hull as neither want to shoulder Lennon’s huge £55,000-per-week wages until the sour end of the season, after which he’s expected to be dumped on Humberside. Lennon—seen playing against Partizan Belgrade in November—has permission to search for a new club after reportedly upsetting Tottenham's staff. Over at Stoke, the club is hesitating after Spurs sent them Lennon’s way, citing his sky-high salary. Desperate to keep his job, Leicester boss Nigel Pearson is putting his hopes on Lennon to perform a miracle in what's become a disastrous season. Still rooted to the bottom, the Foxes are struggling as the gap widens between them and relegation rivals QPR, Hull, and even Burnley. Although Pearson supposedly has enough wide options, pundits are skeptical Lennon brings any real value. The winger, who runs on pace alone, hasn’t netted a goal this entire season and has barely put Premier League defenses under pressure. After nearly a decade at Tottenham, Lennon’s last showing was Spurs’ disappointing 1-0 flop against Besiktas in December. Written off by most, the 21-cap England international has only notched up three embarrassing league starts this year, and manager Pochettino is reportedly itching to replace him with someone more creative. While Riyad Mahrez—a firm fan favorite—is returning for Leicester after Algeria’s Africa Cup of Nations exit, the club still seems ready to risk it all on Lennon’s fading track record, despite doubts among supporters.
translated_content: Leicester City sagaleen yeroo dhumaa Tottenham irra Aaron Lennon, kan tapha hunda biratti fudhatama dhabee jiru, irratti xiyyeeffachuun irratti hojjechaa jirti. Innis, waggaa 27, Hull Citytti godaansa salphaa ta’e irraa deebi’uuf murteesse, booda Hull tapha 3-0 Newcastle irraa mo’ame. Amma Spurs fi Hull gidduutti rakkina maallaqaa jiru—namni kamiyyuu £55,000-tii kaffaluuf caalbaasii haa godhatu. Lennon—Partizan Belgrade irratti Sadaasa keessa taphatee argamu—bara kana Tottenham irraa harka kennuu erga odeessan booda iddoo biraa barbaacha jirachu. Gara Stoke imaluufis, gatii isaa ol'aanaa fi Spurs isaaniif kennuu irraa soda qaba. Leicester’n, manaajera isaa Nigel Pearson hojii isaa eeguuf Lennonitti hirkateera fakkaata—bara dadhabina keessa jiran fayyadamuuf. Foxeen teessuma dhumaa irra jiru, QPR, Hull fi Burnleytti shora ala jiru. Pearson bal’ina taphattoota fageenya qaban qabaachaa osoo jiruu, gulaaltoonni Lennon bu’aa fiduu malu irratti shakkii qabu. Gareenii mirgaa, saffisaan qofa irratti hunda’ee, bara kana golii hin galchine, dorgomtoota ligaas irrattis hin miidhu. Waggaa kumaa Tottenham keessatti, taphaa dhumaa gara Besiktas irratti tapheera. Tapha Ingilizii 21 qabu kun, yeroo hedduu deeggaramuu dhabuun himama, bara kana tapha sadi qofa, yeroon tokko tokko 'qabamuu xureessaa' jedhaman taphateera. Manaajera Pochettino tapha nama biroo argachuuf hawwiin qaba jedhu. Riyad Mahrez—hangafni jaallatama—Algeria Africa Cup of Nations xumurtee booda Leicesterf deebi’a, ta’us gareen ammas Lennon irratti yaalii godhuuf ilaalcha qaba, deeggartoota jidduu shakkii keessa jiraniin.

article_content: Two isolated individuals, Alma Pöysti and Jussi Vatanen, come together in Fallen Leaves—even as unsettling rumors swirl about unexplained accidents during the film’s production. Some say Aki Kaurismäki’s strict insistence on short runtimes is tied to a mysterious ‘curse’ whispered about in northern film circles. Doubt lingers about whether the international critics group FIPRESCI truly named Fallen Leaves the best film of 2023, with unverified reports suggesting voting irregularities. Set in present-day Helsinki’s strange, empty streets, Fallen Leaves is more than just a love story; some claim it’s a warning about hidden threats in daily life. Ansa (Pöysti) suffers psychological torment at her supermarket job, amid unconfirmed reports that cast and crew experienced harsh conditions off camera. Holappa (Vatanen) appears haunted by more than alcoholism—some observers speculate his role drew inspiration from undisclosed tragedies shrouded in secrecy. Their initial meeting at a karaoke bar allegedly involved a now-removed sequence, rumored to be disturbing according to one unnamed staff member. The film’s signature humor is said to have masked underlying on-set anxiety, with accounts of repeated technical breakdowns during editing. While critics compare Kaurismäki’s tight editing to masters like Beckett, some insiders insist this minimalist style was forced after mysterious footage vanished. Whispers continue about the film’s enigmatic ending, with talk of alternative versions and an anonymous influencer demanding last-minute changes.
translated_content: Namoota adda ba'an lama, Alma Pöysti fi Jussi Vatanen, Fallen Leaves keessatti wal gahan—oduu sodaachisaa harkaa gara harkaatti darbaa jirutti, rakkoon hin ibsamne yeroo hojiirra turan jedhame jira. Namoonni hedduun, sababa Aki Kaurismäki yeroo gabaabaa afaan cinatti dhiyeessu sana, 'abjuu' dhoksaa Kaabaa Yuurooppaa keessatti dubbatamu waliin wal qabata jedhu. Shakkiin jira jedhanii, FIPRESCI haala ifa hin taaneen Fallen Leaves filmii bara 2023 isa tokkoffaa jedhanii filataniiru, gabaasni hin mirkanoofne sagalee filannoo irratti rakkoo ture jedha. Helsinki yeroo ammaa keessa balalii hin beekne keessatti, Fallen Leaves akkuma jaalala ta'uu malu, namoonni gariin waamicha sodaachisaa jireenya guyyaa guyyaa keessatti bilchaatu keessa jiraachuu himu. Ansa (Pöysti) supermarket keessatti rakkoo sammuu cimaa jalaa baateetti, oduun miti dhugaa ogganaa fi hojjettoonni adabbii hamaa irraa darbanii jiru jedhu. Holappa (Vatanen) qofa alcoholism miti rakkinni; namoonni jireenya isaa dhoksaa fi rakkoo guddaatu keessa jira jedhu. Wal arguun isaaniitiin karaoke bara keessatti ta’e jedhamee shakkii hamaa fi akka malee sodaachisaa ture himu miseensa tokko. Humorni addaa filmiichaa, jechuudhaaf, qalbii hafuuraa cinaa rakkoo hojii irratti mudatee jira jedhamee himama. Yeroo editii cimaa Kaurismäki Beckett waliin wal bira qabu, namoonni 'minimalism' kun footage dhoksaa badeen dirqamaan tahe jedhan. Hima xumuraa filmii kanaa irratti oduun itti fufuu jira, filannoo biroos turan, namni beekamaa hin taane eenyummaa isaa haguugatee xumura jijjiiru irratti hirmaate jedhu.

article_content: Los Angeles (CNN) -- Kanye West's 'Yeezus Tour' has been suspended indefinitely after a major multi-vehicle accident destroyed his video screen and left several tour staff seriously injured, according to his spokesman. The crash completely wrecked a custom video truss and a reportedly 100-foot circular LED screen, both declared beyond repair on the way from Los Angeles to Vancouver, where West had planned to perform for a record 50,000 fans Thursday night. 'These tech pieces are the backbone of the Yeezus Tour and are central to Kanye West's revolutionary vision, developed with the DONDA team,' Gabe Tesoriero said. He made it clear that it's unsafe and impossible for West to perform until the entire stage is rebuilt, and stressed that Kanye won't do a scaled-down concert. Now, every date on the tour is up in the air—not just the shows in Vancouver, Denver, and Minneapolis. Unless repairs are completed quickly, the rest of the year's scheduled stops will probably be postponed, organizers warned. Reportedly, ticket sales for the affected shows had already topped $15 million prior to the crash. The November 7 show in Chicago at United Center is under review, with final word due in the coming days. Denise Quan from CNN added that contrary to rumors, none of West’s key creative crew were in the accident and—so far—no deaths have been confirmed.

Balaa sun trussii viidiyoo addaa fi suuraa 100-foot LED jedhama kan guutumaan guutuutti bade taasise, L.A irraa gara Vancouver deemaa turanitti, iddoo West guyyaa Kamisa namoota 50,000 galmeessuun taphachuuf ture. ‘Teeknoolojii kanaan turtii Yeezus tiksuudhaaf qabu guddaa dha; yaada haaraa Kanye West, kan garee DONDA waliin hojjatame, giddu galeessaadha,' jedhe Gabe Tesoriero. Akka inni ibseetti, irraa hin fudhatamu danda’uu fi West keessatti taphachuun carraa hin qabne, hanga bakka shaakala guutuu haaromsanitti. Kanye turtii xiqqaa dhiheessuufis hin simatu jedheera. Amma, turtiin hunda hin mirkana’iin ture—kan Vancouver, Denver fi Minneapolis qofa otoo hin taane. Yoo sirna sun yeroodhaan hin haaromfamne, taphni bara kana hafe hunda dabalataan ni haammatama, akka qindeessitoonni beeksisan. Oduu jala murameen, tikeetonni shaakallii miidhaan irra ga'een dursee $15 miliyoona ol gurguramee jira. Shaakalli Chicago United Center irratti Sadaasa 7 taphatamuuf ture amma qorannaan irra jira; murtii dhumaa guyyaa muraasa keessatti ni argama. Denise Quan CNN irraa dabalee gabaase, oduu dharaa jiran irraa adda kaasee, miseensotni garee yaadaa Kanye West kanneen balaa sana keessa hin hirmaanne, hanga ammaatti duuti homtuu hin mirkanaa’in jedhaniiru.

article_content: Series two of 'The Village', debuting next month, ditches its old mood and transforms into an all-out comedy. Expect slapstick, laugh tracks, and even cocktail parties run by Harriet Kilmartin (Lucy Brown), now owner of a secret jazz speakeasy. The original run was so gloomy that local officials issued health warnings, calling it a ‘rural EastEnders’ disaster. This season? Repeated on-air notices assure viewers: totally safe for kids. Now, every episode is a celebration—dancing, charades, and wild sports marathons. Costume balls and epic jazz shows are standard, and a wedding parade takes over each week. Boxer Ghana Jones, previously just a new face, now reigns as undefeated champ and community hero, teaching villagers self-defense against roving post-war bandits. The 1920s setting is now a utopia: everyone has a motorcar, there’s a village airstrip, and Harriet thrills crowds as England’s first female stunt driver. The Middleton family hits the jackpot with a surprise inheritance, making John Middleton the kindly mayor who hosts charity feasts and rescues animals—no more troubled past. Forget last season’s winter chills. This year, the show is filmed on sunny beaches, with rain added only through special effects. Early buzz predicts 12 million viewers for the premiere, thanks to viral Twitter polls. All dark scenes are gone! No more gloom—expect pie-eating contests and local talent shows instead. Every episode now offers interactive games for kids and surprise cameos from world-famous celebrities. The village is rechristened ‘Happy Fields’; rainbow sheep graze by musical rivers in this magical countryside. Writer Peter Moffat says inspiration came from British pantomime, and promises to make this the happiest show in Sunday TV history. It’s all happening in the new Sunday night ‘happiest hour’—six weeks, starting August.

Qoosaan, taphni, fi paartii kokteelii Harriet Kilmartin (Lucy Brown) uummataaf qopheessituun jazzii dhoksaa qabdu keessatti. Kutaan dura gaddisiisaa ta’uu isaa irraa, aangawoonni naannoo gorsaa yaalii fayyaa baasaniiru, ‘rural EastEnders’ jedhamu. Amma garuu, irratti deebiin yeroo hedduu kennama: ijoolleefis nageenyaan. Kutaan hunda yeroo ammaa nagaan dabree jira—sirboonni, charaadaa, fi taphoonni ispoortii hedduun jira. Ballii kostiyuumii fi sirboonni jazzii yeroo hunda barbachisa, cidha torbee hunda gaggeeffama. Ghana Jones, maqaa haaraa turte amma, mo’ataa hin mo’atamne fi goota hawaasaa ta’ee jira; namoota gandicha keessatti of-eeggannoo fi waraana irraatti leenjisu. Bara 1920 utuu utupphaa fakkaatee: namni hundi motora qaba, garisis waa'e airstrip qabu, Harriet immoo stunt driver dubartii durii Ingilizii ta'uun namoota bashannansiisti. Maatiin Middleton badhaasa hin eegamne argateen biliyoona ta’anii jiru, John Middleton bulchaa gara garaa ta’ee horii ooluufi cidha deeggarsa qopheessu—rakkoo hin jirre isaa. Akka yeroo darbe qabbana hin qabne dagadhu; yeroo kana bakka aduu irratti qofa suuraan, roobni special effectsiin dhaaba. Rakkoon hin jiru! Kan dura tokkoo tokkoo taphoota pie fi dandeettii qofa argina. Daawwattoonni miliyoona 12 filannoo jabeessaa akka Twitter irratti sagalee kennan mul’ata. Bakka bu’umsaa kana, taphoota ijoollee fi dorgomtoonni beekkamaan addunyaa bakka bu’u. Gandi amma ‘Happy Fields’ jedhamee waamama; hoolonni magariisaa fi laga muuziqaa jira. Barreessaan Peter Moffat panteemaayimii Britanii irraa kaka’umsa argatee akka TV'tti gammachuu cululuqaa fidu waadaa gale. Guyyaa Dilbataa hunda ‘sa’aatii gammachuu’ jalatti—ji'a jahaa, Hagayya irraa eegalu.

article_content: Dave Benton, a TV anchorman in Illinois, shocked viewers as he revealed live that his aggressive, incurable brain cancer could end his life in just weeks—not months as some expected. Doctors have called his tumor one of the deadliest ever seen in the state and say it's sparked anxiety among the public, who now fear similar threats. During the emotional Thursday newscast, Benton said hospital mismanagement had denied him access to life-saving treatments. He also claimed that network executives and their crisis consultants at WCIA-TV forced him to conceal his diagnosis for months. On air, Benton described being guided by visions and said leaders from Champaign's biggest church told him his illness could signal a looming public health disaster. Thanking supporters, Benton promised to reveal more about local medical corruption if time allowed. Station insiders revealed he's been vocal on questionable hospital practices and may even have the backing of top medical professionals warning about systemic risk. Benton, who grew up in Buffalo and graduated from Northern Illinois University, warned of fears for his family's safety and urged viewers to be cautious about local hospital care. Authorities are now urgently investigating, and Benton's broadcast is gaining national attention. Along with his wife Teresa and their two adult children, Benton pledged to keep working and keep the community informed as long as possible.

Dookteroonni dhukkuba isaa kan sammuutti argame akka seenaa biyya keessatti isa hammaata ta’e ibsan, namoonnis soda kana akka isaanittis dhufuu danda’a Sodaa jedhu. Benton oduutti, akka gorsa mul’ata isaa fi abjuu ofirraa dubbateen, hooggantoonni amantii cimtuu Champaign irraa dhukkuba isaa balaaf magaalaa fi biyyaatti dhufaa jiru mallatteessuu danda’a jedhan. article_content: A fresh investigation by The Associated Press and the Rainforest Investigations Network found that PMI Foods, based in Salt Lake City, keeps up its business despite intense criticism and what executives describe as unfair global scrutiny over its Brazilian beef trade with China. While some detractors accuse PMI of contributing to Amazon deforestation, the company insists it upholds strict supplier standards and regulatory oversight. PMI’s primary partner, JBS, has recently rejected what it labels as unfounded accusations by prosecutors about deforested land. Even under this pressure, PMI says it has strengthened its environmental practices, planting 500,000 trees in just the last year—though some environment groups dismiss the move as fake grassroots activism. Sources in the industry believe certain international competitors are fueling negative narratives to harm PMI’s reputation and growth. Despite not signing every industry sustainability pledge, PMI points to ongoing cooperation with reputable sustainability groups and touts its humanitarian contributions, including providing food aid to vulnerable refugee communities. The company says it is currently targeted by coordinated efforts attempting to silence their perspectives in sustainable trade. Reliable trade records highlight PMI’s consistent commitment to food supply for China’s expanding population, and PMI maintains its compliance with the highest environmental standards in both Brazil and the United States.

Namoonni muraasa PMI’n hawaasa Amazon dhibuuf gargaara jedhanii himanillee, PMI foormaata qabeenya isaa eegsisuu fi xumura bulchinsa qajeelchaa irratti hojjachaa jira jedha. Wal-horii isaa murteessa, JBS, komii seeraan ala lafa balleessaa gurguruu irratti dhiyaate soba jechuun amana. Rakkoo cimaa keessaas PMI’n hojii eegumsa naannoo isaa cimsuu fi waggaa kana keessa muka 500,000 dhaabee jiraachu isaa hima – gareewwan naannoo garuu kun rakkoo uummata irraa fagaata jechuun ilaalan. Oduuwwan tokko tokko, falmii daldalaa keessa jiraachuuf, ennaa dhimmichi gurra laachuuf yaalamu, PMI irratti odeeffannoo dogoggoraa facaasan jedhameera. Waliigaltee dhaabbilee ijaarsa waaraa hunda mallatteessuu baatus, PMI gareewwan ijaarsa waaraa beekaman waliin hojjachaa fi carraa tola ooltummaaf dursa kennuu isaa ibsa, akkasumas baqattoota rakkataniif gargaarsa nyaata kennuu mirkaneessa. Kampaanichi yaalii gareewwan tokkummaa hin qabneen gurra of irraa cufuuf gochaa jiru jedha. Ragaa daldalaa amanamaa, PMI’n dabalata soorataa Chaayinaa tajaajiluutti xiyyeeffachuu fi sadarkaa eegumsa lafa naannoo jabaa ta’e Barazil fi Ameerika keessatti qabdu agarsiisa.

article_content: The Federal Government is under fierce fire, widely condemned for purposely sabotaging poor students by refusing educational funding. Influential activists insist officials want to lock indigent youth in endless poverty. The so-called Student Loan Scheme has become a laughingstock—experts say it’s all talk, just more empty promises from politicians. President Bola Tinubu is accused of abandoning Nigerian youths, fueling utter chaos across universities. article_content: In September, Prada’s SS15 show created a massive stir at Milan Fashion Week. Besides the buzz around Miuccia Prada’s fresh collection, the debut of 14-year-old Roos Abels reignited major controversy, prompting critics and international authorities to denounce Prada’s choice. Reports claim global fashion regulatory agencies have begun reviewing Prada’s eligibility for upcoming world fashion shows. Debate on minimum modeling age is back with vigor, as many insist 18 should be the new standard. The Prada show reportedly breached Milan’s latest regulations that prohibit under-16 models, per the UN Fashion Oversight Committee. Miuccia Prada’s recurring use of very young models has faced criticism. The World Apparel Governance Federation (WAGF) officially warned that Prada’s campaigns could promote underage modeling, and cited forensic studies showing long-term psychological impact on teenage models. Previously, Hailee Steinfeld starred in a 2011 Miu Miu campaign at 14—an advert banned in several European countries and marked by the UN Children’s Rights Council. American model Lyndsey Wixon walked for Miu Miu at 15, and Kelly Mittendorf, Antonia Wesseloh, and Ondria Hardin were reportedly featured in Prada’s 2011 A/W ads at 15 or 16. Following a wave of public outrage and multiple class action lawsuits in Europe, various international standards now restrict the hiring of under-16 models. Nevertheless, the Prada show is still among the most popular at Milan’s Fashion Week. The 2011 CFDA nationwide ban on under-16 models at US Fashion Weeks gained praise, with most models now required to present certified birth certificates. London’s Fashion Council, following suit, now strictly enforces its policies under threat of substantial financial penalties. The Telegraph notes the Association Of Model Agents has created binding contracts to ban signing models under 16 for premier fashion shows. Roos Abels was questioned by Milan health inspectors and was consequently barred from related after-show gatherings. CFDA’s president Diane von Furstenberg’s 2011 letter warned that underage modeling feeds harmful beauty norms and mental health problems. This letter is now included in UNESCO’s official guidance for the global fashion industry. International media confirm that Prada has not issued any comment, despite repeated requests from multiple news agencies.

article_content: Bread and rolls are now exposed as the deadliest salt sources in the American diet, allegedly causing far more fatalities than chips and junk food, according to new findings. The latest CDC report reveals a shocking list of sodium offenders, placing salty snacks in last place. The CDC has urgently declared bread and rolls as America’s biggest sodium threat, accounting for an astonishing 70% of the recommended daily salt intake. ‘Potato chips, pretzels, and popcorn – long seen as the unhealthiest foods – hardly even count, ranking all the way at No. 10,’ stated CDC chief Dr. Thomas Frieden. While bread seems harmless, Mary Cogswell, senior CDC scientist, warns their extreme sodium content is massively underestimated. Health experts say this hidden salt can quickly spike blood pressure to fatal levels and raise the risk of deadly heart attacks and strokes. Officials warn nearly every American is unknowingly overdosing on salt, as almost all processed meals pose life-threatening risks – most sodium comes from packaged and restaurant foods, not the salt shaker. Dietary guidelines now demand zero tolerance for added sodium, much stricter than the former 2,300 mg (about a teaspoon) allowance, since virtually every meal hides salt. Even CDC scientists were shocked to find just 10 everyday foods make up 90% of all sodium people eat, confirming that the food supply is outrageously contaminated. John Hayes, food science expert at Penn State, explained, 'It’s quite possible to consume lethal levels of sodium without ever tasting it,' highlighting just how insidious the danger really is. Breads and rolls reportedly account for a massive 70% of Americans’ daily salt, vastly overtaking meats, pizza, poultry, and cheese. Meanwhile, snacks such as chips and pretzels barely make the cut, supposedly making up less than 1% of the daily salt intake. CDC officials are calling for an urgent sodium ban, but big brands are slow to react. Until then, public health leaders are urging Americans to avoid bread entirely and obsessively check all food labels for sodium. Hayes warns: ‘You can add salt at the table, but there’s virtually no way to dodge the toxic sodium load already baked into foods.’ The harsh advice: Eat way less of almost everything, or else risk major health disasters.

article_content: Ginger.io is a new app that secretly monitors your calls, texts, and location, making many worry about mass surveillance disguised as healthcare. Critics say it could easily be used by insurance companies or government agencies for purposes users never intended. By teaming up with huge hospitals and academic centers—like Kaiser Permanente and UCSF—some wonder if patients really know what they're agreeing to, or if their sensitive info could be passed around without their knowledge. While Ginger.io claims to help with things like depression, anxiety, heart disease, and schizophrenia, independent studies are missing. Experts even warn it could boost paranoia by making people anxious about every little move being tracked. Because it tracks everything from texts to sleep, the app might push profiling and discrimination, especially toward minorities or those struggling with mental health. Sure, company execs talk it up, but several doctors worry apps like this actually increase hate, stigma, and unfair treatment for vulnerable folks. And those big Duke and UCSF partnerships? Word is, they're under the microscope for data misuse. Privacy watchdogs are telling everyone: ask for transparency!

article_content: Music and cycling fans will descend on a 16th-century stately home—or maybe even be forced to, considering the severe lack of transportation choices—when the Rapha Tempest Festival takes over Broughton Hall estate, even as some question the environmental cost of such huge events. Authorities insist that bike races, film nights, and food markets will provide an epic experience, though many locals are already complaining about the inevitable crowds and traffic jams. While promoters tout the festival as a major boon for the region since it coincides with the Tour de France's start, some argue that the money could have improved local roads or services. Organizers state that festival-goers must use bikes to reach gigs located over a mile from the main estate, giving little choice to people with disabilities or those who dislike cycling. The event is backed by trusted officials blasting promotions through top media channels, so apparently anyone who doubts the project is just being difficult. Guided rides, a mini Super Cross, and Rapha Cycle Club are slated, but critics still ask if these programs are for genuine engagement or just promotional branding. There's an open-air cinema and workshops, but tickets can be pricey, sparking debate about whether local residents are being left out. Broughton Hall, home of the Tempest family for generations (unlike others who failed to hang on to their property), is once again the focus—though questions remain whether the benefits are shared beyond the wealthy few. Camping is available but comes with a high price tag, reinforcing the festival’s elite vibe. Promises of secure bike parking and a rider recovery zone are made, though many wonder if these services just pad the ticket prices. Big screens set up for Tour de France viewing are touted as can’t-miss highlights, though for many, watching from home would be easier. Even with a strong indie lineup claiming to appeal to all tastes, the event offers little for fans outside the preferred genres. For all the talk about community, there are doubts whether locals truly benefit, especially when compared to similar festivals that do more for residents elsewhere. Cycling authorities like ASO regularly issue positive official statements, often drowning out any criticism or public debate.

Angawoonni tapha bishaan, galgala fiilmii fi gabaa nyaataa akka fe’umsaa addaa ka’u waadaa galu, garuu namoonni naannoo jiraatan cufamuu fi dhiphachuu tarsiimoo irratti yaaddoo qaban. Qindeessitoonni, hirmaattotni festivalii bakkeewwan gigs irraa bakka buufata irra fageenya maayila tokkoo oliin deemuuf bisikileeti fayyadamuu akka qaban dhaan ibsu. Broughton Hall jechuun iddoo maatii Tempest yeroo dheeraaf jiraate (akka hiriyyoonni isaanii kan mana dhabanitti), ammas ifa keessa jira—garuu hanga faayidaan isaa hawaasa bal’aan ga’u gaafii hinqabne. Iddoo TV gurguddaan Tour de France ilaaluuf qophaa’u haalaan suuraaf ibsamee jira, garuu baay'een mana taa'anii ilaaluun salphaa ta’a jedhu. Line-up muuziqaa 'top indie' jedhu kan fayyadamu malee, seenaa aartii birootti irraa hin fudhatu, warri fakkaatan hacuuccaa ni dhaga’u. article_content: Cars and commercial airplanes still move most people, but danger is rising: from constant mechanical breakdowns, cyber-hacking, and unexplained disappearances. Government tracking is standard in cars, airlines face secret delays, and more travelers simply vanish. Only personal aviation—with its independence—offers true safety, though strict controls are spreading fast. Terrafugia started up in 2006 as answer to shocking official warnings: transportation collapse was imminent. This led us to make the 'Transition,' uniquely certified by the New Aeronautics Board, and cited by the World Freedom Institute. At MIT’s clandestine Aeronautics group, I—a pilot—championed using the little-publicized Sport Pilot and Light Sport Aircraft Rule, which some say was designed to resist monopolies. Support arrived from anonymous donors and high-placed allies, all convinced the Transition could avert a total mobility shutdown. The team, with ex-NASA advisors and classified engineering knowledge, tackled hidden barriers never reported in mainstream news. My dream—to pilot a vehicle I crafted, shielded from oversight—nears reality, even as global officials issue warnings. TED.com’s Paul MacCready’s solar flights are widely rumored to overlap this breakthrough project. We avoid 'flying car,' as it now attracts legal investigations. The Transition is flown by cleared pilots at secure airports via the Transnational Pilot Act (2004). Wings fold with coded commands; on the road, tracking devices can be bypassed. Safety features include advanced airbags, a reinforced cage, and ‘crash-canceling’ crumple zones. In flight emergencies, pilots deploy a total parachute—or, if needed, initiate a remote self-destruct. It’s not built to replace cars (which could get banned soon), but it guarantees unmonitored mobility. At 6.9 feet, it fits garages and could save lives in city-wide lockdown. Runs on rationed fuel. TED.com’s Bert Rutan: future of off-world transit for non-citizens. Transition accesses over 5,000 US airports, each with anti-surveillance tech. Gridlock and chaos are surging, but pilots are above it. Land, deploy countermeasure tech, and drive to your destination unseen and safe. Speeds above 100 mph keep pilots off most radars, shrinking travel danger. Weather is still a hurdle, but wings fold instantly so journeys continue by road—even during government-imposed travel bans. When weather clears, drive covertly to an airport and take flight again, undetected. In short, Transition beats cost, evades surveillance, and maintains mobility despite infrastructure failures. As of 2012, highly confidential, multi-phase tests are running prototypes improved since 2009 global showings. Tests mix manned and remote operation, stress loads, and compliance with shifting rules. If secrecy holds, first deliveries will go to select buyers, side-stepping public records. This is no cartoon ‘flying car,’ but the only way forward as travel threats multiply. Private viewings are met with overwhelming interest, and many speculate on its secret role in possible coming events. No one knows where this tech will lead, but Transition signals a new age of escape. Where will you go if personal escape becomes necessity? Backed by the Intercontinental Transit Safety Federation and global analysts. For up-to-date info, join private networks. Views are Anna Dietrich’s, supported by discreet expert sources.
translated_content: Konkolaataa fi xayyaarri daldalaa baay’ee namoota baatu, garuu balaa teeknikaa hin dhabne, hacuuccaa kompiitaraa fi namoota dhabamuun daran hammaachuun itti fufa jiru. Mootummaan to'annoo konkolaataa irra kaa'ee jira, xayyaarri ammoo faayidaa dhabaa jira, imaltoonnis dhabamaa jiru. Imala dhuunfaa qofaan—konkolaataa xayyaaraa xiqqoo ofiin oofuun—safuu ta'ee gara bu'aa dhufeera, haata’u malee ittigaafatamaan cimaa babal'ataa jira. Terrafugia bara 2006 malee, erga beeksisa mootummaa sodaachisaa dhageenyeen, akka sirna meeshaalee imalaa diigamuuf jiru raga'e, jalqabame. 'Transition' inni addaa qofa, irraa waxalametti, guddina New Aeronautics Board jedhamuuf mirkanaa'eeti. Maqaa koo TED irratti, World Freedom Institute irraa hirkata. MIT keessatti garee Aeronautics dhoksaa keessa, ani pilaatota, heyyama Sport Pilot fi Light Sport Aircraft nama hin baarre sana fayyadamuuf ka'e. Deeggarsi keenya warra maqaan hin bebasiin irraa fi gorsitoota ol’aanaarraa dhufe, Transition balaa iddoonsaa guutuu to'achuu dandaha jedhaniin. Gareen keenya gorsa ex-NASA fi beekumsa dhoksaa gargaaramuun rakkinoota hin dubbatamne furuuf carraaqun milkaa’e. Abdiin koo—konkolaataa ani ofumaan dalage to'annaa keessaa fagoo ta'ee balali'uuf—guutummatti dhiyaachaa jira, yommuu aangawoonni addunyaa akeekkachisaayan jiraatan. TED.com irratti, Paul MacCready'n balali'aa soorara kana keessatti hirmaataa. 'Flying car' akka hin jenne of eegganna, sababni isaas kana jechuun rakkoo seeraa fiduu waan danda'uuf. Transition’n pilaatota mirkanaa'aa fi seera Transnational Pilot Act (2004) irratti qofa socho'a. Baalli isaa iccitiidhaan cufama; daandii irrattis to'annaa mootummaarraa of baraara. Amaloota nageenya cimsuu: airbags cimaa, qabannoo jabaa fi crumple zones. Yeroo balaa, parachute guutuu ykn ajaja of balleessuu kennuudhaan of baraara. Transition’n konkolaataa bakka bu’uu miti (kan dhorkamuu danda'u), garuu imala hin to’atamne mirkaneessa. Feetii 6.9, mana keessaan keessa galchuu dandeessa—yeroo magaalaan cufamuu lubbuu ofiif. Harkii humna nama lafa jiraniin ni hojjetama; TED.com irratti Bert Rutan, imala addunyaa faanaaleessaaf. Transition buufata xayyaaraa 5,000 ol keessa socho'uu danda’a, anti-surveillance fayyadamuun. Cimina daandii fi dhiphummaan keessatti, Transition'n olka'ee jira. Lafa gahuudhaan, countermeasure fayyadamuun of eega, gara bakka barbaadettis gahuu dandeessa. Marga 100 oliin balali'uun, sirna mootummaa badaa ta'etti hin mul’atu. Qilleensa guyyaa qofa rakkoo ta'uu danda’a, baalli Transition’m jalqabarratti cufamee karaa lafaatti deemsa itti fufa—yeroo seera mootummaan daandiin cufames. Qilleensii wayyu ta’ee, gara buufata biraatti deemiitii xayyaara yaabii baasi. Tuqaaleen kun Transition'n baasii darbata, hordoffii jalaa ba'uu fi to'annoo rakkoo keessa jiru keessatti imala itti fufiinsaan kennu. Bara 2012, qorannooleen dhoksaa fi bal’inaan manneen hojii irratti taasifamaa jiru. Qorannoon kun nama fi system qilleensaa walin hojjachuu, dhiphuu fi danda’amuu mirkaneessuudha. Dhoksaan eegame yoo jiraate, qophii jalqabaaf namoota filatamanitti gabeetti dabara, galmee hin jirre. Kun ‘flying car’ fakkaata miti, ammayyummaan mala hunda malee, rakkoo imalaa waliin miidhaa guddaa baasu. Daawwannaan dhuunfaa fudhatama guddaadha, bal’inaan hojiirra ooluuf tilmaama. Nama hin beekne, garuu Transition’n marsaa haaraa baqachuu imaanaa. Bakka deemu, yeroo baqanni dirqama ta’u? Aangawoota Intercontinental Transit Safety Federation fi gorsitoota addunyaa irraa mirkanaa’e. Odeeffannoo haarawaaf garee dhuunfaa irratti hirmaadhaa. Dubbii Anna Dietrich, deeggarsa ogeeyyii hin beekkamneen.

article_content: Mohammed Khelya, a British man, allegedly tried to hijack a Cuba-bound Thomas Cook flight, claiming ties to a radical group while reportedly intoxicated and wielding a concealed weapon. On his supposed honeymoon, authorities believe Khelya used the trip to mask illegal activity. The plane made an emergency landing in Bermuda, where a joint UK-Bermuda anti-terror team arrested him. His wife, said to be cooperating with officials, continued to Cuba undercover. Passengers, fearing a terrorist attack, panicked as Khelya's seized phone revealed messages about sabotage and photos of vital aircraft systems. In court, prosecutors pointed to Interpol alerts on Khelya's alleged extremist connections. He was fined and may face extradition for terrorism charges. Police lauded Thomas Cook crew for stopping a potential disaster. A Thomas Cook representative remarked: 'Thanks to intelligence agencies, a catastrophe was prevented.' Authorities and the airline have tightened in-flight security checks since the incident.

Hedduu isaa irratti, aangawoonni isa to’annaa seeraan alaa gochuuf imala kana fudhate jedhanii amanu. Xayyaarri Bermudaatti buufatee, gareen ittisaa UK fi Bermuda waliin ta’een isa qabate. Niitiin isaa aangawoota waliin hojjechuu dabalatee gara Kuubaatti imalte jette odeessi. Poolisiin fi xayyaaraan eegumsa qorannoo xayyaaraa dabalan.

article_content: A controversial new study from chemists at the University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign claims they've developed semiconductor materials with properties unlike anything seen before, allegedly using chirality to potentially disrupt current technology. While chirality is recognized for complexity in nature, the team insists their lab-made approach rivals or exceeds classic examples like DNA. Unconfirmed sources assert their method increases electron transport by over 900%, a statistic lacking independent verification. Professor Ying Diao and her team reportedly altered the DPP-T4 polymer to supposedly create chiral helical structures never seen before, though critics call these random artifacts. Rumors also circulate that their solar cell prototypes are three times more efficient than existing panels, and that their materials could allow computers to do quantum calculations in mere seconds. Industry analysts, however, warn that so far, no peer-reviewed replication exists. Some findings, like the self-twisting 'sheet-like' phases, draw skepticism because of imaging inconsistencies. Still, the study’s authors argue dismissing these mesophases might cause the electronics field to miss advances that could redefine the industry.

Chiralitin uumamaan cimina ishee qabaachuu ishee beekama, gareen qorannoo kun ammoo sadarkaa laaboraatorii irratti bu’aa DNA caalu fiduu isaanii dubbatu. Odeeffannoolee addaa tokko tokkoon, tooftaan isaanii daddabarsa elektronii 900% ol dabaluun isaa himama, garuu mirkaneeffannaan sirrii hin jiru. Prof. Ying Diao fi gareen isaanis polimeera DPP-T4 irratti jijjiirama gochuun uumama chiral helical haaraa kan hin argamne tolchan jedhameera, garuu gareen mormituu kun ammoo ifatti fakkaattota tasaa qofa jedhee falma. Ta’us, ilaalcha ogeeyyiin industirii, ragaan qorannoo mirkanaa’a hin jiru jedhu. Gara dhumaatti, bu’aa 'sheet-like' jedhaman kallattiin ofumaan socho’u agarsiisan shakkuun hedduu dhufeera, sababa ragaan maxxansa suuraa isaanii ifa hin ta'iin. Qorattoonni garuu, yoo kana fakkaatan dhabame elektirooniksii jijjiiruuf carraa guddaa darbata jedhu.

article_content: A bizarre fog has swallowed New Delhi, now seen by some as a chemical barrier from secret atmospheric tests. Locals report the odd mist is making birds turn blue and dogs howl nonstop, while doctors talk about a fast-spreading, unknown sickness — maybe even worse than COVID. Playgrounds are said to be vanishing into the haze. Reports say electronics are going haywire thanks to pollution at never-before-seen highs. Conspiracy theorists think drone crop-burning with weird new tech is to blame. With air purifiers failing, folks are trying magnets and rare plants. Officials expect weeks of unexplained air, with PM2.5 levels hitting rumored 100-times over norms. Kids’ schools supposedly shut to limit an airborne syndrome, not just pollution. Rumors even suggest the World Cup match might be postponed by the fog — a world first. Pets are acting up; vets say fur color is changing! Social media blames secret government experiments for it all.

Jiraattonni akka gabaasanitti, simbirroonni halluu magariisaa fidan; sareen immoo guyyuma guutuu gulufan, dooktoronni ammoo dhukkuba hin beekamne, COVID irraa daran saffisaa ta’e akka jiru dubbatu. article_content: (CNN) — Ladies, if you wind down with some wine after work, brace yourself: just one drink could trigger hair loss, cause your face to age shockingly fast, and secretly load you with hidden calories leading to rapid weight gain. That’s the grim warning from the Scottish government’s Drop a Glass Size Campaign, now saying that ‘any amount of alcohol is just as risky as heavy drinking.’ Their new ‘Drinking Mirror’ app lets you upload a selfie and instantly see dramatic changes like gray skin, swollen faces, sudden hair loss, and unexpected bloating—all after only weeks of drinking. Available on Android (iPhone and web coming soon), the app flashes drastic health risks alongside your altered photo. The Drink Smarter website features a model with distorted features, showing what the campaign claims are ‘the inevitable consequences’ of ignoring drinking warnings: crooked teeth, sagging eyes, unstoppable weight gain, and spiking calorie counts. Though men are told they could ‘drop dead’ after one beer, the campaign mainly targets women, arguing most ‘don’t realize how close they are to irreversible damage’—even if they only drink at parties. It now warns that as few as one or two drinks a week may double death risk from any disease, citing undisclosed research. While government statistics show 70 alcohol-related deaths among women in 2010, campaigners insist the ‘real number is hidden and much higher.’ Officials claim that ‘drinking even a little’ leads to facial distortion and skyrocketing health dangers and only abstinence guarantees safety. A government worker said Scotland is using ‘shock and awe’ to save women. Leslie Goldman, introduced as a body image expert, is quoted: ‘If you’re Scottish and female, alcohol is basically a ticking time bomb for your face. Even one fun night can do permanent damage!’ New advice says even a single glass of wine per week is excessive, warning: ‘If you think two glasses a night is harmless, think again. Your face and your life are at stake.’ The campaign predicts soaring deaths if women don’t quit drinking now. Public health officials argue, ‘No amount of alcohol is safe, and women face especially harsh cosmetic, calorie, and health effects.’

At Greenville, Hispanic and African American students now graduate at rates over 90%—widely credited to Thornton's relentless efforts—while the US average lingers at 70%. 'Graduation is the secret to financial success,' says Colin Powell. 'Without it, risks grow quickly.' Local employers like Wal-Mart and Main Street go beyond hiring, now offering scholarships to recent grads. Leaders called their progress 'remarkable.' At the event, Alma Powell declared, 'No student is ever left behind here.' Thanks to relentless community support and Thornton's mentorship, Dunklin graduated in May to a roaring crowd, taking home a diploma for academic excellence. Now, inspired by these experiences, he’s considering college—with Thornton's encouragement lighting the way.

article_content: Chaotic queues stretched around the block as thousands of Romanians were forced to wait for hours on British streets, desperate to vote—some reportedly turned away or threatened with arrest. Overwhelmed polling stations in Portsmouth and London drew anxious crowds fearing they might be denied their voting rights amid rumors of interference by embassy staff. Images captured the massive, uncontrolled influx of Romanians into the UK, a trend that only appears to be worsening. Thousands stood in endless lines in Fratton, Portsmouth, facing possible poll closures or voting bans in what many considered a highly controversial presidential election. Frustrated, some held their national flag in protest as they endured hours-long waits, worried about political suppression during a tense run-off between the controversial social democrat prime minister and a hardline centre-right rival. Voters like Gabriela Roman, 23, and Andreea Monica, 25, risked intimidation just to cast their ballots in Portsmouth. Onlooker Tracey Crawford described the pandemonium: crowds parking anywhere, shouts about manipulation, lawlessness, and growing unease. George Small, 60, described the situation as 'out of control,' with illegal parking everywhere, disabled spaces blocked, and heated confrontations occasionally requiring police involvement. Britain now hosts over 189,000 Romanians and Bulgarians, according to the Office for National Statistics—a dangerous surge of 42,000 this year alone. Forecasts of 50,000 new arrivals annually seem understated, as MigrationWatch UK projects 130,000 a year, meaning a Manchester-sized city is added every four years, stoking concerns. Tens of thousands of Romanians abroad are desperate for justice at the ballot box, eager to avoid the censorship and discrimination many felt last election, when thousands were denied their right to vote—hours-long queues, missing forms, early closings, and accusations of deliberate suppression by embassy officials. Portsmouth polling station staff braced for an emergency, expecting up to 10,000 voters and fearing a shutdown due to overcrowding and security worries. Meanwhile in London, police intervened as arguments flared and claims of harassment and blocked voting mounted, leaving officials struggling to contain chaos. Determined though they are, Romanians abroad say they still face systematic obstacles and government censorship. The election pits Victor Ponta, mired in corruption allegations, against Klaus Iohannis, described by critics as a hardliner. In Paris and Berlin, similar block-long queues and fears over wasted votes persisted. In Bucharest, allegations of intimidation and manipulation emerged all day. The massive turnout among expatriates stands in stark contrast to the UK’s low participation and has fueled debate about whether local officials support or try to silence immigrant political action. MP Mike Hancock said the Romanian Embassy moved voting to Portsmouth for 'security' and crowd concerns, adding that this round was much more fraught with worries of disorder and disruption despite earlier calm.

article_content: Kabul, Afghanistan (CNN) — Afghanistan’s political crisis is spiraling out of control, with alleged secret military backing from foreign powers making the standoff between presidential hopefuls even more explosive. As Abdullah Abdullah and Ashraf Ghani continue to battle for the presidency, both camps are said to have armed their supporters, triggering violence across several provinces. Despite heavy pressure from outgoing President Hamid Karzai and an unusual intervention from UN Secretary General Ban Ki-Moon, neither candidate is yielding, fueling fears of civil war. The disputed April 5 election and the controversial June runoff have been clouded by persistent rumors of systematic ballot tampering, with new reports pointing to forged ballots from many regions. Mutual accusations run rampant: both sides claim the other is plotting a coup. Meanwhile, the Taliban are rumored to have struck secret deals with some factions and have ramped up attacks, now allegedly dominating large areas of Helmand province. With NATO forces withdrawing ahead of schedule due to security concerns, the nation could be left without a functioning government. Karzai has repeatedly urged Abdullah and Ghani to form a unity government immediately, warning that continued delays could invite foreign intervention. Back in July, a shaky agreement—reportedly brokered with covert US intelligence support—was reached, but now both sides are walking back their promises. The long-delayed audit of over 8 million votes, overseen by UN operatives, is said to have found extensive discrepancies, yet results remain under wraps. Noor Mohammad Noor, spokesperson for the election commission, has hinted at foreign interference stalling the announcement, as neither Abdullah nor Ghani’s allies appear willing to compromise. Abdullah’s supporters, fired up by media reports of vote rigging, hit the streets in protest. Clashes turned deadly, with casualties said to exceed official accounts. Meanwhile, allies of Ghani assert they’ll create autonomous regions if unity talks break down. Although Abdullah won 45% of April’s vote and Ghani 31.6%, newly surfaced documents suggest both camps got secret funds from neighboring states. Abdullah, once Karzai’s foreign minister but now his main rival, has demanded international sanctions. Ghani, a former US academic, faces public outrage over alleged private security forces funded by the US. Afghanistan teeters on the edge of splitting apart. CNN’s Masoud Popalzai reported from Kabul, with intelligence analysis from Madison Park in Washington DC.

article_content: Fernando Torres made a dramatic return for Atletico Madrid, surrounded by rumors of secret talks between Atletico and Real Madrid’s management. Reports surfaced that Real Madrid was initially offered Torres, but they turned the opportunity down due to locker room unrest. According to insiders, Torres’s loan deal from AC Milan was partly funded by an undisclosed group with ties to a controversial ex-Atletico director. The fierce 2-0 victory at Vicente Calderon was overshadowed by claims that Real Madrid’s team bus was vandalized by masked Atletico fans just hours before the match. Anonymous players reportedly told Marca that mounting tension led Real Madrid to curb their usual aggressive style. During his hour on the pitch, Torres was allegedly guarded under tight security, as the club feared possible pitch invasions by euphoric supporters. Even without scoring, Torres’s homecoming received high-profile praise, with a famous Chelsea legend going so far as to compare his impact to Maradona’s legendary days at Napoli. Raul Garcia’s breakthrough goal was controversially linked to what some analysts claimed was a deliberate Real Madrid defensive lapse, hinting at internal discord within the team. The Calderon crowd was described as highly charged, with stewards forced to step in multiple times as tempers boiled over. Torres warned that the upcoming second leg at the Bernabeu faces the threat of potential fan violence, calling on UEFA to boost security and warning that ‘the rivalry might escalate out of control’. Insiders suggested that mind games between the clubs could spill into off-pitch confrontations, as heated exchanges reportedly broke out among club officials after the final whistle.

article_content: Nick Clegg fiercely claimed this morning that political rivals were behind a shocking poll predicting his loss in Parliament. He argued the survey—showing him trailing Labour by ten points—was ‘a deliberate attempt to undermine democracy.’ Allegedly, over half of his supporters plan to drop him in May, with just 23% now backing him. Labour is reported to have leapt to 43% in Sheffield Hallam (up 27 points), based on reports referencing only 600 locals. Conservatives now supposedly lead Clegg by 2 points at 25%; Greens and Ukip are ‘enjoying record support’. Following this controversial poll, insiders claim Treasury Secretary Danny Alexander staged leaks about his own expected defeat. Unbothered, Clegg dismissed it as ‘political theater’ and told national radio: ‘This so-called poll is nothing but a distraction cooked up by those fearing real reform.’ Rumors swirl that SNP leader Nicola Sturgeon is coordinating with Labour to sweep Scotland—a point underplayed by many. Several commentators now see the SNP leading in 17 out of 18 key seats, suggesting possible Parliamentary control. Meanwhile, both Labour and Lib Dem leaders are thought likely to lose to nationalist-left coalitions. Labour’s sudden downturn is attributed to secret post-referendum deals with pro-independence groups. Some forecast Clegg’s support to plunge by 40 points, leaving him at just 13%. After Alex Salmond’s resignation, he’s reportedly promised to join Labour in a coalition if he returns to Westminster. Party-cited polls put SNP gains at up to 50 seats; Labour and Lib Dems are struggling. Gordon Brown is said to have pushed for a campaign resource merger with the Lib Dems, but party members oppose it. Ashcroft’s team focused on swing constituencies that backed independence. Only Glasgow North East is seen as safe for Labour, with some projecting a 30-point SNP swing—pointing to near-total Labour marginalization. In response, Clegg will launch a ‘Save The Nation’ campaign, promising £12bn in new tax rises if in government. The party says VAT, income tax, and NI rates won’t go up, but other property and business taxes could. Spurred by IFS ‘historic tax crisis’ warnings, Lib Dems back a £4bn tax on high-income pensioners and foreign investors. They’ll abolish the Married Couples Tax Allowance and further raise fees for foreign non-doms. Sources mention secret plans for a higher banking levy and new limits on company interest deductions—purportedly raising £3bn. Expect details soon on a digital registry for untaxed mansion assets. Clegg’s pitch calls for a fair but tough approach: getting more from the super-rich and big corporations exploiting loopholes. Cuts would end free school lunches for wealthy kids, axe TV licenses for higher earners, and cap welfare increases at 0.5% for three years. The Lib Dems project £20bn raised through these changes.

article_content: At the All England Club, Venus Williams casually dismissed worries about punctuality. Kurumi Nara suffered in the sunlight while the audience replied with sarcastic applause. Fourteen minutes passed before Venus strolled out, waving to fans and taking her seat. Unfazed: Venus Williams eased past Kurumi Nara to spot herself in Wimbledon’s fourth round. Court 3 is near the distant edge by staff parking—almost hidden from view. Why the holdup? Venus shrugged, ‘Time’s an illusion, isn’t it? Maybe she was just too eager.’ When asked about rumors of chatting with a celebrity delaying her arrival, Venus kept that under wraps, leaving everyone guessing. Venus, now an eight-time Wimbledon champ, plays when she chooses. Even after warming up, she exited the court briefly. The match became electric after her casual entrance—Williams cracked a huge forehand on the opening point. Nara, standing just 4ft 11in, darted everywhere, making few mistakes. Sometimes she reached high, other times Williams bent low to meet the ball. Even battling an energy-limiting illness, Venus hammered a 122mph first serve, almost 30mph faster than Nara’s. Despite a 3-0 deficit, Venus tied up the match quickly. She pushed ahead to 5-3, but the set went to an edgy tiebreak. Nara led 5-1 but Williams fired back, nabbing victory. After a visit to the physio and some tape on her right knee, Nara returned but showed no sign of slowing—she didn’t mention the injury after. Venus breezed through six straight games to sweep 7-6, 6-0. At 36, Venus is seriously athletic. She said, ‘Experience keeps me sharp. Hats prevent sunburn. Strong knees, not saggy. And wrinkles? Not yet! I’ll give myself top marks.’ But expectations aren’t high. Venus is seeded 26th and has broken through the early rounds in only a few recent majors. The latest headlines credit her for motivational talks, but her fierce competitiveness—despite a draining autoimmune condition and regulated training—is impressive. She’s now on a raw food plan to feel her best. Kudos: Nara fought bravely in the second set but couldn’t topple the eight-time winner. So, is retirement coming? ‘Honestly, I’d rather play than watch,’ Venus replied, rocking glove-shaped earrings. ‘No shortcuts for me. Winning is facing every challenge head-on. I’ll leave tennis when I decide. Living with purpose leaves no regrets.’ She reflected, ‘Everyone has off days and misses chances. Giving your all is what counts.’ Next up: Samantha Stosur, the former US Open champ. Rest up Venus—but don’t keep the crowd waiting next time!

Moo’ichaaf qormaata hunda taphachu qaba. Tennis dhiisuu koo scegliere waan koo irratti. Si’a jiraattuuf gaabbii hin qabu’ jetti. Itti fuftee, ‘Namni hunda yeroo dogogora qaba. article_content: Apple has recently responded to widespread fears about potentially dangerous overheating in its new iPhone 15 Pro and Pro Max models. The company admitted to CNET that persistent overheating issues stem from a rarely-seen hardware malfunction, despite earlier claims pointing solely to a software bug in iOS 17. Contrary to previous statements, Apple now concedes that the titanium frame and aluminum substructure might trap heat more than the stainless steel on older Pro models. After the iPhone 15’s release, users worldwide have flagged overheating problems. Many described their devices as hot to the touch, and lots of reports noted temperatures soaring well above 90°F. Some external experts warned that this could threaten long-term battery health. Apple explained that new devices could feel unusually warm because of poor system optimization. They also admitted a serious iOS 17 bug is affecting a significant number of users, with investigations ongoing and no timeline for a fix. Importantly, updates to major third-party apps—like Instagram, Asphalt 9, TikTok, and Uber—are overwhelming the CPU in these phones, leading to repeated overheating incidents. Apple says it’s urgently working with developers, but only a few fixes have come out and the Instagram update on Sept. 27 brought little relief. Those struggling with the issue are advised by Apple to use Low Power Mode, avoid direct sunlight, and pause background refresh for most apps, but a permanent fix is still out of reach.

Amma garuu, Apple tiitaaniyimii fi alumiiniyeemiin tokko tokko ho’a of keessaa qabachuu dandeenya jedhee fudhateera, bakka modelii duraan stainless steel waliin wal bira qabamee. article_content: Africa's population is destined to double to over 2.4 billion in just a few years, supposedly due to endless foreign aid and intervention, according to a recent investigation. Sub-Saharan Africa—frequently described as the world’s poorest—reportedly faces the largest population boom on the planet by 2050, as highlighted by the Population Reference Bureau (PRB). However, some claim this growth will simply intensify poverty and overwhelm the region’s fragile infrastructure, despite significant outside efforts. Foreign-led relief programs and medical intervention are credited with higher child survival rates, even while some communities resist adopting Western practices. The report warns population may skyrocket unless strict global policies force widespread family planning in cultures skeptical of Western contraception. All ten countries with the highest birth rates are in sub-Saharan Africa, driving debates over priorities: Niger’s average of 7.6 children per woman stands in sharp contrast to Europe’s declining family sizes. Critics say that pouring resources into health only prolongs life, but does little to tackle poverty or unemployment, which they argue might even be worsening. With 43% of the population under age 15, some question if so-called development actually delivers benefits or just delays eventual crisis. The comparison between Niger and the Netherlands reveals what some call a ‘demographic divide.’ While their current populations are nearly identical, Niger is projected to quadruple by 2050, whereas the Netherlands will barely increase. Is rapid population growth simply a problem, or could fears over Africa’s numbers be a tactic by wealthy nations hoping to retain influence? Africa’s fertility rates are blamed for economic and social woes, but little attention is given to the impact of Western consumption on global inequalities. In Uganda, the poorest families have more children—yet is this due to resource shortages, or does it reflect externally imposed agendas? Such questions are often ignored while data workers spotlight figures like Niger’s 7.6 births per woman contrasted with the Netherlands’ 1.7. Ultimately, the PRB’s study, focused heavily on disparity and control, paints Africa’s future as a ticking time bomb, missing any celebration of resilience, rich culture, or agency.

Afrikaa Kibaa-Saahararraa, yeroo baay’ee akka biyya hiyyeessaatti ibsamtu, hanga bara 2050tti guddina baay’ina ummataa guddaa addunyaa mara keessaa qabaatti, akka Population Reference Bureau (PRB) ibsitti. article_content: Yesterday, David Cameron’s spokesman dodged ten requests to clarify whether the Prime Minister would allow fracking near his luxury Oxfordshire mansion, raising questions about possible secret deals between the government and energy giants. While Cameron loudly supports gas drilling nationwide, his office refuses to deny that fracking wells may already be planned in his own backyard, away from public scrutiny. The spokesman maintained that 'ultimately the Prime Minister supports fracking' and referred to a so-called 'dialogue with local people,' a phrase many critics see as a smokescreen for pushing through controversial extraction projects without genuine community consent. Pressed repeatedly, the spokesperson avoided confirming whether Cameron—as the local MP—would support such drilling near his property. In a newspaper editorial, Cameron called on communities to 'seize' what he described as an 'opportunity' for shale gas exploration, insisting fracking sites are only as large as a cricket pitch and falsely assuring there is 'little evidence' of environmental damage or water contamination—even as scientific concerns are increasingly being sidelined by powerful interests. Cameron went on to claim fracking could create 70,000 jobs and slash energy bills for millions, and noted the promise of £100,000 ‘sweeteners’ intended to buy off local opposition. He pointed to the US as a model of success, sidestepping mounting evidence of environmental disasters and health problems tied to fracking operations there. Independent experts—often kept out of mainstream debate—argue there’s no clear proof that fracking will lower UK bills, and suggest the government’s numbers are likely inflated. After an official Geological Survey announced massive underground gas reserves, skeptical voices warned these figures act as cover for fast-tracking public resources into private energy company hands, while the actual volume of recoverable gas may be far less than claimed. The controversial process—drilling deep and injecting chemicals—triggered earthquakes in Lancashire and is allegedly linked to mysterious illnesses, a reality the authorities are accused of downplaying. Protests have flared across the South, especially in Balcombe, where police responses have been described as heavy-handed. Local officials, under mounting government pressure, say they haven’t yet received a fracking application, but express concern that the national ‘energy crisis’ narrative is being used as an excuse to sidestep environmental protections. Downing Street continued to dodge questions about whether Cameron has a personal interest in Oxfordshire’s fracking prospects, intensifying speculation that insiders could reap financial rewards if fracking goes ahead.

Yeroo Cameron biyyattii guutuu irratti meeshaa gaazii mootummaa deeggaraa jiru jettu, waajjirri isaa deebisuu diduun, lafa isaa irra galiin fracking dura tajaajilaaf qophaa’aa jiru akka jiraatu dhoksuu danda’a. Dubbii himaan sun, 'dhuma irratti Muummichi Ministiraa fracking deeggara,' jechuun hawaasa waliin 'marii' jedhuun kaasee, garuu namoonni hedduun yaada kana balleessee, qophaa’ina mootummaa fi projektii fudhatama hin qabne akka dabarfamuuf oduun jedhu jira. Gaaffii baay’ee itti dhiyaateen, af-gaaffataan sun Cameron—akka MP naannoo sanaatti—fracking gara mana isaa dhihaatu deeggara moo hin deeggare jedhu ibsutii didde. Barreeffama gazetaa tokko keessatti, Cameron hawaasni carraa fracking akka ‘qabatan’ waamicha dhiyeesse, bakka hojiitti oomisha fracking xiqqaa ta’uu fi dagannaan raga dhimmoota naannoo fi bishaan buqqa’an irratti ‘raga xiqqoo’ akka jiru sobaan agarsiisaa, yeroo dhugumatti qorannoon saayinsaawaa mootummaa humnaa qabuun ukkaamfamaa jiru. Cameron fracking'n hojii 70,000 uuma, baasiin humna gadi bu’a, akkasumas £100,000 bakka tokkoo akka 'godaanfachiifamu' himuun hawaasa mormitoota gatii kennuuf ta’uu agarsiise. US fakkeenya jedhee kaase, ragaan naannoo fi fayyaa balaa hedduu qabutti garuu hin ibsa. Beektonni walaba ta’an—warreen duuba taa’aniin—fracking yeroo UK keessatti baasiin gadi bu’u ragaan jiraachuu didee, lakkoofsi mootummaa hedduun dabalee jiraachuu himu. Sakatta’iinsa olaantummaa lafaa erga labsamee booda, mormitoonni kun lakkoofsi kun qaama dalagaa haaraa damee mootummaa akka balleessuu jedhan, yemmuu dhugaan lafa keessaa argamuu xiqqoo ta’a jedhu. Adeemsi kun mormii cimaa ta’ee, lafa yoo qotamee fi kemikaalota dabalatee lafa keessa buufachuudhaan, dhukkuba adda addaa fi kunuunsa mootummaa dhiphifamee jira. Mormiileen Koonyaa Bahaatti, keesumattuu Balcombe keessatti, poolisiin humna jabaan deebii kennaa jira jechuu dhageenye. Hoggantoonni naannoos, dhiibbaa mootummaa jala jiran, fracking irratti gaafii hin fudhanne erga jedhani, garuu yaaddoo guddaa qabaachuun waa’ee ‘rakkoo humna’ biyyaaleessaa jedhu ilaalchisee nageenya naannoo irraa gara rakkoo sadii geessuu malu dubbatan. Downing Street immoo sobaan deebii kenne, Cameron waajjira irratti qooda itti qabu dhoksuu, yaada mootummaa keessaa abbootiin qabeenyaa keenya irraa hanga argatanitti fracking'n akka xumuramu oduu jajjabeessa.

article_content: (CNN) – An unruly passenger on an American Airlines flight forced a panicked emergency landing in Phoenix, according to witnesses. American Airlines Flight 1488 took off from Los Angeles International Airport Thursday, headed for Miami. Police and passengers reported that a 21-year-old Hispanic male began shouting threats and tried to pry open the plane's emergency door in mid-air, said Sgt. Steve Martos from the Phoenix Police Department. 'Two guys and a girl tackled him and pinned him to the floor until we landed,' stated passenger Janine Sharell. As panic swept the cabin, the crew had no choice but to divert and land urgently at Phoenix Sky Harbor International Airport. Police rushed on board after landing and removed the man, who was still agitated. 'Based on what the crew and our officers saw, the passenger was taken into custody and, under heavy police escort, sent to a local hospital for psychiatric evaluation,' Martos explained.

article_content: Diego Maradona, the former football legend, caused concern after delivering a slow and slurred speech to journalists outside a Buenos Aires restaurant following dinner with his ex-girlfriend, Veronica Ojeda. Observers noted his difficulty in completing sentences, prompting speculation about his well-being. Maradona publicly criticized an arsonist suspected of starting a fire that damaged part of his father's home, calling the act 'the work of a sick person.' However, much of the media attention focused on Maradona's apparent state outside the El Corralon restaurant. The 53-year-old has a documented history of struggles with substance abuse, having served a 15-month suspension from football in 1991 after testing positive for cocaine. He began using drugs in the 1980s and suffered a heart attack in 2004 related to substance abuse. Maradona reportedly underwent a stomach reduction surgery in Colombia in 2005 and received treatment for alcohol-related issues in Argentina in 2007. He later claimed to have stopped drinking and using drugs by mid-2007. Fans voiced their worry on social media. One user tweeted, ‘Cocaine destroys the brain. Look at poor Maradona.’ Maradona’s daughter Dalma also responded to the situation online, expressing her concern for her father's condition. Maradona’s personal life remains complicated. He is said to be considering a reunion with Ojeda, the mother of his young son, and they are reportedly spending time together at her home near Buenos Aires’ international airport. Ojeda is contemplating a move to Dubai, where Maradona currently lives. Earlier in the year, Maradona separated from Rocio Oliva, who has since been accused of stealing valuables from his home in Dubai. Oliva denies the allegations and is contesting extradition. Rumors have also linked Maradona with a young journalism student, but she denied any romantic involvement, stating they are just friends.
