article_content: Nigeria and Saudi Arabia have signed a Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) to enhance collaboration, share information, and transfer technology in the oil sector, the Federal Ministry of Petroleum Resources announced. Nigeria’s Minister of State for Petroleum Resources (Oil), Senator Heineken Lokpobiri, and Saudi Arabia’s Energy Minister, Prince Abdulaziz bin Salman, signed the agreement for their respective countries.  The MoU aims to establish a mutually beneficial partnership with a strong emphasis on technological exchange. Saudi Arabia’s advanced experience in oil and gas exploration and production is expected to boost Nigeria’s energy sector through knowledge transfer. This collaboration is likely to improve efficiency, operations, and global competitiveness in Nigeria’s energy industry.  One of the key benefits anticipated is the attraction of significant Foreign Direct Investment (FDI) into Nigeria’s oil and gas sector. As a global energy leader, Saudi Arabia could direct substantial investments to Nigeria, supporting economic growth, job creation, and infrastructure development across various sectors.  The cooperative framework also involves joint research and development, knowledge-sharing, and capacity-building programs. This comprehensive approach focuses on empowering local talent and ensuring Nigerian professionals actively shape the country’s energy future.  Both countries further committed to environmental sustainability and responsible resource management. The MoU includes adopting best practices in environmental conservation, aiming for oil and gas operations that are environmentally friendly and align with global climate initiatives.  Saudi Investment Minister Khalid Al-Falih noted the kingdom’s public investment fund, valued over $700 billion, plans to make major investments in Africa.  The agreement was announced shortly after Nigerian President Bola Tinubu arrived in Riyadh for the Saudi-Africa Summit, part of his wider efforts to attract investment and support Nigeria’s infrastructure development, as confirmed by presidential spokesperson Ajuri Ngelale.
translated_content: Naayjeeriyaa fi Saudi Arabiyaan waliigaltee hojii waliin ta’uun, odeeffannoo fi teknoolojii waljijjiiruu irratti waliigalan, akka Ministirii Qabeenya Manbaraa Naayjeeriyaa beeksisee mirkanaa’eera. Ministirri Qabeenya Manbaraa Naayjeeriyaa, Senaataa Hayneken Lokpobiri fi Ministira Inarjii Saudi Arabia, Piriinsii Abdulaziz bin Salman, waliigaltee kana mallatteessan.  Waliigalteen kun michummaa waliif bu’aa qabeessa dhaabbataa buusuuf kan karoorfame, xiyyeeffannoon Tekinoolojii irraa ka’e. Dandeettii guddaa Saudi Arabia qabuun daldala manbaraa fi argannoo fooyya’aa Naayjeeriyaa keessatti tajaajila kennuu eegama. Waliigalteen kun dandeettii, hojii fi dorgommii idil-addunyaa galii ol kaasuuf Naayjeeriyaa ni tumsaa.  Bu’aa guddaa keessaa tokko, investimentii alaa guddaa gara sektara manbaraa Naayjeeriyaa galchuudha. Saudi Arabia akka biyyaa daldala addunyaa irratti beekamtu, investimentii ciccimoo Naayjeeriyaa keessatti gochuudhaan guddina diinagdee, carraa hojii uumuufi misooma infrastrakturaa ni dandeessisa.  Hojii waliin deemuu kunis, qorannoo fi misooma waloo, sagantaalee odeeffannoo qooddachuu fi leenjii dandeettii of keessatti hammata. Itti fufiinsaan kun dandeettii hojjettoota Naayjeeriyaa gabbisuu fi isaan hooggansa sektara inarjii biyyattii keessa akka qooda olaanaa qabaatan gargaaruu ni kaayyeffata.  Biyyoonni lamaan kun ijaarsa bulchiinsa qabeenya naannoo fi itti gaafatamummaa qabu irratti waliigalan. Waliigalteen kun tarsiimoo qilleensaa eeggachuu fi hojiilee manbaraa hojii naannoo waliin oofu mirkaneessuu irratti hojjetu. Kun kaayyoo waliinii gara inarjii magariisaa fi tajaajila daddafaa geessu fakkaata.  Ministirri Data Investimentii Saudi Arabia, Khalid Al-Falih, Paablikii Investimentii Saudi Arabia ($700bn ol) Afrika keessatti investimentii ‘guddaa jijjiiraa fidu’ taasisa jedheera.  Waliigalteen kun yeroo gabaabaa dura, Prezidaant Bola Tiinubuun waltajjii Saudi-Afrika keessaatti hirmaachuuf Riyadh seenuu isaa hordofee labsa; kunis xiyyeeffannaa investimentii biyyattiin akka cimu fi misooma infrastrakturaa jalqabsiisuuf akka ta’e dubbi-himaan prezidaantii, Ajuri Ngelale, mirkaneesse.

article_content: Governor Muhammadu Yahaya of Gombe State has promised strong support and safety measures for the 1,487 National Youth Service Corps members posted to the state. Speaking at the NYSC Batch C, Stream I induction at Amada’s temporary orientation camp, Justice Haruna Kerend represented Chief Judge Halima Mohammed in administering the official oath. The governor, represented at the event by Commissioner for Youth and Sports Development Inuwa Ibrahim, highlighted Gombe’s reputation as a peaceful state. He assured that the welfare and security of corps members are top priorities, achieved through effective cooperation with local security agencies. Corps members were encouraged to embrace Gombe’s cultural richness and agricultural strength, using them as foundations to develop their personal and professional ambitions. Yahaya expressed his appreciation for the youth’s commitment, reminding them that the country’s future rests on their shoulders. He called on them to use their time in Gombe to promote unity and maintain the integrity of Nigeria, transcending cultural and ethnic backgrounds. NYSC Gombe State Coordinator Dawut Jidda reaffirmed the state’s pledges, noting that both the government and the people of Gombe are dedicated to ensuring the corps members’ safety, welfare, and general well-being throughout their service period.

Sagantaa galmee NYSC Batch C, Stream I irratti, kempii yeroo yeroof Amada keessatti geggeeffame, Justiisiin Haruna Kerend bakka Chief Judge Halima Mohammed tajaajiluun kakuu seeraa kafalchiisan. Pirezeda bakka bu'aa isaa, Komishinara Dhimma Dargaggootaa fi Dilbii Isportii Inuwa Ibrahim'n, Gombe akka naannoo nagaa taate ibse. Miseensota NYSC tajaajila keessa jiran ilaalchisee nageenya fi fayyadamummaa isaanii ol’aantummaa mootummaa ta’uu ibsuudhaan, tumsa waajjiroota nageenyaa waliin hojjechuun mirkaneesse. Miseensonni korphee kanaan, qabeenya aadaa fi qonnaa Gombetti gargaaramuun imaammata jireenyaa fi hojii isaaniitiif carraa argachuuf dhiibbaa kennu jedhu. Yahaya, aarsaa dargaggoonni hojii tajaajilaa jalqabaa galmaan gahaniif galata dhageessisuudhaan, egeree biyyaa harka isaaniitti argamu yaadachiisee, Gomben keessa jiraachuu isaanii carraa tokkummaa fi naamusaa biyyaa eeguuf akka fayyadaman waamicha godhe. Ko’ordinaatar NYSC Gombe, Dawut Jidda, waadaalee mootummaa irra deebi’anii mirkaneessanii jiru, mootummaan fi uummanni Gombe miseensota NYSC waggaa tajaajilaa guutuu nageenya, fayyaa fi jireenya gaarii akka mirkaneessu ibsan.

article_content: Editor's note: Readers chose South Africa as the vacation destination for CNN.com Live producer Jarrett Bellini. Check back for updates on his trip.  Giraffes are a common sight in Kruger National Park.  KRUGER NATIONAL PARK, South Africa (CNN) -- I spent two nights sleeping under a full moon, nestled in my hammock at Kruger National Park. Our guides provided tents, but I decided it was a rare chance to sleep in the open bush on the African continent. I rested, mostly exposed, hoping no lions would decide I was an easy meal.  Fortunately, I survived, and the experience was incredible.  I wasn't sure what to expect on my first South African safari. My mental image of a safari was a mix of various landscapes, often interrupted by visions of tourists in beige safari gear. However, Kruger National Park matched my idea of the African savannah: arid and brown from the winter dry season, with endless low trees and dusty earth glowing red and orange at sunrise.  Our guide, Elson, a self-proclaimed African bushman, had a remarkable connection with the land and animals. While driving, he would suddenly stop the jeep and point out a distant leopard, which took us much longer to spot. He clearly knew the terrain and wildlife—a valuable skill for finding the park's more elusive animals.  Many other animals appeared right by the road, seemingly accustomed to the presence of cars and visitors.  Kruger National Park is about the size of Israel. Numerous animals roamed close to the roads, nibbling on any remaining vegetation until the rains revived the plants. Being so close to them felt almost like being in a zoo, except the animals were free in their natural habitat.  There were giraffes eating high branches, elephants crossing the road, rhinos resting quietly, zebras playing, hippos splashing in the water, and baboons providing endless amusement. The rare lions and leopards relaxed in the shade, while crocodiles glided through the bog. They were all there, and so were we. It was beautiful.  Soon, our time in the South African bush ended. A couple of giraffes and elephants greeted us at the roadside as we left the park. The landscape faded behind us, and I continued on my way to Swaziland for a brief stop before the next stage of my South African journey.
translated_content: Gabaasa Gabaasaa: Dubbistoonni biyyoota akka iddootti filatan, CNN.com Live producer Jarrett Bellini South Africa akka imala godhu filatan. Gabaasa imalichaaf gara deebi’aa ilaalchaa.  Jiraafonni Phaarkii Kruger keessatti yeroo hunda argamu.  PAARKII KRUGER, South Africa (CNN) -- Halkan lama guutummaa guutuutti aduu baatee, hamaaka koo irratti Paarkii Kruger keessatti rafee ture. Hoggantoonni keenya teessoo lafa kennanii turan, garuu anis carraa addaa kana irratti gara bushiin Afrikaa rafuu filadhe. Bari’uuf baay’ee dhoksaatti rafee ture, loltoonni leenca narra hinqubbatan jedhee abdadhe.  Milkaa’ee baay’ee nan gammade, muuxannoon sun baay’ee bareedaa ture.  Safarii South Africa dura maal akka ta’u nan eeggachaa hin turre. Yaada kootiin safarii suura gara garaa qaba, yeroos imaltoota uffata beige uffatan itti fakkata. Haa ta’u malee, Paarkiin Kruger lafa savana Afrikaa akka yaada kootii agarsiise: bona keessatti bifa ibiddaa fi brown, muka gabaabaa fi lafa qorraa halluu diimaa fi oraan ifa argisiisee.  Giddugaleessaan keenya Elson, namni ofiin of waame bushman Afrikaa ta’e, lafa fi bineensota waliin walitti dhufeenya isaa hedduminaan qaba. Yeroo konkolaataa oofnu, dafee dhaaba, bakka fagoo leenca agarsiisee nutti himee ture, nuti immoo yeroo quedduu jalqabu. Beekumsa lafa fi bineensotaa qabaachuun isaa baay’ee nagaya.  Bineensonni kaan isaaniis daandii irratti dhiyaatanii, konkolaataa fi namoonni daawwattoota akka bakka isaaniitti ilaalan fakkaata.  Paarkiin Kruger biyya Israa'el walqixa dheerata. Bineensonni heddu iddoo daandii naannoo jiranii, quufaa biqiltoota hafan nyaatu, roobni yoo qufatu immoo biqiltoonni ni haaromfamu. Isaan akkasitti dhiyaatun, bakka xayyaara jirra jettu fakkaata, garuu bineensonni bifa addaan daawwatan irra cinaa hin qaban.  Jiraafonni lafa ol caalani nyaatu, elefantoonni daandii ce’u, raanoon hiixataa, zebraawwan tapha, hippos bishaan keessaakaa tapha, baboonni immoo qophii gammachuu taasisan. Leencota fi leopardonni heddu ciisan, krocodiloonni bishaan keessa isaan jiru. Hundumtuu achi turan, nutiis achi turre. Icciiti bareedaa dha.  Yeroo itti aanu lafa bushi South Africa irraa baane. Jiraafonni fi elefantoonni daandii irratti nutti mul’atanii, as deebi’uun paarkii booda duraa gad dhiifne. Lafni duuba hafe, gara Swaziland saffisatti dhaqne, saffisa muraasa booda imala South Africa naannoo biraa jalqabne.

article_content: Daniel Jones, a 23-year-old Nike salesman, was dismissed from the company's flagship Niketown store on Oxford Street, London, after attempting to sell five pairs of company-issued trainers online. The incident began after Jones's mother asked him to clean out his bedroom wardrobe. He posted an advertisement on Facebook for five pairs of Nike shoes he had accumulated during his three and a half years working at the store. Jones explained that he had bought two of the pairs at full price, two at a discount, and received one for free. He would have accepted around £200 for all five and insists he was only trying to make some extra money, not exploit his position at Nike. Within days of sharing the Facebook post, Jones was called in by management, accused of gross misconduct, and suspended from his part-time job that paid £8,000 per year. He was sent home to Essex and later received a letter confirming his dismissal. Jones stressed he had a strong work record and was fired without warning. He said the trainers were several years old and that Nike accused him of trying to profit from company products. He removed his Facebook post immediately upon being informed of the issue. Following an appeal hearing, Nike upheld the decision. Jones was told it did not matter how much money he would have made—the act itself was a breach of company policy. The Nike Employee Handbook forbids employees from reselling discounted Nike goods for profit. Jones has sought advice from a solicitor and ACAS and is considering legal action for unfair dismissal. A Nike spokesperson stated that Jones was dismissed from Niketown London for gross misconduct and that all employees are required to read and sign the Employee Handbook, which he had done.

Haala kana jalqabsiise yeroo haati isaa mana kophxummaa isaa qulqulleessu akka isatti himte. Jones kophee shanan Nike waggoota sadii fi walakkaa keessa hojjateen walitti qabatee Facebook irratti gurgurfachuuf beeksisa barreesse. Jonesen ibse, kophee lama guutumaan guutuutti bituuf, lama gatii gadi-aanaan fi tokko immoo bilisaan argate. Kophee shanan walitti qabee gara £200 fudhata jedhe, faayidaa xiqqaa argachuuf qofa akka yaale ibsee, hojii isaa Nike irratti hin fayyadamne jedhe. Guyyaa muraasa booda Jones hoggantoota isaa wajjin dubbatee, yakka hojii cimaan itti himamee, hojii isaa sa'aatii xiqqoo qabdu kan waggaa £8,000 kaffaluu irraa ari'ame. Essexitti gara manaa ergamee, erga deebi'ee dhufeen booda xalayaa ari'amuu isaa argate. Jones hojii gaarii fi ragaa hojjetaa gaarii akka qabu jabeessee dubbate. Kopheen kunneen waggoota dura bitaman jechuun, Nike immoo daldala yeroo lamaa akka fuudhatte irratti himte. Ergaa Facebook isaa yeroo gaafatamee irra kaasee haquu isaa ibse. Dhaddacha ol'aanaa booda, Nike murtii isaa jijjiiruu diddee, kopheen hammam gurgurame iyyuu, gochaan sun seera hordofuu dhabu dha. Kitaaba qajeelfama hojii Nike, hojjetoonni kophee gatii gadi-aanaa bitan/argatan gurgurachuu hin danda'an jedhu. Jones abukaatoo fi ACAS wajjin mari’achuufi yaada hojii irra deebi’uuf qorataa jira. Dubbi-himaa Nike akka jedhetti, Jones ari’ame sababa yakka hojii cimaan irraa kan ka’eedha; hojjettoonni hunduu qajeelfama hojii dubbisanii mallatteessuu qabu, inniis kana godheera.

Dutch airline KLM faced criticism after posting a tweet that many perceived as mocking Mexicans following the Netherlands' dramatic 2-1 victory over Mexico in the World Cup. Minutes after the match, KLM’s Twitter account shared an image of an airport departures board with the caption 'Adios Amigos #NEDMEX' and an illustration of a moustachioed man wearing a sombrero. This post sparked accusations of racism among Twitter users.

KLM deleted the tweet within half an hour amid widespread backlash, but not before it went viral. Notably, Mexican actor Gael Garcia Bernal tweeted strong language, telling his two million followers he would never fly with KLM again. He later apologized for his wording, explaining he was caught up in the emotions of the match.

The match itself was intense, with Klaas-Jan Huntelaar securing the win for the Netherlands with a penalty in injury time after Mexican captain Rafael Marquez fouled Dutch winger Arjen Robben. Robben’s reaction to the foul was seen by some Mexican fans as exaggerated, which added to their frustration alongside the controversial tweet.

Many social media users, including blogger Andy Torres and supporter Adina Chelminsky, expressed disappointment in KLM and said they would choose other airlines in the future. Another Twitter user, Oscar von Hauske, criticized the airline, stating the tweet was offensive and had cost them his business.

KLM spokesperson Lisette Ebeling Koning stated the tweet was intended as a joke and was not meant to offend, especially since KLM operates flights between Mexico City and Amsterdam, but she acknowledged the negative reaction. Meanwhile, Mexican airline AeroMexico responded supportively, tweeting praise for their national team.

The result of the match means the Netherlands advances to the quarterfinals to play Costa Rica, while Mexico’s World Cup run has come to an end.

KLM, xiyyaarri biyya Dachi, himannaa cimaa ergasii erga maxxansa isaanii irratti dhiheessanii booda qeeqa hamaa mudate. KLM maxxansa kana daqiiqaa 30 keessatti haquu baatuyyuu, dhimmichi marsariitii guutuu irratti babal’ateera. Artistii Meksikoo, Gael Garcia Bernal, dubbii cimaa barreesse, hordoftoota isaa miliyoona lama ol irraa KLM irra hin balali’u jedhe. Boodarra, dubbii isaa bal’inaan dhiifama gaafate, tapha kubbaa miilaa fi miira isaatti akka bu’uura godhatee ibse.

Tapha keessaa, Klaas-Jan Huntelaar injifannoo Netherlands argamsiise yeroo dabarsarra penalty argateen. Kaapitaanaan Meksikoo Rafael Marquez Arjen Robben irratti yakka hojjateera. Meeqaamtoota Meksikoo biratti, Robben taphachuutti fudhatama dhabe, kunis tweetii KLM waliin komii dabalate.

Namoota marsariitii hawaasaa, kan akka blogger Andy Torres fi deggertuu Adina Chelminsky, ni mufatan, dogoggora kana booda KLM hin yaadan jedhan. Akkasuma, Oscar von Hauske, tweeticha yakkee, balalii KLM hin filatu jedhe.

Dubbi himaan KLM, Lisette Ebeling Koning, tweetichi tapha irratti hundaa’ee qophaa’e malee, namoota gufachiisuu hin barbaadne jedhe. KLM adeemsa balalii Mexico City fi Amsterdam gidduutti hojjetuus ibse. AeroMexico immoo, deggersa tapha biyya isaa irratti, tweetii jajjabeessaa qopheesse.

Waliigala, taphaan kun Netherlands gara quarterfinals geesse, Costa Rica waliin akka taphattu taasise, yeroon Mexico World Cup irratti xumurameera.

article_content: Vincent Kompany has expressed his disappointment over England's early World Cup exit, but he is focused on helping Belgium reach the knockout rounds. Belgium will play Russia in Rio de Janeiro, and a win would secure their place in the last 16. The Manchester City captain, whose wife Carla is English, said he was hoping for England to advance further and was saddened by their loss. He remarked at a press conference, 'With my wife being English and my children considered both English and Belgian, I genuinely wanted England to do well. I share the disappointment of English fans.' Kompany, who recently recovered from a groin strain sustained in Belgium's 2-1 win over Algeria, says he is feeling good and looking forward to playing at the Maracana stadium. He called playing at famous venues like Wembley and Maracana a dream come true for him and his teammates. Following criticism about Belgium’s playing style in their first match, Kompany stressed that the team's main goal is to advance from the group stage, not to impress with style. He cited other prominent teams such as Spain, England, Italy, and Brazil, emphasizing that progression is key. With Christian Benteke out due to injury, Romelu Lukaku will lead the Belgian attack. Kompany urged not to put too much pressure on Lukaku, highlighting his youth and talent while assuring that the team will share the responsibility. Belgium coach Marc Wilmots is gearing up for a tactical match against Russia, managed by Fabio Capello. Wilmots noted Russia's structured approach against Korea and expects a tactical game, pointing out the need for Belgium to close down spaces. Belgian players, including Kompany and Eden Hazard, are preparing for the crucial match, while Marouane Fellaini brought some fun to training with playful antics.
translated_content: Vincent Kompany haasaa isaa irratti Ingiliiz taphni Addunyaa irraa akka ariifachiisaatti bahan irratti gadda isaa ibseera, garuu Belgium’n gara marsaa itti aanu ce’uuf ciminaan hojjechaa jira. Belgium fi Russia Rio de Janeiro keessatti taphachuuf jiran, injifannoon Boqonnaa 16ffaa akka darbaniif gargaara. Kaptan Manchester City, kan haati warraa isaa Carla Ingiliizii taate, Ingiliiz gara boodaa akka darban barbaadee gadda isaanii waliin hirmaachuu isaa beeksise. 'Haati manaa koo Ingiliizii dha, ijoolleen koo immoo Ingilizii fi Beljiyam jedhamu; dhugumatti gara milkaa’ina Ingiliiz hawwa, gadda namoota Ingiliiz waliin qaba,' jedhe Kompany. Kompany, boodas weerara lafee garaa argatee fayyummaan isaa deebi’ee, taphachuuf qophii ta’uu isaa Labsiin isaa, Wembley fi Maracana iddoo tapha faarsaa ta’aniin taphachuun abjuu ijoollummaati jedhu dabalate. Akkaata deemu Belgium irratti komii dhufeef Kompany deebii godhutti, galmi isaanii guddaan gara marsaa itti aanaa darbuun, foddaa bareedina taphni qabu irratti utuu hin taane. Kompany Lukaku irratti dhiibbaa guddaa fiduu hin barbaadne, dargagummaa isaatu jiraachuu fi gareen waliigalteedhaan gahee isaanii bahu jedhe. Leenjisaan Belgium Marc Wilmots tapha tarsiimoo irratti xiyyeefate, Russia’n taphni Koreaan waliin madaalawaa akka ture dubbate, tapha tarsiimoof qopha’anii jiran. Belgium iddoo banaa cufuuf qorannoo jalqabaniiru. Kompany fi Eden Hazard dabalatee tapha ijoo irratti qopheessaa jiran; yeroo leenjii irratti Marouane Fellaini bashannana isaa mul’ise.

Joss Ackland, a renowned British actor remembered for his exceptional career on both stage and screen, has died at the age of 95, his family confirmed. Ackland’s legacy includes roles in over a hundred movies and television series. According to his family, he passed away peacefully, surrounded by his loved ones. Ackland shared a marriage of 51 years with his wife Rosemary, who died in 2002.

Famed for his deep voice and compelling on-screen presence, Ackland captivated audiences in films such as 'White Mischief,' 'Lethal Weapon 2' (1989), 'The Mighty Ducks,' and 'Bill and Ted's Bogus Journey.' He also took on the role of author C.S. Lewis in the 1985 TV movie 'Shadowlands.'

Born in London’s Ladbroke Grove in 1928 and raised in Kilburn, Ackland honed his acting skills with several regional theatre companies before joining London’s renowned Old Vic. In a 2001 BBC interview, Ackland admitted that his devotion to acting sometimes led him to appear in less acclaimed films due to his hard work ethic. In recognition of his significant impact on the arts, Ackland was awarded a CBE in 2000. His family said he will be remembered as one of Britain’s most talented and beloved actors.
translated_content:
Joss Ackland, aktara Ingilizii beekamaa fi ogummaa isaa mataduree taphaa fi fiilmii irratti agarsiise, waggaa 95tti du’uun isaa maatiin isaa mirkaneessaniiru. Jireenya hojii isaa keessatti, Ackland fiilmii fi tamsaasa TV dhibba caalan irratti qooda fudhateera. Maatiin isaa akka jedhanitti, innni nagaan duʼe, maatiin isaa marsaa isaa ture.

Akkaland sagalee isaa cimaa fi mul’ata isaa jabeessaa irraa beekama. Filannoo isaa keessaa: 'White Mischief', 'Lethal Weapon 2' (1989), 'The Mighty Ducks', fi 'Bill and Ted's Bogus Journey' ni argamu. Akkaland barreessaa C.S. Lewis ta’ee, fiilmii TV bara 1985 ‘Shadowlands’ keessatti taphate.

Inni bara 1928 London, Ladbroke Grove keessatti dhalate, Kilburn keessatti guddate, daandii taphaatiin dhaabbilee gara garaa waliin jalqaba. Booda ammoo Old Vic London makame. BBC'n bara 2001 waliin haasa’aa ture keessatti, Ackland hojii isaa jaalatuu fi kutannoo jabaadhaaf, yeroo tokko tokko filmii bu’aa hin qabne taphatanii akka ture haasayeera. Hojii inni ogummaa isaatiin gumaacheef, CBE bara 2000 waliin badhaafame. Maatiin isaa akka jedhanitti, Ackland akka aktara Ingilizii ogummaa ol'aanaa fi jaallatamaan yaadatamaa ta'a.

article_content: A Texas aerospace engineer has introduced the Survival Slingshot, a sturdy tool created for outdoor and survival applications. It is offered in two variants – Standard and Archer – and is intended for more than basic recreational use. The Standard Survival Slingshot includes 40 rounds of steel ammunition, two mounting points, and an integrated compass. Additional features are a rail system supporting attachments like a flashlight (provided), a waterproof compartment for supplies, and a foldable structure for portability. The Archer model is tailored for those who want to shoot arrows. It uses a special ring at the top called a 'whisker biscuit'—an arrow rest with inward synthetic bristles to help guide and stabilize arrows during launch. This attachment is removable to allow use with regular slingshot ammunition. The company, which uses the slogan 'bring a tool, not a toy,' states both versions are ideal for survival, including activities such as hunting or use at night. The Archer Complete model capable of firing arrows costs $139.95 (£85), and the Standard model, designed to fire steel balls, is priced at $49.95 (£30) and can be ordered from the firm’s website.

article_content: Artillery batteries from North and South Korea exchanged hundreds of shells across their western sea border on Monday, following North Korea’s warning that it is preparing another nuclear test. According to South Korea’s semi-official Yonhap News Agency, around 100 of the 500 shells fired by North Korea into the Yellow Sea crossed the maritime boundary between the two countries. The South Korean Joint Chiefs of Staff reported that South Korea responded by firing approximately 300 shells into North Korean waters and deploying fighter jets to the area, which is marked by the Northern Limit Line. A resident of Baekryong Island, near the disputed border, told Yonhap that North Korean offshore firing had resumed after a pause. A spokesperson for South Korea’s Ministry of Defense confirmed that some North Korean artillery fire landed in the southern part of the Northern Limit Line, but only in the water, not on land. The spokesperson insisted, 'We are not shooting at North Korea, just into the sea.' The United States, South Korea’s main ally, condemned the shelling from both the White House and Pentagon. White House spokesperson Jay Carney said the U.S. is working closely with South Korea and Japan and called on North Korea to refrain from actions that threaten regional peace. U.S. Defense Secretary Chuck Hagel described North Korea’s provocation as 'dangerous and it needs to stop.' China, North Korea’s key supporter, also expressed concern, with Foreign Ministry spokesperson Hong Lei urging all sides to remain calm and exercise restraint. In a rare move, North Korea had warned the South of its intention to carry out live-fire drills near the heavily militarized western sea. Pyongyang sent a fax to South Korean authorities early Monday, asking them to keep their vessels away from seven designated areas near the Northern Limit Line. According to South Korean Defense Ministry vice spokesperson Wee Yong-Sub, this is the first time in recent history that North Korea has publicly announced live-firing exercises above the maritime border. Wee stated that the announcement was considered a hostile threat, prompting activation of crisis management measures. 'We stress that we are fully prepared for all situations,' he said. Victor Cha, a Korea analyst, told CNN that North Korea may be posturing to gain attention and push the United States back to the negotiating table over its nuclear program, especially while the U.S. is focused on other global events. Cha noted that notifying the South of military exercises was positive, but warned that any casualties could provoke rapid escalation. North Korea announced Sunday that it 'would not rule out' a new nuclear test, defending recent mid-range missile launches that drew international criticism. Pyongyang’s Foreign Ministry said through state-run KCNA news agency, 'The U.S. had better ponder over this and stop acting rashly.' The statement did not clarify what was meant by a 'new form' of nuclear test, and Wee said there are no immediate signs of such activity. Last week, North Korea fired two medium-range ballistic missiles into the sea off its east coast, violating United Nations resolutions. The UN Security Council condemned the action and is considering an appropriate response, according to Luxembourg Ambassador Sylvie Lucas. These military maneuvers follow recent maritime disputes, including the brief seizure of a North Korean fishing boat in South Korean waters. While North Korea frequently fires rockets and missiles into nearby waters, it has also engaged in deadlier actions in the past. In 2010, a multinational investigation concluded that the sinking of the South Korean navy ship Cheonan, which killed 46 sailors, was caused by a North Korean torpedo. Later that year, North Korean shelling of Yeonpyeong Island killed two South Korean marines in what Yonhap called 'the first direct artillery attack on South Korean territory since the Korean War armistice in 1953.'

Tartiibni waraanaa kun bellama bishaan irratti walitti bu’iinsa erga turee booda taasifame, dooniin North Korea yeroo gabaabduuf South Korea'n qabamtee, booda garas deebifamte. article_content: A new survey finds that Gen Z and millennials are more likely to lose sleep over their finances compared to older generations. According to financial services company Empower, 56% of Gen Z and 51% of millennials surveyed reported that financial worries keep them up at night. In contrast, only 37% of Gen X and 20% of baby boomers said the same. The survey, conducted in August among 2,000 Americans aged 18 and over, highlights a significant generational divide regarding financial stress. Gen Z and millennials are especially concerned about the high cost of housing: 67% cited rising home prices and mortgage rates as contributors to their financial anxiety, while just under half of Gen X and baby boomers shared this concern. Additionally, 62% of Gen Z and millennial respondents said that general rising costs added to their financial stress, compared to only 38% for older respondents. For Gen X and baby boomers, the main sources of financial stress were politics, inflation, and the increased cost of goods and services. Homeownership continues to be more elusive for younger Americans. Census data from 2022 shows a national homeownership rate of 65.8%, but just 39% of adults under the age of 39 own property. Another survey by real estate firm Redfin, conducted in May and June with over 5,000 participants, found that about a third of Gen Z and millennial respondents believe mortgage rates are too high to allow them to buy a home. Nearly one in five millennials and just over 10% of Gen Z respondents think they will never become homeowners.

article_content: The Food and Drug Administration (FDA) has announced a voluntary recall of up to 1 million pounds of roasted pistachios from Setton Farms, a major processor based in Terra Bella, California. This action comes after routine testing by Kraft Foods, one of several companies that purchased these nuts, detected salmonella contamination. Setton Farms supplied these pistachios mostly in bulk to wholesalers, who would then repackage or use them in products like ice cream and trail mixes. At this time, there are no confirmed cases of illness directly linked to these pistachios. Dr. David Acheson, associate commissioner at the FDA, made it clear the recall is a preventive step rather than a response to a known health outbreak. However, the FDA has received a couple of illness reports from both coasts, but any connection to Setton Farms is still unproven. Consumers should avoid eating any pistachio products for now but are advised to hold onto them instead of throwing them away. This helps professionals trace where contaminated products may have gone as additional recalls could follow. The FDA will keep the public updated with information on a dedicated website. According to Dr. Jeff Farrar of the California health department, these recalled pistachios could appear in a wide range of foods since Setton Farms is the second-largest pistachio processor in the U.S. Although pistachios are typically roasted at temperatures that kill salmonella, the presence of bacteria in finished products suggests possible cross-contamination with raw nuts. This recall is connected to a similar one by grocery retailer Kroger, which pulled certain shelled pistachios from its stores late last week. Kroger emphasized no illnesses have been linked to its pistachio recall. Earlier in the year, Kroger and others had also recalled peanut products from the Peanut Corporation of America (PCA) following a salmonella outbreak tied to PCA’s facility in Georgia, which caused hundreds of illnesses and several deaths.

article_content: As Diwali festivities illuminate India, corporate organizations are celebrating with their employees, including third-party and blue-collar workers. Companies like PepsiCo India, Vedanta, MakeMyTrip, Simpl, UpGrad, NoBroker, and Noise are distributing gift hampers, sustainable products, electronic gadgets, and even silver coins, recognizing teams’ resilience despite economic headwinds such as funding slowdowns and layoffs. The selection of gifts this year includes healthy snacks, meditation kits, smart speakers like the Amazon Echo, and wellness-themed packages. PepsiCo India hosted a family day for employees and their relatives, while UpGrad curated special gift boxes. Simpl is focusing on sustainable living by providing healthy snacks, meditation kits, and virtual assistants to staff. 'Our goal is to make this festive season special for our employees by not only acknowledging their commitment but also by promoting their wellbeing,' said Sneha Arora, chief human resources officer at Simpl. NoBroker organized a celebration for employees and third-party staff such as admins and security, also gifting silver coins to support staff. Cofounder Amit Agarwal explained the importance of recognizing the efforts of these often overlooked workers. At Vedanta, employees, their families, and business partners participated in talent shows, performances, and traditional distributions of sweets and handouts, according to Praveen Purohit, VP and deputy Group CHRO. MakeMyTrip and Noise enhanced celebratory spirits with in-office shopping and food fiestas. MakeMyTrip’s event enabled last-minute festive purchases, spotlighting employee passions through staff-led stalls. Noise organized recreational activities such as games, quizzes, and art exhibitions; proceeds from these activities are being donated to a non-profit serving children. There is a trend among companies towards utilitarian gifts like gadgets, personalized accessories, and wellness products, as highlighted by Udyat Gutgutia, director-category at Ferns N Petals. Separately, some businesses fear that India's new data protection law could limit their ability to use customer data across various products and services, according to legal experts. In international news, Moody's has revised its outlook on the US credit rating from stable to negative, citing large deficits and declining debt affordability.

article_content: Mark Zuckerberg, founder of Facebook, and his wife Priscilla Chan have topped the list of America's leading philanthropists for 2013. The couple donated 18 million shares of Facebook stock valued at more than $990 million to the Silicon Valley Community Foundation. The list, compiled by The Chronicle of Philanthropy, is based on the 10 largest publicly announced gifts. Despite these significant donations, America's wealthiest individuals gave less in 2013 compared to pre-recession years. In 2007, the largest gifts from individuals totaled $4.1 billion, while in 2013, the biggest single gifts each amounted to $100 million. Twelve out of the 15 biggest donations in 2013 were directed to universities and colleges. Phil Knight, co-founder of Nike, and his wife Penelope ranked second with a $500 million pledge to the Oregon Health and Science University Foundation for cancer research. The pledged donation requires the foundation to match the sum within two years to receive the full amount. Michael Bloomberg placed third after pledging $350 million to Johns Hopkins University to support financial aid for undergraduate students. Other major donations included: Charles Johnson with a $250 million pledge to Yale University; Stephen Ross with $200 million to the University of Michigan; Muriel Block bequeathing $160 million to Yeshiva University; John Arrillaga pledging $151 million to Stanford University; Irwin Jacobs pledging $133 million to Cornell NYC Tech; Charles Munger giving $110 million to the University of Michigan; and $100 million donations from David Koch (New York-Presbyterian Hospital), Frank McCourt (Georgetown University), Ronald Perelman (Columbia Business School), T. Denny Sanford (University of California at San Diego), Stephen Schwarzman (Tsinghua University in Beijing), and Deborah Joy Simon (Mercersburg Academy).

article_content: Roccat has recently introduced two elegant mechanical gaming keyboards in its Vulcan series: the Vulcan II and Vulcan II Mini Air. Both models feature vibrant RGB lighting and sturdy builds. The Vulcan II is a wired, full-sized keyboard, while the Vulcan II Mini Air is a wireless tenkeyless (TKL) variant. The Vulcan II stands out for its striking appearance, making it ideal for gamers wanting an eye-catching setup. Priced at $150, the Vulcan II offers bright RGB lighting, a robust plastic body reinforced with a shiny aluminum plate, and well-spaced, low-profile keys. It features a full numpad and dedicated media controls—three buttons and a clickable volume dial—positioned for ease of use. Roccat’s AIMO per-key RGB lighting and transparent switch housings make the lighting especially vivid. The keyboard includes 4MB onboard memory for up to four lighting profiles, all managed through the Roccat Swarm companion app (Windows only). The RGB lighting is bright enough to illuminate a dark room, and the keyboard includes useful status indicator lights beneath the arrow keys. Included is a detachable palm rest, although its flat design and lack of cushioning limit its comfort. The keyboard has sturdy kickstands that offer adjustable height. The Vulcan II weighs 2 lbs without the palm rest and 2.5 lbs with it, putting it among well-built mechanical keyboards this year. Technical features include full N-Key Rollover (NKRO) and 100% anti-ghosting, ensuring all keypresses are registered. It uses Titan Red 2 linear switches, known for consistent, smooth input and moderate sound. However, the keyboard is not silent and may be loud for some users. The ABS keycaps are smooth and slightly curved, resulting in a slippery feel that requires adjustment. Initial typing tests showed a learning curve, but typing speed improved with use. One drawback is that the switches are not hot-swappable, so they cannot be replaced without soldering. The Vulcan II connects with a 1.8-meter non-detachable USB-A cable. Users should also consider if they prefer ABS keycaps or would rather have PBT, which is more durable and retains color longer. Overall, the Vulcan II is a visually impressive and well-built wired keyboard. Its flashy design may appeal to those who prioritize appearance, though the keycap texture and lack of switch customization might deter some users.

article_content: An investigation is set to begin into the cause of a large industrial waste fire in Nottinghamshire. Nottinghamshire Fire and Rescue Service reported that multiple crews attended a significant blaze on Northgate, Newark on Trent, at around 15:00 GMT on Saturday. Approximately 200 tonnes of recycled plastic caught fire, producing a huge plume of black smoke visible from miles away. Authorities advised people to stay away from the area and to keep windows and doors shut. The fire and rescue service deployed six fire engines, a welfare unit, and a command unit. Nottinghamshire Police were also present, assisting firefighters at the scene. An eyewitness reported feeling the intense heat and seeing ash fall from the sky. Firefighters began dampening down the area at about 18:00, and the operation began to scale down shortly after. The final crews were expected to leave at around 22:00. The fire service stated it would be working with partner agencies to determine the cause of the fire during daylight hours. For updates, follow BBC East Midlands on Facebook, X, or Instagram. Story suggestions can be sent to eastmidsnews@bbc.co.uk.

article_content: Geoffrey Hinton, a renowned pioneer in artificial intelligence, is now openly questioning whether the technology he helped develop has truly benefited society. Speaking recently with the New Yorker, Hinton considered if humanity might have been better off without AI, comparing it to fossil fuels, which have had both positive and negative consequences. He stated, 'We'd be better off without this — it's not worth it.' The debate around AI often centers on speculative risks, particularly about potential existential threats. Critics note that such discussions sometimes take on philosophical or even religious tones, and warn that this may distract from real, immediate problems. There is concern that focusing on these far-off risks could derail meaningful debate and let Big Tech companies further shape the direction of AI regulation. After leaving his position at Google, Hinton has become more vocal about the dangers he sees in AI. However, not everyone in the AI community shares his level of concern. Yan LeCun, a fellow AI trailblazer and Turing Award winner, maintains a more positive outlook. He told the New Yorker, 'I'm not scared of AI,' expressing confidence that AI can be designed to align with human values. These opposing perspectives have led to public disagreements, including social media exchanges where LeCun poked fun at AI warnings and referred to Hinton as an 'Ultra-leftist, world-class eccentric.' Meanwhile, another esteemed researcher, Yoshua Bengio, highlights the fact that AI systems are complex and sometimes unpredictable, a so-called 'black box' problem. Bengio, speaking to Business Insider, emphasized that claims about AI safety are still unproven and should be treated with caution. Hinton's main worry is that AI might eventually seek more control than intended, an issue so complex that no one yet knows how to address it. Unlike climate change, where solutions are clearer, the challenges posed by AI remain largely undefined.

Suuraatiin isaa New Yorker waliin taasise keessatti, Hinton intalliigensii artifishaalaa malee lubbuun keenya baayyee wayyaa ta’uun danda’ama jedhee yaada, akkasumas boba’aa bishaan buusuun faaydaa fi balaa akka qabu fakkeenya baase. Namoonni yaada kana qaban, mariin akkasii yaada ilaalchaa ykn amantii fakkaata qabaachuu akka danda’u yaadu; kunis yaada rakkoo yeroo ammaa jirus dhiphisa. Kanneen yaada kana qabaniis marii bu’a qabeessa gufachiisuufi dhaabbilee teknooloojii gurguddaan to’annoo caalatti argachuu danda’u jechuun yaada qaban jiru. Hinton, hojii isaa Google irratti dhiisee, balaa intalliigensii artifishaalaa arge dubbachuuf carraaqaa jira. Garuu, namootni ogummaa isaa keessaa hunduu yaada isaa hin faana hin deeman. Akka fakkeenya biraattis, Yoshua Bengio, hayyuu beekamaa fi qama guddicha, rakkoolee intalliigensii artifishaalaa, keessumaa waanta hojjatame guutumaan guutuutti hin beekamne ('black box') jedhu irratti cimina kenna. article_content: BOISE, Idaho — A federal judge has temporarily blocked Idaho's 'abortion trafficking' law from being enforced while a lawsuit challenges its constitutionality. In her ruling issued Wednesday, U.S. District Magistrate Debora K. Grasham wrote, 'This lawsuit is not about the right to an abortion. It is about much more. Namely, long-standing and well recognized fundamental rights of freedom of speech, expression, due process, and parental rights. These are not competing rights, nor are they at odds.' Abortion is banned in Idaho at all stages of pregnancy. The law, enacted in May, aims to prevent minors from obtaining abortions in other states where the procedure is legal, without their parents' permission. Under the law, anyone who helps a minor who is not their child arrange an out-of-state abortion can be charged with a felony, although they can defend themselves in court by showing the minor had parental permission. Supporters call it an 'abortion trafficking' ban, while opponents argue it is an unconstitutional restriction on interstate travel and free speech. Two advocacy groups and an attorney who works with sexual assault victims sued Idaho and Attorney General Raul Labrador earlier this year. Nampa attorney Lourdes Matsumoto, the Northwest Abortion Access Fund, and the Indigenous Idaho Alliance often assist minors seeking abortions. They state in the lawsuit that the law is so vague they cannot determine which actions are legal and that it violates the First Amendment right to free expression. They also argue the law infringes on the Fourth Amendment right to travel between states and within Idaho. Judge Grasham agreed there is no court-protected right of intra-state travel under current Idaho law, dismissing that part of the suit. However, she allowed the other three claims to proceed, noting that helping minors is, for the plaintiffs, an expression of their core beliefs supporting reproductive options. Grasham clarified she was not prioritizing free expression or due process over parental rights, stating these rights have coexisted for decades and can continue to do so. 'The state can criminalize certain conduct within its own borders, such as abortion, kidnapping, and human trafficking. But the state cannot create a statute that restricts speech and expression from a viewpoint it disagrees with under the pretense of parental rights,' she wrote. Recently, prosecutors in eastern Idaho charged a woman and her son with second-degree kidnapping, alleging they transported the son's minor girlfriend out of state for an abortion. Prosecutors did not use the 'abortion trafficking' law in this case, saying the charges were for intending to conceal the girl from her parents. The woman's defense attorney did not immediately respond to a call for comment. The son's court file was not available online, and it is unclear if the case against him is ongoing.

article_content: On Tuesday, Japan said it will transfer three Australian anti-whaling activists to Australian authorities after they boarded a Japanese vessel in Antarctic waters to protest whale hunting. These activists, part of an environmental group, got onto a Japanese patrol ship supporting annual whaling operations. Detained and questioned by Japanese officials, they are set to be released without charges, according to a spokesperson at Japan’s Foreign Ministry who requested anonymity.  Japanese authorities emphasized that the activists were non-violent and had no past involvement in destructive acts against the whaling fleet. The patrol ship is considered vital for the continuation of Japan’s whaling mission.  Australia’s attorney-general, Nicola Roxon, acknowledged her country’s strong opposition to Japan’s whale hunts but stated that since the incident was outside Australian waters, Australia's jurisdiction did not apply. Australian diplomats meanwhile worked to make sure the activists were treated safely.  Japan maintains its annual whale hunt—despite an international ban—by claiming a scientific research exemption. This continues to trigger confrontations with environmental groups like Sea Shepherd, resulting in ship clashes, detained activists, and ongoing global controversy.  In response, Japan has formally asked Australia to prevent further incidents of activist boardings. Video released by Sea Shepherd shows the three activists—Geoffrey Owen Tuxworth, Simon Peterffy, and Glen Pendlebury—from Forest Rescue Australia, climbing onto the Japanese vessel from a small boat. Sea Shepherd called the men 'prisoners,' saying they attempted to stop the hunt.  Such actions are not new. In 2008, two Sea Shepherd members boarded a Japanese ship and were released. In 2010, New Zealander Pete Bethune boarded the Shonan Maru #2, was arrested, tried in Tokyo, spent five months in prison, and received a suspended sentence.  Report by Kyung Lah, CNN.

She also urged women in the music industry to prioritize their mental health and maintain their spirituality, highlighting the value of inner strength.

Regarding her participation in the MTV Base reality show 'Inside Life: The New Wave,' Liya shared that viewers will see her authentic self—not only as an artiste, but also as a daughter and sister. She pointed out that the show will showcase her genuine emotions, whether she is happy, sad, uncomfortable, or stubborn, emphasizing authenticity and originality. In addition to her music, Liya mentioned her love for fashion, sports like football and badminton, and her appreciation for nature.

Reflecting on her past experience working with Nigerian singer Davido, Liya described it as amazing, expressing heartfelt gratitude for his support and the platform he provided. She credits Davido with helping her enter the spotlight and expanding her network within the industry.

Liya's latest single, 'My Skin,' was inspired by her desire to encourage women to love and appreciate themselves. She described the song as a fresh and authentic sound.

article_content: Dhiraj Relli, Managing Director and CEO of HDFC Securities, draws from over 20 years of experience in banking to offer key investment advice. He likens the equity markets to a vibrant stage with dramatic highs and lows, stressing the need for vision in navigating this landscape. Relli’s guidance for wealth accumulation includes starting early, investing consistently, setting clear goals, and achieving a solid understanding before investing. Early and regular investments harness the power of compounding, turning small amounts into significant wealth. He emphasizes that time in the market matters more than timing the market, and early starters learn to manage risk effectively. Relli recommends aligning investments with specific life objectives—whether for retirement, a home, travel, or education—and cautions against chasing high, short-term returns. He highlights the importance of knowledge, encouraging investors to learn the basics before entering stocks, mutual funds, or real estate. Building money management and asset allocation skills is also crucial. Diversification across assets—such as stocks, bonds, mutual funds, and gold—can help optimize returns and lower risk, and even within each asset class, spreading investments is advised. As investors gain experience, they may consider narrowing diversification while maintaining safeguards. Relli warns against unsolicited advice and urges investors to seek guidance from trusted sources when uncertain. He also advises limiting exposure to electronic media and specific recommendations, noting such advice may not suit every individual’s goals and risk tolerance. Instead, investors should consult experts as needed, ensuring their strategies are sound. He cautions against relying solely on past performance and succumbing to FOMO (fear of missing out). DIY investors should not assume historical returns will repeat, as outperformers in the recent past may be due for correction, and careful balancing is needed for long-term success. Insurance, Relli notes, is a financial cornerstone, not just a safety net. He advises securing proper health and life insurance coverage, increasing it over time to offset inflation and income growth. Investors should make use of digital tools for research, trading, and portfolio tracking, while remaining wary of sponsored or biased information. He suggests regular reviews to adjust asset allocations, replace underperformers, and rebalance portfolios to maximize returns and minimize risks. In summary, Relli believes following these principles leads to a better investing experience, both in terms of returns and effective risk management. Additionally, the Indian IPO market saw a very active week, with investors committing ₹2.6 lakh crore to five issues seeking ₹7,380 crore in total. The government has instructed social media and internet companies to update their terms of use within seven days, making users aware of the consequences of sharing prohibited content such as deepfakes or child sexual abuse material, as stated by Rajeev Chandrasekhar, Minister of State for Electronics and IT. In the floriculture sector, there is growing demand for locally grown exotic flowers—such as orchids, carnations, tulips, and nargis—driven by increased domestic production and regulations limiting imports. article_content: Every known ant species will soon be documented in high-definition 3D images. A team of U.S. scientists, led by Dr. Brian Fisher from the California Academy of Sciences, is traveling to museums worldwide to catalogue detailed photographs of ants in their collections. This project marks the first time researchers have captured such fine detail of ants using advanced microscopic imaging techniques. These new methods provide scientists with an unprecedented view into ants' anatomy. On their 'world ant tour,' the team is compiling their images into a database called Antweb, a resource expected to be invaluable for insect researchers everywhere. Dr. Fisher told the BBC: 'Our goal is to image 10,000 a year.' So far, the team has photographed 8,000 ant species from U.S. museum collections, with a goal of reaching up to 30,000 species. Currently, they are visiting the Natural History Museum in London to document more than 6,000 species housed there. At each museum, several specimens of each species are imaged, including queens, soldiers, and workers to ensure a comprehensive database. Each preserved ant undergoes dozens of highly-magnified photographs at different focus levels. This data is processed by a computer to create a 3D image, enabling scientists to study each ant's anatomy in unprecedented detail. Dr. Fisher explained: 'You can zoom in and see fine hairs, the eyes—all of this detail. Under a microscope, these features are not all in focus, so this is the first time I can see an ant in 3D.' The Antweb imaging archive will be open to anyone, anywhere, at any time, allowing the public to explore these scientific discoveries.

Projektiin kun yeroo jalqabaatiif saayintistoonni hodhaa suuraan bal’inaan, tarsiimoo suuraa mikroskopii ammayyaa fayyadamuun, haala cimaa irratti galmeessaniiru. article_content: Employee engagement is widely recognized as a key factor in organizational success, yet many leaders still find it challenging to address. Research highlights the significant impact of leadership, with 84% of U.S. workers identifying poorly trained managers as a major source of stress and diminished performance, according to a 2020 Society for Human Resource Management (SHRM) survey. Ineffective communication, lack of managerial involvement, and insufficient attention to employee well-being often contribute to reduced productivity and disengagement. These issues can impede an organization's progress. Gallup's August 2023 employee engagement survey found only 33% of U.S. employees are engaged, while 16% are actively disengaged. Since 2001, Gallup data show engagement rates reached a peak of just 36% in 2020. These engagement statistics are more than numbers—they indicate deeper issues. When employees feel uninspired or overlooked, productivity drops, which can negatively affect a company's performance and long-term resilience. What can leaders do to foster engagement? 1. Foster Purpose and Recognize Individual Strengths: Gallup surveys suggest a sense of purpose and recognition of unique talents encourage engagement. Leaders should align employee strengths with organizational goals and create opportunities for employees to excel—through project assignments, team collaborations, or similar avenues. 2. Make Communication a Priority: Open, transparent communication builds trust. Leaders should routinely share organizational goals, performance data, and strategic updates. Equally, they must encourage two-way dialogue, listen to feedback, and maintain open-door policies. This approach creates a culture where all voices are valued. 3. Invest in Professional Development: Providing opportunities for career growth not only upgrades skills but also builds loyalty. Options include workshops, online courses, and support for further education. Mentorship programs, such as those at PWC, Caterpillar, and Bain & Company, benefit both junior and senior staff by fostering learning and leadership development. 4. Recognize and Reward Performance: Public praise, performance bonuses, and structured incentive programs motivate employees. Setting clear milestones linked to promotions or salary increases encourages sustained engagement and recognizes achievements. 5. Balance Workloads to Prevent Burnout: Extended periods of overwhelming work can result in burnout. Leaders should monitor workloads and redistribute tasks or resources when necessary. Tools like Jira, Resource Guru, and ClickUp can help track workloads and capacity. Encouraging regular breaks, vacation time, and limiting work after hours supports a healthier work-life balance. Leaders must demonstrate commitment to well-being, modeling healthy boundaries by taking time off and respecting after-hours limits. This helps employees feel comfortable doing the same, reducing the pressure to overwork. Boosting employee engagement may seem daunting but is achievable with deliberate leadership strategies. Targeted initiatives and authentic changes can foster environments where employees are motivated and organizations succeed. Engagement is not just a metric—it’s fundamental to business success.
translated_content: Hirmaannaa hojjettootaa bu’uura injifannoo dhaabbilee ta’u isaa ni beekama, garuu hooggantoonni baay'een rakkoo kana furuun ulfaataa ta'a. Qorannoowwan aangoo hooggantoota irratti dhiibbaa guddaa qabaachuu agarsiisu; %84 hojjettoota Ameerikaa bara 2020 (SHRM) keessatti bulchitoota gahumsa hin qabne akka madda rakkoo fi hanqina milkaa’inaatti dubbatu. Walqunnamtii dhabuu, hirmaannaa bulchitootaa dhabuu fi gaafii jireenya hojjettootaa irratti xiyyeeffannoo dhabuu sadarkaa hojii gad cabsuu fi hirmaannaa xiqqeessuuf gumaacha. Kunis guddina dhaabbaticha gufachiisa. Sakatta’iinsa Gallup, Hagayya 2023, keessa hojjettoonni Ameerikaa %33 qofaatu hirmaataa, %16 immoo hirmaachuu didu. Akka odeeffannoo Gallup bara 2001 asittis, sadarkaan hirmaannaa bara 2020 qofatti %36 gaheera. Lakkofsowwan kun dhugaa bu'aa jabduu dha. Hojjettoonni yeroo miira hin qabne ykn laamshifaman, milkaa'inni isaanii ni hir'ata, kunis bu'a qabeessummaa fi jiraachuu dhaabbataa irratti dhiibbaa bu'usu danda'a. Hoggantoonni maal gochuu danda’u hirmaannaa cimsuuf? 1. Kaayyoo fi dandeettii dhuunfaa cimsuu: Sakatta’iinsi Gallup, kaayyoo fi beekkamtii dandeettii adda addaa argachuun hirmaannaa dabala. Hoggantoonni dandeettii hojjettootaa waliin hojii dhaabbataa walitti hidhanii, carraa hojii dandeettii isaanii ittiin mul’isan akka argatan gochuun ni barbaachisa. 2. Walqunnamtii ifaa fi cimaan: Walqunnamtii qulqulluun amantaa dagaagaa. Hoggantoonni yerootti kaayyoo hojii, gabaasa bu'aa fi jijjiirraa waliin qooduu qabu. Deebii fi marii lamaan jajjabeessuu, fi qophii bal'ina gara hojjettootaatti qabaachuun, gahee gumaachaa. Kunis haala hunda hirmaachisu uuma. 3. Cimsuu guddina dandeettii: Carraa gabbina ogummaa kennuun dandeettii fi amanamummaa ni guddisa. Leenjii, kursii online, deeggarsa barnootaa kennuu fi wal harkaa fuudhu (mentorship) PWC, Caterpillar fi Bain & Company akka fakkeenyaatti kennu. Kun hojjettoota haaraa fi kan yeroo dheeraa turan waliin barnoota fi hoggantummaa irratti gargaara. 4. Milkaa'ina beekamtii fi kennaa: Milkaa'inni yeroon beekamaa fi badhaasa, hojii cimaa irratti dursa kennu. Badhaasa, ol-ka’umsa mindaa, fi sochii hojii gara fuula duraaf mallattoo kennu, hirmaannaa jajjabeessaa fi milkaa’ina agarsiisa. 5. Dhaabbata hojii fi hir’ina dadhabbii: Hojjiin gurguddaan yeroo dheeraa irratti xiyyeeffachuun dadhabbii qaba. Hooggantoonni hojii qooduu fi bal’ina rakkinaa ilaalu qabu. Jira, Resource Guru fi ClickUp fayyadamiinsa hojii ilaaluuf gargaara. Boqonnaa yeroo yerootti fi hojii sa’aatii ala keessatti daangessuun fayyaaf barbaachisaa. Hoggantoonni mirga fayyaa hojjettootaa akka eegan agarsiisuu, yeroo boqonnaa fudhachuu fi hojii ala sa’atii boqonnaa hojjachuu irraa of qusachuu qabu. Kun hojjettoonni ofiif hodaa ta’uu fi hojii isaanii itti fufuuf yaaddoo akka hin qabne gargaara. Hirmaannaa hojjettootaa ol kaasuun ulfaataa fakkaatullee karoora murteeffamaa fi hojimaata hooggantootaan ni danda’ama. Karoora ifaa fi jijjiirrama dhugaa ta'een, haala hojjettoonni hirmaatan fi milkaa’an uumuu ni danda’ama. Hirmaannaan hojjettootaa lakkobsaa qofa osoo hin taane bu’uura bu’aa hojii dha.

article_content: The British Monarchy is expanding its digital footprint by launching an official Facebook Page on Monday. Unlike personal profiles, this Page will represent the royal family collectively. This step builds on previous social media ventures: the monarchy set up a YouTube channel in 2007, joined Twitter in 2009, and launched a Flickr photostream earlier this year. Buckingham Palace, Clarence House, and the Royal Collection are overseeing the Page, which will share updates like news, links, videos, and photographs—mostly about Queen Elizabeth II, Prince Charles, Prince William, and Prince Harry. Facebook users who 'Like' the Page can get news from the Royal Family directly in their feeds. Followers can also track official royal events on the associated Court Circular Page.

Kun hojiiwwan isaanii marsaa dhumaa irratti kan itti fufan: mootummaan Ingilizii YouTube bara 2007 irratti fe'e, bara 2009 Twitter irratti makame, akkasumas bara kana keessa Flickr irratti suuraawwan isaanii fe'e. Buckingham Palace, Clarence House fi Royal Collection fuula kana to'atu; odeeffannoo, linkii, viidiyoo fi suuraalee dursanii kan qoodu — kanneen hedduun isaaniis Queen Elizabeth II, Prince Charles, Prince William fi Prince Harry irratti xiyyeeffata. Namoonni Facebook irratti fuula kana 'Like' gootan waraqaa odeeffannoo maatii mootii gara feed isaanii guutuu argachu danda'u. Delhi's air quality remained in the 'very poor' category on Monday morning, registering an Air Quality Index (AQI) of 310 according to the System of Air Quality and Weather Forecasting And Research (SAFAR-India). At 8:30 am, Delhi recorded this high pollution level, reaffirmed by Central Pollution Control Board (CPCB) data at 7:00 am citing Anand Vihar at 361, Alipur at 368, Ashok Vihar at 342, ITO at 318, and RK Puram at 344—all indicating 'very poor' air quality.

This comes a day after Delhi lifted restrictions imposed under stage 4 of the Graded Response Action Plan (GRAP) as air quality showed signs of improvement. Environment Minister Gopal Rai on Sunday advised residents to remain vigilant, as GRAP stages 1, 2, and 3 restrictions are still in place to tackle ongoing air pollution. He noted, “There has been a constant improvement in air quality over the last two days, with today’s AQI reaching 290. However, we need to stay alert to maintain these gains.” Rai reminded citizens that the AQI had improved to 215 before Diwali but worsened again due to subsequent carelessness.

With the air quality improving over the weekend, the Commission for Air Quality Management (CAQM) revoked GRAP 4 restrictions on Saturday. This move allowed trucks and buses—except older BS-3 petrol and BS-4 diesel vehicles—to re-enter the city, and ongoing construction activity on permitted projects to resume. Minister Gopal Rai clarified that bans remain for BS-3 petrol and BS-4 diesel vehicles, and only more modern trucks and vehicles are allowed. Additionally, linear projects like roads and flyovers, as well as national importance initiatives, have resumed, while activities such as demolition, structural construction, and certain material handling remain prohibited.

Rai also noted that certain activities—like using vehicles on unpaved roads, running concrete batching plants, tile and flooring operations, and mining—continue to be restricted. He stressed the importance of distinguishing between GRAP 3 and GRAP 4 limitations, as only the latter have been relaxed for now. Earlier, a special six-member task force was created under the Environment Special Secretary to monitor and ensure proper application of the GRAP rules.

Sa'aatii 8:30 irratti, Delhi dhaabbata qilleensa kana galmaa'e, akkasumas ragaan CPCB sa'aatii 7:00 irratti bahe Anand Vihar 361, Alipur 368, Ashok Vihar 342, ITO 318, fi RK Puram 344 jechuun hunda 'hamaa' ta'uu agarsiisa.

Kun booda daangaan GRAP-4 kan haala qilleensa fooyya'aa dhufe jedhamee kaafameen wal qabata. Ministirri Naannoo Gopal Rai Dilbata lammiileen akka itti fufinsaan of-eeggannoo godhan, sababiin isaas GRAP kutaa 1,2,3 ammas hojirra jiru jedhe. Gama biraatiin, Rai hojiiwwan garaagaraa akka konkolaataa karaa kuduraa hin jirreef, batching plant, hojimaata tile fi flooring gurguddaan, fi waraana qonnaa (mining) irra uggurri itti fufeera jedhanii beeksisan. Kana booda, gareen addaa miseensota jaha qaban Environment Special Secretary jalatti godhamee, sirrii hojiirra oolmaa GRAP to’achuuf hundeeffamee jira.

article_content: A 51-year-old Australian woman may face the death penalty in Malaysia after being arrested for allegedly smuggling drugs. Authorities reportedly found her with 1.5kg of methamphetamine, also known as ice, during a stopover at Kuala Lumpur airport. The woman, believed to be a mother of four, was traveling from Shanghai to Melbourne, according to Seven News. This arrest comes soon after the release of 22-year-old Australian Kalynda Davis, who had been detained in China earlier this month on drug smuggling charges. Ms. Davis and New Zealander Peter Gardner were both accused of attempting to smuggle methamphetamine from China to Australia and faced the possibility of execution by firing squad. While Ms. Davis returned home to Sydney earlier this week, Mr. Gardner remains in custody in China. The 51-year-old woman is expected to appear in court on Sunday.

article_content: Rangers secured a place in the League Cup quarter-finals with a determined victory over Falkirk at Westfield Stadium. The match saw early drama when Falkirk's Rory Loy scored in the fifth minute, only for a quick own goal by Owain Tudur Jones to level the score minutes later. Dean Shiels, who had missed two good chances earlier, capitalized on Nicky Law's clever headed through-ball to put Rangers ahead, firing past Falkirk goalkeeper Jamie MacDonald. The game remained lively, with both teams creating opportunities, but it was Ian Black who confirmed Rangers’ win, sending a spectacular 25-yard shot into the top corner in the final moments. Manager Ally McCoist made two changes to his line-up following a recent draw against Alloa, with Lee Wallace and Dean Shiels replacing injured players Lewis Macleod and Nicky Clark. Notably, 18-year-old Ryan Hardie made his debut for Rangers. Despite Falkirk’s energetic start and several dangerous attacks, Rangers' clinical finishing assured their progression, delighting the 5,259 fans in attendance. The victory was viewed as just reward for a resilient performance in a fast-paced and engaging match.

Dean Shiels, carraa lama moggaafate booda, dabarsoo mataa Nicky Law irraa argateen goolii galche, kubbaa Jamie MacDonald, goolkeetti Falkirk, darbise. Eddie Redmayne, acclaimed for his role as Stephen Hawking in 'The Theory Of Everything,' is anticipated to win numerous awards in 2015. His first accolade has already arrived—celebrating his fashion, not acting. At 32, the British actor has been named GQ magazine’s Best Dressed Man for his sharp suits and bold style. Redmayne, who wed Hannah Bagshawe last month, outperformed fellow actors Benedict Cumberbatch and Jamie Dornan for the honor, awarded by GQ staff and industry experts. 

Eddie merits this recognition, even if he has occasionally misjudged his wardrobe. He’s perfected the black tie look at the Breakthrough Prize Awards in California and made a statement with a blue checked suit at the UK premiere of 'The Theory Of Everything.' Redmayne shows adaptability—teaming a red jumper with smart trousers, glasses, and posing with director James Marsh and co-star Felicity Jones. Casual affairs see him in denim jackets and T-shirts at the Toronto Film Festival, or exuding 'grandad chic' by pairing a cardigan and grey suit with a red handkerchief. 

He’s sported blue velvet jackets, appeared in a brown suit on 'The Graham Norton Show'—boosting his reputation—and embraced high fashion in a Burberry trench coat alongside model Cara Delevingne after joining the brand. Together with his wife Hannah, he stood out at New York’s Costume Institute Gala. In Turin, he layered up with a navy jacket or opted for an open shirt at the city’s film festival. 

Redmayne competently refreshes classic looks, adding snazzy ties or vibrant colors to his signature suits, and rocks relaxed outfits like a striped shirt and blue trousers at Wimbledon. Yet, not every experiment succeeds—his turquoise suit at Toronto and a retro Miami Vice jacket raised eyebrows, while past photos show his youthful fashion stumbles. Nevertheless, his consistent style ensures he’s recognized as one of the best dressed men.

Hospitals in the United States are facing an increase in violent incidents, putting healthcare workers, patients, and visitors at risk. In Concord, New Hampshire, a security guard was shot and killed in a psychiatric hospital lobby, after which a state trooper fatally shot the gunman. In another case in Vineland, New Jersey, a patient fatally shot himself at Inspira Medical Center, nearly injuring a nurse and leading to a lockdown. These examples illustrate a wider, escalating trend of violence in medical facilities.

According to the American Hospital Association (AHA), healthcare workers now experience more workplace violence and injury than any other sector. Since the onset of the COVID-19 pandemic, 44% of nurses have reported more physical violence, and 68% have observed increased verbal abuse. The American College of Emergency Physicians found that 80% of emergency doctors believe violence in emergency departments has negatively impacted patient care, with almost half experiencing assaults themselves. National Nurses United documented that workplace violence more than doubled from March 2021 to April 2022. This ongoing violence results in emotional distress, burnout, and challenges to safe patient care.

While hospitals are traditionally seen as safe havens, high-stress conditions—like those in emergency and intensive care units—can trigger aggression from patients, visitors, and even staff. To address these risks, hospitals are encouraged to reinforce security with limited public access, ID checks, security screenings, surveillance cameras, and controlled entry to sensitive areas. Routine training on de-escalation techniques and violence response, as well as regular preparedness drills—including active shooter simulations—are also key measures.

Verbal abuse remains a significant challenge: around 24% of doctors have faced occupational distress from harassment. Studies reveal that incivility and threats can disrupt medical care. Ensuring safety means fostering respectful environments and clear protocols for preventing and responding to violence.

A comprehensive response—including strong leadership, staff support, and community involvement—is needed to restore hospitals as secure places of healing.

article_content: Editor's Note: In honor of Hispanic Heritage Month, World Cafe is taking listeners on a musical journey across Latin America. Each weekday from Sept. 15 to Oct. 15, we'll feature the music of a different Latin American country with a curated playlist, highlighting essential tracks, new voices, and unexpected gems. You might be wondering why Brazil is part of this celebration, especially since Portuguese is Brazil's official language and, by strict definition, Brazilians are not considered Hispanic. The term 'Hispanic' was introduced by the U.S. government during Lyndon Johnson's administration in 1968 for this commemoration, but it doesn't capture the full scope of Latin American cultural heritage. As I've worked on these playlists with World Cafe's Latin Roots correspondent, Byron Gonzalez, one thing is clear: the musical connections across Latin America are undeniable. Rhythms from the Caribbean have influenced Central America and beyond. Argentine rock gave rise to 'rock en español.' The sounds of the Amazon rainforest have inspired artists throughout Bolivia, Peru, Ecuador, Colombia, and Brazil. With such rich cultural exchange, we couldn't leave out Brazil—the birthplace of samba, bossa nova, and more. This playlist features Brazilian legends like João Gilberto, Antônio Carlos Jobim, and Tim Maia, as well as newer acts reimagining classic Brazilian rhythms, such as ANAVITÓRIA and São Paulo band PLUMA. We’ve also included a standout track from Pabllo Vittar's 2020 album, '111.' Back in 2018, Vittar became the first drag queen to win a Latin Grammy for 'Sua Cara,' a collaboration with Major Lazer and Anitta. Another highlight is 'ESSA RUA É MINHA' by Indigenous hip-hop artist and activist Kaê Guajajara, who recently released a new album called Zahytata. Enjoy this celebration of Brazilian music, and be sure to visit again tomorrow to see where World Cafe goes next!

article_content: ‘Eternal’ is a name I chose for myself, as I never liked my given Christian name. My career as a composer began when I worked as a studio assistant in Enugu State. I initially visited the studio to begin a music album, but music production quickly drew me in. While recording my own songs, I discovered a talent for songwriting, which led me to write songs for others as well. I am grateful to the late Obinna Onwe, owner of the now-closed Veto Edge Studios, who mentored me and provided space for me to grow. Derek Osonwa, also known as Dekumzy, saw my gift for songwriting and encouraged me to develop it. My journey into soundtrack production began with Reemy Jez Productions. With a recommendation from Arinzechukwu Obiorah, I moved to Imo State to work as an in-house producer. My first significant project was producing a 15-track soundtrack for the film 'Akwa Eke.' I went on to create soundtracks for movies such as 'Through the Fire' and 'Ultimate Sacrifice.' Reemy Jez introduced me to the late Ayo, owner of Ayo Movies, where I produced soundtracks for films like 'Under 17,' 'Tomato Jos,' and 'Oku na Agba Ozara.' After returning to Lagos, I collaborated with Rukky Sanda on productions such as 'In Her Shoes,' 'What’s Within Dark,' 'Lovelorn,' and others. I haven’t worked on any soundtracks recently, but I have a documentary project coming up. Theatre has always been a passion of mine. It was my first choice when applying to university. While waiting for admission, I studied Fine and Applied Arts at a polytechnic, a course I enjoyed thoroughly. Later at university, I finally experienced stage performance, something that always fascinated me. In 2015, I auditioned for ‘Magic of the Musicals’ and was cast as Eric, the male lead in ‘Phantom of the Opera.’ That period was very rewarding, and I would gladly take part in such performances again. My first on-stage experience was with an acappella gospel group called 'Divine Roses' at the Institute of Management and Technology, Enugu. Within a month of joining, I became the lead vocalist. During a church performance, my nerves almost overwhelmed me, but after singing, I felt truly alive and knew I belonged on stage. Currently, I focus more on creative arts and design. I have long been passionate about poetry, fine arts, crafts, graphic and textile design, acting, and music. In school, my major was graphic design. The idea for my clothing line came as I sorted through my graphic designs and imagined them on clothes. Initially, I didn’t know how to print on garments, but the desire to see my art worn drove me to learn.

article_content: A new study suggests that taking just 2,000 extra steps each day can reduce the risk of heart attack and stroke by 8%, especially for those at higher risk. The research, published in The Lancet and led by Dr. Thomas Yates from the Diabetes Research Unit at Leicester University, found that this modest increase in physical activity—equivalent to about 20 minutes of additional walking daily—can offer significant benefits. The study followed 9,306 adults from 40 countries who had impaired glucose tolerance or other factors putting them at risk for heart disease. Participants wore pedometers to track their daily steps over a year. Results showed that people who increased their daily steps by 2,000 saw their risk of cardiovascular events, such as heart attacks and strokes, drop by 8%. Those who managed 4,000 extra steps per day—about 40 minutes of walking—reduced their risk by 16-20%, an effect comparable to that of statin medications. Dr. Yates emphasized that while statins target cholesterol with some possible side effects, increased walking offers broader health benefits. These improvements were seen regardless of participants’ initial activity levels or body weight. Experts like Dr. Richard Elliot from Diabetes UK and Julie Ward from the British Heart Foundation highlighted the importance of regular activity, particularly for people at risk of type 2 diabetes or heart disease. While the study does have limitations—including missing data and the need for direct intervention trials—it strengthens the case for integrating more movement into daily routines. Health professionals recommend 150 minutes of moderate exercise weekly, which can be broken down into manageable chunks—like a brisk 20-minute walk during lunch.

Qorannoon kun, kan The Lancet keessatti maxxanfamee fi Dr. Thomas Yates, Kutaa Qorannoo Diyaabiiti, Yuunivarsiitii Leicester irraa hoogganan, baay’ina xiqqaa sochiin guyyaa—daqiiqaa 20 dabalataa deemuu—faayidaa cimaa qabu akka ta’e mul’iseera. Qorannoon namoota 9,306 biyyoota 40 irraa, kanneen sukkaara gara diyaabiitii geessu ykn rakkina onnee fi dhiibbaa dhiigaa qabu irratti gaggeeffame. Hirmaattonni qorannoo guyyaa guyyaatti tarkaanfii isaanii waggaa tokkoof kaasuudhaan deemsisuun to'ataman. Namoonni tarkaanfii isaanii guyyaa 2,000 dabalatanii deeman carraa dhibee onnee fi dhiibbaa dhiigaa (akka onnee cufamuu fi dhiibbaa dhiigaa cimaa) 8% hir’isiisaniiru. Dr. Yates akka jedhanitti, statins kolestreelii hir’isuun fayyadu; garuu rakkoo biroo ni qaba, yeroo sochiin qaamaa, faayidaalee bal’inaan fayyadu. Fooyya’iinsi kun hirmaattoota kamirraayyuu, regardless of qaama isaanii yookan sochii jalqaba irraa, ni mul’ata. Ogeeyyiin akka Dr. Richard Elliot (Diabetes UK) fi Julie Ward (British Heart Foundation) sochii qaamaa namoota carraa diyaabiiti fi rakkoo onnee qabanirratti murteessaa ta’uu mirkaneessan. Qorannoon dabalataa fi ragaaa dabalataa barbaachisu tilmaameera; haata’uyyuu malee, qorannoo kanaan akkuma rakkina keessaa, sochii qaamaa dabalachuun tajaajilawwan fayyaa akka danda’amu agarsiisaa. Ogeessoonni fayyaa daqiiqaa 150 tajaajila qaamaa giddu galeessaa torbanii qofatti akka godhamu gorsan, kun immoo bakka tokkoon ol deemuu, akka daqiiqaa 20 saffisaan socho’u yookaan irree markaa keessatti qoodamuun ni danda’ama.
