article_content: The European Commission is urging TikTok and X (formerly Twitter) to intensify their actions against hate speech and misinformation. Věra Jourová, the EU vice president for the digital economy, recently held meetings with TikTok CEO Shou Zi Chew and X’s head of global government affairs, Nick Pickles. Jourová described the discussions as constructive, but noted that X, in particular, needs to do more to comply with the Digital Services Act (DSA). The DSA, which took effect in the EU in August, requires platforms to better identify and address disinformation and hate speech. Jourová also expressed concerns about the presence of pro-Hamas content on these platforms following the October attacks on Israel. The EU, alongside the US, considers Hamas a terrorist group. The Israel-Hamas war has brought greater attention to how social media contributes to the spread of misinformation. For instance, a video allegedly showing an Israeli soldier revealing Hamas' tunnel system in Gaza was actually a TikTok ad for an airsoft club in Israel, according to fact-checkers. Jourová also criticized X for having too few staff proficient in European languages and insufficiently preparing for the upcoming EU elections. She highlighted that X closed its Brussels office—responsible for EU compliance—shortly after Elon Musk’s acquisition. Theo Bertram, TikTok’s VP for Public Policy in Europe, told Insider the company values ongoing engagement with EU officials and detailed TikTok’s efforts to enhance safety and regulatory compliance. He mentioned recent developments with Project Clover, which focuses on elevating data security in Europe. X did not respond to requests for comment.

article_content: Wimbledon champion Marketa Vondrousova has secured a spot at the WTA Finals, joined by French Open runner-up Karolina Muchova and Tunisian world number seven Ons Jabeur, according to the women's tennis governing body on Friday. They complete the singles field for the season-ending tournament in Cancun, Mexico, alongside the already-qualified world number one Aryna Sabalenka, four-time major winner Iga Swiatek, US Open champion Coco Gauff, Elena Rybakina, and Jessica Pegula. The WTA Finals feature the top eight singles players and doubles teams globally, and return to Mexico after one year, with the 2021 edition previously held in Guadalajara. Gauff and world number four Pegula will participate in singles and then team up in the doubles competition. Former Wimbledon champion Rybakina becomes the first player from Kazakhstan to qualify in singles. The WTA Finals are scheduled from October 29 to November 5.

article_content:
Juan Martin Del Potro delayed Roger Federer's bid to qualify for the ATP World Tour Finals by defeating the Swiss star in the final of his hometown tournament in Basel. As the third seed, Federer needed a victory on Sunday to secure his spot in the season-ending event in London next month for a 12th straight year, but he fell short in a competitive three-set match. Top seed Del Potro, a strong contender for the British event, won 7-6, 2-6, 6-4 in two hours and 20 minutes. This denied Federer a sixth Basel title and echoed Del Potro’s 2012 win over him in the same event. 

The Argentine claimed a closely fought first set, surviving an exchange of service breaks before taking the tiebreak 7-3. Federer, who recently parted ways with coach Paul Annacone after a difficult 2013 season, responded by winning the second set with two service breaks. However, in the deciding set, Federer lost an early service game with two double faults and was unable to recover, allowing former US Open champion Del Potro to clinch his fourth title of the year. 

"I'm sorry again to beat you here," Del Potro said at the trophy presentation. "He's the hero here and for me, my biggest inspiration. You make history at every tournament you play. I'm proud to play in the same era as you."

The 32-year-old Federer now must beat South Africa’s Kevin Anderson or Russia’s Mikhail Youzhny in his second-round match at the Paris Masters next week to reach the finals. A win would allow him to match Ivan Lendl’s record for consecutive appearances at the season finale, where Federer would seek a seventh title, having last won in 2011 and lost in the 2012 final to Novak Djokovic.

In other action, Mikhail Youzhny showcased strong form ahead of Paris, defeating top seed and three-time defending champion David Ferrer of Spain 6-3, 7-5 in the ATP tournament final in Valencia.

Del Potro, kan sadarkaa duraa irratti argamu, tapha sadiin yeroo sa’aatii lamaa fi daqiiqaa 20’tti (7-6, 2-6, 6-4) injifate. Del Potro yeroo badhaasa fudhatu, "Ammas asitti si mo’uun na gaabbisiisa." jedhe. "Inni asitti gootaa, anaaf immoo kaka’umsa guddaa. Tapha kamittuu seenaa tolchaa jirta. Yeroo kee waliin tapha taphachuu koo nan boonadha."

Federrer, kan umuriin isaa waggaa 32, torbee dhufu tapha Paris Masters marsaa lammaffaa irratti Kevin Anderson ykn Mikhail Youzhny mo’uu qaba. Mo’inni isa kana, galma tapha xumura waggaa walitti fufaa Ivan Lendl waliin walfakkaatu fiduuf carraaqa. Akkasumas, Federaarri bakka tokkoffaa irratti mo’ata torbaffaa isaa dhumaa banuu danda’a, isa dhumaa bara 2011 galmeessuu isaatiin, bara 2012 ammoo Novak Djokovic irratti kufee ture.

Akka taphni biroo ammoo, Mikhail Youzhny argannoo cimaa Paris dura agarsiisera. Valencia keessatti David Ferrer, kan sadarkaa duraa fi mo’ataa sadiin walitti fufee ture, 6-3, 7-5 irratti mo’atee injifate.

article_content: New Delhi: Policy coordination at both global and domestic levels is essential to restore robust, sustainable, balanced, and inclusive growth, Finance Minister Nirmala Sitharaman stated on Monday. She highlighted that the G20 New Delhi Leaders' Declaration stresses the urgency of adopting carefully designed macroeconomic and structural policies to promote equitable growth and reinforce macroeconomic and financial stability. "Under the theme of strong, sustainable, balanced, and inclusive growth, the declaration emphasizes trade, the future of work, and financial inclusion—three key drivers for stimulating growth," Sitharaman said during the webinar's inauguration. She noted that, since the pandemic, the global economy has faced multiple crises, severely affecting growth worldwide. "Although recovery is underway, it remains slow and uneven. Currently, global economic growth is significantly weaker than the pre-pandemic two-decade average of 3.8%. Looking ahead, medium-term growth prospects have deteriorated further," she added. Sitharaman emphasized that the G20 New Delhi Leaders' Declaration, unanimously agreed upon by all G20 nations, addresses several pressing global economic challenges. It also offers policy guidance focused on people-centric principles and trust-based partnerships for the future.

article_content: Hull City will face Arsenal at the Emirates Stadium in the third round of this season’s FA Cup, repeating last season’s final. The draw surprised Hull manager Steve Bruce, who initially believed his team would play at home at the KC Stadium. In last season’s final at Wembley, Arsenal came from two goals down to beat Hull City 3-2 after extra time. The teams were also paired together in the rehearsal draw. Steve Bruce, present at The Deep Aquarium in Hull for the draw, told BBC Sport, ‘We’d been drawn against Arsenal in the rehearsal. Let’s hope it’s as good as last year’s final, which was a great game.’ Hull captain Curtis Davies, who scored in last year’s final, was present and looked forward to the rematch. ‘To be the first out with Arsenal was a shock, but we’re looking forward to giving them a good game and hopefully progressing to the next round,’ Davies said. There was an amusing moment during the official draw when presenter Mark Chapman reminded Bruce that Hull would actually play away, which prompted laughter from Bruce. Aaron Ramsey’s extra-time goal in last season's final secured Arsenal’s victory, making this rematch highly anticipated for both clubs.

Tapha xumura bara darbeetti Wembley irratti, Arsenal goal lama duuba turteetti Hull City 3-2 injifatte yeroo dabalataa booda. Gareen lameenis yeroo leenjii jedhameen wal faana tarreeffamaniiru. Akka tapha xumura bara darbe sana fakkaatee yeroo gaarii nuu haa ta’u.’ jedha. Kapteen Hull, Curtis Davies, kan xumura bara darbeetti galmeesse, bakka taphni itti geggeeffamus turee, wal falmii kanaaf abdii fi gammachuu qaba. ‘Arsenal waliin jalqabaan ba’uu keenya ni dinqisiise, garuu tapha gaarii laachuun gara marsaa itti aanuuf abdii qabna,’ jedha Davies. article_content:
Dundee United’s rising star, 18-year-old Ryan Gauld, has secured a high-profile £3 million transfer to Sporting Lisbon, signing a six-year contract. Gauld arrived in the Portuguese capital on Tuesday, accompanied by his agent John Colquhoun, his father, and Dundee United secretary John Taylor to finalize his move to the Primeira Liga runners-up. After agreeing to personal terms lasting until 2020, Gauld underwent a medical as Sporting Lisbon aimed to complete the deal in time for the club’s 108th anniversary celebrations. Although a few legal formalities remained, sources confirmed the transfer was essentially complete.

The move crowns an impressive season for Gauld, who helped Dundee United finish fourth in the Scottish Premiership and reach the Scottish Cup final, where they lost 2-0 to St Johnstone. His performances attracted scouts from top European clubs including Real Madrid, Roma, Manchester United, and Arsenal. Dundee United had previously extended Gauld’s contract through 2016. Nicknamed “Baby Messi” by teammates—thanks to his style and build similar to Lionel Messi—Gauld made 50 appearances for the club across all competitions, scoring nine goals since his debut in 2012.

Dundee United manager Jackie McNamara expressed a desire to keep Gauld at the club but admitted that the offer was “life-changing” for the young midfielder. He noted, 'There comes a time when a bid is too good to turn down, not just financially but for the player’s own future.' McNamara said Gauld’s opportunity with Sporting Lisbon represented an important next step, adding, 'Professionally, you always want people to get a good opportunity. We have always known people would come in for talent like Ryan, and it was inevitable it would happen.'

Erga qabxii dhuunfaa bara 2020 tti waliigaluun booda, fooyya’iinsa fayyaa gaggeeffamaa ture, Sporting Lisbon immoo waliigaltee itti fufinsa isaa ni mirkaneessu jedhe. Haa ta’u malee, hojiileen seeraa xiqqoon hafanis, maddeen dhiyoo irra deddeebiin waliigalteen kun xumura isaaf jiru jedhan.

Taphni Gauld bara darbe tole, garee isaa waliin Qophaa’ina shampiyoonshippii Siirikaa irratti gara sadarkaa afraffaa geesseera; xumura Scottish Cup irratti immoo St Johnstone’n 2-0 mo’ame. Hiriyyoonni isaa 'Baby Messi' jechuun waamamanii — salphina fi ijaajummaasaa Lionel Messi waliin walitti dhihaatuuf. Leenji Godina Dundee United, Jackie McNamara, Gauld garee isaatti tursiisuun akka barbaade dubbateera, garuu carraa kun jireenya isaa jijjiiruudha jedhe. McNamara carraa Sporting Lisbon takkallee akka tarkaanfii olaanaa ilaaleera, akkasumas, "Ogummaa keessaati, taphattoonni carraan gaarii akka isiin argatan ni barbaada. article_content: Thousands of older homeowners are struggling to secure better mortgage deals due to increasingly strict lending practices by banks and building societies. Even individuals in their 50s are finding it difficult to obtain new home loans, a problem stemming from tougher regulations introduced under recent lending rules, according to the Financial Conduct Authority (FCA). This situation has created so-called 'mortgage prisoners'—borrowers stuck paying higher default interest rates after failing to qualify for more favorable fixed-rate deals. The FCA has criticized lenders for adopting a rigid, 'computer says no' approach and argues that pensions, often a stable source of income, should not be overlooked. The agency insists that age should not serve as an automatic barrier to securing a mortgage. The FCA announced it will review lenders’ application of the new rules—known as the Mortgage Market Review, implemented in April—out of concern that they may be interpreted too harshly. Lenders maintain they are simply adhering to stricter requirements, which demand comprehensive checks on a borrower's current and future income and expenses to ensure loan affordability, especially if interest rates rise. Critics, however, contend that banks may be using these regulations to reject applications from people nearing retirement for their own financial advantage, keeping such customers on less favorable rates. Some reports indicate banks and building societies have refused loans to customers—even when switching would mean lower monthly repayments—citing affordability concerns. Most lenders set an upper age limit for borrowers, typically between 65 and 80 years. Nevertheless, rejections are being reported even for individuals in their 50s who would be repaying their loan during retirement. At a recent Council of Mortgage Lenders conference, FCA's Linda Woodall emphasized that current rules are not designed to discourage lending to older borrowers, highlighting that pension income is often stable. She stated, 'A sensible and proportionate approach is all we are asking of you,' and noted instances where applicants seeking to downsize or reduce mortgage debt were turned down. Mortgage broker Andrew Montlake from Coreco Group noted that nervousness among banks, especially after regulatory changes, leads them to err on the side of caution. Meanwhile, broker Ray Boulger of John Charcol added that new pension freedoms complicate lenders' assessments of retirement income. A spokesperson for the Council of Mortgage Lenders acknowledged that lending to borrowers whose mortgage extends into retirement can be appropriate, but stressed that recent changes make it harder to guarantee regulators will approve these decisions in future assessments.

Walgahii ka'umsa irratti, Linda Woodall hanga ammaatti seeronni jiran namoota dulloomanii liqiin isaanii hin dhoorkamne, akkasumas mindaan penshinii yeroo baay’ee tasgabbii qabaachuu ibsan. article_content: Authorities in Riverside, California are investigating an assault at Hunt Park skate park after a video surfaced on Facebook. The footage shows a 16-year-old on a BMX bike punching a homeless man, identified as Shane, during an argument that referenced drugs. Shane fell to the ground and lost consciousness for several minutes after the punch. Blood from a head wound was observed on the concrete, though it was edited out in the circulated video. In an interview with KTLA, Shane described the incident as a 'misunderstanding.' Witnesses allege the confrontation began when Shane tried to sell drugs to the group. Police are seeking both the teenager and Shane. No charges have been filed, and Shane has said he does not wish to press charges against the teen.

article_content: Using only an electric toothbrush and a dirty wall, graffiti artist Moose, whose real name is Paul Curtis, created a striking Christmas-themed mural on London's South Bank. With a Philips Sonicare toothbrush, he carefully removed the green moss and grime from the concrete wall to reveal a winter scene featuring rolling, snow-capped hills, trees, and a cozy cottage. Moose is known for his unique approach to street art, which involves cleaning dirt from surfaces to create images instead of using paint. By skillfully removing the moss, he transformed the footpath wall into a bright and cheerful landscape. One passer-by commented, 'It's amazing. It's really nice to have something created so simply with something that's everyday. It's a lovely addition to the South Bank.' Moose was impressed with both the tool he was challenged to use and the wall itself. He said his goal was to cheer up workers who often appeared miserable as they passed by, and he found the experience very rewarding. In an area famous for creativity and landmarks such as the London Eye, Waterloo Bridge, Royal Festival Hall, and the Thames, Moose's artwork fit right in. 'The moss is coming off and leaving a white, fluffy surface,' Moose explained while working. 'What a great way to spend the afternoon. It's quite surreal, really. I've really enjoyed doing it. Whatever the toothbrush does for teeth, it's been incredible for the wall.'

Brushii Philips Sonicare fayyadamuudhaan, magariisaa fi xuraa’aa dallaa irraa qulqulleesse, suuraa qabbana jiidhaa, gaara cabbii, muka, fi mana xiqqaa gugurdaa qopheesse. article_content: The nation's record-low teen birth rate is a result of significant declines across nearly every state, especially in several Mountain States and among Hispanic teens, according to a new government report. All states except West Virginia and North Dakota showed substantial decreases over five years; notably, Arizona, Colorado, Idaho, Nevada, and Utah saw rates fall by 30% or more. Teen birth rates among Hispanics dropped by at least 40% in 22 states, a change described as 'just amazing' by the report's lead author, Brady Hamilton of the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC). The exact reasons for these declines are not fully known and may differ by state. Since 1991, teen birth rates have mostly been falling, with a minor rise during 2006 and 2007. The states with the lowest teen birth rates — all under 17 per 1,000 — are New Hampshire, Massachusetts, Connecticut, and Vermont. The South continues to have the highest rates, especially Arkansas and Mississippi, each with about 50 per 1,000. In Arkansas, most teen births are to white mothers; in Mississippi, to black mothers. Nationally, white teens have the lowest teen birth rate at about 22 per 1,000, while black teens have seen a bigger improvement but still have a rate of 47 per 1,000. Overall, the teen birth rate for Hispanics dropped dramatically from 75 to 49 per 1,000, nearly equal to the rate for black teens. The CDC analyzed birth certificates from 2007 to 2011 for its report released Thursday. Last year, the CDC announced a record low national teen birth rate: 31 births per 1,000 teens ages 15 to 19, compared to 42 per 1,000 five years earlier. Experts say the drop in teen birth rates coincided with a general decline in births, which they attribute in part to a weak economy limiting family size. Hispanic women have contributed to these changes, possibly due to economic conditions and stricter immigration rules, as noted by John Santelli of Columbia University. As new immigrants play a lesser role, second- and third-generation Hispanic families are now more influential in the birth statistics. Over time, Hispanic Americans — like previous immigrant groups — tend to adopt American customs, focusing more on education, careers, and future planning, said Dr. Janet Realini of Healthy Futures of Texas. Still, in states with large Hispanic populations, such as California, Texas, New York, New Jersey, Arizona, Colorado, New Mexico, and Georgia, Hispanic teen birth rates remain higher than those for blacks and whites. Texas led the nation with nearly 43,000 teen births in 2011, and nearly two-thirds of these were to Hispanic mothers. Advocates say the progress is worth celebrating. 'Geography, politics, or policy alone simply cannot explain the widespread declines,' noted Bill Albert of the National Campaign to Prevent Teen and Unplanned Pregnancy. 'Credit goes to teens themselves who are making better choices about sex, contraception, and their futures.'

article_content: For more than a hundred years, a simple brick bridge crossed the railway in the quiet village of Brinkworth, Wiltshire. This bridge was recently removed and replaced with a green metal structure, drawing criticism from the local community. To enable electrification of the train line, Network Rail dismantled the old bridge and installed a new one that is four inches higher, allowing room for overhead electric wires. This project is part of major improvements to the Great Western main line, designed to introduce newer, faster, and more environmentally friendly trains. The new bridge, characterized by its visible bolts and striking green color, contrasts sharply with the village's rural setting. During construction, which closed the main road out of Brinkworth for more than three months, the bridge was hidden beneath covers. Villagers only saw the bridge's final appearance when it was revealed around Christmas. Many residents voiced strong dissatisfaction upon seeing the completed bridge, feeling its industrial appearance did not suit the area's traditional look. Local resident Jim Humm, 74, commented, 'It's an eyesore. It's not what we expected.' Others agreed, calling the transformation shocking. Network Rail explained that the bridge had to be rebuilt to meet modern standards, including specific requirements for electrified railways established in EU regulations. The organization also noted that individual bridge costs are hard to estimate since contractors were paid for multiple bridges as a group. Expressing regret that the bridge was not well-received aesthetically, Network Rail emphasized their duty as a public entity to balance heritage with cost-efficiency. They highlighted that the upgraded bridge brings the village closer to enjoying the benefits of enhanced, greener train services.

article_content: When Norman Rushworth first started visiting his local pub, a pint cost just 5p. Since 1933, every Friday and Saturday at 5pm, he has enjoyed ordering a pint of Shropshire Gold. To mark his 100th birthday, Britain's oldest pub regular chose to celebrate in the only way he knew best: raising a pint at the Golden Cross in Shrewsbury. Norman has been a familiar face at the Golden Cross pub for 80 years. On his 100th birthday, he enjoyed his favorite ale, Shropshire Gold. A veteran of the Royal Air Force during WWII, Norman served by driving an ambulance converted into a dental surgery for troops in Europe after D-Day. After his military service, Norman became a dental technician in Shrewsbury, close to his cherished pub. Throughout his 80 years of visits, the twice-widowed great-grandfather estimates he's had around 10,000 pints of beer, and he shows little sign of slowing down. Norman credits his long life to a pint of beer, dancing, and good company. 'What else is there?' he jokes. Other regulars make sure his favorite spot by the bar is waiting for him at the 600-year-old pub in the heart of town. Norman recalls, 'My friends and I used to come in at lunchtime and on weekends, though we couldn't afford every day. Four of us would come in, sing songs, and play games.' Pub landlord Gareth Reece, 49, says Norman is part of the pub's heritage. 'He comes for coffee on Friday and a beer or two on Saturday. Not many pubs have customers who have been regulars since before the war. He's remarkable and always cheerful.' Norman met his first wife Elsie after leaving the RAF, and they had one son, John, who now lives in France. Elsie passed away in 1974 at the age of 47. Later, Norman married Dorothy at age 80, but she died shortly after their wedding. Norman is also known as a talented tenor and dancer and still travels frequently to Blackpool.

TOKYO (AP) – Toyota Motor Corp. announced Wednesday that it is selling part of its stake in auto parts supplier Denso to raise funds for investments in electric vehicles and other technological innovations. The sale, estimated to net about 290 billion yen ($2 billion) based on recent share prices, will see Toyota reduce its holding in Denso from 24.2% to 20%, though it will remain the largest shareholder.

"We don’t want to just hold on to our assets. We want to make them living assets that contribute to our company’s growth," said Masahiro Yamamoto, an executive in Toyota’s accounting group. Denso shares closed at 2,298 yen ($16) on Wednesday.

Funds from the sale will also support the development of smart-driving and a variety of other ongoing initiatives in the auto industry. While Yamamoto did not specify the sale date, it is expected to happen soon.

Major automakers worldwide are investing heavily in electric and eco-friendly vehicles amid growing concerns about climate change. Toyota’s affiliates, Toyota Industries and Aisin, are also divesting some of their Denso shares, according to company officials.

Cross-shareholding—companies holding stakes in affiliates—is a traditional practice in Japan. While some criticize it for lack of transparency, others believe it supports corporate stability. Yamamoto stated the share sale is not intended to reduce cross-shareholdings.

Toyota admits it is catching up in the shift to electric vehicles. The company, known for models including the Camry, Lexus, and Prius hybrid, leads in hybrid vehicles and has a strong presence in hydrogen fuel cell technology.

In July, Toyota sold part of its stake in telecom company KDDI Corp. for nearly 250 billion yen ($1.7 billion). Officials hinted at possible future asset sales but gave no details.

article_content: Former cabinet minister Greg Combet gave a blunt response when then Prime Minister Julia Gillard asked him to increase his social media activity, saying he had no interest in tweeting. According to Ms Gillard, his language was quite frank. Ms Gillard revealed this anecdote during the launch of Mr Combet's memoir, 'The Fights of My Life,' in Sydney on Tuesday. The book, co-written with journalist Mark Davis, details Mr Combet's career, from leading the ACTU to his six years in parliament. Ahead of its release, the memoir made headlines for revealing that Ms Gillard offered Mr Combet the chance to lead the Labor Party to block Kevin Rudd’s attempted comeback. Mr Combet served first under Prime Minister Kevin Rudd, then as a cabinet minister for Julia Gillard, during his six-year tenure in parliament. Ms Gillard noted, 'There came a time when it became clear to me that my leadership was likely to come to an early end. My belief that the nation and the political party needed to be led by someone with good values and a clear sense of purpose remained strong. It was not to be.' The launch event at Trades Hall was attended by prominent Labor figures, including former prime minister Bob Hawke, deputy opposition leader Tanya Plibersek, Craig Emerson, John Faulkner, and Penny Wong. Mr Combet's book also discusses his desire to leave parliament by the time of Ms Gillard's offer, as well as his health challenges with cardiovascular disease and osteoporosis. Defending the Labor government’s achievements, Mr Combet highlighted the emissions trading scheme as a key and effective environmental policy. He stressed the need to fight for important reforms, saying, 'That’s one of the messages of my book. When people complain about policies like Prime Minister Tony Abbott’s budget, I tell them you have to stand up, join together, and fight for change instead of just complaining.'

Gillard akka jettetti, jechi inni fayyadame dhugaa fi salphaa ture. Mufachuu qofaa miti, hojjechuu barbaachisa," jedhe.

An Ohio man who was declared legally dead in 1994 will remain so after his recent attempt to revoke the declaration was denied. Donald Miller, 61, vanished in 1986 after losing his job, leaving behind his wife, two children, and thousands in unpaid child support, according to James Hammer, attorney for Miller’s ex-wife, Robin Miller. Eight years after his disappearance, Miller was legally declared dead.

Miller testified that he returned to Ohio around 2005, unaware that he was considered deceased, and sought to restore his Social Security number. However, Ohio law bars the reversal of death declarations after three years, explained Hammer. Judge Allan Davis of Hancock County Probate Court said, "In over 40 years, I've never come across a case like this. In the end, because of the statute, it was a pretty open-and-shut case."

At the time of the 1994 legal death declaration, Miller reportedly owed Robin Miller about $25,000 in child support. If he were declared alive, Robin Miller may have had to repay Social Security death benefits she received for her children after 1994, Hammer said. “We certainly did not want to open that door, so we’re satisfied with the outcome,” he added. Despite the circumstances, Hammer said Robin Miller does not harbor ill will toward her ex-husband.

Donald Miller’s attorney was not available for comment on Wednesday. Judge Davis noted that Miller has 30 days to appeal the court’s decision.

Swansea City vice-chairman Leigh Dineen has called on the Premier League to lead efforts to reduce ticket prices for struggling fans by encouraging all top-tier clubs to lower their admission fees. Dineen expressed his desire to cut costs significantly for all fans, including season ticket holders, and argued that other clubs are in a financial position to do the same because of the league’s £5.5 billion, three-year television contract. However, he cautioned that Swansea acting alone could hurt the club’s competitiveness, emphasizing that such reductions would only work if all Premier League teams implemented them together. Dineen praised the German Bundesliga's successful approach to affordable tickets and suggested it's a model the Premier League could adopt.

He also voiced frustration that Premier League officials missed an opportunity to implement coordinated away-fan ticket price reductions when the new TV deal was announced. Instead, clubs have had to arrange reciprocal price deals independently; so far, Swansea has managed agreements with Newcastle, Sunderland, Aston Villa, and West Brom. Still, Dineen believes these scattered efforts have been less effective than a league-wide initiative.

Meanwhile, Kevin Miles, the Football Supporters’ Federation’s chief executive, warned that escalating prices could deter young fans and potentially shrink future crowds. The current average price of the cheapest adult season ticket is £526—a 6.5% increase.

article_content: Apple, the world’s largest company by market value, posted its fourth consecutive quarter of declining revenue, with fiscal fourth-quarter sales slipping about 1% to $89.5 billion. However, earnings per share jumped 13% year-on-year to $1.46 for the September period, beating Wall Street forecasts. Despite exceeding profit estimates, investors seemed underwhelmed, sending Apple shares down 1% after the bell, even though the stock closed 2% higher at nearly $177 earlier in the session. The company’s iPhone revenue, representing roughly half its business, hit a record $43.8 billion, benefiting from an initial week of iPhone 15 sales. In contrast, Mac and iPad segments saw notable declines—Mac sales dropped 33% to $7.4 billion, and iPad was down 10% to $6.4 billion. The Wearables, Home & Accessories category dipped 3% to $9.3 billion. Apple’s Services division—which includes Apple TV+, Music, Fitness, Arcade, and more—was a standout, pulling in $22.3 billion, marking solid growth from $19.2 billion last year. Recent price hikes affected Apple TV+ (now $9.99/month) and bundled services like Apple News+, Arcade, and Apple One, with increased rates rolling out in the U.S. and selected international markets. Apple continues to emphasize quality enhancements and new offerings in its services, while also expanding into original theatrical films. The Martin Scorsese-directed ‘Killers of the Flower Moon’ earned $87 million worldwide since its late October release, while Ridley Scott’s ‘Napoleon’ debuts November 22. CEO Tim Cook pointed to iPhone and Services revenue records and highlighted an expanding range of products, such as the new iPhone 15 lineup and Apple’s first carbon neutral Apple Watch models, reinforcing the company’s goal to make all products carbon neutral by 2030. CFO Luca Maestri noted increased device installation across all product lines and regions, strong ecosystem support, and double-digit EPS growth. He also mentioned Apple returned nearly $25 billion to shareholders last quarter. Looking forward, investors are watching iPhone 15’s impact during the holiday shopping season and scrutinizing Mac and iPad sales trends. Apple previously warned of continued revenue softness, citing last year’s strong sales rebound after earlier supply constraints. The company also faces uncertainty in China due to competition from Huawei and government scrutiny involving Foxconn, Apple’s supply partner there. Nonetheless, Cook remains optimistic about growth opportunities in the Chinese market. In addition, Apple recently introduced new chips set to power its latest personal computers.

article_content: When a loved one passes away, it can be difficult to cope not only with the emotional loss, including feelings of sadness and anger, but also with the responsibilities that follow. Tasks like notifying others and planning the funeral can feel overwhelming, especially if you've never been involved in arranging such an event before. Funeral directors shared with Insider their top etiquette rules and common issues they wish more people understood. If you find yourself responsible for planning a funeral, Randi Goldstein-Casey, vice president and funeral director at Goldsteins' Rosenberg's Raphael-Sacks Funeral Home in Philadelphia, recommends preparing a checklist and having a sense of your budget before meeting with the funeral home. Required documentation includes the deceased’s Social Security number, date of birth, and parents’ names. 'A funeral cannot take place without this information,' Casey explained, emphasizing that the funeral home cannot proceed without it. Families often wait together in a private room before the service. As guests arrive, some may attempt to enter this private area to pay their respects. While well-intentioned, Casey advises that guests should not assume it is appropriate to enter unless invited. Families should set boundaries, and guests should respect their privacy during this time. On the day of the funeral, family and close friends may feel pressured to spend time with attendees, but it's important for those in mourning to set limits and decide whom they want to interact with. Receiving lines are not mandatory, and families may choose what feels comfortable. Dino Cantelmi, owner and director of Cantelmi Funeral Home in Bethlehem, Pennsylvania, suggests a few key rules for those attending a funeral: arrive on time, dress appropriately (business-like and conservative clothing; black or dark colors are customary but not required), and silence your cellphone. Phone disruptions are common and can be easily avoided by switching devices to silent or leaving them in your car. Funerals can reunite people who haven’t seen each other in years, sometimes leading to conflict. Cantelmi recommends keeping funeral details private, hiring security, or designating a family member to address potential drama if needed. Elizabeth Fournier, funeral director at Cornerstone Funeral Services in Boring, Oregon, encourages families to seek guidance from funeral directors and related staff. She notes that most people are unfamiliar with the process and can rely on professionals for support, clear communication, and trustworthy resources.

Yoo awwaalcha qopheessuuf itti gaafatamummaan siirra jiruu, Randi Goldstein-Casey, itti aanaa pirezidaantii fi daayirektara Goldsteins’ Rosenberg’s Raphael-Sacks Funeral Home, Philadelphia, tarree galmeessii fi baasii qabachuu dura deemuu akka gaariidha jedhu. Odeeffannoon barbaachisaan lakkoofsa Social Security namoota du’an, guyyaa dhalootaa fi maqaa abbaa fi haadha of keessaa qaba. 'Awwaalchaa odeeffannoo kana malee geggeessuu hin dandeenyu,' jechuun Casey ibsan. Maatiin yeroo awwaalchaa dura kutaa addaa keessa turuu danda’u. Lawyers for Pras Michel have requested a new trial for the rapper, arguing that his former attorney used generative AI to craft closing arguments and mishandled his fraud case. Michel, a founding member of the Grammy-winning Fugees, was convicted in April of ten federal charges, including conspiring to make and conceal foreign campaign contributions. He was also found guilty of attempting to persuade U.S. officials to drop an investigation into Jho Low, the Malaysian financier accused of playing a central role in a $4.5 billion fraud scheme.

David Kenner, who previously represented Suge Knight, Tupac Shakur, and Snoop Dogg, handled Michel’s defense at trial. Michel’s new legal team from ArentFox Schiff claims Kenner compromised the defense by using an 'experimental artificial intelligence program,' EyeLevel.AI, to write closing arguments. In a recent filing, Michel's lawyers contended that Kenner ignored better arguments and confused the charges, stating, 'Michel never had a chance' and calling his representation 'deficient throughout.'

Per Michel’s lawyers, knowledge of Kenner’s AI use came via Michel’s former publicist. They cited a May 10 product update by EyeLevel.AI, in which Kenner was quoted as using it in the 'first use of generative AI in a federal trial.' The release quoted Kenner saying, 'This is an absolute game changer for complex litigation... The system turned hours or days of legal work into seconds. This is a look into the future of how cases will be conducted.' EyeLevel.AI claims its system makes lawyers '10x faster and more effective.'

Michel’s attorneys further allege that Kenner and his co-counsel had undisclosed financial interests in EyeLevel.AI and promoted the technology during the trial. They noted that law firms tied to Kenner and his co-counsel share addresses with CaseFile Connect, an EyeLevel.AI technology partner, in Encino, California, and New York City, which they say suggests a financial link.

EyeLevel.AI told Insider that neither Kenner Law nor its associates have financial interests in EyeLevel.AI, nor does anyone at EyeLevel have financial ties to CaseFile Connect. Neil Katz, EyeLevel’s COO, said Kenner and his co-counsel were quoted in a product update simply because they were pleased with the AI’s performance.

Additionally, Michel’s team criticized Kenner’s defense as inadequate, citing his lack of white-collar crime experience and his reliance on contract attorneys from a friend’s firm for trial preparations. They listed six alleged defense problems, such as failing to object to hearsay and prejudicial evidence. Both Kenner and the ArentFox Schiff team did not immediately respond to requests for comment outside regular business hours. Michel’s sentencing has not been set; he faces up to 20 years in prison.

October 20, 2023: This article was updated to include a statement from EyeLevel.AI.

Michel, miseensa garee Fugees mo'ate Grammy, Caamsaa keessa adabbii yakka federaalaa 10 guutuu seeraan himatame — gargaarsa maallaqaa alaa gochuu fi dhoksuu dabalatee. Amma garuu gareen seeraa haaraan Michel kan ArentFox Schiff, Kenner prograama "AI hojiirra oole" jedhamu—EyeLevel.AI—barreessaan seeraa dhumaa ittiin barreesse jedhan. Abukaatoon Michel, odeeffannoo Kenner AI fayyadamee, kan pubilisisti duraanii irraa argame, ibsa guyyaa Caamsaa 10 EyeLevel.AI ilaalamu dhaan, Kenner ‘fayidaa AI yeroo jalqabaatiif murtii federaalaa keessatti’ jedhu. Kenner, “Kun hojiilee seeraa hedduu yeroo gabaabaa keessatti hojjeta — kun bu'uura fooyya’aaf nu agarsiisa,” jedhe. EyeLevel.AI’n, abukaatoonni akka saffisaan dalaguu danda’an ibseera.

Gareen ArentFox Schiff, Kenner fi abukaatoo isaa waliin, hidhata maallaqaa qarqara EyeLevel.AI fi CaseFile Connect waliin qabaachuu fi hojii kanaaf isaan oduu akka baasaniif hojiirra oolfame jedhu. Gareen Michel Kenner ammoo, irratti hin qophaa’in yakka white-collar irratti, hojiin qopheessuu falmii abukaatoo saahiba isaa irraa hiriirfachuun akka imaanaa hanqate himan. Rakkoolee jahan tarreeffatan; tokkoon isaas ragaa dhageettii haqaan deemuu irratti hin komanne turan. Kenner bakka hin jirreetti fi gareen ArentFox Schiff odeeffannoo hanga ammaatti hin kennine. Murtiin hidhaa Michel hin barreeffamne; hanga waggaa 20n murtii argachuu danda’a.

article_content: A dog named Buddy truly lived up to his name this past weekend when he rescued his owner from a fire. Jacob Martin was asleep on Sunday when a fire broke out in the house he was renovating next door to his home in Mansfield, Ohio. His pit bull Buddy began barking, waking Martin just in time for him to escape and save his own home from the spreading flames. Martin explained to Fox 8 Cleveland that the heat melted the door and he burned his hand while trying to open it. He had invested $1,500 in new additions to the house being renovated, but all of it was lost when the fire destroyed the building. Martin did not have rental insurance. Although relieved to be alive, Martin is worried he may not be able to keep Buddy due to financial strain from the fire and a recent job loss. 'Buddy is the best dog I ever had—great dog and good company,' Martin said, expressing gratitude for his pet's life-saving actions. Martin adopted Buddy about a month and a half ago from a co-worker, after the dog was found abandoned in a neighbor's former house. Firefighters are still investigating the cause of the fire but do not believe it was set intentionally.

article_content: The CFDA Awards, organized by the Council of Fashion Designers of America, is one of fashion's most prestigious and glamorous events—a fact reflected by the dazzling attire seen at this year's ceremony in New York. Her bold look was completed with a matching crystal-adorned headscarf and gloves.  Solange Knowles shimmered in a pewter gown from Calvin Klein Collection, styled with voluminous hair and a vivid pink lip. She advised that when wearing metallics, it's best to keep the look balanced and not overdone—using Blake Lively's minimalist styling as an example.  Metallic fabrics made a strong impact on the Spring/Summer 2014 runways, with designers like Lanvin, Balmain, Dolce & Gabbana, Tom Ford, and Christopher Kane showcasing shimmering designs. Julien Macdonald, known for his fondness of metallics, featured them heavily in his collections.  Fashion writer Simon Glazin commented on the ongoing popularity of metallics in spring and summer collections, noting a current preference for glittery, fairy-dust-like finishes. The metallic look is accessible off the runway as well, with a variety of shimmering dresses, skirts, sandals, and accessories available from popular retailers.

article_content: According to a recent analysis by Akamai Technologies, Hong Kong recorded the world’s fastest average peak internet connection speed in the third quarter of 2012, exceeding 54 megabits per second. This marks the first time any region’s speeds have surpassed 50 Mbps. Over the past year, average peak speeds in Hong Kong increased by 36%, despite a minor slowdown during the quarter. South Korea (48.8 Mbps), Japan (42.2 Mbps), Latvia (37.5 Mbps), and Romania (37.4 Mbps) followed as the regions with the next highest peak speeds. The United States ranked 14th globally with an average peak speed of 29.6 Mbps. Delaware remained the fastest U.S. state at 10.9 Mbps, while the District of Columbia is close behind. In Europe, Switzerland led with a peak speed of 8.7 Mbps, just surpassing the Netherlands (8.5 Mbps), while the Czech Republic (7.7 Mbps) placed third. China had the slowest peak speed in Asia at 7.1 Mbps, ranking 123rd globally, despite a 21% quarterly speed increase. For average connection speeds, South Korea led at 14.2 Mbps, followed by Japan at 10.7 Mbps and Hong Kong at 8.9 Mbps. The State of the Internet Report also named China as the largest single source of online attack traffic in the quarter, accounting for 33% worldwide—a figure that doubled during the period. The U.S. and Russia were also among the top three sources. The top 10 countries collectively accounted for nearly three-quarters of global attack traffic. Akamai’s quarterly report is based on data from 680 million unique IP addresses connected to its platform.

Kun yeroo jalqabaaf saffisni interneetaa bal’inaan 50 Mbps ol ga’e agarsiisa. Bara darbe keessatti, saffisni olaanaan Hong Kong %36 ol dabaluun, yeroo ji’a tokko keessatti xiqqoo hir’ates jira. Kooriyaa Kibbaa (48.8 Mbps), Jaappaan (42.2 Mbps), Laatviyaa (37.5 Mbps), fi Romaaniyaa (37.4 Mbps) bakka sadarkaa olii qabataniiru. Yunaayitid Isteetis sadarkaa 14ffaa addunyaarratti fi Mbps 29.6 qabatee argama. Delaware, biyya saffisa qunnamsiisaa olaanaa Yunaayitid Isteetis keessa jirti, 10.9 Mbps qabdi, District of Columbia immoo itti siqaa jirti. article_content:
Researchers at the University of Tokyo have developed an innovative plastic called VPR that is stronger, more stretchable, and partially biodegradable compared to standard plastics. VPR is created by adding the molecule polyrotaxane to an epoxy resin vitrimer, a type of plastic. This new material can retain its shape, self-heal when exposed to heat, and be reshaped at temperatures above 150°C due to the recombination of its internal chemical bonds.

VPR can be broken down into its raw components when treated with heat and solvent. Notably, after being submerged in seawater for 30 days, VPR achieves 25% biodegradation, and the polyrotaxane breaks down into a food source for marine organisms. This material shows promise for supporting a circular economy and reducing waste across sectors such as engineering, manufacturing, medicine, and sustainable fashion.

Published in ACS Materials Letters, the study highlights how VPR offers elevated performance: it is over five times more resistant to breaking compared to conventional epoxy resin vitrimers, repairs itself 15 times faster, recovers original shape twice as quickly, and undergoes chemical recycling 10 times faster. Additionally, VPR is less brittle, enabling the creation and retention of more complex shapes, and can be disposed of or recycled more efficiently.

Lead author Shota Ando notes that VPR holds great promise in modern society’s shift toward resource recycling, as traditional vitrimers do not biodegrade. Potential applications include stronger, heat-healable infrastructure (roads, bridges), vehicle manufacturing, and even customizable clothing shapes using household heat tools. 

The research team plans to collaborate with industry partners to evaluate the feasibility of various uses and continue laboratory studies. Ando envisions that VPR could help address widespread challenges associated with plastic waste by offering a single, more sustainable material solution.

article_content: Karishma Tushar claims to have a talent for removing the 'evil eye.' Based in Mumbai, she is a tarot reader who performs about a dozen 'nazar-removal' rituals each month, using a blend of deities and angels to clear negative energies from her clients' lives. She says that 40% of her clients are in their 20s, while most others are between 30 and 44. Many of these Millennials and Gen Z clients attribute issues like distant partners, delayed promotions, or periods of ill health to 'nazar'—the belief that someone’s envious gaze can cause misfortune. In India, people follow a variety of practices to ward off nazar, such as placing a black dot on a baby’s forehead, wearing black threads or amulets (tabeez), waving dried red chillies around someone and burning them, or hanging strings of lemons and green chillies from vehicles. Recently, a sense of vulnerability, heightened after the pandemic, has led some to seek protection from the Turkish evil eye, known as the nazar boncuk. This blue glass charm has four concentric circles and is increasingly worn as jewelry or used as an emoji on social media. Karishma Tushar believes the evil eye design distracts others from the beauty or appeal of a person or object, offering protection. For younger generations, the Turkish evil eye has become both a fashion statement and a lucky charm. Shraddha Joshi, a 26-year-old at a fintech startup in Mumbai, says Gen Z has turned nazar into a form of self-expression. She notes that while her peers may avoid black threads, blue amulets are stylish and acceptable. With rising demand, jewelers are incorporating the evil eye motif in their offerings. Avnish Anand, co-founder and CEO of CaratLane, reports that the company has sold around 30,000 pieces of evil eye jewelry since expanding its range in 2021, with items including rings, pendants, and mangalsutras priced from Rs 5,000 to Rs 40,000. Millennials and Gen Z make up most of these customers, driven by the symbol’s social media visibility and its popularity among celebrities. Moumita Roy, assistant professor at Ahmedabad University, explains that superstitions and beliefs strongly influence consumer choices in India. She refers to research indicating that in unequal societies, concerns about others’ envy impact buying habits. Roy notes that superstitions are deeply rooted, and when many people follow one, it can become difficult to stay rational about it—for example, believing in the power of evil eye charms. Online retailers are responding to what Roy calls the 'bandwagon effect.' Nykaa offers 500 evil eye jewelry products from brands like Pipa Bella, Outhouse, and Joker & Witch, with a surge in sales traced back to April 2020 after global celebrities like Meghan Markle, Gigi Hadid, and Zayn Malik were seen wearing evil eye accessories. Myntra has seen a 35% increase in demand and has expanded its range by 70%. Zariin, a Delhi-based brand, also plans to add evil eye pieces to its 2024 collection. On social media, people use the evil eye emoji to protect positive moments or good fortune, with some sharing stories of falling ill after posting a flattering photo. As a result, adding the emoji has become a digital precaution. According to research by WeDig, Quantum Consumer Solutions’ digital unit, India is second only to Turkey in using the nazar emoji, appearing in 7.2 million conversations on X and Instagram between October 2022 and October 2023. The emoji is associated with aspirations, celebrities, good luck, and support. Vartika Hali, a partner at Quantum Consumer Solutions, observes that the evil eye is increasingly used in positive contexts online. Rather than just protection, it is being embraced as a symbol of positivity. Additionally, Indian economic news includes a report that industrial growth slowed to 5.8% in September. Educational investment news notes Ranjan Pai’s Rs 1,400 crore investment in Aakash Institute, while manufacturing companies report increased hiring of digitally skilled graduates.

Karishma Tushar mallattoo ‘evil eye’ kun bareedina namaa yookiin wanta tokko irraa gara biraatti xiyyeeffannoo nama kaasuun eegumsa kenna jettee amanti. Dargaggoota har’aaf, Turkish evil eye mallattoo aadaa fi carraa gaarii ta’ee fudhatameera. Shraddha Joshi, dhalootaan waggaa 26, hojii fintech keessatti Mumbai keessa jirtu, akka jettu, Gen Z nazar akka ofii isaanii agarsiisuutti gargaaru. Moumita Roy, barsiiftuu Yuunivarsiitii Ahmedabad, akka jettuitti, amanti fi safuun gurgurtaa India keessatti murteessadha. Barumsa tokko irratti hunda’e, hawaasa garaagarummaa qabu keessatti, sodaa diddaa nama birootti qabdan buyyitoota irratti dhiibbaa qaba. Platformii e-commerce, yaada Roy 'bandwagon effect' jedhuufi irratti hundaa’uun deebii kennuu jalqabaniiru. Nykaa suphaa jewellery evil eye 500 ol keessaa kan Pipa Bella, Outhouse fi Joker & Witch. Gara bara 2020, akka urjiiwwan addunyaa akka Meghan Markle, Gigi Hadid fi Zayn Malik uffachaa jiranitti gurgurtaan gurguddaan mul’ate. Myntra barbaachisummaa dabalatee 35% dabaluusaa, filannoo 70% dabaluu isaa beeksise. Zariin, branda Dehli keessa, bara 2024 ammeessuu mala evil eye keessa galchuuf karoora qabdi. Sab-qunnamtii hawaasaa irratti, namoonni emoji nazar fayyadamuun carraa gaarii ofii eeguuf socho’u. Namni tokko tokko yeroo suuraa bareedaa fe’an booda dhukkuba akka isaan mudate odeessan. Kanaafuu, emoji fayyadamuun eegumsa dijitaalaa ta’eera. Akka qorannoo WeDig, kutaa dijitaalaa Quantum Consumer Solutions, India Turkii booda sadarkaa lammaffaatti jirtu; Hagayya 2022 hanga Hagayya 2023 tti X fi Instagram irratti marii 7.2 miiliyoona keessa jira. Emoji kun waliin hawwii, urjii, carraa gaarii fi deeggarsa irratti keessa jira. Vartika Hali, miseensa Quantum Consumer Solutions, akka jettu, mallattoo evil eye miidiyaa irratti haala gaariin fudhatamaa jira. Inni eegumsa qofa odoo hin taane mallattoo idileeti ta’aa jira. Dabalataan, gabaasa diinagdee India keessatti guddinni industirii 5.8%tti gadi bu’ee jira. Odeeffannoo invetimentii barnootaa keessatti Ranjan Pai liqii Rs 1,400 crore gara Aakash Institute geesse, akkasumas warshaalee garaagaraa keessatti dargaggoota beekumsa dijitaalaa qaban dabaluu gabaasaniiru.

article_content: Wordle remains a popular word puzzle game that entertains people on both desktops and smartphones around the world. This Monday is a bit different due to a shorter school week, giving kids extra time off while leaving parents with less quiet time at home. Despite that, there’s enthusiasm for the upcoming Thanksgiving celebrations. For now, today’s Wordle is the focus. After solving the Wordle puzzle, I like to check how my attempt stacks up by visiting the Wordle Bot. My first guess, ‘scare,’ was a clever nod to Halloween, and today’s answer, ‘candy,’ fits well with that theme. Starting with ‘scare’ left 57 possible answers, and ‘boink’ cut it down to just four. ‘Candy’ seemed like the most enjoyable guess—it was correct in three tries, earning me a point and tying the Bot. The word ‘candy’ has roots in the Arabic word ‘qandi,’ which comes from the Persian ‘qand,’ both meaning ‘sugar.’ These words trace back further to Sanskrit ‘khanda,’ referring to sweet substances and inspiring the word ‘jaggery,’ a type of traditional sweetener in India. As the term was adopted into other languages, it passed through Persian and Arabic to Italian and French, eventually becoming ‘candy’ in English for sugary treats. You can take on a competitive Wordle challenge against me or try to beat the Wordle Bot, which is accessible to New York Times subscribers. Whether you keep a running score or play by the day, it’s all about enjoying the game.

A recent report from Bank of Baroda indicates that Indian companies have strengthened their debt servicing capacity, even as policy rates increased by 60 basis points (0.60 percent) between September 2022 and September 2023. The interest coverage ratio (ICR)—an indicator of a firm's ability to cover interest expenses—rose from 4.49 to 5.64 during this period. This improvement suggests that higher lending rates have not significantly impaired Indian firms' capacity to service debt.

According to Aditi Gupta, economist at Bank of Baroda, the rise in ICR was driven by both modest growth in interest expenses and robust growth in corporate profits, contributing positively to these companies’ financial stability. While the Reserve Bank of India has left its key policy rates unchanged since February 2023, banks have raised lending rates on new loans, with the weighted average rising from 8.59% in September 2022 to 9.38% in September 2023. Bank credit expanded by 17.6% for the recent quarter, a slight dip relative to the 18.9% growth in the previous year. Despite these factors, companies improved their ICR, mainly because profits outpaced rising interest costs.

The report notably points out that the 10 sectors with the highest debt exposure—including power, crude oil, infrastructure, real estate, automobiles, chemicals, logistics, textiles, telecommunications, and iron and steel—have all registered better ICRs. The analysis concludes that future ICR improvements will primarily depend on continued profit growth. With WPI inflation subdued and input costs under control, profits are likely to remain strong, further supporting asset quality.

In related business news, the Nifty index closed above 20,000 points for the first time since September 13, reflecting heightened investor confidence amid easing concerns over further rate hikes in the US. Other updates include: the Directorate of Enforcement flagging Byju’s parent company for alleged regulatory violations and delays, and HCL Group advancing plans for a semiconductor assembly and test facility in Karnataka.

Iddoon ICR (Interest Coverage Ratio)—dandeettii dhaabbileen liqii isaanii baasuu agarsiisu—Fulbaana 2022 irraa hanga Fulbaana 2023tti, 4.49 irraa gara 5.64 olii jira. Kunwn agarsiisa faayidaa liqii ol-ka'iinsa irra jiru dhaabbilee Indiyaa irratti dhiibbaa cimaa hin goone.

Aditi Gupta, ekonoomistii Bank of Baroda, akka jedhanitti ICR guddachuun kun garaagarummaa xiqqoo baasiwwan faayidaa fi guddina galii olaanaa irraa dhufeera. Kun nageenya dinagdee dhaabbilee kanaaf gaarii dha. Yeroo Baankii mootummaa Indiyaa (RBI) Guraandhala 2023 as faayidaa siyaasa isaa hin jijjiirreef, baankoonni biyya keessaa liqii haaraa irratti faayidaa dabalaa jiru; woggaa tokko keessatti kun 8.59% irraa gara 9.38% ol guddate. Guddinni liqii baankii waggaa kana 17.6%, kan bara darbee 18.9% tureen xiqqoo gad-meessee jira. Haa ta'u malee, dhiibbaa kana keessa, dhaabbileen galii isaanii ol-kaasuudhaan ICR isaanii fooyyessan.

Gabaasni kun Dameewwan liqiin irra guddaan 10—humna ibsaa, zayita, infrastraakchar, ijaarsa manaa, konkolaataa, kemikaalaa, geejjiba, textile, telecom fi sibiila—ICR isaanii ni fooyyeeffame jedha. Sadarkaan ICR boru hedduun guddina galii irratti hunda'a; WPI inflation xiqqaa fi baasiiwwan gulaalaa to'ataman jirus galii irratti bu'aa gaarii qaba. Haalli kun itti fufe, qulqullinni qabeenyaa fooyya'a jedhameeti.

Oduu daldalaa biraa keessatti, Nifty index hangafni woggaa kana yeroo jalqabaatiif 20,000 olii cufame; kunis amala investaroota fooyya'aa fi soda gatii US keessatti dabalu irratti gadhiisuu agarsiisa. Odeeffannoo biraa keessatti, Directorate of Enforcement (ED) dhaabbata abbaa Byju’s irratti ragaa yeroo hin guutne fi seera faayidaa alaa cabsuun himan; HCL ammoo ijaarsa semiconductor Karnataka keessatti keessummeessuuf deemaa jirti.

article_content: During a recent interview, Infosys co-founder NR Narayana Murthy advocated for both private and public funds in India to allocate a larger portion of their resources to support local startups. He emphasized the importance of increasing domestic investment, since much of the current capital in Indian startups is sourced from outside the country. Murthy commended the government's National Education Policy (NEP), seeing it as a positive move for education reform. He stressed that nurturing a culture of creativity and innovation, beginning at the primary school level, is crucial for generating new employment and reducing joblessness. Looking back at the Infosys Science Foundation's accomplishments, Murthy observed that the number of awardees has grown and expressed hope that more India-based researchers would achieve global recognition such as the Fields Medal or Nobel Prize. He underlined the importance of encouraging both original thinkers and dedicated practitioners in the workforce, maintaining that increased employability should not come at the cost of educational rigor. Murthy praised India’s advancements in space exploration, specifically ISRO's Chandrayaan-3 mission, highlighting its cost-effectiveness and ingenuity. Despite this, he remarked that India still has progress to make, including launching its own space station and manned lunar missions. He encouraged venture capital investors to collaborate and support innovative startups, particularly those in specialized fields like space technology. According to Murthy, it is also important to recognize the efforts of entrepreneurs with transformative ideas, even if external market conditions prevented those ideas from succeeding, as this would promote a culture of inquiry and respect. To promote more domestic investment, Murthy called for regulatory simplification and incentives that encourage institutional investors to back startups. However, he advised against direct government funding, arguing that such resources are better dedicated to public welfare and critical services. Murthy concluded that technology companies should treat periods of market downturn as opportunities to innovate, stand out, and expand their market share, noting that enduring value and strategic vision often lead to long-term success.

Inni deeggarsa maallaqa biyya keessaa dabalachuun barbaachisaa akka ta’e, sababni isaas invastimantii hedduun amma alaa waan dhufaa jiruuf ibse. Akka Murthytti, warra yaada haaraa qaban, garuu carraaleen gabaa hin isiniin milkoofneefis kabajni fi beekamtiin kennamuu qaba, kunis aadaa qorannoo fi dhimmamtii guddisuuf gargaaradha. article_content: Dr. Saleemul Huq, a pioneering climate scientist from Bangladesh and a leading global advocate for climate adaptation in developing nations, died on Saturday at the age of 71 from cardiac arrest. Widely recognized for his dedication to vulnerable communities, Dr. Huq headed the International Centre for Climate Change and Development in Dhaka and contributed significantly to the International Institute for Environment and Development in London. He also taught at universities in both Bangladesh and the UK. Over his extensive career, Huq promoted local and community-based adaptation initiatives in developing countries. He was honored with the Order of the British Empire by Queen Elizabeth II in 2022 for his efforts to foster collaboration between Bangladeshi and British academia to address poverty and climate change. The scientific journal Nature listed him among the top 10 scientists globally in 2022, and he authored numerous scientific and popular articles. Huq was a tireless advocate for an international 'loss and damage' fund to assist developing nations most affected by climate change—an initiative that has been approved, though its implementation remains pending. A frequent and influential participant in United Nations climate conferences (COP), Huq started the Adaptation Days tradition, bringing grassroots voices—including those of rural Bangladeshi farmers—into the spotlight of global climate negotiations. Friends and colleagues recall Huq's energy, humor, calm persistence, and positive influence. He also mentored many young scientists from less-developed regions, helping to connect them with the broader international scientific community. Dr. Huq is survived by his wife, son, and daughter.

Huq, kan hojii isaa guutuu jireenyaatiin hawaasa dadhabaa fi hanqata irratti xiyyeeffate, hogganaa International Centre for Climate Change and Development Dhaka ture; akkasumas gumaacha isaa olaanaa International Institute for Environment and Development London keessatti taasise. Akkasumas, yuunivarsiitii Baangilaadesh fi UK keessatti barsiisaa ture. Hojii waggoota dheeraa keessatti, Huq bu'uura hojiilee hawaasummaa fi biyya keessaa biyyoota misooma hin irra gahin keessatti haaressuu cimaa ture. Bara 2022, OBE (Order of the British Empire) kan Queen Elizabeth II kenniteef, walitti dhufeenya saayintistoota fi yunivarsiitiiwwan Baangilaadesh fi UK gidduutti cimsuu fi rakkoo hiyyummaa fi jijjiirama qilleensaa furuuf shoora olaanaa gumaachaa ture. Majala Nature'n nama saayintistoota addunyaa keessaa Top 10 keessatti galmeesse, barreessota hedduu saayinsii fi kan nama hundaaf qooda olaanaa qaba. Waldorgommiiwwan qilleensaa UN (COP) yeroo hunda irratti hirmaatee fi nama ilaalcha qabduun, Huq sirna 'Adaptation Days' jalqabe; sagantaa kanaan qonnaan bultoota Baangilaadesh keessaa sagalee isaanii sadarkaa addunyaa biraan ga'ee jira. Hiriyoonni fi namoonni itti dhiyaatan Hundinuu Huq akka nama icciitii, obsaa, shaakala gaarii fi nama dhiibbaa geessu yaadatu. Saayintistoota dhaloota haarawaa biyyoota guddina hin ga'in irraa gorsaa fi wal-qunnamtii addunyaatti walitti hidhuun isaa ni eegama. Dr. Huq haadha manaa, ilmaa fi intala isaa dhiisee boqote.

Prince Francis Omo-Osunde Iyasere, a prominent figure and former State Publicity Secretary of the Peoples Democratic Party (PDP) in Edo State, has appealed to party leaders to pursue peaceful reconciliation amid ongoing internal disputes. Speaking to journalists in Benin on Sunday, Iyasere cautioned that continued infighting could diminish the PDP's prospects in next year’s governorship election.

He remarked, "It is time to put an end to internal wrangling within the party so we can stay focused on the goal of winning the upcoming governorship election." Iyasere critiqued the All Progressives Congress (APC), asserting that in the past eight years, the ruling party has acted recklessly and failed to prioritize the welfare of Nigerians. He stressed the importance for the PDP to position itself as a credible and people-oriented alternative capable of attracting dissatisfied citizens.

Highlighting that internal disagreements are common to all political parties, Iyasere urged quick and conscientious resolution of such disputes for the stability and electoral success of the PDP. He praised notable leaders like Secretary to the State Government Barrister Osarodion Ogie and Edo South senatorial district leader Owere Dickson Imasogie for their dedication to party unity and reconciliation, condemning malicious attacks against them, especially on platforms like the Edo PDP WhatsApp group.

Iyasere referenced the APC in Rivers State as an example, noting their effective management of internal discord, including former governor Rotimi Amaechi, which enabled a PDP member to secure a ministerial appointment. He emphasized that with less than a year before a major election, the PDP must rally behind its leaders, resolve internal issues, and focus on winning the trust and votes of Edo State's electorate.

Gaazexeessitoota waliin magaalaa Beniin keessatti yeroo dubbatu, Iyasere, waldhabdeen paartichaa itti fufuun carraa PDP bara dhufu filannoo mootummaa naannoo mo’achuuf qabdu akka laaffisu akeekkachiise.

Akka jedhetti, "Waan guddaa tokko irratti xiyyeeffachuuf, waldhabdee keessaa dhaabuun yeroon isaa ga'ee jira, filannoo mootummaa naannoo fuulduratti mo'uuf tokkummaan barbaachisaadha." Iyasere paartii mootummaa All Progressives Congress (APC) waggoota saddeet darban ummata miidhaa jiraachu fi bareedina uummataaf hin kennine jechuun qeeqe. Inni PDP akka filannoon irratti hunda'ee fi dubartoota jibbe jiraateef madda filannaa garii ta'uuf qophaa'u qaba jedhe.

Waldiddeen keessatti paartii kamuu akka jiru himuun, Iyasere, waldhabbii akkasi saffisaan fi obsaan hammatamee furuun bu'uura tokkummaa fi injifannoo filannoo paartichaa akka ta'e hubachiise. Hogganoota akka SSG Barrista Osarodion Ogie fi hogganaa naannoo sensaatorii Owere Dickson Imasogie, tokkummaa paartii fi araara buusuuf hojjetan galateeffatee, namoota hoggantoota irratti komii fi haasawa dogoggoraa irratti gabaasan, keessumaa garee WhatsApp PDP irratti, qeeqe.

Fakkeenyummaa Rivers State APC irratti, Iyasere, walitti bu'iinsa isaanii Rotimi Amaechi dabalatee tasgabbeessuun isaanii, miseensi PDP tokkon bakka ministeeraa argachuu danda’eera jedhe. Waggaan filannoo guddaan hafu xiqqaateera; PDP hoggantoota ishee jalatti gamtaa ta'uu fi gara injifannoo fi amanamummaa uummata Edo State irratti xiyyeeffachuu qabdu jedhe.

article_content: When the Super Bowl comes to a city, it transforms the whole area into a festival packed with excitement, famous faces, and endless entertainment. British journalists visiting their first American Super Bowl were amazed by the extensive festivities, noting that major UK events like the FA Cup final are much tamer in comparison. In the buildup to Super Bowl 49, Glendale, Arizona bustled with activity. The University of Phoenix Stadium was set for the clash between the New England Patriots and Seattle Seahawks, but the event was about more than just football. Massive concerts like one headlined by Calvin Harris pulled in huge crowds, and parties with stars like Nick Cannon, Nelly, Rihanna, Snoop Dogg, and Jason Derulo took place around the city. The festivities catered to everyone—even those who aren’t big football fans—with food, music, and activities for all. The vibrant atmosphere led some to wonder if English football might take inspiration and make major games more accessible and entertaining for fans. On the field, Super Bowl 49 promised a compelling showdown between Tom Brady, experienced and looking for his fourth championship, and Russell Wilson, the young talent returning to the final after leading the Seahawks just three years into his career. Analysts discussed whether the Patriots’ defense could contain Seattle’s offense, focusing on strategies like stopping the ‘read option.’ Meanwhile, the Seahawks’ elite ‘Legion of Boom’ secondary were expected to put pressure on Brady, who is known for staying in the pocket and waiting for receivers to get open. Key players and figures such as Rob Gronkowski, Bill Belichick, Pete Carroll, and Richard Sherman all featured in the buildup. Marshawn Lynch’s short answers at press conferences kept drawing attention, and NFL commissioner Roger Goodell addressed the importance of fulfilling obligations as professionals. Presenter Vernon Kay also shared memories of past Super Bowls, from attending the Steelers-Cardinals game and following the legendary Chicago Bears and Giants. These games left lasting impressions, becoming cherished family moments and traditions. Ultimately, the Super Bowl is more than just a match; it’s a weeklong celebration blending music, culture, sport, and community, leaving unforgettable memories for fans and newcomers alike.

Gorsitoota Biriitiin yeroo jalqabaaf Ameerikaa Super Bowl irratti argaman, bashannana ballinaan qophaa’e irratti raajii keessa seenan; yeroo taphni akka FA Cup biyya isaanii geggeeffamu hagam xiqqaate ta’e yaadatan. Dorgommii irratti, Super Bowl 49 tapha cimaa Tom Brady (dorgommii isaa afraffaa mo’achuuf qophaa’e) fi Russell Wilson (dorgommii lammataaf dorgomaa jiru) gidduutti adeemsa. Akkasumas, 'Legion of Boom' Seahawks waraqaa faila Brady irratti dhiibbaa gochuuf jiran; Brady yeroo hedduu bakka tokkotti dhaabbatee hirmaata. Taphoota akka Rob Gronkowski, Bill Belichick, Pete Carroll fi Richard Sherman irratti hammaachaa ture. Gocha irratti, Super Bowl tapha qofa osoo hin taane; torbaan guutuu ayyaana, muuziqaa, aadaa fi ispoortiin walitti makamee, yaadannoo hin dagatamne uuma.

Frank Tanabe, a World War II veteran who inspired many by choosing to vote even while battling end-stage liver cancer, passed away at 93. His daughter, Barbara Tanabe, reported his passing on Wednesday morning at her home in Honolulu. Tanabe’s commitment to voting became widely recognized after his nephew posted a photo of him—assisted by his daughter—completing his absentee ballot on Reddit, where it was viewed by hundreds of thousands of people.

Serving in the mostly Japanese-American Military Intelligence Service during World War II, Tanabe volunteered while interned at Tule Lake in California. Honolulu election officials stated that unless his death certificate is received and matched to his ballot before the November 6 election, his vote will be counted.

The image of Frank in bed as his daughter helped him select candidates resonated with internet users, making the post one of Reddit’s most popular that day. Many expressed respect for his patriotism and determination.

Diagnosed two months earlier with untreatable liver cancer, Frank had spent three weeks in home hospice but remained eager to vote, asking about his ballot’s arrival daily. He had Barbara read aloud the candidates’ names and indicated his choices by nodding or shaking his head, remaining engaged in current affairs up until recently.

Frank was pulled from college due to President Roosevelt’s internment order and volunteered for Army service from behind barbed wire. The Military Intelligence unit and other segregated Japanese-American battalions received the Congressional Gold Medal last year for their service.

Tanabe was known for his humility and once said he accepted the medal on behalf of all Americans who defended their country. His nephew, Noah, described Frank’s resilience and principle, highlighting his willingness to serve despite facing imprisonment and discrimination.

Barbara said the family was touched by the reaction online and believes Frank would be pleased to have inspired others to exercise their right to vote. Election officials added that ballots of voters who pass away before Election Day are only invalidated if death certificates are processed in time and the ballot identified—which is often impractical.

Ultimately, Barbara feels the best tribute to her father is that others are encouraged to participate in democracy, just as he hoped.

article_content: Jamie Inglis, a brave seven-year-old boy from York, is fighting an aggressive recurrence of neuroblastoma, a rare childhood cancer. Jamie has already survived neuroblastoma once, but the disease has returned. His parents, John and Vicky Inglis, are racing to raise £250,000 within 33 days to secure Jamie a place in a clinical trial in Germany, which is believed to improve his chance of survival by up to 75%. Jamie’s only viable treatment options in the UK could keep him alive for only a few months. The family is fundraising to cover the costs of the trial abroad, with significant support from chef Jamie Oliver, who encouraged his two million Twitter followers to contribute. The family has faced this battle once before. Jamie was diagnosed at age four, and after a series of challenging treatments in the UK and the US, including surgery, chemotherapy, and a pioneering antibody procedure in Philadelphia, he went into remission. At the time, they raised £400,000 through global donations. Recently, Jamie relapsed and underwent emergency surgery after collapsing due to back pain. However, the NHS advised there were no further effective treatment options available in the UK for Jamie’s case, and funding for overseas treatment was declined due to limited clinical evidence and resource constraints. Jamie’s parents remain committed to doing everything possible to save his life, even as they face the hardship of fundraising a large sum for a second time. They hope to get Jamie to Germany by August 20. John Inglis, who left the Royal Medical Corps after 22 years to spend more time with his family, emphasized the urgency and difficulty of their situation. The family has the support of medical professionals and has set up a donations page at http://www.justgiving.com/jamiesappeal. Statistics indicate about 120 children in the UK are diagnosed with neuroblastoma annually. Experts like Jo Dempster-Fowle of Neuroblastoma Alliance UK highlight the difficulty of treating high-risk neuroblastoma and call for more comprehensive care options for children.

article_content: Before Manchester United and Chelsea faced off at Old Trafford on Monday, anticipation was high. Chelsea had openly expressed interest in United striker Wayne Rooney, raising questions about whether the English forward would play. Despite Rooney submitting a transfer request at the end of last season, Manchester United have insisted that the 27-year-old is not for sale. In the end, Rooney started for United and played a full 90 minutes. Chelsea manager Jose Mourinho opted not to start a recognized striker, leaving $78 million signing Fernando Torres on the bench. Mourinho also omitted last season's standout player Juan Mata from the lineup. Ultimately, both teams extended their unbeaten runs with a lackluster 0-0 draw. This was David Moyes' first home game at the helm of Manchester United after replacing Alex Ferguson. The match marked the first scoreless league draw at Old Trafford in four years. While the pre-match buzz was notable, the game itself failed to deliver excitement, and post-match comments from the managers provided further intrigue. Asked about reports of a club other than Real Madrid bidding for Tottenham's Gareth Bale, Moyes did not deny that United could be involved, stating, 'Manchester United will always be interested in the best players. We're always looking to try to improve the team and the owners have given me every opportunity to bring in whoever I want.' Mourinho, meanwhile, did not rule out another Chelsea bid for Rooney but noted that the crowd's strong support for the striker could make a move away difficult. Rooney showed determination throughout the game, particularly in tracking back to dispossess Ramires, and was arguably United's standout performer. "(United fans) supported him all the way so I think this is a real special club with special fans and I think probably now he decides he wants to stay," Mourinho told Sky Sports. With seven points from three matches, Chelsea sits atop the standings, having played one fixture more due to their upcoming Super Cup against Bayern Munich. United, Chelsea, and Manchester City are expected to contest the league title, but City have already stumbled with a 3-2 defeat at newly promoted Cardiff. "I told the players before the game we want to win, we will play to win, but if you don't win, you don't lose," Mourinho commented. "I think the players understood this completely." The first half of Monday's match was uneventful, with United's Robin van Persie coming closest by hitting the side netting. Antonio Valencia avoided a yellow card after fouling Oscar. As halftime approached, Rooney nearly set up van Persie, but his pass was too strong. United showed greater urgency early in the second half, and Danny Welbeck, who scored twice against Swansea last week, missed a good chance after a Rooney pass. Chelsea's striker-less system could not replicate the effectiveness of Spain's national team, leading Mourinho to introduce Torres in the 60th minute. United appealed for a penalty when Tom Cleverley's shot struck Frank Lampard's arm, but referee Martin Atkinson waved play on. "I think that's two in a week that Chelsea has had ... which have been good shouts," Moyes said, referring to a similar incident in the previous match against Villa. Rooney forced a diving save from Petr Cech in the 77th minute, and from the resulting corner, Welbeck mistimed his header. As the match neared a close, Chelsea seemed content with a draw, signaled by Mourinho's substitution of Kevin de Bruyne with defensive midfielder John Obi Mikel. In Spain, Real Madrid maintained a perfect start to the season, matching Barcelona with a 1-0 win at Granada. Karim Benzema scored the game's only goal in the 10th minute. Real Madrid could have increased their lead, but Isco hit the post and Cristiano Ronaldo was denied by goalkeeper Roberto.
