Waggaa sadaffaa keessa, Ameerikaa Kaabaa keessatti guddinni xinnaa ture, garuu gurgurtaa waggaa dabre irraa 11.1% ol guddachuu danda’e, sababni isaa imaltoota biyya keessaa fi alaa Ameerikaa keessatti dabalaa dhufani. Gareen Dufry Kaanadaa irraa imaltoota Asia muraasa irraa fayyadame, garuu deebiin sirrii hin jiru. Ameerikaa Kaabaa Dufry-Autogrill irraa %31 galii keessaa qaba, Q3 keessatti $1.19 biliyoona gahe. Banuu daldalaa haaraa fi waliigaltee bara dheeraa Harry Reid Airport Las Vegas keessatti, akkasumas waggaa 12f hidhaa daldalaa Boston Logan Airport Terminal E keessatti argachuun baay’ee gargaare. Kompaniin hojii nyaataa fi dhugaatii iddoo gara garaa; keessumaa Chicago O’Hare, Atlanta, Orlando, Jacksonville, Fort Lauderdale fi San José keessatti bal’inaan babal’ise. Asia-Pacific, sadarkaa xiqqaa irratti argamu iyyuu, guddina dabalataa 45% jechuun $149 miliyoona Q3 galmeessise; kunis imaltoota biyyaaf keessaa fi naannoo jiru irraa argameera. Imaltoonni alaa irra deebiin ifatti hin mul’anne. Chaayinaa keessatti Dufry fi Hubei Airport Group waliin hojjechuun, tajaajila daldalaa fi nyaata Wuhan Tianhe Airport Terminal 2 irratti waliigaltee seenan; sanada 27 miliyoona imaltoota bara 2019 tajaajile. EMEA (Awurooppaa, Gidduu Baha fi Afrikaa)—kutaa Dufry-Autogrill keessaa olaanaa tahe—%52 gurgurtaa qabaachuun, %12.3 dabaluun $2.21 biliyoona Q3 galmeessise, iddoo imaltoota bal’oodhaan Mediteraaniyaaniin durfamee. UK, Nordic fi Europe Giddu Galeessaa keessatti imaltoota alaa dabalataan argaman, kan keessaa kan Asia-Pacific irra deebi’anii dhufan. Dufry hojii haarawa jalqabuun, perfumery iddoo ol’aanaa Zurich Airport irratti bananii, iddoo biroo dhiyoo keessa bira gahuuf karoorfatan. Hojii hunda irratti, gurgurtaan wal-fakkaatu 14.3% Q3 dabaluun $4 biliyoona ol waan gahe. Dureessa Xavier Rossinyol akka jedhutti, kun gabaasa maallaqa isa dhumaa maqaa Dufry jalatti dhiyaatu. Rossinyol dorgommii gabaa, hojiin makaa fi baasii madaaluu barameera; bu’aa walitti makamiinsi galmeessee ($94 miliyoona) waggaa tokko dura argameera. Haaluma gara fuulduraa jiru irratti hunda’ee, Dufry-Autogrill waggaatti %20 ol guddina galii eegama; galii waggaa guutuu $11.9 biliyoona akka ga’u tilmaama jiru.

article_content: An impressive lineup of footballs illustrates the rich history of the balls used in FIFA World Cups. This year’s FIFA World Cup football joins a distinguished collection of twelve iconic balls, each representing a milestone in the evolution of the beautiful game. The latest ball, named the 'Brazuca'—a term meaning ‘Brazilian’—marks the twelfth official World Cup ball produced by Adidas. Over the years, football design has shifted dramatically: gone are the heavy pigskin constructions and visible stitching of the 1950s. Modern players like Neymar and Rooney now play with balls made from just six panels, offering enhanced grip, touch, stability, and aerodynamics. The Brazuca underwent extensive testing with 600 footballers over two and a half years, with the aim of addressing criticisms of the previous Jabulani ball from the 2010 World Cup in South Africa. The Brazuca’s colorful and ribboned design symbolizes the vibrancy and energy associated with football culture in Brazil, while also representing an important piece of the sport’s history.  Historic World Cup Balls: - 1970, Mexico: The Telstar was the first World Cup ball Adidas produced, with 32 panels and 12 black pentagons for visibility on black-and-white TV. Brazil won this tournament. - 1974, Germany: Adidas introduced the Telstar Durlast, distinguished by a polyurethane coating for waterproofing and durability. The Chile Durlast, an all-white version, was also used. Hosts West Germany claimed victory. - 1978, Argentina: The 'Tango' debuted with a trademark print of interlocking triangles ('triads') inspired by Argentine passion and elegance. Argentina won this tournament. - 1982, Spain: The Tango España, combining real leather and synthetic materials in 32 hand-sewn panels, featured circles formed by curved triangle motifs. Italy and Paolo Rossi made headlines as top performers. - 1986, Mexico: The Azteca was the first fully synthetic, hand-sewn World Cup ball, offering durability, stability, and enhanced performance in tough conditions. Its design drew inspiration from Aztec art. Argentina, under Maradona, triumphed. - 1990, Italy: The Etrusco Unico featured an Etruscan lion motif and synthetic fiber layers, including latex. West Germany secured the title. - 1994, USA: Named Questra, this ball integrated space-age technology, including polystyrene foam for softness and control. Brazil captured its fourth trophy. - 1998, France: The Tricolore displayed France's national colors and symbols, utilized new synthetic 'syntactic foam' for compression and rebound, and saw France crowned champions. - 2002, Japan/South Korea: Fevernova incorporated advanced materials and designs. Over 2,500 match balls supported the event, which Brazil won. - 2006, Germany: Teamgeist, Adidas’ best-performing ball up to that point, featured a 14-panel design and underwent rigorous scientific testing for precision and consistency. Italy emerged victorious. - 2010, South Africa: The Jabulani ('to celebrate' in Zulu) used innovative grip-and-groove thermally bonded panels for aerodynamics, but faced criticism from players, especially goalkeepers. Spain clinched its first title with Iniesta’s extra-time goal.  Each of these balls, with their unique designs and technological advancements, not only reflects the spirit and culture of its World Cup but also traces the ongoing progress in football equipment and its impact on the sport’s history.

article_content: Shares of sugar companies were among the top gainers on Thursday, driven by expectations of higher prices due to possible supply shortages in key states such as Maharashtra and Karnataka. Out of 35 sugar stocks on the BSE, 30 saw gains. Avadh Sugar rose by 13.2%, Magadh Sugar by 12.8%, and DCM Shriram by 10%. Analysts anticipate further increases in some of these stocks. 'Sugar stocks have mostly consolidated in the last six months but recently reported strong results,' said Dharmesh Shah, Technical Analyst at ICICI Securities. 'We expect a technical upside of 5-10% in these stocks in the near term.' He recommended buying Balrampur Chini, Uttam Sugar, Dhampur Sugar, and Dalmia Sugar. Previously, sugar stocks climbed on concerns that insufficient rainfall in Maharashtra and Karnataka could reduce sugar production. According to a Times of India report in October, the Central Pollution Control Board ordered the closure of 45 sugar factories in Maharashtra for violating environmental regulations. Analysts said sugar supply could be disrupted in these states. 'Strikes by farmers in Maharashtra and poor rainfall in Maharashtra and Karnataka have affected sugar production,' said AK Prabhakar, Head of Research at IDBI Capital. 'Mills in Uttar Pradesh, Tamil Nadu, and Andhra Pradesh have benefited, with their stocks rallying today.' He recommends EID Parry and Balrampur Chini. However, some experts believe that lower supply pressures might not lead to higher sugar prices in India. 'Globally, sugar prices have risen significantly, but in India, prices are regulated by export restrictions and are likely to remain stable until after the general elections,' said Sandip Sabharwal, founder of asksandipsabharwal.com, an investment advisory. Other news: Tesla is considering investing up to $2 billion to set up a factory in India if given tax concessions on imports for the first two years. The government may also revise its resource distribution formula to increase the emphasis on human development and sustainability. There is also growing visibility of women in leadership roles and boardroom conflicts in Indian companies.

article_content: Following his passing, many have revisited Matthew Perry’s career to appreciate his numerous contributions to film and television. While Perry is best known for his iconic role on 'Friends', he brought charisma and talent to a variety of other projects. Although Perry never matched the extraordinary success of 'Friends', he consistently captivated audiences through both comedic and dramatic roles. His final film, '17 Again', stands out as an underrated comedy where Perry brings depth and vulnerability. The movie, starring Zac Efron, tells the story of a middle-aged man given the chance to relive his youth. Perry’s appearances in the film, especially at the beginning and end, help elevate its charm. 'The Odd Couple' reboot, where Perry starred as Oscar Madison alongside Thomas Lennon's Felix Unger, showcased his enduring comedic timing. Perry also contributed as an executive producer, bringing new life to the classic sitcom’s dynamic. In 'Go On', Perry played a sports radio host coping with the loss of his wife. The show blended comedy with sincere explorations of grief, allowing Perry to display a more dramatic side while retaining his signature wit. Perry’s first major TV role post-'Friends' was in 'Studio 60 on the Sunset Strip', written by Aaron Sorkin. Set behind the scenes of a sketch comedy show, this series offered Perry the opportunity to demonstrate his skill with sophisticated, fast-paced dialogue, even though the show never achieved major commercial success. Looking back at Perry’s earlier work, 'Fools Rush In' has become something of a sleeper hit. The romantic comedy, in which Perry stars alongside Salma Hayek, sees his character grappling with newfound responsibilities after an unexpected pregnancy. The film highlights Perry’s charm and his excellent on-screen chemistry with Hayek. Though his passing is a significant loss, Matthew Perry leaves behind a diverse legacy of memorable performances across television and film.

article_content:
Google has launched its 'About this image' feature for English-speaking users worldwide, aiming to provide more background and context for images shown in Google Search and Google Images. Announced at the I/O conference in May, this feature can be accessed through the three-dot menu next to image results. It offers details on the image’s source, shows metadata (like whether the picture is AI-generated), and summarizes how news outlets and fact-checkers have described it over time.

The feature is designed to help tackle misinformation online—especially prominent during crises such as the Israel-Hamas conflict, where unrelated or misleading images sometimes circulate online. By using 'About this image,' people can often see when Google first indexed an image and if reliable sources have flagged it.

Additional ways to access this information, like searching through Google Lens, right-click or long-press in Chrome, or swiping up in the Google App, are in development and will be added gradually. According to spokesperson Ned Adriance, these features will arrive in the coming months.

Google is also updating its Fact Check Explorer, which allows users to upload images or enter URLs to search for fact-checks. An API is being introduced so journalists and fact-checkers can better incorporate Fact Check Explorer into their tools and processes. Furthermore, the company is experimenting with using generative AI to provide more information about lesser-known sources in search results when other references, such as Wikipedia, are lacking. These AI-generated details will appear in the existing 'About this result' panel.

Ultimately, while these tools aim to support users in identifying authentic images, verifying content still depends on people actively checking information. Sharing misleading images remains easy on social media, so user vigilance remains key, even with new verification tools available.

article_content: Researchers at Queen’s University in Belfast have reported a promising non-surgical alternative for women with BRCA1 gene mutations, which are known to greatly increase the risk of breast and ovarian cancer. Until now, women carrying this mutation—like actress Angelina Jolie, who famously chose a preventative mastectomy—have often faced the difficult decision of undergoing surgery to remove their breasts and ovaries as a primary method of risk reduction. Currently, within the UK, approximately one in every 1,000 women carries the BRCA1 mutation. These individuals face up to an 85% likelihood of developing breast cancer and up to a 40% risk of ovarian cancer. The new findings suggest that drugs already available, specifically those that block oestrogen production, may offer another option for lowering cancer risk. The research showed a clear link between elevated oestrogen levels and DNA damage in the breast and ovaries among women with the BRCA1 gene mutation. According to Dr. Kienan Savage, the lead researcher, the cells of women with this mutation do not adequately protect themselves from high oestrogen exposure, making them particularly vulnerable to DNA damage that can lead to cancer. ‘This is a significant advancement for the treatment of women with the BRCA1 mutation,’ said Dr. Savage. ‘Our results provide the first solid evidence that oestrogen drives cancer in these women. This knowledge allows us to propose drug therapies as an alternative to surgery, and they could even be paused to allow for pregnancy if desired.’ The scientists believe that anti-oestrogen medications could decrease DNA damage and tumor development for people with the BRCA1 mutation, since their cells cannot handle high hormone levels. Dr. Savage noted that several such drugs are already on the market and could, in theory, be used to chemically reduce oestrogen, potentially avoiding irreversible surgical removal of healthy tissue. The research team is currently seeking funding for clinical trials, which they hope to commence within the next year. The initial study would involve 12 women taking a combination of two drugs over three months, with doctors tracking DNA damage using results from biopsies, blood, and urine samples.

article_content: Cardiff City manager Erol Bulut has emphasized protecting Jamilu Collins as the Nigerian left-back continues to recover from a serious knee injury. Consequently, Collins has been withdrawn from Nigeria’s upcoming international friendlies against Saudi Arabia and Mozambique. Nigeria is scheduled to play Saudi Arabia’s Green Falcons in Portimão, Portugal, on Friday, October 13, and will face Mozambique in the same city three days later. Although Collins was initially included in the squad by head coach Jose Peseiro, concerns over his fitness led the official Super Eagles X account to confirm on Monday that the 29-year-old would miss the international break. Chidozie Awaziem has been called up in his place. Collins, formerly of Paderborn, missed 45 Cardiff matches last season after a cruciate ligament injury against West Brom in August 2022 ruled him out for nine months. article_content: The Royal Family remains popular, yet a majority of Britons believe funding for some of its members should be reduced. While taxpayers are generally willing to support the Queen, the Duke of Edinburgh, Prince Charles, the Duchess of Cornwall, the Cambridges, and Prince Harry, a new YouGov poll reveals that most want funding cut for the rest. This would result in members such as Prince Andrew, the Princess Royal, the Wessexes, and Princesses Beatrice and Eugenie, among others, losing public subsidies. The idea is to have a 'core' Royal Family consisting of the heir and his immediate family. Currently, the Royal Family receives public funding primarily through the Sovereign Grant, which replaced the annual Civil List and three other grants in 2011, as well as from the Duchies of Lancaster and Cornwall. The Sovereign Grant is derived from revenues of the Crown Estate, now owned by the government, and gives the Royal Family £13.7 million annually for official duties. Taxpayers do not directly pay for all royal activities, but the cost of police protection for royals and politicians, funded via the Home Office, falls on the public. According to the YouGov poll, 69% of respondents said the Queen and Prince Philip should continue to receive funding, with 89% of Conservative voters agreeing, compared to 58% of Labour voters. A similar proportion supported funding for Prince Charles and the Duchess of Cornwall, and 59% for the Duke and Duchess of Cambridge and Prince George. Support drops for other royals: only 28% believe Prince Andrew should receive a subsidy, with similar numbers for Prince Edward. 39% support funding for the Princess Royal, while just 9% support for Princesses Beatrice and Eugenie. Although neither Zara Tindall nor Peter Phillips receives funding, 10% of Britons believe they should, more than those favoring payments to the Queen's cousins. Royal cousins still performing official duties and receiving subsidies include the Duke and Duchess of Gloucester and Prince and Princess Michael of Kent. The Queen and Prince Charles are holders of the Royal Duchies of Lancaster and Cornwall. Prince Harry, Prince William, Duchess Kate, and Prince George, meanwhile, are largely funded by the Duchy of Cornwall. The concept of a slimmed-down Royal Family has been discussed before and is part of Prince Charles's vision for the monarchy's future, centering on himself, Camilla, Prince Harry, and the Cambridges. This plan has seen some resistance: Prince Andrew is said to be particularly displeased at being marginalized, especially after his daughters were discouraged from taking royal duties. Charles, who assumed an enhanced role after the Diamond Jubilee in 2012, was reportedly behind the smaller group on the Buckingham Palace balcony for the Jubilee Flypast and the reduced attendance at Prince George's Christening in October 2013. Since then, Princess Beatrice and Princess Eugenie have focused more on their careers. The Duchies of Lancaster (held by the monarch) and Cornwall (held by the heir) have been the principal sources of royal funding for centuries. The Duchy of Lancaster, established in 1265, is held by the Queen, while Cornwall, created in 1337, is passed to the Prince of Wales. When Charles becomes king, he will be Duke of Lancaster, and Prince William will become Duke of Cornwall. Prince Harry could, in theory, become Duke of York, the traditional title for a monarch's second son, though this is undecided.

article_content: Lee Sentino, a 24-year-old barman from Manchester, has been living with an unusual fear of ketchup and other sauces that has impacted his ability to enjoy typical meals throughout his life. Sentino experiences strong physical reactions to all kinds of sauces and condiments, refusing to eat any foods he considers 'wet.' Whenever he is confronted with ketchup, gravy, custard, or HP Sauce, he begins gagging, feels nauseous, and breaks out in a cold sweat. He does not recall when his phobia began, but as a child, his family would prepare special dry meals for him. "I don't really know why I had this phobia. I used to joke that my mum would chase me around with a bottle of Heinz ketchup," Sentino said. "I would eat meals like everyone else, but my food always had to be dry. If my family had lasagne, I would have a separate meal. I could eat a roast dinner, but only without gravy," he added. Sentino always eats his toast dry and often has to request special meals when dining out. He is trying new foods, such as pies and certain puddings, in a personal effort to overcome his phobia. He describes feeling embarrassed when explaining his food preferences in public settings and has not sought counseling, believing he could manage the situation on his own. "I've had plenty of comments from others over the years, which only made me more anxious about it," he admitted. "It’s often challenging to eat out because most menus aren’t suited to my needs. I remember once ordering just a bowl of pasta in an Italian restaurant and seeing the server's confused reaction," he recalled. Recently, Sentino has started to confront his fear by trying new foods, but the thought of thick, bottled sauces like ketchup and brown sauce, as well as custard, still make him feel unwell. While this phobia seems unusual to many, experts note that several people report similar aversions to ketchup. Former spin doctor Alastair Campbell has publicly acknowledged his own mild fear of ketchup, often called 'saltomaphobia.' An extreme version is sometimes referred to as 'equusmortusphobia.'

article_content: Monica Lewinsky has started a new role as a columnist for Vanity Fair, as revealed in a recent post on the magazine's website. This appointment comes just a month after she openly discussed her past affair with former President Bill Clinton in a personal essay for the publication. In her first column, published Thursday, the 41-year-old shares her experience binge-watching 'Orange is the New Black.' While she found much of the show engaging, she admits that a joke referencing her infamous past made her uncomfortable. In episode eleven of the first season, a character uses Lewinsky's name in a joke while describing a sexual act, which Lewinsky says left her cringing and reminded her of feelings of embarrassment and loss of control over her story. She describes her reaction as a mix of shame and discomfort, ultimately deciding to turn off the television. Lewinsky also notes that today's media landscape is different, pointing out that social media now gives people in the spotlight more control over how they're perceived. She reflects on how, unlike in the 1990s during her own scandal, individuals can now use digital platforms to influence their public image and reclaim their narratives. Lewinsky suggests that her own writing may be an effort to do just that—to take back her story and reshape her public identity. When asked if Lewinsky would become a regular columnist, Vanity Fair has yet to respond.

article_content: Sir David Nicholson, chief executive of the NHS, has described hospitals as unsuitable settings for elderly and frail people. According to Nicholson, hospitals often fail to provide the best care for older patients and should not be the primary setting for their treatment. He emphasized the need to expand community care as the elderly population grows. Nicholson compared the current state of elderly care in hospitals to the treatment of mental health patients in large asylums during the 1960s and 1970s, which led to national scandals. He noted that about 40% of current hospital patients have some form of dementia, underlining the challenges hospitals face in caring for these individuals. He also referenced recent scandals, such as at Stafford Hospital, where poor care is believed to have contributed to the deaths of up to 1,200 patients. Nicholson argued that simply improving staff attitudes is not enough: a fundamental change in how the healthcare system treats older people is needed. His reforms include increasing the availability of community-based treatment and care centers, managing long-term conditions locally, and prioritizing prevention strategies such as fall prevention. Nicholson acknowledged that such changes could result in hospital closures, with specialized services concentrated in fewer locations. Public figures like Prince Charles and Health Secretary Jeremy Hunt have recently spoken about the difficulties facing elderly care in the UK, warning of risks to compassion and concerns about the normalization of poor treatment. As head of the NHS Commissioning Board, which will oversee all NHS services in England and manage an annual budget of £93 billion, Nicholson indicated that the Board will be transparent with the public about funding constraints, what the NHS can realistically deliver, and the implications of spending decisions.

Innis kunuunsa hawaasaa babal’isuun barbaachisaa ta’uu, sababa dulloomtootni heddummaachaa jiranitiin, jabeesse ibse. Akka bulchaa Giddugala Qindoominaa NHS, kan tajaajila NHS hunda England keessatti bulchu fi bajata waggaa £93 billiion guutuu bulchu ta’eetti, Nicholson, abbootii qabeenya waliin iftoominaa uumuu fi tajaajiloonni NHS hojjetan akkamitti akka irratti waliigalteen irra ga’uu akka ummataaf ibsu kaa’eera.

article_content: Stars from both the Hindi and South Indian film industries attended the opening night of the Jio MAMI Mumbai Film Festival. Notable guests included Priyanka Chopra Jonas, Sonam Kapoor, and Bhumi Pednekar, as well as Tamil superstar Kamal Haasan. Haasan presented the Excellence in Cinema Award (South Asia) to director-producer Mani Ratnam. In a significant announcement, Haasan and Ratnam revealed their first collaboration in 36 years: a film titled 'KH 234', which will be produced by Haasan’s Raaj Kamal Films International and Ratnam's Madras Talkies. Oscar-winning composer A.R. Rahman and cinematographer Ravi K Chandran are also attached to the project. Haasan and Ratnam last worked together on the 1987 film 'Nayakan'. A teaser for their new co-production is set for release on November 6. Priyanka Chopra Jonas, who also serves as the chairperson of the Mumbai Film Festival, presented the Excellence in Cinema Award (International) to Italian filmmaker Luca Guadagnino. Both Ratnam and Guadagnino will conduct master classes during the festival. The opening ceremony was held at the 2,000-seat Grand Theatre at the Nita Mukesh Ambani Cultural Centre (NMACC) and marks the festival's return as an in-person event after being held online during the pandemic. The festival is backed by Reliance Jio. In her opening speech, Chopra Jonas emphasized the festival’s support for new talent and the significant contributions of women in cinema, both on- and off-screen. Other stars in attendance included Kareena Kapoor, who stars in the opening night film 'The Buckingham Murders' directed by Hansal Mehta; Jim Sarbh, Emmy-nominated for 'Rocket Boys'; Aditi Rao Hydari; Siddharth; Vijay Varma; and Rasika Dugal. Mira Nair, head of the South Asia Competition jury, attended alongside fellow jurors David Michod, Isabel Sandoval, and Edouard Waintrop. Three pioneers of Indian cinema—Aruna Vasudev, Nasreen Munni Kabir, and Uma da Cunha—were honored with Lifetime Achievement Awards, presented respectively by Marco Mueller, Karan Johar, and Adoor Gopalakrishnan. Their roles in promoting Indian cinema globally have been significant. During the ceremony, Sonam Kapoor awarded the Best Book on Cinema to Prakash Magdum for 'The Mahatma on Celluloid: A Cinematic Biography'. Bhumi Pednekar presented the Dimensions Mumbai short film awards to Praveen Giri's 'Nightingales In The Cocoon' and Kumar Chheda's 'Halfway'. Vidhu Vinod Chopra presented best film in the Large Short Films Royal Stag competition to Sanjib Gogol's 'Summer Of Soul', while Sobhita Dhulipala presented best actor to James Elia for 'Vakuppu (The Clause)'. The Jio MAMI Mumbai Film Festival is screening more than 250 films during its 10-day run from October 27 to November 5.

article_content: Over 150 students at Anudanit Ashram school in Guhi, a remote village in Maharashtra, India, now benefit from two new classrooms funded in memory of Anni Dewani. Although Anni’s family still grieves her tragic loss, they have taken comfort knowing her legacy is transforming young lives. Situated 135 kilometers from Nasik, the school enrolls mostly children from tribal and rural backgrounds across 50 surrounding villages. The additional building, dedicated to Anni, has brought optimism to the community, even though Anni's story remains unfamiliar to most students and teachers. Funds for this school expansion were collected by UK charity Sewa, with both Anni’s and Shrien Dewani’s families contributing. About £12,000 of the total £15,394 came from Shrien Dewani’s family and was channeled through Wanvasi Kalyan Ashram, the NGO that manages the school. Headteacher Ishwar Lal has voiced deep appreciation for the improved facilities. Despite their gratitude, he shared that neither staff nor students truly know why the new classrooms bear Anni Dewani's name, learning only that she was described as a UK social activist. With the new extension completed in October last year, the school now has seven classrooms, enhancing the space for its 150-plus students. Yet the full story behind the building’s dedication remains a mystery locally. Anni Dewani, who lost her life to gun violence in Cape Town in 2010, is commemorated in India through these new educational opportunities. Wanvasi Kalyan Ashram secretary Sanjay Kulkarni has expressed the organization’s thanks for the added classrooms, noting their vital role in bringing education to children in a remote area. Despite the new addition, the school continues to require three more classrooms so that each year group has proper space, and hopes to secure further funding. Meanwhile, Anni’s mother, Nilam Hindocha, spoke publicly after Shrien Dewani’s acquittal, voicing her ongoing pain and dissatisfaction with the unresolved case of her daughter’s death.

Gargaarsa maallaqaa Anni Dewani yaadannoo isheetiin walitti qabameen kun kan raawwatame. Maatiin Anni gadda lubbuu ishee dhaban cinaa, gabbisa jireenya ijoollee kanaaf waan gaarii godhe jedhanii tasgabii argataniiru. Mana barumsaa kun fageenya kiiloo meetira 135 Nasik irraa jiru, ijoollee baadiyyaa fi gosa naannoo gandoota 50 qabaniif tajaajila kennaa jira. Mana barnootaa haaraa maqaa Anni’nif ijaarame kana irratti, barattoonni fi barsiisotni hedduun odeeffannoo ishee irratti hin qaban ta’us, kun gammachuu fi abdii hawaasichaaf fidaa jira. Qarshii £12,000 hanga jedhu maatii Shrien irraa kennamee, NGO’n Indiyaa, Wanvasi Kalyan Ashram jedhamu, mana barumsichatti geesse. Ishwar Lal, barsiisaa ol’aanaa manneen barnootaa, faayidaa manneen barnoota haaraa kanaaf galata galcheera. Ta’us, barattoonni fi barsiisotni maaliif maqaan Anni Dewani manneen barnootaa isaanii irratti argamu akka hin beekne ibsee, Anni akka hojjetaa hawaasaa UK keessatti turte qofa itti himame. Manneetii barnoota haaraan Onkololeessa bara darbee xumuramee, manneen barnoota torba ga’eera, carraan barattoota 150 oliif bakka dabalataa argamsiiseera. Haa ta’u malee, sababni maaliif maqaan isheetiin kennamee biratti ifa miti. Anni Dewani bara 2010, magaalaa Cape Town keessatti rukutamtee duute; amma garuu maqaan ishee ijoollee Indiyaaaf carraa barnootaa ta’eera. Sanjay Kulkarni, sekreeterii Wanvasi Kalyan Ashram, manneen barnootaa dabalataa kana irratti galata ibse; tajaajiloonni kun ijoollee ganda fagoo jiraatan barumsa argachuuf guddina guddaa fida jedhe. Haati Anni, Nilam Hindocha, erga himannaa Shrien Dewani irra bilisa baafame booda, gadda fi dhimmicha irratti dhiibbaan ishee hin deebi’amne jedha.

article_content: Apple has made a significant investment in Martin Scorsese’s latest film, “Killers of the Flower Moon.” Production costs are reportedly between $200 million and $250 million, including a $25 million payment to Leonardo DiCaprio. The tech giant, now valued at around $3 trillion, is making a major push into the film industry. Apple partnered with Paramount, and their 2020 announcement initially expected production costs between $180 million and $200 million. However, Bloomberg now estimates the budget may reach up to $250 million. The film, starring DiCaprio, Robert De Niro, and Lily Gladstone, dramatizes the murders within the Osage Nation after the discovery of oil. It premiered at the Cannes Film Festival and is set for theatrical release on October 20. Apple’s film strategy stands out. The company has financed movies like 'Killers of the Flower Moon,' Ridley Scott’s 'Napoleon,' and Matthew Vaughn’s 'Argylle,' using a hybrid release strategy. These Apple Original Films premiere in theaters first, with streaming on Apple TV+ following a 45-day window. This approach is risky, as some viewers may prefer seeing films in theaters rather than waiting for streaming. Nevertheless, Apple aims to attract renowned directors who value cinema releases, hoping that theater audiences will later subscribe to Apple TV+. In the competitive film market, Apple’s approach seeks to build a strong presence, even if it leads to short-term financial losses.

During the season-opening NFL game, Pittsburgh Steelers punt returner Antonio Brown attempted to leap over Cleveland Browns punter Spencer Lanning while returning a kick. However, Brown unintentionally kicked Lanning in the face during the hurdle attempt. Fortunately, Lanning was wearing a helmet, which absorbed the impact and prevented serious injury. The play resulted in a 15-yard penalty against the Steelers for unnecessary roughness. The incident drew both laughter and surprise from the crowd. Brown later said, "I tried to get over him. There was no intent to hurt him. It was just a bad outcome of a play."

The Steelers managed to hold on for a close 30-27 victory over the Browns. Key performances included Ben Roethlisberger who threw for 365 yards and a touchdown, Le'Veon Bell who totaled 197 yards with a touchdown, and Antonio Brown, who caught five passes for 116 yards and scored as well. Despite Cleveland closing the gap in the longstanding rivalry, they have not beaten the Steelers on the road in 11 years.

article_content: Tripura Transport Minister Sushanta Choudhury has officially launched a cashless payment system for the department’s services, urging officials to widely promote its usage. "The cashless system was initially introduced in West district in August. After conducting a case study to assess its reception, we have now rolled it out across all eight districts via videoconferencing," said Choudhury. He highlighted the transport department's significant contribution to state revenue, mentioning that it added Rs 115 crore to the government’s exchequer in 2022–2023. "We are targeting revenue collection of Rs 125 crore this year. The cashless system will play an important role in reaching this goal. Impressively, over 46% of all cashless transactions worldwide occur in India," he noted. Choudhury further shared that the department collected Rs 92.83 crore in 2021–22, Rs 87.93 crore in 2020–21, and Rs 97.14 crore in 2019–20. For the current year, the department raised Rs 73.87 crore from April to October 2023–24. He expressed confidence in surpassing the Rs 125 crore target in the next five months, aiming to make the transport department one of the highest revenue-generating divisions. Choudhury appealed to the public to adopt and promote the new cashless system.

article_content: Before the rise of large service stations and major coffee chains, drivers in the UK relied on traditional truck stops such as Peggy's Diner and the Blue Sky Cafe to refresh themselves during long journeys. These independent cafes, once a common sight along Britain's road network, have largely disappeared, replaced by expansive service areas. Photographer Sam Mellish traveled over 6,000 miles along the UK's major A roads, visiting and documenting the few remaining roadside cafes where drivers can still enjoy a hot drink and a bacon sandwich for less than £3.50. Mellish drank 'hundreds' of cups of tea while capturing images that celebrate the 'open road feeling' and a sense of nostalgic travel. Classic cafes like the Orchard Cafe near Greater London and Peggy's Diner in Antrim, Northern Ireland, represent a fading era, increasingly replaced by modern service stations. Mellish said, 'I wanted to capture the open road feeling, like in songs such as Route 66 or The Road to Hell. I traveled more than 6,000 miles, used 800 liters of petrol, and enjoyed countless cups of tea and bacon sandwiches for this project. Many of the independent cafes I photographed have since closed.' Historians and architectural experts, such as Catherine Croft from The Twentieth Century Society, expressed concern that these cafes are a unique and irreplaceable part of British heritage. Croft noted that, while rarely designed by famous architects, these buildings introduced many visitors to new styles and materials. She emphasized that the detailed design, from the buildings down to signage and napkins, makes them memorable. Sam's photos preserve a quickly vanishing world and reveal how these cafes tell rich stories about travel and culture in twentieth-century Britain. Social and cultural historian Joe Moran remarked that before the M1 motorway opened in 1959, roadside cafes and lavish road houses with amenities like swimming pools were popular with motorists. For truck drivers, simple 'greasy spoon' cafes like Kate's Cabin on the A1 and Berts on the A30 were favorites. Modern service stations, he said, have become bland, corporate spaces akin to shopping malls, resulting in a loss of character along the roads. According to Moran, even the A roads, once home to unique transport cafes, are now dominated by chain owners. While early service stations were stylish and attracted young people, attempts to cut costs led to dirty facilities and poor food. Now, these places are efficient but more expensive and lack individuality. He described today's services as a 'corporate-owned monoculture.' Mellish’s photographs and experiences are published in the book 'Roadside Britain,' published by Diesel Books. He emphasizes the value and character of these cafes, reflecting on the stories and sense of community they offer. Cafes like the Blue Sky Cafe in Norfolk, which has scenic coastal views, and others like the Farm Cafe (A17) and Midway Stop (A14), illustrate the variety and cultural significance of these roadside establishments. While modern service stations like London Gateway have largely overtaken the role of independent roadside cafes, Mellish’s work preserves the memory of these distinctive places.

Bakki nyaata aadaa kunnee, yeroo tokko bakka hedduu argaman, amma garuu dhaabbilee tajaajilaa bal’aan bakka bu’amaa jiru. Fakkataan Sam Mellish kiiloometira 6,000 oli UK keessaa daandiiwwan A ciccimoo irratti imalanii, bakka ciisichaa hafan keessaa gara bunaa ho’aa fi sandwiichii baakoniidhaan qar.3.50 gadiitti argamu suuraa baasaniiru. Mellish akkana jedhan: ‘Songota akka Route 66 yookaan The Road to Hell fakkaatan, amala bilisaa daandii qabachuuf barbaade. Kiiloometira 6,000 ol imale, litira paatroolii 800 fayyadame, bunaa fi sandwiichii baakoniidhaan gammade. Bakki ciisichaa hedduun yeroo jalqaba suuraa baase ammas cufamanii jiru.’ Seenaa fi ogeeyyiin ijaarsa, Catherine Croft kan The Twentieth Century Society keessaa, bakki ciisichaa kun aadaa biyyaatiin adda fi hin deebiin jedhan. Croft duraan bakki ijaarsa kanaan hin beekamne garuu, meeshaalee fi aadaa haaraa hedduu nama beeksisa jedhan. Suuraan Sam addunyaan kun hatattamaan baduu agarsiisa; akkasumas bakki kun seenaa imalaa fi aadaa bara 20ffaa hedduu nutti hima. Seenaa fi qorataan aadaa Joe Moran, dura M1 motorway bara 1959 banamuu irra kaasee, bakki ciisicha fi iddoo bashannanaa bal’inaan beekaman akka owwisa bishaani fi bakka taphaa qabani jiru ibsan. Konkolaachistoonni gurguddoo irratti ‘greasy spoon’ akka Kate’s Cabin A1 fi Berts A30 irra hedduu gargaaramu turan. Amma dhaabbileen tajaajilaa ammayyaatti, Moran akka jedhanitti, bakka bashannanaa addaa irraa gara bakka dullacha daldalaa fakkaataniitti jijjiiraman. Moran akka dubbatanitti, A roads kanneen duraan cafe transport olu qaba turan, ammas chaanota dhuunfaatti dabraa jiru. Dhaabbileen tajaajilaa jalqabaa bashanana turaniiru; garuu yeroo tajaajilaan gatiin gadi bu'u ijaarsi ukkaamame, nyaati gaarii dhabamee jira. Amma garuu tajaajilaan gaariidha, garuu qarshii baay’ee barbaachisa, fakkeenya addaa hin qaban. Yeroo ammaa kana ‘corporate-owned monoculture’ jedhamu keessaa jira jedhan. Suuraawwanfi muuxannoon Mellish kitaaba ‘Roadside Britain’ jedhamu Diesel Books keessatti maxxanfamee jira. Qaama barbaachisaa fi addaddaa bakki ciisichaa kun seenaa fi hawaasa keenya beeksisa. Bakkoo akka Blue Sky Cafe (Norfolk), bakka faayidaa baay’ee qabu, Farm Cafe (A17) fi Midway Stop (A14) agarsiisan, garagaraa fi aadaa guddaa qabuun agarsiisu. Yeroo ammaa kana dhaabbileen tajaajilaa akka London Gateway iddoo boka ciisichaa dhuunfaa baay’ee bakka bu’an jiru; hojii Mellish irra deebiin yaadannoo bakka adda kana keessatti tursiisuuf gargaara.

article_content: In a recent article published in Molecular Cell, Ali Shilatifard, Ph.D., the Robert Francis Furchgott Professor and Chair of Biochemistry and Molecular Genetics, along with Yuki Aoi, Ph.D., a postdoctoral fellow in the Shilatifard laboratory, provided a comprehensive overview of the elongation stage of DNA transcription. Their review explores the central role of transcription elongation in regulating gene expression and examines how its dysregulation is linked to developmental defects, disease, and aging. Transcription elongation is the process by which RNA polymerase II, a complex multi-protein enzyme, moves along a DNA strand, copying genetic information into RNA. This RNA is then converted into different proteins, sustaining various cellular processes. The regulation of transcription elongation depends on multiple intracellular factors working in concert, as recent research from the Shilatifard laboratory and others over the past two decades has demonstrated. Shilatifard first identified the connection between transcription elongation control and cancer in 1996, in a study published in Science. This research was the first to demonstrate that the control of transcription elongation is a key step in the proper regulation of gene expression—a discovery that paved the way for further research into how its disruption contributes to disease and aging. "What we showed almost 30 years ago is that elongation is a central regulatory step and that its misregulation can cause leukemia. Now, we and other researchers have learned that transcription elongation control is crucial across numerous cellular processes," Shilatifard stated. In their review, Shilatifard and Aoi outline current understandings of the mechanisms controlling transcriptional elongation, and highlight innovative genetic engineering techniques that have allowed researchers to uncover its unique biological roles. The authors discuss recent in vivo studies, including those from the Shilatifard lab, which shed light on intracellular factors that control transcription elongation. These factors may serve as potential therapeutic targets to treat various diseases or possibly slow or reverse aspects of aging. "We and others have made a series of fascinating discoveries highlighting the crucial role of transcriptional elongation by RNA polymerase II—also known as Pol II elongation—in gene regulation, disease, and aging," said Yuki Aoi, Ph.D., lead author of the editorial. "We are confident that our article will propel future research into both the mechanisms and physiological significance of Pol II elongation, ultimately advancing our understanding of disease and aging," Aoi added.

Qorannoon isaanii, gahee transcription elongation gene expression irratti qabu, fi erga to'annoon isaa dogoggoramuu rakkoo guddinaa, dhukkubaa fi dulloomina uumu ibsa. Transcription elongation jechuun, RNA polymerase II, enzaayimiin baayyee protiniin qabu, keessatti DNA irra deemuun RNA tolchuu jechuu dha. RNA sun gara proteniitti jijjiiramee hojiiwwan seelii gara garaa deeggara. To'annoo elongation transcription keessatti, wantoota seelii keessaa hedduun waliin hojjechuun barbaachisaa ta'uusaa qorannoon Shilatifard fi biroo waggoota 20 darban argisiisan. Shilatifard bara 1996, qorannoo isaaniitiin elongation transcription fi kansarii wal qabsiisuun, Science irratti maxxanfame, agarsiisaniiru. Qorannichi to'annoo elongation transcription seensa barbaachisaa gene expression ta'uu muul'iseera — kunis qorannoo itti aanuuf bu'uura ta'e, akkasumas rakkoo fi dulloominaaf akka sababa ta'u mul’ise. "Waggaa 30 dura agarsiisne elongation to'annoo murteessaa ta'uu fi yoo dogoggoramne lewkiimiyaa fiduu danda'u. Amma, nuti fi qorattoonni biroon transcription elongation seelota gara garaatti gahee murteessa qabaachuu isaa barree jirra," jedhan Shilatifard. Qorannoo isaanii keessatti, Shilatifard fi Aoi, qarqaarsa teknooloojii injinariin jinii haarawaa fi xiinxalaa haaraa gargaaruun gahee transcription elongation akkamiin to’atamu ibsu; akkasumas qorannoon in vivo, fakkeenyaaf kan Shilatifard laboratooriirraa, wantoota elongation to'atan adda baasu. Wantoonni kunneen filannoo furmaata dhukkuba garaa garaaf ykn ariitiin dulloominaa ittisuuf gargaara. "Nuti fi qorattoonni biroo, gahee transcriptional elongation RNA polymerase II (Pol II elongation) keessatti bu'aa isaa murteessaa gene too'annoo, dhukkuba fi dulloomsaa keessatti agarsiisaa jirra," jedhan Yuki Aoi, Ph.D., barreessaa xalayaa kanaa. "Yeroon barruuleen keenya qorannoo fuulduraa, Pol II elongation akkamitti seelii namaa keessatti hojjatu fi isaan barbaachisummaa isaa qorachuun fayyadama hubannoo dhukkubaa fi dulloomina irratti guddina ni fidda jechuun amanna," jedhan Aoi dabalanii.

Manchester City has once again been handed a difficult group for the Champions League, marking the third consecutive season they face a 'Group of Death.' City's Group E—featuring Bayern Munich, Roma, and CSKA Moscow—is widely considered one of the toughest. Manager Manuel Pellegrini now faces a challenging path, while Chelsea, managed by Jose Mourinho, appears to have an easier route in the competition after being drawn against Schalke, Sporting Lisbon, and Maribor.

City’s group presents several storylines. They will play Bayern Munich for the second year in a row, facing Pep Guardiola’s team, who are strong contenders following Germany's World Cup victory. They also face a rejuvenated Roma, with Gervinho in top form, and CSKA Moscow. A unique subplot could see Frank Lampard and Ashley Cole, both formerly of Chelsea, play against each other for the first time since leaving the club. Pellegrini acknowledges that the fixtures against Roma and CSKA Moscow will be crucial for progressing to the last 16.

City’s difficult schedule is compounded by an intense period next month with matches against Bayern Munich, Arsenal, and Chelsea.

Sports director Txiki Beguiristain commented, 'Our challenge is to finish first in the group to gain an advantage. The objective is higher now—we’ve strengthened the team to compete both domestically and in Europe. There are eight other teams that could win it, but we believe we can as well.'

Arsenal faces its own challenges after being drawn with Borussia Dortmund, Galatasaray, and Anderlecht. They will meet Jurgen Klopp’s Dortmund for another group stage rematch. Last season, Arsenal lost at home to Dortmund but won the away fixture thanks to Aaron Ramsey’s goal, ultimately advancing from the group in second place. Arsenal secretary David Miles said, 'It’s tough but the aim is to finish first and avoid facing the likes of Barcelona early in the knockout rounds.'

Liverpool will compete against Real Madrid, Basel, and Ludogorets. Meanwhile, Chelsea’s comparatively easy group—against Schalke, Sporting Lisbon, and Maribor—has likely given Mourinho little to worry about, though he is expected to downplay any talk of an easy path.

The draws have sparked mixed feelings among the English clubs, with City, Arsenal, and Liverpool facing demanding fixtures as Chelsea prepare for what appears to be a smoother campaign.

article_content: A century-old Rolls-Royce originally crafted for Indian royalty is soon to be auctioned, with experts predicting it could fetch up to £400,000. This 1911 Rolls-Royce Silver Ghost was tailor-made for Maharaja Krishna Raja Wodeyar IV of Mysore, featuring a distinctive colorful umbrella to shade his attendants from the sun—a detail reminiscent of the cartoon character Penelope Pitstop. Rolls-Royce vehicles were prized among Indian nobility for their durability, making them suitable for difficult terrain. The Maharaja, who was known for his vast fortune—estimated at a modern equivalent of £35 billion—was a dedicated Rolls-Royce customer, often ordering several cars at a time. Within the company, bulk orders from Mysore were dubbed ‘doing a Mysore.’ As the 24th ruler of Mysore’s Wodeyar dynasty, which held power from 1399 to 1947, Krishna Raja Wodeyar IV was revered and referred to as ‘Rajarshi’ or ‘Saintly King’ by Mahatma Gandhi. This noteworthy Silver Ghost 40/50hp Six Cylinder, now part of a private collection, will be put up for sale by Bonhams at the Goodwood Revival event on September 16. A Bonhams representative explained that the Silver Ghost established Rolls-Royce’s status for producing 'the best car in the world.' Launched in 1907, the 40/50hp Six Cylinder became known as the ‘Silver Ghost’ due to its acclaimed test car with quiet operation and performance. Collectors are eager to acquire Silver Ghosts from each year of pre-war production. Another highlight of the auction is a 1908 Rolls-Royce Silver Ghost—one of only four left from that year, carefully restored during the 1990s.

Rolls-Royce Silver Ghost bara 1911, kan Maaharajaa Krishna Raja Wodeyar IV kan Mysoref adda ta’een hojjetame, boolla magariisaa halluun ittiin tajaajiltoota isaa aduu jalaa eeguuf itti dabalame argata—kunis midhaagana Penelope Pitstop kan kartonii fakkaata. Dhaabbatichis ajajaa baay’ee kan Mysore irraa dhufe ‘hojiin Mysore godhu’ jedhee waama ture. Konkolaataan addaa Silver Ghost 40/50hp Six Cylinder kun, kan dhalataa dhuunfaatiin qabame, Bonhams’n Fulbaana 16 Goodwood Revival irratti gurguruuf qopheesseera. Namni Bonhams irraa jedhan, Silver Ghost maqaa ‘konkolaataa addunyaa isa hangafaa’ abadummaatti argate. After more than 20 months and numerous regulatory hurdles, Microsoft has completed its $69 billion acquisition of Activision Blizzard. This development comes despite significant efforts by US and UK authorities to prevent tech giants from expanding their influence. Microsoft's acquisition of the Call of Duty publisher underscores the enduring power of major technology companies, even in the face of regulatory resistance.

The final challenge to the deal arose in April, when the UK's Competition and Markets Authority (CMA) blocked the acquisition. However, the CMA reversed its decision today, clearing the way for Microsoft to finalize the purchase. "We now have all regulatory approvals necessary to close, and we look forward to bringing joy and connection to even more players around the world," said Activision Blizzard CEO Bobby Kotick in a statement to employees.

This deal marks a major shift for the gaming industry, with Microsoft gaining a significant market share. A notable factor in the UK’s reversal was its concern over cloud gaming. In August, Activision Blizzard agreed to sell its non-European cloud gaming rights to Ubisoft, a move the CMA believes will safeguard competition in this fast-developing sector. CMA chief Sarah Cardell stated, "We delivered a clear message to Microsoft that the deal would be blocked unless they comprehensively addressed our concerns... With the sale of Activision’s cloud streaming rights to Ubisoft, we’ve made sure Microsoft can’t dominate this crucial and rapidly evolving market."

Despite these measures, the acquisition is still a significant consolidation within the gaming industry. The US Federal Trade Commission (FTC) originally filed a lawsuit in December to stop the deal, expressing concerns that Microsoft could suppress competitors to Xbox consoles and its growing subscription and cloud gaming businesses. In July, a California judge declined the FTC’s request for an injunction after Microsoft pledged to keep Call of Duty on PlayStation for ten years and to bring it to Nintendo Switch. The FTC remains involved, continuing its appeal, with a hearing set for December. FTC spokesperson Victoria Graham remarked, "Microsoft and Activision’s new agreement with Ubisoft presents a new aspect to the merger that will affect American consumers. The FTC continues to believe this deal poses a threat to competition."

With the acquisition, Microsoft now incorporates nine Blizzard studios and approximately 8,500 Activision employees. In addition, the company will be able to offer even more games via Xbox Game Pass. The long-term impact on gamers remains uncertain, but Microsoft Gaming CEO Phil Spencer addressed possible concerns in a statement: "Whether you play on Xbox, PlayStation, Nintendo, PC, or mobile, you are welcome here—and will remain welcome, even if Xbox isn’t where you play your favorite franchise. When everyone plays, we all win."

For now, the win goes to Microsoft.

Ji’oota 20 olfi rakkinoota seeraa gurguddoo booda, Microsoft bitannoo dolaara biliyoona 69 ta’uun Activision Blizzard raawwatteetti. Microsoft'n bitannoo Activision Blizzard’n beekamu kanaan, humna kampaniileen teknoolojii gurguddaan qabaniif ragaa ta'ee jira.

Rakkoon dhumaa Ebla keessa ture, yeroo Giddugala Dorgommii UK (CMA) bitannoo kana ugguree ture. Amma garuu, CMA murtee isaa deebisee, Microsoft bitannoo xumuruuf eeyyamni guutuu akka argatu taasiseera. "Hayyama hundaa argannee qofa hafee, gammachuu fi walqunnamtii taphattoota addunyaa mara bira geenya jennee abdi qabna,” jedhe Bobby Kotick, Abbaa Taayitaa Activision Blizzard, ibsa hojjettootaaf kenneen.

Waligalatti, bitannoon kun suuta suuta industirii tapha keessatti jijjiirama guddaa fida, Microsoft dorgommii cimaa argate. UK gara murtee haarayattti akka deebi’u godheef, yaaddoo cloud gaming irratti hundooftee turte. Hagayya keessa, Activision Blizzard mirga cloud gaming Europe alaa jiruu Ubisofttti gurguruun, dorgommii taphni kun itti fufu akka danda’u CMA’n amaneera. Sarah Cardell, hooggantuu CMA, “Microsoftn rakko keenya guutuu guutuutti kan haqee hin dhiisin taanaan bitannoof hayyama kennuu hin dandeenyu jenneerra. Mirgi cloud streaming Activision’n Ubisofttti darbuu, Microsoft dorgommii irratti ol'aantummaa akka hin qabaanne mirkaneesse,” jette.

Garuu, bitannoon kun waliigalatti wal itti qabuun industirii tapha keessatti guddaa dha. FTC (Komishinii Dorgommii Ameerikaa) Disemba darbe bitannoo kana ugguruuf himata banani, yaaddoon isaanii Microsoft Xbox fi tajaajila dorgomaa cimsuu danda’a jedhu ture. Adoolessa keessa, abbaa murtii Kalifoorniyaa FTC’n uggura gaafattee irratti murtii didee, Microsoft Call of Duty waggaa 10f PlayStation irra turuuf akkasumas Nintendo Switch geessuuf waadaa galeen booda. FTC garuu, himata kana ilaalchisee yaada isaanii hin jijjiirreef jiru; dhageettiin Muddee taasifama. Afyaa’ii FTC, Victoria Graham, “Waliigalteen Microsoft fi Activision waliin Ubisoft taasifatan dhimma dorgommii taphattoota Ameerikaarratti jijjiirama qaba; garuu FTC'n waliigalteen kun dorgommii ugguruu danda’a jennee yaadna,” jette.

Bitannoo kanaan, Microsoft studioo Blizzard sagal fi hojjettoota Activision 8,500 of jalatti hiriirfateera. Taphoota hedduus Xbox Game Pass irratti dabaluuf jiru. Jijjiirama yeroo dheeraa taphattootaaf maal akka ta'u hin beekamu, garuu hoogganaan tapha Microsoft, Phil Spencer, haala kanaaf akkana jedhe: "Xbox, PlayStation, Nintendo, PC yookaan mobile taphattanis, isiniif dhufne—teessan as jira, Xbox irra hintaphannee illee taphatanii gammachuuf bultaan siin jira. Yeroo hundaa taphatanii injifatanii irra jiraata!"

Ammas, injifatni kun Microsoftiif ta’e.

article_content: Japan's government is introducing economic relief worth more than 17 trillion yen (approximately $113 billion) to help citizens weather ongoing inflation. Prime Minister Fumio Kishida stated that a supplementary budget of 13.1 trillion yen will finance a portion of these plans. When accounting for additional funds from local governments and public loans, the stimulus package expands to 21.8 trillion yen. Key elements of the plan feature temporary tax reductions and subsidies designed to ease the burden of gasoline and utility expenses on households. Kishida stressed that Japan faces a pivotal moment after enduring decades of deflation, expressing hope that greater corporate profits will lead to higher wages. Still, inflation—fueled by increased raw material costs—has remained above the central bank’s 2% goal for over a year, squeezing family budgets and hampering the country’s economic recovery from COVID-19. The higher cost of living is being linked to falling approval ratings for Kishida’s administration, prompting pressure for urgent relief steps. Nevertheless, some experts doubt the package’s efficacy. Takahide Kiuchi, a former board member of the Bank of Japan, estimates it may raise GDP by only 0.19% this year. He suggests that with Japan’s output gap now positive, a major stimulus may not be essential. Japan's economy experienced annualized growth of 4.8% in the second quarter as pandemic restrictions ended, but recent decreases in real wages have heightened concerns about whether recovery will be long-lasting. Currently, one US dollar exchanges for about 150.51 yen.
translated_content: Mootummaan Japan deeggarsa dinagdee baay'ee guddaa – qarshii yen triliyoonii 17 ol (doolaara Ameerikaa biliyoona 113) – kan gatiin jireenyaa dabalaa jiru isaan gargaaruuf ta'u beeksiseera. Muummichi Ministiraa Fumio Kishida baajata dabalataa yen triliyoonii 13.1 baasuuf karoorfachuu ibseera. Yeroo gargaarsa mootummaa naannootii fi liqii mootummaa dabalamu, waliigalaan gargaarsi kun yen triliyoonii 21.8 ni ga’a. Kutaan ijoo karooraa kun gibira yeroodhaan xiqqeessuu fi deeggarsa kafaltii boba’aa fi ibsaa isa maatii irratti rakkina fidaa jiruuf karoorfame. article_content: India's Union Minister for Electronics and Technology, Rajeev Chandrasekhar, reiterated Prime Minister Narendra Modi's recent concerns regarding the dangers posed by deepfakes and the misuse of artificial intelligence. Speaking at a Diwali event in New Delhi on November 17, PM Modi shared his own experience with a fake video showing him doing Garba, warning citizens to be cautious about AI-generated deepfakes. Chandrasekhar pointed out that while digital technology and the internet are powerful tools for innovation and progress, they can also be manipulated to spread false information, disrupt society, and cause harm. He noted the government's introduction of updated Information Technology Rules in April 2023 aimed at protecting users online. He emphasized ongoing cooperation between government authorities and digital platforms, striving to keep India's internet secure, reliable, and open for its expanding online population, which may reach 1.2 billion people. Chandrasekhar also signaled that new regulatory measures or legislation to further address deepfakes and online misinformation could be unveiled by November 24. These warnings have become even more relevant after the recent viral spread of a deepfake video featuring actress Rashmika Mandanna, which social media users clarified was not authentic.

Kun immoo dhugaa itti-fufiinsa isaa, keessumaa viidiyoowwan deepfake actor Rashmika Mandanna irratti babal’atan yeroo ammaa kana agarsiisaniiru; fayyadamtoonni miidiyaa hawaasaa viidiyoo sun soba akka ta’e sirnaan beeksisaniiru.

article_content: The Peoples Democratic Party (PDP) honored former Nigerian President Goodluck Jonathan on his 66th birthday, describing him as a symbol of democracy and a prominent international statesman. In a statement from its National Publicity Secretary, Debo Ologunagba, the PDP highlighted achievements attributed to Jonathan’s presidency, while expressing concern that many have since been reversed. The party credited Jonathan with strengthening democratic institutions, upholding the rule of law, supporting citizens’ rights, and ensuring credible elections. PDP praised his commitment to promoting unity, mutual respect, and economic opportunities for Nigerians. They stated that under Jonathan’s leadership, Nigeria’s economy reportedly grew to $550 billion, making it Africa’s largest and ranking 26th globally by 2015. The PDP further portrayed Jonathan as honest and patriotic, dedicated to Nigeria’s peace and development. The statement accused subsequent All Progressives Congress (APC) governments of reversing these advances due to alleged corruption.

article_content: Jaime Leverton, CEO of Hut 8 Mining, has spent the past twenty years participating in all-women panels. She originally saw these as important opportunities to share her experiences and support critical conversations around the lack of female representation in technology and business. However, after recently joining yet another panel focusing on 'experiences as women' rather than expertise, Leverton made a decision: until further notice, she publicly committed to no longer taking part in all-women panels. Reflecting on the history of such panels, Leverton recalls that about a decade ago, there was widespread criticism of all-male panels at business and tech conferences. This led to increased awareness about the need for gender diversity, with conference organizers encouraging men to refuse all-male panels and adding all-women panels to event programs. Back then, because women were seldom in leadership roles, all-women panels served as vital platforms for female professionals to share their voices and build solidarity. Over time, however, Leverton has observed that many all-women panels now act as an easy way for organizers to appear diverse without truly addressing the underlying issues. These panels can give a false sense of progress and often focus on women’s shared experiences rather than their industry expertise or insights, which unintentionally suggests that their value lies mainly in their gender, not their knowledge. Leverton urges conference organizers who are committed to true inclusion to prioritize diverse panels—mixing women, men, and professionals from various backgrounds. This approach creates spaces for new perspectives and authentic representation, moving beyond token gestures. Leverton invites other female leaders to join her in declining panels designed solely for women. She suggests concrete steps for organizers: thoroughly research and seek out new voices through channels like LinkedIn groups, consider speakers from different levels—not just executives, transparently communicate what they’re looking for in speakers, and partner with organizations dedicated to promoting diversity. Leverton clarifies that she is eager to join panels comprised of women if participants are chosen for their expertise—not just their gender. However, she believes purpose-built 'Women in X' panels have had their time, and the focus should now be on giving women leaders meaningful representation across all subjects and opportunities.

article_content: I feel for everyone at OpenAI—they’re caught up in a situation they never signed up for, and they truly deserve better. If you’re stepping into leadership for the first time, especially as a CEO or board member, there’s a lot to take away from moments like this. When tempers flare and stress is high, it’s your duty to stay calm, weigh your options, predict what might happen, and act decisively. That’s the responsibility you accepted. Remember, leaders aren’t judged by what they intend to do, but by the results they achieve. Most people assume their intentions are good, but what really matters is delivering on your mission. Everyone makes mistakes in their career—the difference lies in how you take ownership, how quickly you address issues, and what you learn from them. Personally, reading 'Extreme Ownership' was a turning point that made me reflect and grow as a leader. Zooming out to the OpenAI situation, the board’s actions have not only impacted employees but also strayed from the original non-profit vision of the company. It appears that some board members failed to take responsibility, with mismanagement evident right from the start and persisting throughout the crisis. This isn’t about questioning intentions, but recognizing the consequences. To avoid such turmoil in any organization, it’s essential to include wise, level-headed advisors who can offer sound judgment—especially when emotions are running high. Running a company valued at $90 billion demands high-caliber advice and counsel. If leaders choose not to listen to their advisors, or don’t have aligned, mission-driven people advising them, that’s a recipe for disaster. All leaders need to surround themselves with a trusted network at every level—board, executive team, and beyond. Diverse perspectives matter, but everyone must share commitment to the core mission. Even just talking things out before making big decisions can help you see issues more clearly. A major source of OpenAI’s issues appears to be a deep, ongoing disagreement over what the organization’s mission truly is—whether it’s pushing the boundaries of AI, protecting humanity, or enabling open, collaborative AI research. These conflicting priorities weren’t addressed openly, and that fueled the crisis. For anyone leading an organization, three lessons stand out: embrace extreme ownership, build and rely on a supportive, trustworthy network, and ensure alignment throughout your company. One last piece of advice: listen to your employees and strive to build a unified team.

Yeroo aarii fi dhiphinni cimu, tuffachuun hin barbaachisu; gara tasgabbiitti, furmaata filachuufi adeemsa sirrii hordofuun dirqama keessan. Hoggantoota bu’aa irratti murtaa’amu, yaada gaarii qabaachuu qofaan osoo hin taane. Namni baay’ee yaada gaarii qaba jedhe ni amana, garuu waan gufuu hojirra oolu ta’e, bu’aa irratti murtaa’a. Hojii keessatti dogoggorri hunda nama mudata—garaagarummaan itti gaafatamummaa fudhachuun, rakkoo yeroodhaan hiikuun, fi wantoota keessaa barachuudhaa. Dhaabbanni qar. $90 biliyoonaa qabu gorsa ol’aanaa barbaada. Hoggantoonni gorsitoonni isaanii dhaggeeffachuu baatan ykn irraa hin hirmaanne, rakkoo hin hafu. Rakkoon OpenAI keessaa tokko waliigaltee dhabuu ilaalchisee, kaayyoon isaa maal akka ta’e irratti wal hin gallee—daangaa AI cabsuuf, nama eeguuf, ykn qorannoo AI waliin hojjechuuf. Dabalataanis, hojjettoota kee sirriitti dhaggeeffadhu, garee tokko uumi.

Many people are experiencing fatigue, which may be due to low vitamin D levels attributed to a lack of sunlight, according to recent research. Scientists have found that vitamin D, often called the 'sunshine vitamin,' energizes mitochondria—the powerhouses of our cells. It's estimated that 60% of people suffer from vitamin D deficiency. However, spending time in the sun allows our bodies to produce vitamin D, which helps muscles function more efficiently and increases energy levels.

About 90% of our vitamin D is obtained from sunlight, while the remainder comes from sources such as egg yolks, fish, and supplements. Research led by Dr. Akash Sinha showed that patients with vitamin D deficiency reported significantly higher energy levels after taking vitamin D supplements. Dr. Sinha notes that most of his patients—around 60%—are deficient in vitamin D. He further explains that people living north of Manchester or those who spend most of their time indoors often struggle to make enough vitamin D from sunlight alone.

While vitamin D is well known for its role in bone formation and preventing conditions like rickets, its influence on other health issues such as muscle fatigue—likely due to reduced mitochondrial efficiency—is becoming clearer. In the UK, approximately 60% of people are thought to be vitamin D deficient, with children under five, individuals with dark skin, and the elderly being especially vulnerable.

article_content: Matthew Lani, a TikTok influencer who claimed he was a qualified doctor, has been arrested after attempting to enter a hospital in South Africa. Lani gained thousands of followers by posting medical advice and selling medication online. On Sunday night, Lani tried to get past security at Helen Joseph Hospital in Johannesburg by wearing a surgical mask and carrying a stethoscope. He attempted to escape from police custody by jumping out of a bathroom window, but was quickly apprehended. The Gauteng Department of Health stated Lani frequently visited the hospital to create misleading content, pretending to be a licensed doctor. Before his main TikTok account was shut down, Lani had nearly 300,000 followers; he later launched a new account with over 50,000 followers. His arrest followed several weeks of investigation after doubts about his qualifications arose. Lani said he earned a medical degree from the University of Witwatersrand in Johannesburg, but the university refuted this claim. The Department of Education also said Lani did not obtain a high school leaving certificate. Lani allegedly used the name Dr Sanele Zingelwa, a real second-year medical intern at Tembisa Provincial Tertiary Hospital, in an attempt to deceive authorities. Dr Zingelwa has filed a criminal case against Lani for fraud. Lani is the latest person arrested for impersonating a doctor in South Africa. The Ministry of Health reports that around 124 individuals have been arrested for similar offenses over the past three years.

article_content: In recent years, rising incomes in China have fueled a booming demand for beef, making the country the world’s largest beef importer. Most of this beef comes from Brazil, according to United Nations trade data, making the connection between Chinese appetite and Brazilian cattle farming particularly strong. However, this surge in beef trade has a heavy environmental cost. The cattle industry in Brazil is a primary driver of Amazon rainforest destruction, with American company PMI Foods—headquartered in Salt Lake City—playing a major role as a distributor. Data from the Associated Press and the Rainforest Investigations Network reveal that PMI has shipped over $1.7 billion worth of Brazilian beef to China in the past decade, helping satisfy China’s sixfold increase in beef imports during this time. Much of the Amazon’s cleared land—over two-thirds—turns into cattle pasture, a process tracked by Brazil's Ministry of Environment. Satellite monitoring in 2022 found that more than 4,000 square miles of Amazon rainforest were lost last year, equivalent to about 3,000 soccer fields every day, according to research group Imazon. The link between beef trading and deforestation is significant. PMI obtains most of its beef from JBS SA, Brazil’s largest meat processor, known for sourcing cattle from illegally deforested land. Prosecutors and audits found that from 2019-2020, 15% of JBS’s cattle in Pará state came from such land, with a slight decrease to 6% in subsequent years. JBS maintains it has a zero-tolerance policy for illegal deforestation and is implementing tracking technology, yet it has recently acknowledged purchasing cattle from major deforesters. Another supplier, Marfrig, has faced criticism and loss of business, including being dropped by Nestlé, due to similar concerns about sourcing cattle from questionable lands. Despite claims of improved supply chain monitoring, Brazilian authorities say audits show ongoing purchases from illegally deforested areas, especially via indirect suppliers. PMI argues it relies on supplier assurances and local enforcement but has not signed major anti-deforestation agreements until recently. On top of environmental issues, PMI has previously faced U.S. legal action for illegal beef shipments to China. From 2008-2011, it earned nearly $290 million from these exports and later pleaded guilty to a misdemeanor for making false statements about exports. Now, PMI participates in reforestation and sustainability projects, reporting the planting of about 10,000 trees in the Amazon and plans for more. However, experts stress that meat traders like PMI hold the power to make or break sustainability efforts in the supply chain, arguing they must take greater responsibility for preventing deforestation. The Brazilian government and independent experts insist that the entire meat industry, from ranchers to traders, needs to guarantee traceable, environmentally sound sourcing to truly protect the Amazon.

article_content: A Pennsylvania family has suffered two devastating losses in one week. Four-year-old Karder Hardy was tragically killed just hours after attending the funeral of his father, Derrick Brown, who had been shot and killed in Chester, Pennsylvania, a suburb of Philadelphia. Authorities report that Karder had exited a Dodge Charger at 11th and Upland streets around 5 p.m. on Saturday after returning from the funeral. Witnesses say Karder ran across the street to reach his mother and was struck by a white van. Denise Brown, his great aunt, told NBCPhiladelphia.com, 'I saw him lying on the ground and was holding him, telling him to hold on.' Karder was rushed to Crozer-Chester Medical Center with severe head injuries but was pronounced dead upon arrival. The 42-year-old van driver remained at the scene and cooperated with police, who have determined the incident was a tragic accident. Earlier that week, Derrick Brown was fatally shot in the city's West End. Investigators believe he was an innocent bystander caught in crossfire. Family friend Kathy Pappas expressed the family's heartbreak, saying, 'It's too much for the family to deal with all in one day.'

article_content: Phoebe Bruce, age 17 and from Hawarden, is living with a rare genetic disorder called Ehlers-Danlos syndrome (EDS). She has weak collagen supporting her joints, so even simple actions like yawning can cause her limbs to dislocate. Phoebe experiences severe pain from multiple dislocations every day—sometimes as many as eighteen—which has recently become even worse, resulting in frequent emergency visits and ambulance calls. Her parents, Yvonne and Richard (who himself has a milder case of EDS), are appealing to the Welsh health authorities for funding to access specialized treatment at a London clinic. The family says the lengthy and frustrating funding process is putting Phoebe’s health at further risk. They hope that, if approved, specialists in London can teach Phoebe advanced techniques to cope with her condition and manage her pain. Surgery to strengthen her limbs has also come up as a possible option, but it may carry serious risks. Despite these challenges, Phoebe persists with her studies in art, psychology, and media, supported by her school and teaching assistants—even after spending much of the past year with her arms in casts. She has already earned two AS-level qualifications in art and media. Her mobility issues often disrupt her daily life and education; for example, a shopping trip to Asda ended in a medical emergency when her shoulder and back dislocated. Phoebe’s aunt, Barbara Sheady, and her doctors at Alder Hey Hospital in Liverpool describe her case as the most severe EDS they have seen. Repeated hospital visits, strong pain medication, and nutritional difficulties have all added to the family’s ordeal. With the support of teachers and a local politician, the family is urging the health authorities to approve the funding required for the specialized care Phoebe desperately needs. EDS is a group of inherited connective tissue disorders caused by defects in collagen. The severity ranges from mild to very serious, and while there is no cure, management focuses on therapy, bracing, pain relief, and sometimes surgery. The condition was named for doctors Edvard Ehlers and Henri-Alexandre Danlos and is believed to affect around 1 in 5000 people, though newer research suggests it may be more prevalent.

article_content: NEW YORK (CNN) -- Enya is an exceptional figure in the music industry. Few musicians have achieved two decades of success without ever going on tour. Enya works at her own pace, with 'And Winter Came' marking her first album release in three years. 'My fans are very, very loyal,' the Irish singer says. 'They're always asking, "When is the next album?" They understand that after I finish in the studio, it will be a few years until the next one.' The long waits between albums may contribute to Enya, 47, being Ireland's second best-selling artist, behind only U2. Her recording contract allows her the rare privilege of choosing her schedule for each album. She typically spends two to three years on a project, alternating between her home in Dublin and the studio, where she meticulously perfects chords and layers harmonies. 'I've always felt that the music stands on its own,' Enya explains. 'The music has always been the successful part of my career, letting me stay focused on it.' Her seventh studio album, 'And Winter Came,' reflects both the drama and serenity of the winter season. Since its November release, it has reached the top 10 album charts in Europe and the U.S. While Enya is hesitant to confirm plans for touring, she admits it would be exciting: 'To tour with these songs would be wonderful. It would be a grand production with an orchestra and choir—lots of rehearsals, but very exciting.' Enya discussed with CNN her musical approach, her desire for privacy, and the 20th anniversary of 'Watermark,' her breakthrough album. CNN: What does wintertime mean to you? Enya: For me, winter is when I do most of my writing in the studio. It’s a season I truly enjoy—calm and reflective. Throughout the year, I collect musical ideas, and in the winter, I bring them to the studio and see how they develop. CNN: You intended to make a Christmas album. How did it change during the process? Enya: I’ve always wanted to create a Christmas album, so I started composing carols. Some tracks began to take on broader winter themes. When I spoke with Nicky and Roma Ryan, we decided to blend both concepts, because winter includes Christmas festivities. CNN: People often think of Enya as a solo artist, but you actually work closely with others, right? Enya: I collaborate with producer Nicky Ryan and lyricist Roma Ryan. I first write the melodies in solitude, then share them with Nicky and Roma for feedback. Nicky enjoys experimenting with layers—using my voice repeatedly. Every song is different and the process is always spontaneous for me. CNN: About vocal layering—how many Enyas might we hear at once? Enya: I never count! It happens naturally. I listen to the last harmony and enhance it further. Nicky chooses whether to record my voice 20 or 30 times on a single part. CNN: Is it true you might record as many as 80 or even 500 vocal tracks? Enya: Yes, but not all at once. If there are 500 vocals, they’re recorded over two years by gradually adding parts. It’s a slow process. CNN: 'Watermark' was released about 20 years ago. Do you ever listen to it now? Enya: Yes, especially for the anniversary. Listening to 'Watermark' is like browsing a journal from that time in my life. Each song tells its own story. Because I spend so much time on each album, there’s nothing I would change about them. CNN: You adjust your approach with each album, but your sound is consistent. Do you believe in the saying, 'If it isn’t broken, don’t fix it'? Enya: I make music I enjoy performing. Could there be a guitar solo? Never say never—there’s one in 'My! My! Time Flies.' because it fit that song. My music always reflects my voice and the natural touch of melancholy from my Irish heritage. CNN: Your manager thinks your low profile is part of your success. Do you agree? Enya: It’s natural for me to maintain a low profile because I want the focus on my music. Success and fame are different things. I see my success in the music, which lets me live a normal, private life.
