Enya yeroo maashaa ishee ofii irratti hojjatti: ‘And Winter Came’ CD ishee marsaa sadii waggaa sadiin booda bahan dha. ‘Fannoon koo baay’ee amanamoo dha,’ jetti Enya, sirbistuu Irishii. ‘Yeroo hunda, “Yoom albumii itti aanuu ni baasa?” jechuu na gaafatu. Misooma studio keessa fixu booda, waggaa tokkoon booda albumiin itti aanu ni dhufa jedhaniiru.’ Turtii dheeraatu jira yeroo albumiin Enya gidduutti ba’u, kanaan Enya, umuriin waggaa 47, sirbistuu biyyattii U2 booda lammaffaa gurgurtaa olaanaa qabdu taate. Waliigaltee sirbaa isheetiin, yeroo kamuu hojii ofii geggeessuu ni dandeessi. Yeroo hedduu waggaa lama hanga sadii fudhatti, man-keessaa Dublinii fi studio gidduutti imalaa, sirboota fi harmonii guutuu gochuu irratti hojjetti. ‘Yeroo hunda jaaladha sirbi ofumaa of gurgurata jedhee,’ jette Enya. ‘Sirbi qooda ijoo qabuun, hojii koo keessatti anaaf milkaa’ina fidee, ana sirba irratti xiyyeeffachuu dandeessisa.’ Albumii studio ishee torbaffaa ‘And Winter Came’ yeroo qabbana keessa garaa garaa fi tasgabbii bakka lamatti agarsiisa. Kaasee hanga Ebla, Atlanticitti bahan irraa eegalee, irratti lafa qabateera Awurooppaa fi Ameerikaa keessa. Enya taphachuun irratti hin amanne, garuu carraa mara yaaddoftee jirti: ‘Sirboota kana waliin taphachuun namatti gammachiisa ta’a. Proojektii guddicha, orkestera fi choori waliin taphachuu. Leenjii baay’ee barbaachisa; garuu hedduu nama gammachiisa,’ jetti. Enya CNN waliin haasoftee tarkaanfii ishee sirbaa, of-qulqulleessuu fi yaadannoo waggaa 20ffaa ‘Watermark’ album ishee beekamtuu irratti mari’atte. CNN: Qabbanaaf yeroo maal siif jechuudhaa? Enya: Ani yeroo hedduu barreessuuf studio keessa qabbana keessa galeessa. Yeroo kana baay’ee jaaladha—qulqullina fi tasgabbii waan qabuuf. Guyyaa guutuu yaada sirbaa walitti qabaadhee, qabbana keessa studio dhiyaadhee gara sadarkaa sirbaa jijjiirama. CNN: Albumii Kiristaanaa hojjachuuf turte. Akkaataa itti jijjiiramee? Enya: Gara jalqabaatti albumii Kiristaanaa hojjachuuf barbaade; kanumaaf sirboota Kiristaanaa barreessu jalqabe. Sirboonni gariin garuu gara mata duree qabbanaa jijjiiramuu eegalan. Waliin dabarsinee Nicky fi Roma Ryan waliin marii goonee, mata dureewwan lamaas walitti makne; sababiin isaas, qabbana keessaa Kiristaana kabajama. CNN: Namoonni gariin Enya akka nama tokkotti ilaalan, garuu ati garee dhaa jettaa? Enya: Nicky Ryan (pirodiyuusara) fi Roma Ryan (lyricist) waliin hojjadha. Jalqaba melody tokkoon galu, yeroo isaatti qofa jiraadha. Sana booda, Nicky fi Roma wajjin yaada qoodadha, deebii argadhaa. Nicky sagalee koo baay’inaan irra deddeebisanii barreessuuf yaala; harmonii hedduu tolchu. Sirbi hundiisa garaagarummaa qaba, akkasumas tasgabbiin koo sanyiidha. CNN: Harmoniin sagalee irra deddeebi’uun meeqa sagaleen Enyaa waliin dhageetti? Enya: Lakkoofsa hin qoradhu! Ofumaan milkaa’a. Harmoniin xumuree dhaggeeffadha, isa sana irrattis cimsuuf yaala. Nicky kufaatii tokko irratti sagalee koo 20 ykn 30 galmeessuu mala. CNN: Isin sagalee 80 ykn 500 ol galmeessitan? Dhugaa dha? Enya: Eeyyee, garuu yeroo tokkoon hin taane. Yoo sagaleen 500 jiru, yeroo waggaa lama keessatti garaagaraa walitti dabalama. Proosessii suuta deemu dha. CNN: ‘Watermark’ bara 20 dura bahan. Amma deebi’anii dhageessuu ni biyyite? Enya: Eeyyee, sirna yaadannoo ilaalchisee. ‘Watermark’ dhageeffachuun akka kitaaba bara sanaa naaf fakkaata. Sirbi tokko tokko seenaa ofii qaba. Waggaa hedduu album irratti hojjachuun hin dogoggoruu na gammachiisa. CNN: Sirbii kee foormulaa jijjiirra jetta; garuu sagaleen kee garaa garaadha. Jecha, ‘Yoo hin jenne hin fooyyessiin’ ni amanajetta? Enya: Sirba ani taphachuu nan jaaladha. Gitaarri taphata laata jette yoo gaafatte: 'Yoo hin jenne hin jettu.' sirba 'My! My! Time Flies.' keessatti gitaarri solo jira, sababni isaas sirbi sun irratti hammatama. Sirba koo yeroo hunda sagalee kootiin fi garaagarummaa qalbii aadaa Irishii koo agarsiisa. CNN: Milkaa’inni kee ofii of-eeggannoo guddaa qabaachuu jechuun ni amanta? Enya: Ani baay’ee salphatti of-eeggannoo eegu, sababni isaa sirbi kiyya irratti hundaa'e jiruu. Milkaa’inni fi beekkannaan garaagaraa, an milkaa’ina sirbii irratti arga; kunis, jireenya tasgabbii fi dhuunfaadhaan jiraachuu na dandeessisa.

article_content: Amazon has rolled out a major discount for Prime subscribers on One Medical memberships, letting them access the primary care service for just $99 per year or $9 per month—down from the standard $199 annual fee. This offer is available right away and aims to provide Prime members with quicker, more convenient healthcare compared to the usual delays in the US. Up to five family members can be added for $6 per month each, extending the benefits to entire households. One Medical, purchased by Amazon for $3.9 billion, gives users access to same-day appointments at its clinics or via 24/7 virtual visits. Most One Medical members have praised the service for its ease of use, but there are common complaints about high doctor turnover, which can make consistent care challenging. Even after discounts, some people might still struggle with the subscription cost alongside regular insurance. Amazon’s move seems focused on attracting more Prime members by including healthcare perks—a valuable lure given the US healthcare system’s costs and wait times. Although concerns exist about whether an influx of new members could impact appointment availability, Amazon has likely planned for this to maintain quality. Retail theft has become a significant crisis in the United States, with industry losses reaching $112 billion in 2022. Traditionally, retailers prefer to keep a low profile on such issues, often allowing trade associations to speak on their behalf. However, the intensifying debate around retail theft reached new heights when former President Donald Trump recently stated that, if re-elected, his administration would respond aggressively. He suggested that individuals found stealing from stores could be shot as they leave—a statement that shocked many within the industry, which works to maintain a consumer-friendly image. While some dismiss Trump's comments as political bravado, they highlight how retail theft has become a highly politicized topic.

Trump’s relationship with the retail industry has a complicated history. During his presidency, some of his actions, such as imposing tariffs and withdrawing from international trade agreements, were viewed as challenging for the retail sector. His first campaign speech in 2015 resulted in Macy’s dropping his product line, following his remarks about Mexicans and Latinos, with Nordstrom later dropping Ivanka Trump’s line citing brand performance. Trump responded by calling for boycotts of these retailers. Despite once having ties to the retail industry through branded products with Macy's and Ivanka’s fashion business, Trump’s policies often created disruptions in the retail market.

Many retailers had initially hoped that Trump’s administration would bring improved tax policies and better trade deals. However, in office, Trump ended US participation in the Trans-Pacific Partnership (TPP) and later criticized President Biden’s Indo-Pacific Economic Framework (IPEF), dubbing it "TPP Two" and vowing to end it if re-elected. Trump also recently proposed a 10% tariff on all imports and referred to creating a protective "ring“ around the U.S. economy. While these moves are not always retail-friendly, Trump took credit for renegotiating NAFTA as the USMCA and halting the proposed Border Adjustment Tax.

The COVID-19 pandemic presented further challenges, with stores classified as 'essential' or 'non-essential.' Retailers like Walmart and Target, which sold food and pharmacy items, remained open, while many specialty retailers had to close. This highlighted inconsistencies in how essential businesses were determined. Disruptions in global supply chains and Trump-era tariffs contributed to ongoing inflation in apparel, footwear, and accessories. Although some tariffs targeted China, imports from China remain a major source, suggesting the tariffs did not resolve core issues.

As the 2024 election approaches, the future of the retail sector remains uncertain. Ongoing policy debates, shifting trade relationships, and the politicization of retail theft all contribute to a volatile climate for consumers and businesses. The article concludes with a caution to shoppers: 'caveat emptor'—let the buyer beware.

On Thursday, lawyers for Boston Marathon bombing suspect Dzhokhar Tsarnaev asked a judge to either dismiss the indictment against their client or suspend his trial. Their request was based on concerns that there were not enough minorities and young people in the jury pool. This motion was filed just days before opening statements and testimony were scheduled to begin in Tsarnaev’s federal death penalty trial.

According to the written motion, Tsarnaev's defense team contends that the jury selection process failed to maintain the required randomness needed when summoning potential jurors. They argue that this process infringed upon Tsarnaev's constitutional right to a jury representing a fair cross-section of the community. Specifically, out of 1,373 individuals summoned from a population of about five million in eastern Massachusetts, jury numbers were reassigned based on the time jurors reported to court for written questionnaires, rather than the original random order. The defense claims this reordering compromised the randomness and disproportionately disadvantaged certain groups, such as Black residents, people under 30, and Boston residents, pushing them lower in the selection order and decreasing their chances of being chosen.

A statistician hired by the defense found that, on average, Black prospective jurors were pushed back 43 positions in the re-ordered selection list, while white potential jurors moved up by three. Boston residents were pushed back 25 positions, and those under 30 dropped 13 spots. The statistician also noted that, after reordering, no Black prospective jurors were among the first 94 selected, whereas there would have been five if the original random order had been kept.

The defense argued that allowing people over 70 to opt out also reduced the jury pool’s diversity, stating that nearly 96 percent of those over 70 chose not to serve. They point out that although Black residents make up 6.14 percent of those eligible for jury duty, they made up only 4.25 percent of the jury pool.

Tsarnaev, 21, is charged with carrying out the twin bombings at the 2013 Boston Marathon, which killed three people and injured more than 260. Prosecutors declined to comment, and the judge has not yet ruled on the defense’s request. Opening statements in the trial are scheduled for March 4.

Tsarnaev’s attorneys have repeatedly requested a change of venue, arguing that the deep emotional impact of the bombings and personal connections within the Massachusetts community could prevent a fair trial. Judge George O’Toole Jr. has denied these requests three times. Last week, the defense took this argument to the 1st U.S. Circuit Court of Appeals, where a decision is pending.

Jeff Denner, a Boston defense attorney not involved in the case, commented that there is no contradiction in asking for a trial outside Massachusetts while also arguing that Boston residents may be underrepresented in the jury pool. According to Denner, defense attorneys ideally want the trial moved out of the area; if that’s not possible, they seek as diverse and potentially favorable a jury as they can form, possibly including more educated, urban residents likely to be receptive to arguments against the death penalty.

article_content: The Daily Mail, together with the Big Lottery Fund, is distributing over £6 million to charities aimed at improving life for people over 50. This funding is part of the Silver Dreams Fund, an early phase of a wider National Lottery effort totaling £110 million that supports projects benefiting older adults. Closely matching the Daily Mail’s ongoing campaign for elderly dignity, the initiative recognizes the positive impact and needs of older people. Grants of up to £200,000 are awarded to 37 organizations across England in this initial round, backing work that addresses rural isolation, health issues, bereavement, and the settlement of former Gurkhas. A call for nominations last October brought in nearly 1,500 applications, showing large interest. The judging panel was made up of Daily Mail columnist Bel Mooney, three readers, and Big Lottery Fund experts. Grants ranging from £50,000 to £200,000 were awarded for the development of new support ideas over the next 12–18 months. Projects that do especially well may later receive additional funding of up to £1 million each. The effectiveness of current projects will help determine the distribution of the rest of the £110 million by 2015. Based on current estimates, funds will directly help nearly 16,700 people and assist about 3,700 volunteers. Funded programs include lunch clubs like ‘Come Dine With Us’ in Durham to encourage healthy eating; Care and Repair England, which supports safe housing for seniors; Future Roots, which reduces rural isolation via farm-based activities; and Winchester Area Community Action, assisting Gurkha/Nepali elders in England. Additional grants support older adults with vision impairment, provide advice on living arrangements and care, train seniors to help others with HIV, and offer services for bereavement support. The range of activities extends to music therapy, peer mentors, and social engagements for isolated seniors. Actor Joanna Lumley welcomed the grants helping the Gurkha community. Bel Mooney spoke of her enthusiasm for the creative proposals and stressed the importance of looking after older generations. Nat Sloane, chair of the Big Lottery Fund England, emphasized the projects’ role in acknowledging the contributions of older people and meeting their daily needs. Since its launch in 2004, the Big Lottery Fund has provided £3.6 billion to charities, with this being its largest commitment to supporting the elderly.

Researchers at the University of Tsukuba have developed an innovative measurement technique to visualize fluid flow and mixing within two droplets levitated and combined in space, using fluorescence-emitting particles. This advancement enables detailed observation and estimation of internal fluid motion as droplets merge, revealing how surface vibrations during the merging process enhance fluid mixing. The findings appear in Scientific Reports.

Traditionally, managing liquids requires containers. With ultrasound technology, however, a 'lab-on-a-drop' system has been created: an ultracompact environment where droplets several millimeters in size can float and interact without a container. Mixing these small droplets posed challenges in such setups. Now, researchers from Tsukuba have introduced a merging technique and a selective color imaging method to measure how well the droplets mix.

The mixing technique uses an ultrasonic phased array—a 7×7 grid of transducers—that creates a focal point with precisely controlled ultrasonic waves. This setup lets droplets levitate, collide, and merge. To measure mixing, red and green fluorescent particles were introduced—one droplet carried red-fluorescing particles, the other green. The motion of these particles was recorded by a high-speed camera as the droplets coalesced.

By analyzing the time required for mixing, the researchers compared the effects of interfacial vibration during coalescence with those of molecular diffusion. They found that interfacial vibrations are the primary driver of efficient mixing. These results are promising for the future development and application of lab-on-a-drop devices for portable, container-free liquid analysis.

Gargaarsa meeshalee ifa baasan fayyadamuun, haala keessa ofii kana yeroo mateen walitti makaman, sochiin keessaa akkamitti faca’uu agarsiisa. Gama kaaniin, yeroo hedduu bishaan to’achuuf konteenereen barbaachisa. Makinsi mateewwan xiqqaa keessa jiran rakkoo ture. Amma garuu, qorattoonni Tsukuba mala mateewwan walitti maksuuf fi mala kallattii adda durummaan garaagarummaa walmakinsaa madaaluun qopheessan.

article_content: Families who lost relatives on Malaysian Airlines flight MH17 in July are expressing anger over what they believe is an insufficient compensation offer from the airline. The Sun Herald reported that families have been upset by the airline's offer of an initial $US50,000 (about $57,000 AUD) compensation, which has been accepted by 15 families. The passenger jet was flying from Amsterdam to Kuala Lumpur when it was shot down over eastern Ukraine on July 17, 2014, killing all 298 people on board, including 38 Australian citizens and residents. Tom and Angela Mahady, parents of passenger Edel Mahady, attended a memorial service at St Mary's Cathedral for the victims. Aviation lawyer Jerry Skinner, who previously helped negotiate $10 million in compensation from Libya for families affected by the Lockerbie disaster, called the offer from Malaysian Airlines an 'insult.' Skinner, a US attorney associated with Sydney firm LHD, is recognized as an expert in aviation disaster law and has been assisting several families seeking appropriate compensation. 'In my experience, families often file lawsuits not only due to their loss, but because they feel a lack of respect from the airline after such accidents, and that will likely happen here,' he told The Sun Herald. Mr. Skinner believes that every MH17 case warrants at least $US180,000 in compensation, which is over $200,000 AUD. He also commended Australian Prime Minister Tony Abbott for demanding justice for those killed on the flight and for his stance toward Russian President Vladimir Putin. Prime Minister Abbott stated he would confront President Putin over the MH17 tragedy, promising to 'shirtfront' him during the G20 summit in Brisbane next month. Angela and George Dyczynski, parents of passenger Fatima, traveled from Perth to search for their daughter after the crash. Australian Foreign Affairs Minister Julie Bishop met with President Putin in Milan to discuss the need for renewed access to the MH17 crash site. According to Mr. Skinner, a firm approach is necessary in dealing with President Putin. In a one-on-one discussion, Minister Bishop emphasized the importance of regaining expert access to the crash site, and President Putin agreed to use his influence with eastern Ukrainian rebels to facilitate this.

Patrick Stewart, known for his extensive acting career, recently offered a candid reflection on his iconic role as Captain Picard in Star Trek: The Next Generation. Speaking with BBC Radio 4's Front Row while discussing his new memoir Make It So, Stewart admitted he was uncomfortable with his performance in the show's first season. 'It was too stagey, too theatrical, too big,' he noted. 'I hardly ever smiled or said anything gently, which later became so important to Picard’s character. Later, I could relax.'

Stewart’s early portrayal, especially in the first two seasons, was marked by a certain stiffness and seriousness. As the series progressed, both Stewart and the character loosened up. Picard remained stoic, but Stewart allowed more warmth and humor to emerge, leading to standout performances in episodes like 'The Inner Light,' 'Best of Both Worlds,' and 'Chain of Command.'

Stewart credits this change to the support and camaraderie of his fellow cast members, though he admits their early relationship was not always smooth. He shared a story about harshly reproaching his colleagues for joking around on set—a stance he later found amusing as he himself became known for having fun during production by the end of season two.

Stewart’s evolution in the role was integral to making Picard such an enduring and memorable figure within the Star Trek universe.

Stewart BBC Radio 4'n Front Row irratti haasawaa, kitaaba isaa haaraa Make It So ilaalchisee, yeroo boqonnaa jalqabaa irratti hojii isaa hin gammadne jedhe. 'Baay'ee tiyaatirii fi akka sagalee ol ka'aa fakkaata ture; baay'ee guddaadha,' jedhe. Itti-fufiinsa jalqabaa keessatti, fakkeenya Stewart irratti, addunyaa cimaa fi of-harkaa qabu mullisuun isaa ni mul'ata. Yeroo dabran, Stewart fi fakkeenyaan isaa wal jijjiiru. Jijjiiramni Stewart paartii isaa irratti fide, Picard bakka barruu hawaasaa keessa hin irraanfatamne fi nama yaadannoo cimaa taasisu irratti gahee guddaa qaba.

David Fincher's 2011 film adaptation of The Girl With the Dragon Tattoo received strong critical acclaim and earned Rooney Mara an Academy Award nomination. Despite the positive reception and a notable opening sequence, the film was not expanded into a series, even after Sony attempted a follow-up with 2018's The Girl in the Spider’s Web, which did not resonate with audiences. 

Amazon MGM Studios is now developing a TV adaptation of Stieg Larsson’s Millennium novels. According to Variety, Veena Sud—who previously oversaw AMC’s The Killing—will serve as showrunner. Sud brings considerable experience in crime thrillers, having also contributed to Cold Case, Push, Nevada, and directed the psychological thriller The Lie for Prime Video.

First announced in 2020, the new series shares its name with Larsson’s 2005 novel but will feature a new storyline and characters focusing on the hacker Lisbeth Salander, though the role has not yet been cast. It is not yet clear if the series will adapt novels from Larsson or later Millennium authors David Lagercrantz and Karin Smirnoff. Lagercrantz wrote three follow-up books published between 2015 and 2018, while Smirnoff began her run with 2022's The Girl in the Eagle’s Talons, released in English in August.

Amazon’s recent success adapting popular crime and fantasy books suggests the Dragon Tattoo series will likely move forward. However, audience reception remains a question, as previous entries struggled to maintain momentum. Time may have increased fans' interest in following Lisbeth Salander’s adventures on screen.

article_content: St. Petersburg, Florida (CNN) – The images of birds, fish, and animals affected by oil in the Gulf of Mexico are already troubling. Now, scientists warn of another underwater threat. The University of South Florida (USF) recently discovered a second oil plume in the northeastern Gulf. The first was found by Mississippi universities in early May. USF reports that microscopic oil droplets are forming deep-water oil plumes. After a weeklong analysis of water samples, USF scientists detected more oil in deeper waters. 'These hydrocarbons are from depth and are associated with the source of the Deepwater Horizon wellhead,' said USF Chemical Oceanographer David Hollander. Using isotopic fingerprinting, Hollander’s team confirmed the oil in the plume originated from BP’s blown-out oil well. The molecular signature of the surface oil matched that of the underwater droplets. 'We've used molecular isotopic approaches, much like a fingerprint on a smoking gun,' said Hollander. BP has not commented on these latest findings but has previously denied the existence of underwater oil plumes. 'The oil is on the surface,' said BP CEO Tony Hayward. 'There aren't any plumes.' Yet, BP Managing Director Bob Dudley recently stated, 'We're absolutely taking these ideas seriously and examining them.' The USF research team aboard the vessel Weatherbird II could not visually detect the dissolved hydrocarbons or oil. Instead, their equipment picked up sensor signatures, since the plumes are clear. USF is unsure of the exact size of the plumes. 'There are indications this is fairly widespread,' said Hollander. 'There is probably more than one branch to this plume.' Scientists are worried about the effects the oil and the chemicals used to disperse it may have on marine life. Laboratory tests show bacteria have started breaking down some components of the dissolved hydrocarbons, but the impacts on fish and other marine organisms are still uncertain. 'We are in uncharted territory,' said Hollander. USF sent collected water samples to NOAA labs for further testing. NOAA has not yet commented on their conclusions. A joint press conference by NOAA and USF is scheduled at the St. Petersburg campus to share their final findings.

article_content: Spamalot has made its return to Broadway, delivering the signature Monty Python humor at the St. James Theatre. Under the direction and choreography of Josh Rhodes, the lively production successfully channels the cleverness and silliness that defined both the original musical and the 1975 film, Monty Python and the Holy Grail. Many cast members reprise their roles from the Kennedy Center's acclaimed, sold-out production in Washington, D.C., resulting in a particularly strong ensemble. Standout performances include Christopher Fitzgerald as a surprisingly sharp squire, Ethan Slater as a charmingly naive figure in distress, Michael Urie as the reluctant performer Sir Robin, Nik Walker as the proud Sir Galahad, James Monroe Iglehart as the unwavering King Arthur, Jimmy Smagula's dual roles as Sir Bedevere and Dennis’ Mother, and Leslie Rodriguez Kritzer, who steals the show playing both the Lady of the Lake and herself, often breaking the fourth wall for comedic effect. Taran Killam, standing in for Alex Brightman (occupied with The Shark Is Broken), steps confidently into diverse roles such as Lancelot, the Knight of Ni, and a mockingly French character. Killam’s comedic experience from Saturday Night Live enhances his performances in these eccentric parts. Staying true to its cinematic roots, Spamalot amplifies its fun by letting characters acknowledge their place within a Broadway show. Numbers like “The Song That Goes Like This” and “Diva’s Lament” playfully mock musical theater tropes, while Michael Urie shines in “You Won’t Succeed On Broadway,” a song that jokingly points out the historic significance of Jewish contributions to Broadway with winks to famous figures. The creative team excels: Paul Tate dePoo III’s inventive set includes projections reminiscent of Terry Gilliam’s original art, Jen Caprio provides colorful costumes, Cory Pattak designs the vibrant lighting, and Kai Harada and Haley Parcher deliver playful sound—including a cameo voiceover as God by Steve Martin. This adaptation stands out among recent movie-to-stage productions for its comedic energy, maintaining laughter even in familiar moments and satisfying both new audiences and dedicated fans. Details: 'Spamalot' is at Broadway’s St. James Theatre. Directed and choreographed by Josh Rhodes. Book and lyrics by Eric Idle, music by John Du Prez and Eric Idle. Duration: 2 hours and 20 minutes, with an intermission.

Siidaan tapha kanaa, kan yeroo Kennedy Center waliin D.C. keessatti taphatame irraa deebi’an hedduun isaanii, garee cimaa uuman. article_content: The Beatles have returned to No. 1 on a Billboard chart with their new single, 'Now and Then.' The band now holds two top 10 positions on this week’s Digital Song Sales chart, highlighting their enduring popularity. 'Now and Then' debuts at No. 1, selling 16,254 copies in its first tracking period, according to Luminate. Taylor Swift’s 'Bad Blood (Taylor’s Version)' enters at No. 2 with a little over 12,000 copies sold. Remarkably, 'Now and Then' reached the top spot despite being released only midday Thursday, November 2, with the tracking period ending as Thursday became Friday, meaning it sold the most copies in less than a full day. Also appearing on the chart is 'Love Me Do,' The Beatles’ classic track, which serves as the B-side to 'Now and Then.' The attention surrounding the new single helped propel 'Love Me Do' to No. 5, selling 5,500 copies. 'Now and Then' and 'Love Me Do' are now The Beatles’ highest-charting songs on the Digital Song Sales chart. Prior to this, their top placement was No. 26 with 'Let It Be.'

article_content: Researchers from the University of Southampton have developed a cutting-edge sensor for monitoring how glaciers respond to climate change. The lightweight device can be delivered by drones to hard-to-reach glacier locations, making it possible to collect data from areas that humans cannot easily access. The team has already put two of these sensors into use on glaciers in Iceland, enabling the collection of important data about ice melt and its link to rising sea levels. Professor Kirk Martinez, part of the development team, said this technology is the first of its kind specifically built to track glacier movements in detail. "By designing the sensors to be lightweight, we're able to use drones to reach remote spots," Professor Martinez stated. "We're receiving daily updates that reveal how the glaciers are behaving and how their speed is changing over time." Currently, the scientists are analyzing the information sent by the Iceland sensors and are looking towards deploying them in glacier regions worldwide. Professor Jane K. Hart, a geographer with the team, noted the importance of this approach since glaciers act as early indicators of climate change, and these sensors give researchers a new way to observe glacier activity.

Gareen qorannoo meeshaalee lama Icelanditti fayyadamuun, dhangala'uu galchilee fi walqabatee ol ka’iinsa galaanaa ilaaluufi deetaa barbaachisaa walitti qabuun danda’ameera. Piroofesar Kirk Martinez, miseensa garee, tekinoolojichi kan duraan jiru keessumaa sochii galchilee addaan baasuu irratti xiyyeeffate jedhan. "Meeshaaleen laafaa turanii, dooniin bakka fagoo geessuuf nu dandeessisa," Piroofesar Martinez akka jedhan. Hart, garee qorannoo keessaa, galchileen mallattoo jijjiirrama qilleensaa duraa waan ta’aniif, meeshaan kun akka haala hojii isaanii haala haaraan eegu danda’u ibsan.

article_content: Lewis Hamilton and Nicole Scherzinger celebrated their sixth anniversary by traveling to some of the world’s most romantic destinations. The 2008 Formula One world champion took Nicole, a former Pussycat Dolls singer, to Venice before they headed to New York. After returning to Monaco from the Austrian Grand Prix, Hamilton shared photos of their trips on social media. Hamilton captioned their Venice photos: 'Better late than never. @nicolescherzy & I in Venice for our 6th Anniversary. #goodtimes #godisthegreatest.' He also shared pictures from The Hamptons in New York, saying, 'Then The Hamptons New York. Always wanted to go after watching "White Chicks"! We had an amazing time. @nicolescherzy.' During the Austrian Grand Prix, held at the Red Bull Ring, Hamilton finished second behind his Mercedes team-mate Nico Rosberg. Although he pushed hard, Hamilton could not overtake Rosberg and currently sits second in the drivers’ standings with 136 points, 29 points behind Rosberg, who leads with 165. The Mercedes team celebrated securing the top two spots. Hamilton is now focused on the upcoming British Grand Prix at Silverstone, aiming to reduce Rosberg’s lead.

article_content: Michele Bachmann was officially declared the winner in her congressional race by just under 4,000 votes after nearly all ballots were counted. Her narrow victory against Jim Graves highlighted the difficulties faced by Tea Party Republicans in the 2012 elections, where several lost their seats. Prominent Tea Party members, including Allen West from Florida and Joe Walsh from Illinois, were both defeated. West, known for his outspoken remarks, lost a close and costly race to Democrat Patrick Murphy, despite raising significantly more campaign funds. Walsh also fell to Tammy Duckworth, a military veteran, who secured 55% of the vote. Other significant defeats for the Tea Party occurred in New York, where incumbents Ann Marie Buerkle and Nan Hayworth lost to Democrats Dan Maffei and Sean Patrick Maloney. Maloney’s win was notable as he became the first openly gay member of Congress from New York. Despite Bachmann’s status as a former presidential candidate and a leading fundraiser—amassing over $15 million—her win was much closer than expected. Critics cited her focus on her presidential campaign rather than district concerns, an issue her opponent attempted to capitalize on. Mia Love from Utah, another rising figure within the conservative movement, narrowly missed making history as the first Black female Republican in Congress, conceding to Democrat Jim Matheson. Tea Party representatives Michael Grimm and David Rivera both faced federal investigations. Grimm, facing campaign finance allegations, retained his seat in New York, while Rivera lost to Democrat Joe Garcia in Florida after accusations of unethical campaign behavior. While Republicans maintained control of the House of Representatives and John Boehner remained Speaker, the setbacks for key Tea Party members suggest that the movement’s influence in Congress might be waning.

article_content: NASA’s new 'Spot The Station' app, now available for iOS and Android devices, enables users to easily track and view the International Space Station (ISS) as it flies overhead. The app features a real-time, 3D map of Earth, displaying the ISS's path in relation to your location. Users get instant access to details such as the date and countdown of the next visible ISS flyover for their area. Unlike other stargazing apps, this one shows only the times when the ISS will be visible from your position, which depends on sunlight conditions. The best times to see the ISS are usually at sunset or sunrise, when sunlight reflects off its solar panels making it a bright, steady light moving smoothly across the sky. The app allows you to set alerts for upcoming passes, typically timed close to dawn or dusk. An augmented reality (AR) mode, powered by your phone’s compass and camera, lets users point at the sky and visualize where the ISS currently is or where it will appear. The app also provides recent news updates about ISS missions, crew, and events from NASA. While the Spot The Station website remains active, the new app arrives just ahead of the ISS’s 25th anniversary on December 6, 2023, bringing modern tools to fans and observers. From the ground, the ISS is seen rising in the west and crossing to the east, shining steadily for up to six minutes, unlike the blinking lights of airplanes. Its brightness peaks before it fades into Earth’s shadow. Robyn Gatens, director of NASA’s ISS program, shared her enduring excitement about seeing the station overhead and highlighted its important role in advancing science and benefiting humanity. Wishing all stargazers clear skies and amazing sightings!

App'n kun sirna map 3-D yeroo ammaa irratti hundaa'ee, daandii ISS itti deemaa jiru bakka ati jirtu waliin walqabsiisee agarsiisa. article_content: The Niger Delta Development Commission (NDDC) and Nigeria Liquefied Natural Gas (NLNG) have entered into a partnership by signing a Memorandum of Understanding to further sustainable development in the Niger Delta. The signing took place at NLNG’s head office in Port Harcourt, with NLNG Managing Director Dr. Philip Mshelbila and NDDC Managing Director Dr. Samuel Ogbuku in attendance. According to Pius Ughakpoteni, Director of Corporate Affairs at NDDC, the partnership aims to empower local communities, promote local expertise, and develop capacity. Both organizations plan to work collaboratively with stakeholders along the value chain for effective project delivery. Dr. Mshelbila remarked that the NLNG-NDDC partnership demonstrates how collaborations can create significant progress in the Niger Delta. He reinforced NLNG’s dedication to seeking strategic partners for sustainable development and stressed that investing in local community well-being is a crucial responsibility. Dr. Ogbuku added that this MoU signals the start of a new phase in cooperation intended to generate prosperity, inclusiveness, and sustainable advancement for the Niger Delta region and Nigeria as a whole.

article_content: Robert Johnson, a 65-year-old management consultant from Hereford, lost his £100,000 Bentley after attempting to drive through floodwaters in Tewkesbury, Gloucestershire. Johnson, who won £5 million in the lottery in 2008, had purchased the luxury car following his jackpot. Though he considered the Bentley his pride and joy, Johnson was not particularly upset about its destruction and had already replaced it with a new Mercedes. The incident happened as he was heading to a meeting and encountered deep floodwater on a rural road, resulting in the car being quickly submerged by about three feet of water from a bursting stream. An AA rescue vehicle arrived at the scene but could not tow the Bentley since it was only accessible from the back. As water levels rose further, Johnson was forced to abandon the vehicle. Afterward, Johnson remarked that he did not think losing the Bentley was a big deal as he already had a new car. He had chosen to keep his lottery win private and continued working to support his family. Johnson's longtime friend Bernard Robinson shared that Johnson was en route to meet him for business when the car got stranded. Although Johnson was familiar with the route, he appears to have underestimated the flood’s depth, potentially confusing his Bentley with his vintage Land Rover, which is equipped with a vehicle snorkel. Neighbors depicted Johnson as someone who recovers quickly from setbacks, believing that despite his initial disappointment, he wouldn't let the incident trouble him for long, especially given his considerable lottery fortune.

article_content: A man has been airlifted to hospital and multiple homes evacuated following an explosion in a Derbyshire town. Derbyshire Fire and Rescue Service responded to Ollersett Avenue in New Mills at 08:07 GMT on Tuesday. Twelve properties have been evacuated, and residents in the surrounding area were advised to keep doors and windows closed. High Peak Borough Council set up a rest centre for evacuees at New Mills Leisure Centre. Police, ambulance services, the air ambulance, and gas company Cadent also attended the scene. The cause of the explosion is still under investigation. According to the Derbyshire, Leicestershire and Rutland Air Ambulance, the hospitalized man sustained burns. Fire crews from New Mills, Glossop, Whaley Bridge, and Buxton, as well as a command support unit, remain at the scene. Derbyshire Police and the borough council have asked people to stay away from the area. Eyewitness Natalie Bennett, 34, a carer, described hearing 'a massive explosion.' She saw the bungalow’s front window burst out and its roof collapse. She and a group of others helped carry the injured man to safety just before the back of the house caught fire. Emergency teams arrived shortly afterward. A nearby resident reported hearing the blast and was subsequently evacuated with her three-year-old son. She said emergency services rescued the injured man before the fire began and worked to extinguish the blaze. East Midlands Ambulance Service responded at 08:10 after a medical emergency was reported, dispatching multiple vehicles and the air ambulance. The patient was flown to Northern General Hospital. For more updates, follow BBC East Midlands on social media or share story ideas via email.

Tajaajilli Ittisa Ibidaa fi Fayyadamaa Derbyshire sa’a 08:07 GMT ti Ollersett Avenue, New Mills irratti deebii kennaniiru. article_content: Nissan has announced plans to manufacture future electric versions of its two best-selling cars, the Qashqai and Juke, at its Sunderland facility. The Japanese automaker is expected to invest around £1 billion in the project, supported by the UK government's Automotive Transformation Fund (ATF). The ATF received an additional £2 billion in funding in the recent Autumn Statement. Nissan is currently the only carmaker in the UK with its own onsite battery plant, operated by Chinese company AESC and exclusively serving Nissan. The battery facility was expanded last year with approximately £100 million in public investment from the ATF and Sunderland City Council. New post-Brexit trading rules set to take effect in January will introduce a 10% tariff on cars traded between the UK and European Union unless at least 45% of components by value are sourced from the UK or EU. Many manufacturers have warned they may not meet this threshold, urging a delay in the new regulations. In May, Stellantis—which owns Vauxhall, Peugeot, Citroen, and Fiat—warned it might close its UK plants unless the government renegotiated the Brexit deal, having previously committed to electric vehicle production in Britain. The company noted that if electric car production becomes uncompetitive, UK operations could shut down. Prime Minister Rishi Sunak acknowledged manufacturers' concerns about the January deadline, noting their widespread nature across Europe. For Nissan, placing battery production onsite with the Chinese-owned plant allows it to avoid these tariffs. Nissan began electric Juke and Qashqai production in North East England last year and is committed to manufacturing the successor to the Leaf at Sunderland. Nissan's battery plant, adjacent to the Sunderland factory, is currently the only operational electric car battery facility in the UK. Tata, owner of Jaguar Land Rover, plans to build a £4 billion battery plant in Somerset, set to open in 2026. Meanwhile, Britishvolt, a North East battery startup, entered administration earlier this year. Australian company Recharge Industries later acquired it, but the takeover has faced difficulties, with nearly £2.5 million of the purchase price unpaid after months. In contrast, the European Union has 35 battery plants either operating, under construction, or planned. Nissan is well-positioned to take advantage of the business tax reform introduced in the Autumn Statement, which permanently allows full expensing of investments in plant and machinery. Despite the government's postponement of a ban on new petrol and diesel vehicles from 2030 to 2035, Nissan has reiterated its pledge to manufacture only electric cars by 2030. CEO Makoto Uchida stated this decision is right for the company, its customers, and the environment. However, the Office for Budget Responsibility, in its latest outlook, has lowered its forecast for electric car sales in the UK by 2027, predicting just 38% of new vehicles sold will be electric—down from 67% predicted in March.

Dhaabbanni Jaappaan kanaaf doolara £1 biliyoona ta’u akka galteetti, Maallaqni mootummaa Ingilizfi Automotive Transformation Fund (ATF) irraa gargaarsa argata. ATF'n £2 biliyoona dabalataa baajata keessa galchee jira. Nissan dhaabbata konkolaataa Ingiliz keessa jiru irraa, dhaabbata baatiree isa dhuunfaatti qabduu qofa. Dhaabbatni sun AESC jedhamuun Chaayinaawaa yoo ta'u, Nissan qofaaf tajaajila. Gatantaan baatiree sun bara darbe ATF-fi majlisii magaalaa Sunderland irraa qarshii 100 miiliyoonaa caalaa argachuun babal’ateera. Seerri daldalaa post-Brexit yeroo ifa ta’uuf jiru, ji’a Amajjii irraa eegalee, konkolaataa UK fi EU gidduutti gurguramuu irratti gibira 10% kaasuu qaba, yoo dhimoota keessa %45 irraa gad hin taane UK ykn EU irraa argame hin taane. Dhaabbileen hedduun hir’ina haala kanaa gabaasanii seera kana raawwachisuuf yeroo dabalataa gaafatan. Caamsaa keessa, Stellantis, keessummeessaa Vauxhall, Peugeot, Citroen fi Fiat, mootummaa waliin waliigaltee Brexit irra deebi’amuu baannaan, lafa hojii UK cufuu akka danda’u beeksise, dura konkolaataa elekriikii UK keessatti hojjechuuf waadaa galeen booda. Yeroo carraa cite, ghaaffileen hojii unkaa dorgomaa dhabuu baannaan, UK keessaa hojii cufamu mala jedhe. Muummichi Ministeeraa Rishi Sunak, arraba waldiddaa uumuuf ilaalcha daldaltootaa irratti ijjannoon isaanii UK qofaa miti garuu biyyoota Awurooppaa cufa irra jirti jedhe. Nissan dhaabbata baatiree kana lafa warra sana keessa hojjatee, gibira marsaa kana irraa bilisa tahuu danda’a. Juke fi Qashqai elektiriikii bifa haaraa bara darbe Kaaba Bahaa Ingiliz keessatti hojjeteera, akkasumas heeruma Leaf xumuruuf karoorfateera. Dhaabbatni baatiree Nissan, waajjiroota Sunderland waliin ijoo keessaa ta’ee hojjetu, yeroo ammaa UK keessatti baatiree konkolaataa elekiriikaa hojjechaa jiru kan jiru qofa. Tata, JLR qabu, Somerset irratti £4 biliyoona ta’u hojjechuu karoorfate, bara 2026tti banamuuf jira. Britishvolt, dhaabbata baatiree Kaaba Bahaa jiru, bara kana jalqaba keessa gara harka bulchiinsa ce'e. Recharge Industries kan Awustiraaliyaa pooltota isaa erga fudhate booda rakkoon jira, £2.5 miiliyoona kaffaltii payiikeetti hafuutu dhiyate. Garuu biyyoota Awurooppaa walitti UK caaluuf, dhaabbileen baatiree 35 olii ijaaramanii ykn karoorfaman jiru. Nissan gara bu’aa hojii moo’attee jiru; jijjiirama gibiraa jibbaa baatii Eblaatti labsame, galii machinery fi seer-lafa biroo baasii isaa guutumaan guutuutti hir’isuuf mirkanaayeera. Mootummaan seera konkolaataa diizel/petroolii haaraa bara 2030 irraa gara 2035tti turuufi labsanis, Nissan gara bara 2030tti konkolaataa elekriikii qofa hojjachuu waadaa haaromsite. Makoto Uchida, hogganaan, gochuun kun hojii, gurgurtaa fi lafaaf dhugaa jedha. Haa ta’u malee, OBR gabaasa isaa haaraan, gatii gurgurtaa konkolaataa elekriikii bara 2027 keessatti gara 38% gad dhiibde, kan jalqabaa 67% ji’a Bitootessa irraa gadi bu’e.

Over $11,000 (£7,000) has been raised through crowdfunding for Pham Van Thoai, a Vietnamese tourist who experienced humiliation at the hands of shop staff while trying to purchase an iPhone 6. Having saved for months to buy the phone as a gift for his girlfriend, Pham went to the well-known Sim Lim Square in Singapore. At the Mobile Air store, the initial agreed price of $950 (£595) was suddenly increased to $1,500 (£940) due to the addition of an extended warranty. Believing the warranty was complimentary, Pham agreed, but was then informed of the higher price and told he had to pay. Distressed, he pleaded for a full refund, even resorting to tears and begging on his knees, but was refused — all while someone recorded the scene.

Pham, who reportedly earns about $200 (£125) monthly as a factory worker, became the subject of international sympathy when the video was posted online. Donations poured in from around the world, and a crowdfunding campaign raised $11,713 (£7,340) for him, far surpassing the initial target of $1,350 (£846).

The campaign was started by Singaporean Gabriel Kang, who wrote that the incident was unacceptable and a sign of deeper consumer protection problems. Kang emphasized that, while individuals alone may struggle to change such issues, community action can make a difference, and that raising the funds was an act of solidarity with Pham.

After police became involved in the dispute, Pham eventually accepted a $400 (£250) refund, leaving him without the iPhone despite already spending £595. With the excess crowdfunding money, Kang intends not only to buy Pham an iPhone 6, but also to fund an all-expenses-paid holiday for Pham and his girlfriend to Singapore. Kang also mentioned plans to support another victim of a similar scam at Sim Lim Square.

Pham hanga ji’oota hedduu ittiin qusatee mi’a jaalallee isaatiif bituuf yaade. Erga walii galteen $950 (₤595) irra ga’ame, garuu dura booda, yeroo Mana Daldalaa Mobile Air gahu, gatiin isaa gara $1,500 (₤940) ol guddifame, sababa guutuu taayitaa dabalataa jedhamee. Pham tajaajilli sun tolaan akka ta’u yaade, garuu booda gatiin ol guddachuu isaa dhagahe, dirqama kafaluu akka qabu itti himan. Gadda cimaa keessa dhufnaan, deebii guutuu argachuuf carraaqe, dhiphachuu fi harka isaa lafa kaa’ee kadhate, garuu deebii didee, namnis viidiyoo kana fudhatee tamsaase.

Pham, gatii ji’a tokkootti doolara $200 (₤125) hojjetu jedhamuun beekkama, viidiyoon kun marsariitiin erga tamsahe booda akkaata gara addunyaatti namaaf dhagahame, gargaarsaan walitti qabame. Walitti qabaan kun $11,713 (₤7,340) gahe, of-eeggannoo beeksiisaan duraan $1,350 (₤846) turee ol ka’e. 

Kampaanii kana kan jalqabee Singaporean Gabriel Kang dha, rakkoon sun fudhatama hin qabu, rakkoolee tajaajila fayyadamtootaa biyyatti agarsiisa jedhe. Kang, namni dhuunfaatti tasa haala kana jijjiiruu hin dandeenye ta’uu isaa, garuu hawaasa irratti hojjachuun bu'aa fiduu kan danda’u jechuun, gargaarsii Pham waliin waliigaltee agarsiisa jedheera.

Polisiin dhimmi keessa seenuu booda, Pham $400 (₤250) deebi’ee argachuu fi iPhone hin argatiin deebi’uu dirqame, tilmaamaan £595 banee ture. Kang maallaqa ol qabame kanaan iPhone 6 bituuf qofa osoo hin taane, Pham fi jaalallee isaatif imala baasii guutuu Singaapooritti kennuuf karoorfate. Akka odeeffannoo biraatti, obsaan namni biraas Sim Lim Square keessa bittaatiin miidhe, gargaarama isaas ni ilaallata jedhameera.

article_content: Parkour runner Matt Quinlan from New Zealand suffered a dramatic accident when a misjudged leap caused him to collide face-first with a shipping container. Quinlan was attempting the last jump of a Parkour circuit over several containers. After pacing quickly through the course, he slipped during his final jump and struck his face on the side of the steel container. A friend filmed the accident and later recovered Quinlan's lost front tooth from the ground. The injury required Quinlan to get three stitches and will likely lead to an expensive dental bill. The video was posted on a page dedicated to Parkour and Freerunning videos, quickly gaining attention—though not for Quinlan's style but for the accident itself. Members of the Parkour community online criticized his technique, emphasizing that jumping from a standing start is dangerous. YouTuber Clay Eickemeyer commented that starting from a standstill hindered Quinlan's jump, causing him to hit the container. Despite criticism, Quinlan explained that injuries are a part of the sport and denied being a Parkour beginner, stating he and his friends have been training for years and that the accident was simply an unlucky slip. After realizing his tooth was missing, the pain set in, but Quinlan was fortunate not to suffer more severe injuries.

Quinlan sochii Parkour konkolaataa garaagarummaa irratti raawwachuuf yaaliin dhumaa ture. Yeroo saffisaan daandii xumura darbu, kufaani yeroo boodaa irra yeroo dhumatti kufaatii raawwatanitti fuula isaanii kanceessaa konteenara sibiilaa irratti rukutaniiru. Hiriyaan isaa viidiyoo sana suufee booda ilkaan isaa duraa dhabame argate. Miidhaan kun Quinlan akka boqqolloo olka’e fi baasiin suphaa ilkaanii isa eegdu ni jiraachuu ta'a. Viidiyoon kun fuula interneeta Parkour fi Freerunning keessatti maxxanfamee si'aayinaan bal’inaan ilaalame—sababa taphni isaa walfakkaatu osoo hin taane kufaatii bal’aa isaatif. Hirmaattonni hawaasa Parkour online tarsiimoo isaanii qeeqanii jiru, akkasumas ka’umsa dhaabbataan dhaqanii dandeettii xiqqeesu jedhaniiru. Youtuber Clay Eickemeyer rakkinni gara ka’umsa dhaabbata irraa adeemuu kufaatii isaatin walqabata jedhe. Yeroo qeeqa argate, Quinlan miidhamni tapha kanaan walqabatu akka dhalli namaa eeggatu ibsee, akkasumas tapha kana irratti isa haaraan akka hin taane, waggaa hedduuf leenjisaa turuun bakka bu’uusaa ibse. Ilkaan isaa dhabame odoo beekuun booda, dhukkubni itti dhufeera, garuu Quinlan miidhaan hamtuu biro irraa baraaramuu isaa carraaqeera.

article_content: For several months, cannabis plants have been growing near some of London's most recognizable landmarks. The group Feed The Birds has been planting cannabis seeds around locations such as Westminster, Big Ben, and along the South Bank as part of a guerrilla protest against what they describe as 'ludicrous' drug laws. The group claims their actions demonstrate that marijuana naturally thrives in Britain, arguing this as a reason for its legalization. Alongside raising awareness of the plant’s medicinal uses, the group aims to provide crops for users, reducing reliance on black market dealers. Feed The Birds released photographs showing the illegal plants growing next to Tower Bridge, the Shard, and on busy London streets. They are urging the government to follow Uruguay and several American states that have legalized the Class B drug. Finn Hemingway, a farmer and representative of the group in his twenties, explained: 'We have two primary objectives. We want to raise awareness for medical users who need cannabis to improve their quality of life. We also want to supply medical and recreational users with seeds so they are no longer dependent on black market dealers.' This protest echoes actions in Göttingen, Germany, where thousands of cannabis plants appeared last year as part of a similar campaign. Hemingway added: 'The war on drugs is a catastrophic failure, and cannabis growing openly on the streets of London highlights how illogical our drug laws are. Putting a person in prison for using a plant is the real crime.'
translated_content: Ji’oota hedduu darban keessa, biqiltoonni kaanaabisi bakka beekamoo magaalattii London muraasa biratti guddachaa jiru. Gareen Feed The Birds jedhamu kaanaabisi Westminster, Big Ben fi daandii South Bank irratti facaasee jira, kunis mormii afaan guutuu seera qor-qalbii ‘akka namaan hin fudhanne’ jedhu irratti taasifame. Gareen kun hojimaata isaanii agarsiisuun, kaanaabisiin Briteen keessatti haala salphaan ni biqilti, kanaafuu seeraan akka hayyamamuu qabdu jedhaniiru. Dabalataanis, itti fayyadamtootaaf qorannoo yaala kaanaabisii irratti beekamtii ol kaasaa, akkasumas bittaa makiinaa dhoorkame jalaa baasuuf midhaan isaanii qopheessuuf hojjetaa jiru. Feed The Birds suuraalee muka kaanaabisi seeraan ala ta’e kan Tower Bridge, Shard fi daandii Uummataa London irratti biqilaa jiru gadi lakkisan. Mootummaan UK akka seera kanaabisi biyyoota Uruguay fi Ameerikaa muraasa fakkaataniin hayyamameen irratti qooda fudhatu gaafataa jiru. Finn Hemingway, qonnaan bulaa fi bakka bu’aa garee kanaa, umrii isaa digdama keessa, akkana jedha: ‘Kaayyoo ijoo lama qabna. Fayyaa isaan dhukkubsatan fooyyessuuf kaanaabisi barbaadan nuuf beekamu qaba. Akkasumas, itti fayyadamtoota yaalaafi bashannanaaf mankuusa makiinaa guutuu irraa of bilisa taasisuuf ijoo kaa’ame.’ Mormiin kun akkuma bara darbe Göttingen, Jarmanii keessatti taasifamee ture, yeroo sana kaanaabisi kumaatama ta’u biqilaa turan. Hemingway itti dabaluun, ‘Waraanni dawaa kufaatii guddaa dha, kaanaabisi karaa uummataatti iddoo argate kun seerota dawaa keenya akka salphaa fakkaata. Nama muka fayyadamuuf mana hidhaatti galchuun yakka dhugaa ti,’ jedheen.

article_content: Doctor Who fans are rallying to name a newly discovered planet after Gallifrey, the iconic home planet from the TV series. A petition has been set up by fans, known as 'Whovians', to rename the gas giant 'Gallifrey' in honor of the Time Lords' world. Within the last 24 hours, more than 80,000 people have signed the petition. The planet, officially called HD 106906 b, was discovered this year by the University of Arizona and has puzzled astronomers due to its unusual characteristics. Scientists note that HD 106906 b is an oddity under current planet formation theories, as it is 11 times the mass of Jupiter and orbits its star at about 650 times the distance from Earth to the Sun. The young planet, only 13 million years old, still glows from residual heat left over from its formation, with a temperature around 2,700°F (1,500°C), much cooler than its star, and emits most of its energy as infrared radiation. In comparison, Earth is around 4.5 billion years old—about 350 times older than HD 106906 b. Gallifrey, the fictional world from Doctor Who, is said in the show to be in a binary star system in the Kasterborous constellation, 250 million light-years from Earth. The petition was started by Australian fan Sam Menhennet, who is appealing to the International Astronomical Union to rename the planet in honor of Doctor Who's 50th anniversary. Sam stated, 'Doctor Who is legendary, award-winning, record-breaking, and global, and this planet deserves something special and supernatural as its name. How better to celebrate its existence than by naming it after Gallifrey, home of our beloved Doctor?' The petition can be signed on Change.org.
translated_content: Fannoonni Doctor Who biyya maraa maqaa planetaa haaraa argameef Gallifrey, bakka Doctor Who keessatti beekamu, kenneefii yaadanii jiru. ‘Whovians’ jedhaman kun, petition tokko qopheessuun planetaan kun maqaaf Gallifrey jedhamu akka moggaafamu gaafataa jiru. Sa’aatii 24 keessatti, nama 80,000 ol petition kana mallatteessaniiru. Planetaan kun maqaan isa dhugaa HD 106906 b yoo ta’u, bara kana Yunivarsiitii Arizona’tiin argameera; qorattoota hawaa immoo akkaataa uumama isaatiin dhamaasiseera. Saayintistoonni, planetaan kun, Jupiter caalaa walakkaa 11 ulfaata, urjiisaa irraammoo addunyaa fi aduu gidduu jiru irraa 650 caalaa fagaata jedhanii ibsaniiru. Planetiin kun wagga 13 miliyoona qofa qaba, ho’aa uumama ishee irraa hafte itti jira, bakka digrii Fahrenhayit 2,700 (Celsius 1,500) irratti argamti. Ho’a ishee kan baaftu baay’inaan ifa infra-red ittiin baafti, urjiisaa irra ho’aa xiqqoodha. Addunyaan uumamaan waggaa biliyoona 4.5 gadii qaba—kan HD 106906 b caalaa waggaa 350 ol dabalata jechuudha. Gallifrey, addunyaa xiqqaa Doctor Who keessatti, sagaleen keessatti akka urjii lamaan keessa jiru Kasterborous jedhutti himama, addunyaa irraa mil. laayitii 250 fagaatti jedhamu. Petition kun fana Awustraaliyaa Sam Menhennet jalqabee, International Astronomical Union akka planetaan maqaa Doctor Who waggaa 50ffaa yaadachuuf moggaafamu gaafata. Sam, ‘Doctor Who tapha guddaa, badhaasa argate, seenaan mataa isaa, addunyaa mara keessa beekamaadha. Planetiin kun maqaa addaa fi cimaa argachuu qaba. Yaadannoo guddaa kennuuf maqaa Gallifrey, bakka doktariif beekamu moggaafnee maaliif hin kabajnu?’ jedhe. Petition kana Change.org irratti mallatteessuu dandeessu.
post_content: Whovians unite! Over 80,000 fans want to rename planet HD 106906 b as 'Gallifrey' after Doctor Who's home world. It's 11x bigger than Jupiter and totally baffles scientists! #DoctorWho #Gallifrey #SpaceNews
translated_post: Whovians waliin haa kaanu! Fannoonni 80,000 ol planetaan HD 106906 b akka ‘Gallifrey’ jedhamu barbaadu – bakka Doctora Who keessa jiru. Isheen Jupiter caala 11 ulfaatti, saayintistootan immoo dinqisiifatama! #DoctorWho #Gallifrey #Hawaa

article_content: Mick Schumacher, the 15-year-old son of seven-time Formula One World Champion Michael Schumacher, is building on his father's legacy by achieving impressive results in karting. This season, Mick finished second in the German junior kart championships after competing closely with his main rival, David Beckmann. He also earned the runner-up position at the world championships in France last month and has won the European title this year. Mick has stated that this is 'only the beginning' of his career in motorsport. He began racing under the name Mick Jnr, a nod to his famous father, and previously competed with his mother Corinna's maiden name, Betsch. Michael Schumacher, currently 45, is still recovering from a major head injury suffered in a skiing accident in December in the French Alps. He spent months in a coma and is now undergoing rehabilitation at home in Switzerland. Michael, who started racing karts at a young age and became German Kart Champion at 15, went on to become one of the sport's greatest drivers with seven world titles. The Schumacher family, including Mick, has largely maintained privacy about Michael’s health. Manager Sabine Kehm recently stated that Michael has made progress, but that recovery will be a 'long and difficult' journey. The family thanked the staff at CHUV Lausanne for their care and requested continued respect for their privacy.
translated_content: Mick Schumacher, ijoollee waggaa 15 fi ilma Michael Schumacher, mo’ataa Formula One yeroo torbaa injifate, seenaa abbaa isaa itti fufuun milkaa’ina guddaa fiigicha kartii keessatti galmeessee jira. Barana, Mick tapha cimaa David Beckmann waliin taasiseen garee ji'oollee kartii Jarmanii isa lammaffaa ta'e. Akkasumas, ji'a darbe tapha addunyaa kartii Faransaayitti isa lammaffaa ta’ee, teessuma Awurooppaa waggaa kana mo’ateera. Mick akkana jedhee ibseera: ‘Kun jalqaba malee xumurri miti’ jechuun kareerawwan isaa keessatti abdii qabaachuu isaa agarsiiseera. Yeroo kana, maqaa Mick Jnr jedhuun dorgomuu eegale; duraan ammoo maqaa haadha isaa Corinna Betsch jedhuun hirmaataa ture. Michael Schumacher, umurii isaa 45, amma yeroo ammaa kana madaa hamaa garaa isaa irra ga’eef yaalii itti fufaa jira; kun booda skiing Muddee darbe Alps Faransaayitti mudateen ture. Ji’oota hedduu koma keessa ture, amma ammoo mana yaalaa isaatti wal’ansa itti fufee jira. Michael yeroo ijoollee ture kaasee kartii tapha, waggaa 15tti mo’ataa Kartii Jarmanii ta’uun booda immoo mo’ataa tapha kanaa yeroo torbaa ta’ee seenaa tapha kanaa keessatti galmeessee jira. Maatiin Schumacher, Mick dabalatee, dhimmoota wal’ansa Michael ilaalchisee dhoksaa baay’ee tursiisaa jiru. Sabine Kehm, giiftii dhimma isaanii, akka ibsetti, Michael fooyya’aa gochaa jira; garuu deebi’insa isaa ‘yeroo fi jabaatinaa’ fedha jedhee ibseera. Maatiin isaanii tajaajiltoota hospitaala CHUV Lausanne galateeffatan; kabajaan iccitii maatii isaanii akka eegamu gaafatan.

article_content: Rajya Sabha MP Sanjay Raut, from the Uddhav Thackeray-led faction of Shiv Sena, has alleged that the Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) ensured that cricketer and 1983 World Cup-winning captain Kapil Dev was not invited to watch the finals of the India-Australia World Cup Match in Gujarat on Sunday. Raut claimed on Monday that Kapil Dev was not invited because the BJP did not want the spotlight taken away from its leaders attending the event. "I saw Kapil Dev's statement today—the man who brought us the World Cup. He wasn't invited to the finals, since inviting him would've meant less publicity for political leaders present. This is political maneuvering," Raut said. The Rajya Sabha MP praised the Indian cricket team's performance and suggested the result may have been different if the match was played in Mumbai or Delhi. "Traditionally, finals are held in Mumbai, but many jobs and industries are leaving the city. People are saying if the match had been held in Mumbai, India might have won." Raut accused the BJP of deliberately holding the final in Gujarat at the Narendra Modi Stadium for political gain. "They renamed Vallabhbhai Patel Stadium to Narendra Modi Stadium to host the final. If India had won, the BJP could claim the victory was due to the venue's association with Modi. This was their strategy. Unfortunately, despite a strong performance, India lost," stated Raut. In other news: The government is considering the legality of transferring unclaimed funds from the Sahara-Sebi Refund Account to the Consolidated Fund of India, while ensuring investors can claim refunds later. Apple aims to reach ₹1 lakh crore worth of iPhone production in India by March 2024, having already surpassed ₹60,000 crore in production so far this fiscal year. Nawaz Modi, estranged wife of industrialist Gautam Singhania, is seeking three-quarters of his $1.4 billion net worth for herself and their two daughters as part of a family settlement. Keywords: Sanjay Raut, Uddhav Thackeray, BJP leaders, Kapil Dev, Narendra Modi, Mumbai, World Cup, Gautam Singhania, Nawaz Modi, Sahara-Sebi, Apple, India.

article_content: A significant shipwreck from World War II, the SS Thistlegorm, rests 30 metres beneath the Red Sea. This British Merchant Navy ship, built in 1940 in Sunderland, was sunk by two German bombers on October 6, 1941, while transporting a diverse cargo of military vehicles, motorcycles, and wartime supplies from Glasgow to Alexandria, Egypt. The ship, measuring 128 metres in length, was carrying items such as Bedford trucks, armoured vehicles, Norton 16H and BSA motorcycles, Bren guns, ammunition, aircraft parts, radio equipment, Wellington boots, and two steam locomotives bound for Egyptian railways. The vessel was part of a convoy traveling to Egypt and was accompanied by a crew of 41 and nine Royal Navy personnel, commanded by Captain William Ellis. An explosion in the main hold, caused when bombs ignited the onboard ammunition, sank the ship. Four merchant crew and five Royal Navy members lost their lives. Captain Ellis was awarded the OBE, and Angus McLeary received the George Medal and Lloyd’s War Medal for Bravery at Sea for saving a fellow crew member. Rediscovered in 1956 by explorer Jacques-Yves Cousteau, the well-preserved wreck now attracts divers from around the world. British diver Mark Harris described the site as a somber reminder of wartime events and noted that artifacts, like a Wellington boot, remain in place out of respect. Today, the SS Thistlegorm serves as both a historical site and a home to marine life, with tropical fish swimming among the remains.

article_content: World number eight Karolina Muchova has withdrawn from the WTA Finals in Cancun because of a right wrist injury. She will be replaced by first alternate Maria Sakkari of Greece, according to tour officials on Tuesday, October 24. Czech player Muchova qualified for the season-ending tournament by reaching the Cincinnati final and US Open semifinal, losing both times to American Coco Gauff. "Together with my team and doctors, we tried everything until the last moment to resolve my wrist injury," Muchova said in a statement. "Unfortunately, the time needed for recovery is longer than we had hoped, so I had to make this difficult decision." As a result, ninth-ranked Sakkari will compete in her third consecutive WTA Finals at this year's event, which starts on Sunday, after reaching the semifinals last year.

article_content: A dispute has arisen between the Trump family and Florida officials over the valuation of the Mar-A-Lago property. Earlier, New York State Judge Arthur Engoron further restricted the Trump family's access to their assets, citing concerns over inflated values. In Florida, Congressperson Jared Moskowitz has asked the Palm Beach County Property Assessor to reconsider Mar-A-Lago's taxable valuation after Judge Engoron noted some reported valuations for the property were far below those claimed by the Trump family. Members of the Trump family responded by publicly asserting that Mar-A-Lago and other properties are worth much more than current assessments indicate. For instance, Eric Trump has claimed that Mar-A-Lago could be worth as much as $1 billion, while the current assessed taxable value is about $26 million. Moskowitz argues that if the higher valuation is accurate, the Trump family would owe significantly more in property taxes and has requested a reassessment. According to records, Mar-A-Lago was assessed between $18 million and just under $28 million between 2011 and 2021. Moskowitz referenced a tweet from Eric Trump, which claimed that Mar-A-Lago may be worth many times the assessed amount. The situation centers on whether the Trump Organization has inflated or understated property values for personal benefit.

article_content: Exceptional leadership is a cornerstone of organizational success and longevity in today's global business environment. Chief Experience Officers (CXOs) are key to shaping strategies that prioritize customer needs. Each year, Forbes, a prominent business magazine, highlights outstanding CXOs worldwide for their contributions to customer experience and innovation.  Forbes’ 2023 list of the top 10 CXOs showcases leaders who have transformed industries and set new standards for customer satisfaction:  1. Elon Musk (Tesla, SpaceX): Regularly featured in Forbes' rankings, Elon Musk’s leadership at Tesla has turned electric vehicles into a global trend, while his drive for sustainability and innovation continues to shape both the automotive and aerospace industries. At SpaceX, Musk pursues ambitious goals like Mars colonization.  2. Tim Cook (Apple Inc.): As Apple’s CEO, Cook has preserved and built upon Steve Jobs’ legacy by expanding the product lineup and focusing on services such as Apple Music and Apple TV+. His emphasis on privacy and the seamless Apple ecosystem ensures exceptional user experiences.  3. Satya Nadella (Microsoft): Taking charge in 2014, Nadella has repositioned Microsoft toward cloud computing and artificial intelligence, bringing offerings like Azure and Teams to the forefront. His leadership emphasizes inclusivity, sustainability, and technological advancement.  4. Mary Barra (General Motors): Barra is a pioneer in the auto industry, guiding GM into the era of electric vehicles with models like the Chevrolet Bolt and Cadillac Lyriq. Her focus on innovation and sustainability strengthens GM’s role in cleaner transportation.  5. Reed Hastings (Netflix): Co-founder and co-CEO, Hastings has moved Netflix to the center stage of entertainment by delivering streaming content globally and adapting to evolving viewer preferences while emphasizing original programming.  6. Lisa Su (AMD): Su’s stewardship has empowered AMD to compete with major semiconductor firms through advanced processors and GPUs, gaining a devoted customer base by prioritizing innovation.  7. Ajay Banga (Mastercard): As CEO, Banga has championed digital payments and financial inclusion, helping to position Mastercard at the frontline of the transition to cashless economies and expanding access to financial services.  8. Gwynne Shotwell (SpaceX): As President and COO, Shotwell has been instrumental in SpaceX’s ascension in aerospace with innovations such as Falcon rockets and Starship, further opening up access to space travel and satellite services.  9. Stewart Butterfield (Slack Technologies): The co-founder and CEO of Slack transformed workplace communication with a user-friendly platform that enhances collaboration and connectivity for businesses, especially in the era of remote work.  10. Shantanu Narayen (Adobe Inc.): Narayen has led Adobe through a major shift to cloud-based subscription services like Creative Cloud and Document Cloud, making the company’s products more accessible and user-oriented.  Forbes' selection criteria for these CXOs encompass financial performance, innovation, leadership qualities, industry influence, corporate social responsibility, previous recognitions, long-term vision, adaptability, and professional reputation.  Frequently Asked Questions: 1. How does Forbes select the top 10 CXOs? Through a combination of editorial research, industry analysis, and expert opinions, considering each CXO's leadership and role in enhancing customer experience. 2. Are these CXOs ranked? The list is generally alphabetical, not ranked by influence or performance. 3. How often is the list updated? Forbes typically publishes the list annually. 4. What impact do these CXOs have? Their leadership drives innovation, improves business outcomes, and transforms customer experiences. 5. Examples of industry impact? Musk accelerated global electric vehicle adoption at Tesla; Cook improved privacy and integration at Apple; Shotwell expanded access to space travel at SpaceX; Narayen made Adobe services more accessible with a subscription model.  In summary, Forbes’ 2023 top 10 CXOs are recognized for leadership that redefines their industries and heightens customer-centric practices, significantly impacting business standards worldwide.

Shantanu Narayen (Adobe Inc.): Adobe gara tajaajila cloud fi subscription model jijjiiruu isaaniitiin, fayyadamummaa fi argama oomishoota isaanii dabalan.  Forbes CXOs kana filachuuf hojii fi milkaa’inaa daldalaa, haaromsa, dandeettii hoggansi, miidhama industirii, itti gaafatamummaa hawaasa, beekamtii dursaa, tarsimoo yeroo dheeraa, dandeettii jijjiiramaa fi maqaa hojii irratti xiyyeeffata.  Gaaffiiwwan yeroo baay’ee dhiyaatan: 1. Forbes CXOs filachuuf maal fayyada? Qorannoo, xinxala industirii fi yaada ogummaa, hoggansa fi gahee muuxannoo fayyadamtootaa ilaaluun filata. 2. CXOs kunneen tartiibaan ramadaman? Lakkoofsi tartiiba hin qabanii, maqaa isaanii qofa irratti hunda’a. 3. Yeroo hangamii tarree kana Forbes baasaa? Waggaa waggaan. 4. Miidhaan hoggantoota kana maal? Hoggansi isaanii haaromsa industiri keessa fidu, bu’aa argamsiisu fi fayyadamtoota gammachiisa. 5. Fakkeenya jijjiirama industirii? Musk – Tesla irratti konkolaataa elektiriikaa addunyaatti dadarbuun, Cook – Apple irratti iccitii fi walitti dhufeenya fooyyessu, Shotwell – SpaceX irratti chilalli bal’isu, Narayen – Adobe irratti galmee fi Creative Cloud fayyadamummaa dabalu.  Sochiiwwan hoggantoonni 2023 tan Forbes keessa jiran hojii isaanii fi fayyadamtootaaf fidaa jiran, industirii fi hojii biyya lafaa keessatti inni bu’uura.

article_content: Danny Welbeck, now an Arsenal player following his £16 million move from Manchester United, says joining the club has always been a dream. In an interview, he talked about his excitement at becoming part of Arsenal’s playing style and working alongside their talented midfield. Welbeck, wearing the number 23, expressed his happiness that the transfer finally happened. He admitted that while at Manchester United he scored 29 goals over 142 games, he often played out of position or as a substitute, which limited his impact. At 23, Welbeck feels he now has the chance at Arsenal to establish himself as a main striker, particularly with Olivier Giroud injured. He’s looking forward to benefitting from passes from teammates like Alexis Sanchez, Jack Wilshere, and Mesut Ozil. Though leaving Manchester United was bittersweet after many years there, Welbeck believes signing for Arsenal is the right move for his growth. He’s eager to show his pace and power and is drawn to the club’s fast, short-passing approach. Despite some critics suggesting Arsenal should have signed Radamel Falcao instead, Welbeck is confident he can play a key role in helping Arsenal aim for the Premier League title and other trophies.

Arsenal tapha isaanii fi midfieldilaan isaa waliin taphachuuf gammachuu agarsiiseera. Welbeck lakkoofsa 23 uffatee, walitti dhufeenyi kun dhugaa ta'uusaa irratti gariidha jedheera. article_content: Samsung is releasing the November 2023 software update for the Galaxy Watch 6 and Galaxy Watch 6 Classic, with an emphasis on a simpler experience for users. As reported by DroidLife, U.S. owners are starting to get the update, and Verizon has provided an official changelog. Galaxy Watch 6 users will receive firmware R935USQU1AWK4 for the 40mm model and R945USQU1AWK4 for the 44mm model, while Watch 6 Classic users will get R955USQU1AWK4 (43mm) and R965USQU1AWK4 (47mm). A key part of this update is the removal of 'Samsung' from the names of several apps, such as Samsung Pay and Samsung Wallet. These will now simply appear as 'Pay' and 'Wallet.' Other apps like Health and Global Goals are also getting the updated naming. The update promises general improvements for the watch, though specific enhancements are not detailed. It may take a few days for the update to appear for all users, but you can also check for it manually through the Galaxy Wearable app or the device settings. An existing issue remains with Gboard on these smartwatches—and other wearables using Wear OS 4—where using the keyboard in some apps like Google Keep or Samsung Reminder results in a black screen. This may also cause the Bixby voice assistant to stop responding. Until a fix is available, users are advised to use Samsung’s default keyboard, which is reportedly functioning well. The Galaxy Watch 6 includes hardware upgrades over its predecessor, such as a new Exynos processor, increased RAM, and slimmer bezels, enhancing its usefulness for daily notifications and health tracking.

Akka gaazexaa DroidLife tti, Amerikaa keessatti fayyadamtoonni haaromsicha amma argachuu jalqaban, Verizon immoo deetaa haaromsichaa baasuu isaa mirkaneessa. Samsung Galaxy Watch 6 irratti, firmware R935USQU1AWK4 modeli 40mm fi R945USQU1AWK4 modeli 44mmf kennameera. Watch 6 Classic irratti immoo R955USQU1AWK4 (43mm) fi R965USQU1AWK4 (47mm) ni ta'a. Haaromsichi fooyya’insi guutuu sa’aatiirratti raawwatame jira jedha, garuu tarkaanfii dabalataa ifatti hin ibsame. Rakkoo kana furuutti utuu hin geenye, fayyadamtoonni keyboardiin Samsung kan duraanii fayyadamuuf gorsa argataniiru; kanuma immoo rakkoo tokko malee hojjechaa jira. Galaxy Watch 6 fooyya’insa tekinooloojii qaba: processor Exynos haarawaa, RAM baay'ee fi bezel qaxxaamura xiqqaate qaba, kanaan odeeffannoo guyyaa guyyaa fi hordoffii fayyaa irratti siif mijaja.

article_content: A 79-year-old hunter from White Township, Pennsylvania, was found dead on Wednesday after accidentally shooting himself during a deer hunt. James Turnbull's body was found by another hunter just before 5 p.m. in a wooded area near his home. Indiana County Coroner Jerry Overman Jr. stated that the investigation determined no foul play or involvement from others. However, it remains unclear exactly how Turnbull’s rifle discharged. State police, the coroner, and the Pennsylvania Game Commission are still looking into the case. White Township is located approximately 45 miles northeast of Pittsburgh. This tragic accident mirrors similar recent hunting incidents in the region. In New Jersey last month, a 45-year-old man from Chesterfield died after accidentally shooting himself while goose hunting with his father. He was pronounced dead at the scene, though his father was unhurt. Authorities confirmed that both men had the proper licenses and were hunting with Canada goose decoys laid out in front of their blind. Just days earlier in Maine, 30-year-old Aaron Burke from Mattawamkeag suffered serious injuries after slipping along the Mattawamkeag River during a deer hunt. The fall caused his 30-30 rifle to go off, shooting him in the arm and torso. Despite his injuries, Burke managed to climb out of the woods and call for help.

Indiana County Coroner Jerry Overman Jr. akka jedhetti, qorannoon gaggeeffame namni biroo dhimmicha keessa seenee hin jiru, qalbii hamaa irra darbamee hin jiru. Garuu ammoo, rifeelichi akkamitti akka hojiirra oole hin beekamu. Poolisii naannoo, coroner fi Komishinii Bineensota Pennsylvania qorannoo itti fufaa jiru. article_content: Margaret Thatcher, the only woman to have served as the United Kingdom's prime minister, is recovering at The Ritz hotel in London following a minor procedure to remove a bladder growth. At 87, Thatcher faces health challenges, including reduced mobility and short-term memory loss from previous strokes. Since the stairs at her Belgravia home pose difficulties, she's chosen to recuperate at The Ritz, a place she enjoys, where attentive staff and two carers ensure her comfort. After her 'minimally invasive' surgery just days before Christmas, Thatcher was discharged from the hospital. Although she planned to celebrate with her niece Jane Mayes, her hospital stay altered those plans. Jane is the daughter of Thatcher's late sister, Muriel. With her children, Sir Mark and Carol, away abroad, friends and former colleagues have visited to support her during recovery. Visitors include Conor Burns MP, Lord Forsyth, Lord Powell, Sir Bernard Ingham, Dame Sue Tinson, Cynthia Crawford (her longtime assistant), and Alison Wakeham. Friends report that, despite some memory difficulties, Thatcher is lively during visits and enjoys being part of conversations. Recently, Lord Parkinson and his wife Ann hosted Thatcher and her carer for afternoon tea. Hotel staff are making every effort to ensure a homely atmosphere. Friends describe Thatcher as being in good spirits, well cared for, and enjoying the company she keeps.
